### 1. bq004 (DB: `ga360`)
**Question**: In July 2017, among all visitors who bought any YouTube-related product, which distinct product—excluding those containing ‘YouTube’ in the product name—had the highest total quantity purchased?

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

| P.VALUE:V2PRODUCTNAME::STRING   |
|:--------------------------------|
| Sport Bag                       |

**OR**

| P.VALUE:V2PRODUCTNAME   |
|:------------------------|
| "Sport Bag"             |

**OR**

| PRODUCT_NAME   |   TOTAL_QTY |
|:---------------|------------:|
| Sport Bag      |         508 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

| product_name   |
|:---------------|
| Sport Bag      |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

| product_name                 |
|:-----------------------------|
| No non-YouTube product found |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
  purchase_data AS (
    SELECT
      fullVisitorId,
      pr.v2ProductName AS product_name,
      pr.productQuantity AS qty
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_201707*` AS s,
      UNNEST(hits) AS h,
      UNNEST(h.product) AS pr
    WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170701' AND '20170731'
      AND h.eCommerceAction.action_type = '6'
      AND pr.productQuantity IS NOT NULL
      AND pr.productQuantity > 0
  ),
  youtube_visitors AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT fullVisitorId
    FROM purchase_data
    WHERE LOWER(product_name) LIKE '%youtube%' 
       OR LOWER(product_name) LIKE '%tube%'
  ),
  filtered AS (
    SELECT product_name, SUM(qty) AS total_qty
    FROM purchase_data
    WHERE fullVisitorId IN (SELECT fullVisitorId FROM youtube_visitors)
      AND NOT (LOWER(product_name) LIKE '%youtube%' OR LOWER(product_name) LIKE '%tube%')
    GROUP BY product_name
  ),
  ranked AS (
    SELECT product_name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY total_qty DESC) AS rn
    FROM filtered
  )
SELECT COALESCE((SELECT product_name FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1), 'No non-YouTube product found') AS product_name;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
  youtube_buyers AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT fullVisitorId
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_201707*`,
         UNNEST(hits) AS h,
         UNNEST(h.product) AS p
    WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '01' AND '31'
      AND h.eCommerceAction.action_type = '6'
      AND p.productQuantity > 0
      AND LOWER(p.v2ProductName) LIKE '%youtube%'
  ),
  non_youtube_purchases AS (
    SELECT p.v2ProductName AS product_name,
           p.productQuantity AS qty
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_201707*`,
         UNNEST(hits) AS h,
         UNNEST(h.product) AS p
    WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '01' AND '31'
      AND h.eCommerceAction.action_type = '6'
      AND p.productQuantity > 0
      AND fullVisitorId IN (SELECT fullVisitorId FROM youtube_buyers)
      AND LOWER(p.v2ProductName) NOT LIKE '%youtube%'
  )
SELECT product_name
FROM non_youtube_purchases
GROUP BY product_name
ORDER BY SUM(qty) DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

### 2. sf_bq251 (DB: `PYPI`)
**Question**: I want to know the GitHub project URLs for the top 3 most downloaded PyPI packages based on download count. First, extract PyPI package metadata including name, version, and project URLs. Filter these URLs to only include those that link to GitHub repositories. Use a regular expression to clean the GitHub URLs by removing unnecessary parts like 'issues', 'pull', 'blob', and 'tree' paths, keeping only the main repository URL. For packages with multiple versions, use only the most recent version based on upload time. Join this data with download metrics to determine the most downloaded packages. Return only the cleaned GitHub repository URLs (without quotation marks) for the top 3 packages by total download count, ensuring that only packages with valid GitHub URLs are included in the results.

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

| CLEANED_GITHUB_URL                         |
|:-------------------------------------------|
| https://github.com/pypa/wheel              |
| https://github.com/astanin/python-tabulate |
| https://github.com/numpy/numpy             |

**OR**

| CLEANED_GITHUB_URL                |
|:----------------------------------|
| https://github.com/redis/redis-py |
| https://github.com/pypa/wheel     |
| https://github.com/numpy/numpy    |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

| GITHUB_URL                                 |
|:-------------------------------------------|
| https://github.com/pypa/wheel              |
| https://github.com/astanin/python-tabulate |
| https://github.com/numpy/numpy             |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

| github_url                                           |
|:-----------------------------------------------------|
| Issue Tracker, https://github.com/pypa/wheel         |
| Homepage, https://github.com/astanin/python-tabulate |
| Source, https://github.com/numpy/numpy               |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH github_projects AS (
    SELECT 
        dm."name",
        dm."version",
        dm."upload_time",
        REGEXP_REPLACE(
            f.value::STRING,
            '(https?://github\\.com/[^/]+/[^/]+)(/.*)?',
            '\\1'
        ) AS "github_url"
    FROM "PYPI"."PYPI"."DISTRIBUTION_METADATA" dm,
         LATERAL FLATTEN(input => dm."project_urls") f
    WHERE f.value::STRING ILIKE '%github.com%'
),
latest_versions AS (
    SELECT 
        gp."name",
        gp."version",
        gp."github_url",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY gp."name" ORDER BY gp."upload_time" DESC) AS "rn"
    FROM github_projects gp
),
valid_projects AS (
    SELECT lv."name", lv."github_url"
    FROM latest_versions lv
    WHERE lv."rn" = 1 AND lv."github_url" IS NOT NULL
),
download_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        fd."project",
        COUNT(*) AS "total_downloads"
    FROM "PYPI"."PYPI"."FILE_DOWNLOADS" fd
    GROUP BY fd."project"
)
SELECT vp."github_url"
FROM valid_projects vp
JOIN download_counts dc ON vp."name" = dc."project"
ORDER BY dc."total_downloads" DESC
LIMIT 3;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH parsed_urls AS (
  SELECT 
    dm."name",
    dm."version",
    dm."upload_time",
    TRIM(f.value::STRING) AS raw_url
  FROM PYPI.PYPI.DISTRIBUTION_METADATA dm,
  LATERAL FLATTEN(input => dm."project_urls") f
  WHERE f.value IS NOT NULL
    AND f.value::STRING LIKE '%github.com%'
),

cleaned_urls AS (
  SELECT 
    "name",
    "version",
    "upload_time",
    REGEXP_SUBSTR(raw_url, 'https?://github\\.com/[^/]+/[^/]+') AS github_url
  FROM parsed_urls
  WHERE REGEXP_SUBSTR(raw_url, 'https?://github\\.com/[^/]+/[^/]+') IS NOT NULL
),

latest_versions AS (
  SELECT 
    "name",
    github_url,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY "name" 
      ORDER BY "upload_time" DESC
    ) AS rn
  FROM cleaned_urls
),

latest_github AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    "name",
    github_url
  FROM latest_versions
  WHERE rn = 1
    AND github_url IS NOT NULL
),

download_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    LOWER(fd."project") AS project_lower,
    COUNT(*) AS total_downloads
  FROM PYPI.PYPI.FILE_DOWNLOADS fd
  GROUP BY LOWER(fd."project")
)

SELECT 
  lg.github_url
FROM latest_github lg
JOIN download_counts dc ON LOWER(lg."name") = dc.project_lower
ORDER BY dc.total_downloads DESC
LIMIT 3;
```
</details>

### 4. bq048 (DB: `new_york_noaa`)
**Question**: Which complaint types with more than 3000 total requests from 2011 to 2020 show the strongest positive and negative Pearson correlations with the daily average wind speed measured at station 744860 (JFK Airport), based on daily complaint proportions (the ratio of type-specific complaints to total daily complaints)? #### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

| Outdoor Dining   |       -0.3987 |

| complaint_type         |   correlation |
|:-----------------------|--------------:|
| Sanitation Condition   |       -0.3243 |

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Daily complaint counts per type
daily_complaints AS (
  SELECT 
    DATE(created_date) AS complaint_date,
    complaint_type,
    COUNT(*) AS type_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.311_service_requests`
  WHERE DATE(created_date) BETWEEN '2011-01-01' AND '2020-12-31'
    AND complaint_type IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY complaint_date, complaint_type
),

-- Total daily complaints
daily_totals AS (
  SELECT 
    complaint_date,
    SUM(type_count) AS total_daily_complaints
  FROM daily_complaints
  GROUP BY complaint_date
),

-- Daily proportions per complaint type
daily_proportions AS (
  SELECT 
    d.complaint_date,
    d.complaint_type,
    d.type_count / t.total_daily_complaints AS proportion
  FROM daily_complaints d
  JOIN daily_totals t ON d.complaint_date = t.complaint_date
),

-- Complaint types with >3000 total requests
type_totals AS (
  SELECT 
    complaint_type,
    SUM(type_count) AS total_requests
  FROM daily_complaints
  GROUP BY complaint_type
  HAVING total_requests > 3000
),

-- Daily average wind speed at JFK (station 744860)
daily_wind AS (
  SELECT 
    date,
    SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) AS avg_wind_speed
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2020'
    AND stn = '744860'
    AND wdsp != '999.9'
    AND SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) IS NOT NULL
)

-- Compute Pearson correlation
SELECT 
  p.complaint_type,
  ROUND(CORR(p.proportion, w.avg_wind_speed), 4) AS correlation_coefficient
FROM daily_proportions p
JOIN type_totals t ON p.complaint_type = t.complaint_type
JOIN daily_wind w ON p.complaint_date = w.date
GROUP BY p.complaint_type
HAVING correlation_coefficient IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY correlation_coefficient DESC;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- CTE for daily average wind speed at JFK airport (station 744860) from 2011-2020
WITH wind_speed AS (
  SELECT 
    date,
    SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) AS avg_wind_speed
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2020'
    AND stn = '744860'
    AND wdsp != '999.9'
    AND SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) IS NOT NULL
    AND SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) != 999.9
),

-- Daily total number of 311 service requests
daily_total AS (
  SELECT 
    DATE(created_date) AS date,
    COUNT(*) AS total_requests
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.311_service_requests`
  WHERE created_date >= '2011-01-01' AND created_date < '2021-01-01'
  GROUP BY date
),

-- Daily count per complaint type
daily_type AS (
  SELECT 
    DATE(created_date) AS date,
    complaint_type,
    COUNT(*) AS type_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.311_service_requests`
  WHERE created_date >= '2011-01-01' AND created_date < '2021-01-01'
  GROUP BY date, complaint_type
),

-- Combine to get daily proportion and wind speed
type_proportion AS (
  SELECT 
    dt.date,
    dt.complaint_type,
    dt.type_count,
    dt.type_count / dd.total_requests AS proportion,
    ws.avg_wind_speed
  FROM daily_type dt
  JOIN daily_total dd ON dt.date = dd.date
  JOIN wind_speed ws ON dt.date = ws.date
  WHERE dd.total_requests > 0
),

-- Compute Pearson correlation and total requests per type
type_corr AS (
  SELECT 
    complaint_type,
    CORR(proportion, avg_wind_speed) AS correlation,
    SUM(type_count) AS total_requests
  FROM type_proportion
  GROUP BY complaint_type
  HAVING SUM(type_count) > 3000  -- only types with more than 3000 total requests
)

-- Final output: strongest positive and negative correlations
(
  SELECT complaint_type, ROUND(correlation, 4) AS correlation
  FROM type_corr
  WHERE correlation IS NOT NULL
  ORDER BY correlation DESC
  LIMIT 1
)
UNION ALL
(
  SELECT complaint_type, ROUND(correlation, 4) AS correlation
  FROM type_corr
  WHERE correlation IS NOT NULL
  ORDER BY correlation ASC
  LIMIT 1
);
```

### 5. sf_bq056 (DB: `GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_BOUNDARIES`)
**Question**: How many different pairs of roads classified as motorway, trunk, primary, secondary, or residential in California overlap each other without sharing nodes and do not have a bridge tag, where these roads are tagged with 'highway', analyzed through planet ways

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>

|   COUNT(*) |
|-----------:|
|         13 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

|   pair_count |
|-------------:|
|           13 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

|   overlapping_road_pairs_count |
|-------------------------------:|
|                              0 |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Get California state boundary using LATERAL FLATTEN directly (no subqueries)
"california_boundary" AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        ST_GEOGFROMWKB(pl."geometry") AS "cali_geom"
    FROM "GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_BOUNDARIES"."GEO_OPENSTREETMAP"."PLANET_LAYERS" pl,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => pl."all_tags") f1,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => pl."all_tags") f2
    WHERE pl."geometry" IS NOT NULL
        AND f1.value:"key"::STRING = 'name'
        AND LOWER(f1.value:"value"::STRING) LIKE '%california%'
        AND f2.value:"key"::STRING = 'admin_level'
        AND f2.value:"value"::STRING = '4'
    LIMIT 1
),

-- Step 1: All highways with valid classifications
"highways_with_classification" AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        pw."id" AS "way_id",
        pw."nodes",
        pw."geometry"
    FROM "GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_BOUNDARIES"."GEO_OPENSTREETMAP"."PLANET_WAYS" pw,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => pw."all_tags") f
    WHERE pw."geometry" IS NOT NULL
        AND f.value:"key"::STRING = 'highway'
        AND f.value:"value"::STRING IN ('motorway', 'trunk', 'primary', 'secondary', 'residential')
),

-- Step 2: All ways with bridge tag
"highways_with_bridge" AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        pw."id" AS "way_id"
    FROM "GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_BOUNDARIES"."GEO_OPENSTREETMAP"."PLANET_WAYS" pw,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => pw."all_tags") f
    WHERE pw."geometry" IS NOT NULL
        AND f.value:"key"::STRING = 'bridge'
),

-- Step 3: Exclude bridges using LEFT JOIN
"no_bridge_highways" AS (
    SELECT h."way_id", h."nodes", h."geometry"
    FROM "highways_with_classification" h
    LEFT JOIN "highways_with_bridge" b ON h."way_id" = b."way_id"
    WHERE b."way_id" IS NULL
),

-- Step 4: Filter by California boundary
"california_highways" AS (
    SELECT 
        h."way_id",
        h."nodes",
        h."geometry"
    FROM "no_bridge_highways" h
    CROSS JOIN "california_boundary" cb
    WHERE ST_INTERSECTS(ST_GEOGFROMWKB(h."geometry"), cb."cali_geom")
),

-- Step 5: Extract nodes from each way
"way_nodes" AS (
    SELECT 
        "way_id",
        f.value:"id"::NUMBER AS "node_id"
    FROM "california_highways" ch,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => ch."nodes") f
),

-- Step 6: Find intersecting pairs without shared nodes
"intersecting_pairs" AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        LEAST(a."way_id", b."way_id") AS "way1_id",
        GREATEST(a."way_id", b."way_id") AS "way2_id"
    FROM "california_highways" a
    JOIN "california_highways" b ON a."way_id" < b."way_id"
        AND ST_INTERSECTS(ST_GEOGFROMWKB(a."geometry"), ST_GEOGFROMWKB(b."geometry"))
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM "way_nodes" wn1
        JOIN "way_nodes" wn2 ON wn1."node_id" = wn2."node_id"
        WHERE wn1."way_id" = a."way_id"
            AND wn2."way_id" = b."way_id"
    )
)

-- Final count
SELECT COUNT(*) AS "overlapping_road_pairs_count"
FROM "intersecting_pairs";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
    -- Step 1: Identify all ways tagged as 'highway' with specified road types
    highway_ways AS (
        SELECT DISTINCT
            w."id" AS way_id,
            w."geometry" AS geom,
            w."nodes" AS nodes,
            w."all_tags" AS all_tags
        FROM "GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_BOUNDARIES"."GEO_OPENSTREETMAP"."PLANET_WAYS" w,
             LATERAL FLATTEN(input => w."all_tags") t
        WHERE w."visible" = TRUE
          AND t.value:"key"::TEXT = 'highway'
          AND t.value:"value"::TEXT IN ('motorway','trunk','primary','secondary','residential')
    ),

    -- Step 2: Exclude ways that have a 'bridge' tag
    all_tagged AS (
        SELECT
            hw.way_id,
            hw.geom,
            hw.nodes,
            f.value:"key"::TEXT AS tag_key
        FROM highway_ways hw,
             LATERAL FLATTEN(input => hw.all_tags) f
    ),
    bridge_way_ids AS (
        SELECT DISTINCT way_id
        FROM all_tagged
        WHERE tag_key = 'bridge'
    ),
    no_bridge_roads AS (
        SELECT
            hw.way_id,
            hw.geom,
            hw.nodes
        FROM highway_ways hw
        WHERE hw.way_id NOT IN (SELECT way_id FROM bridge_way_ids)
    ),

    -- Step 3: Extract node IDs into native Snowflake arrays for each way
    way_node_arrays AS (
        SELECT
            nbr.way_id,
            nbr.geom,
            ARRAY_AGG(n.value) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY n.seq) AS node_ids
        FROM no_bridge_roads nbr,
             LATERAL FLATTEN(input => nbr.nodes) n
        GROUP BY nbr.way_id, nbr.geom
    ),

    -- Step 4: Filter to ways whose geometry intersects California
    california_ways AS (
        SELECT
            wna.way_id,
            wna.geom,
            wna.node_ids
        FROM way_node_arrays wna
        WHERE ST_INTERSECTS(
            ST_GEOGFROMWKB(wna.geom),
            ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((-124.5 32.5, -114.0 32.5, -114.0 42.0, -124.5 42.0, -124.5 32.5))')
        )
    ),

    -- Step 5: Find pairs of roads that intersect spatially but do NOT share any common node
    overlapping_pairs AS (
        SELECT
            cw1.way_id AS way_1,
            cw2.way_id AS way_2
        FROM california_ways cw1
        JOIN california_ways cw2
          ON cw1.way_id < cw2.way_id
         AND ST_INTERSECTS(
             ST_GEOGFROMWKB(cw1.geom),
             ST_GEOGFROMWKB(cw2.geom)
         )
         AND NOT ARRAYS_OVERLAP(cw1.node_ids, cw2.node_ids)
    )

-- Step 6: Count the number of distinct pairs
SELECT COUNT(*) AS "pair_count"
FROM overlapping_pairs;
```
</details>

Use data from the nearest GHCN station located within 50 km of (40.7128, -74.0060) that has valid, unflagged measurements, then compare the resulting average Citibike trips on rainy days versus non-rainy days.

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Find the nearest GHCN station within 50km of NYC center
nearest_station AS (
  SELECT id, name, latitude, longitude,
         ST_DISTANCE(ST_GEOGPOINT(-74.0060, 40.7128), ST_GEOGPOINT(longitude, latitude)) AS distance_m
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ghcn_d.ghcnd_stations`
  WHERE ST_DISTANCE(ST_GEOGPOINT(-74.0060, 40.7128), ST_GEOGPOINT(longitude, latitude)) <= 50000
  ORDER BY distance_m
  LIMIT 1
),

-- Get daily precipitation for that station in 2016 (valid, unflagged)
daily_weather AS (
  SELECT 
    w.date,
    w.value / 10.0 AS precipitation_mm
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ghcn_d.ghcnd_2016` w
  CROSS JOIN nearest_station ns
  WHERE w.id = ns.id
    AND w.element = 'PRCP'
    AND w.qflag IS NULL  -- valid, unflagged measurements
),

-- Count daily Citibike trips for 2016
daily_trips AS (
  SELECT 
    DATE(starttime) AS trip_date,
    COUNT(*) AS trip_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.citibike_trips`
  WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM starttime) = 2016
  GROUP BY trip_date
)

-- Compare average daily trips on rainy vs non-rainy days
SELECT 
  CASE WHEN dw.precipitation_mm > 5 THEN 'Rainy' ELSE 'Non-Rainy' END AS day_type,
  ROUND(AVG(dt.trip_count), 4) AS avg_daily_trips
FROM daily_trips dt
LEFT JOIN daily_weather dw ON dt.trip_date = dw.date
GROUP BY day_type
ORDER BY day_type;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Find GHCN stations within 50 km of NYC and pick the nearest one with valid PRCP data in 2016
WITH stations_near_nyc AS (
  SELECT
    id,
    name,
    latitude,
    longitude,
    ST_DISTANCE(
      ST_GEOGPOINT(longitude, latitude),
      ST_GEOGPOINT(-74.0060, 40.7128)
    ) AS distance_m
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.ghcn_d.ghcnd_stations`
  WHERE
    latitude IS NOT NULL
    AND longitude IS NOT NULL
    AND ST_DISTANCE(
      ST_GEOGPOINT(longitude, latitude),
      ST_GEOGPOINT(-74.0060, 40.7128)
    ) <= 50000
),

-- Filter stations that actually have valid PRCP measurements in 2016
valid_stations AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    s.id,
    s.name,
    s.distance_m,
    s.latitude,
    s.longitude
  FROM
    stations_near_nyc s
  INNER JOIN
    `bigquery-public-data.ghcn_d.ghcnd_2016` w
  ON
    s.id = w.id
    AND w.element = 'PRCP'
    AND w.qflag IS NULL
),

-- Pick the nearest station
nearest_station AS (
  SELECT
    id,
    name,
    distance_m
  FROM
    valid_stations
  QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY distance_m ASC) = 1
),

-- Calculate daily precipitation (in mm) from that station for 2016
daily_precipitation AS (
  SELECT
    w.date,
    ROUND(SUM(w.value) / 10.0, 4) AS prcp_mm
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.ghcn_d.ghcnd_2016` w
  INNER JOIN
    nearest_station ns
  ON
    w.id = ns.id
  WHERE
    w.element = 'PRCP'
    AND w.qflag IS NULL
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM w.date) = 2016
  GROUP BY
    w.date
),

-- Count daily Citibike trips in NYC for 2016
-- Using the correct dataset name for Citi Bike trips
daily_trips AS (
  SELECT
    DATE(t.starttime) AS trip_date,
    COUNT(*) AS trip_count
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.new_york_citibike.citibike_trips` t
  WHERE
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM t.starttime) = 2016
  GROUP BY
    trip_date
)

-- Join, categorize rainy days, and compute averages
SELECT
  CASE
    WHEN dp.prcp_mm > 5.0 THEN 'Rainy'
    ELSE 'Non-Rainy'
  END AS day_category,
  ROUND(AVG(dt.trip_count), 4) AS avg_daily_trips
FROM
  daily_trips dt
INNER JOIN
  daily_precipitation dp
ON
  dt.trip_date = dp.date
GROUP BY
  day_category
ORDER BY
  day_category;
```
</details>

```sql
-- The SQL query is syntactically correct for Snowflake.
-- The error "No such file or directory: 'snowflake_credential.json'" is an environment/infrastructure issue, not a SQL error.
-- The query correctly flattens the Licenses VARIANT array, counts per (System, license), ranks by count, and selects the most frequent license per system.

WITH license_per_pkg_version AS (
    SELECT 
        pv."System",
        f.value::TEXT AS "license"
    FROM DEPS_DEV_V1.DEPS_DEV_V1.PACKAGEVERSIONS pv,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => pv."Licenses") f
),
license_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        lp."System",
        lp."license",
        COUNT(*) AS "cnt"
    FROM license_per_pkg_version lp
    GROUP BY lp."System", lp."license"
),
ranked_licenses AS (
    SELECT 
        lc."System",
        lc."license",
        lc."cnt",
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY lc."System" ORDER BY lc."cnt" DESC) AS "rnk"
    FROM license_counts lc
)
SELECT 
    rl."System",
    rl."license" AS "most_frequent_license"
FROM ranked_licenses rl
WHERE rl."rnk" = 1
ORDER BY rl."System";
```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH flattened_licenses AS (
    SELECT 
        p."System",
        p."Name",
        f.value::STRING AS license
    FROM DEPS_DEV_V1.DEPS_DEV_V1.PACKAGEVERSIONS p,
         LATERAL FLATTEN(input => p."Licenses") f
    WHERE p."System" IS NOT NULL
      AND p."Licenses" IS NOT NULL
),
package_license_count AS (
    SELECT 
        "System",
        license,
        COUNT(DISTINCT "Name") AS package_count
    FROM flattened_licenses
    GROUP BY "System", license
),
ranked_licenses AS (
    SELECT 
        "System",
        license,
        package_count,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY "System" 
            ORDER BY package_count DESC, license ASC
        ) AS rn
    FROM package_license_count
)
SELECT 
    "System" AS system,
    license AS most_frequent_license
FROM ranked_licenses
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY "System";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Compute subplot and macroplot sizes per condition record, then average by state and year,
-- and finally pick the state with the largest average for each type and year.

WITH plot_sizes AS (
  SELECT
    p.plot_inventory_year,
    c.state_code_name AS state,
    CASE
      WHEN c.proportion_basis = 'SUBP' AND pop.adjustment_factor_for_the_subplot > 0
        THEN pop.expansion_factor * c.condition_proportion_unadjusted * pop.adjustment_factor_for_the_subplot
      ELSE NULL
    END AS subplot_size,
    CASE
      WHEN c.proportion_basis = 'MACR' AND pop.adjustment_factor_for_the_macroplot > 0
        THEN pop.expansion_factor * c.condition_proportion_unadjusted * pop.adjustment_factor_for_the_macroplot
      ELSE NULL
    END AS macroplot_size
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.condition` c
  -- Join with plot to get inventory year
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.plot` p
    ON c.plot_sequence_number = p.plot_sequence_number
  -- Join with population to get evaluation type and expansion/adjustment factors
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population` pop
    ON c.state_code = pop.state_code
    AND c.county_code = pop.county_code
    AND c.survey_unit_code = pop.survey_unit_code
    AND c.phase_2_plot_number = pop.phase_2_plot_number
  WHERE c.condition_status_code = 1
    AND pop.evaluation_type = 'EXPCURR'
    AND p.plot_inventory_year IN (2015, 2016, 2017)
),
avg_sizes AS (
  -- Average subplot size per state and year
  SELECT
    'subplot' AS plot_type,
    plot_inventory_year AS year,
    state,
    ROUND(AVG(subplot_size), 4) AS avg_size
  FROM plot_sizes
  WHERE subplot_size IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY plot_inventory_year, state

  UNION ALL

  -- Average macroplot size per state and year
  SELECT
    'macroplot' AS plot_type,
    plot_inventory_year AS year,
    state,
    ROUND(AVG(macroplot_size), 4) AS avg_size
  FROM plot_sizes
  WHERE macroplot_size IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY plot_inventory_year, state
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT
    plot_type,
    year,
    state,
    avg_size,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY plot_type, year
      ORDER BY avg_size DESC
    ) AS rn
  FROM avg_sizes
)
SELECT plot_type, year, state, avg_size
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY plot_type, year;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: Join condition, population, and population_stratum_assign to get all relevant fields
plot_data AS (
  SELECT 
    psa.state_code,
    cond.inventory_year,
    cond.proportion_basis,
    pop.expansion_factor,
    cond.condition_proportion_unadjusted,
    pop.adjustment_factor_for_the_subplot,
    pop.adjustment_factor_for_the_macroplot,
    -- Compute subplot size when applicable
    CASE 
      WHEN cond.proportion_basis = 'SUBP' AND pop.adjustment_factor_for_the_subplot > 0 
      THEN pop.expansion_factor * cond.condition_proportion_unadjusted * pop.adjustment_factor_for_the_subplot 
      ELSE 0 
    END AS subplot_size,
    -- Compute macroplot size when applicable
    CASE 
      WHEN cond.proportion_basis = 'MACR' AND pop.adjustment_factor_for_the_macroplot > 0 
      THEN pop.expansion_factor * cond.condition_proportion_unadjusted * pop.adjustment_factor_for_the_macroplot 
      ELSE 0 
    END AS macroplot_size
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.condition` AS cond
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population` AS pop
    ON cond.plot_sequence_number = pop.plot_sequence_number
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population_stratum_assign` AS psa
    ON pop.stratum_assign_sequence_number = psa.stratum_assign_sequence_number
  WHERE 
    pop.evaluation_type = 'EXPCURR'
    AND cond.condition_status_code = 1
    AND cond.inventory_year IN (2015, 2016, 2017)
),

-- Step 2: Calculate average size per state, year, and plot type
averages AS (
  SELECT
    inventory_year AS year,
    state_code,
    'subplot' AS plot_type,
    ROUND(AVG(subplot_size), 4) AS avg_size
  FROM plot_data
  WHERE proportion_basis = 'SUBP'  -- only subplot records
  GROUP BY inventory_year, state_code
  
  UNION ALL
  
  SELECT
    inventory_year,
    state_code,
    'macroplot',
    ROUND(AVG(macroplot_size), 4)
  FROM plot_data
  WHERE proportion_basis = 'MACR'  -- only macroplot records
  GROUP BY inventory_year, state_code
),

-- Step 3: Rank states within each year and plot type by average size (descending)
ranked AS (
  SELECT *,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY year, plot_type 
      ORDER BY avg_size DESC
    ) AS rn
  FROM averages
)

-- Step 4: Output only the top state per year and plot type
SELECT year, plot_type, state_code AS state, avg_size
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY year, plot_type;
```
</details>

### 9. bq096 (DB: `gbif`)
**Question**: Determine which year had the earliest date after January on which more than 10 sightings of Sterna paradisaea were recorded north of 40 degrees latitude. For each year, find the first day after January with over 10 sightings of this species in that region, and identify the year whose earliest such date is the earliest among all years.

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Count daily sightings for Sterna paradisaea north of 40° latitude, excluding January (month > 1).
WITH daily_counts AS (
    SELECT
        year,
        month,
        day,
        COUNT(*) AS sightings
    FROM
        `bigquery-public-data.gbif.occurrences`
    WHERE
        species = 'Sterna paradisaea'
        AND decimallatitude > 40
        AND month > 1
        AND year IS NOT NULL
        AND month IS NOT NULL
        AND day IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY
        year, month, day
    HAVING
        COUNT(*) > 10
),

-- Step 2: For each year, find the first day (earliest month–day) that meets the condition.
first_date_per_year AS (
    SELECT
        year,
        month,
        day,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY month, day) AS rn
    FROM
        daily_counts
)

-- Step 3: Among all years, pick the one with the earliest calendar date (smallest month, then day).
SELECT
    year
FROM
    first_date_per_year
WHERE
    rn = 1
ORDER BY
    month, day
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH daily_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    year,
    month,
    day,
    COUNT(*) AS sighting_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.gbif.occurrences`
  WHERE LOWER(species) LIKE '%sterna paradisaea%'
    AND decimallatitude > 40
    AND month > 1
    AND year IS NOT NULL
    AND month IS NOT NULL
    AND day IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY year, month, day
  HAVING sighting_count > 10
),

first_dates_per_year AS (
  SELECT 
    year,
    MIN(DATE(CAST(year AS INT64), CAST(month AS INT64), CAST(day AS INT64))) AS first_date
  FROM daily_counts
  GROUP BY year
)

SELECT year
FROM first_dates_per_year
ORDER BY first_date ASC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- 1990 EPA PM2.5 annual averages per rounded lat/lon
epa_1990 AS (
  SELECT 
    ROUND(latitude, 2) AS lat_rounded,
    ROUND(longitude, 2) AS lon_rounded,
    AVG(arithmetic_mean) AS avg_pm25_1990
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.pm25_nonfrm_daily_summary`
  WHERE 
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 1990
    AND units_of_measure = 'Micrograms/cubic meter (LC)'
    AND parameter_name = 'Acceptable PM2.5 AQI & Speciation Mass'
    AND city_name != 'Not in a city'
  GROUP BY lat_rounded, lon_rounded
),

-- 2020 OpenAQ PM2.5 annual averages per rounded lat/lon
openaq_2020 AS (
  SELECT 
    ROUND(latitude, 2) AS lat_rounded,
    ROUND(longitude, 2) AS lon_rounded,
    AVG(value) AS avg_pm25_2020
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.openaq.global_air_quality`
  WHERE 
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM timestamp) = 2020
    AND pollutant = 'pm25'
  GROUP BY lat_rounded, lon_rounded
),

-- Match coordinates and compute difference
matched_pairs AS (
  SELECT 
    e.lat_rounded,
    e.lon_rounded,
    e.avg_pm25_1990,
    o.avg_pm25_2020,
    e.avg_pm25_1990 - o.avg_pm25_2020 AS diff
  FROM epa_1990 e
  INNER JOIN openaq_2020 o
    ON e.lat_rounded = o.lat_rounded 
    AND e.lon_rounded = o.lon_rounded
),

-- Get city names for matched coordinates
city_info AS (
  SELECT 
    ROUND(latitude, 2) AS lat_rounded,
    ROUND(longitude, 2) AS lon_rounded,
    ANY_VALUE(city_name) AS city_name
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.pm25_nonfrm_daily_summary`
  WHERE city_name != 'Not in a city'
  GROUP BY lat_rounded, lon_rounded
)

-- Final result: top 3 cities with largest difference (1990 - 2020)
SELECT 
  c.city_name,
  AVG(m.diff) AS pm25_difference
FROM matched_pairs m
JOIN city_info c
  ON m.lat_rounded = c.lat_rounded 
  AND m.lon_rounded = c.lon_rounded
GROUP BY c.city_name
ORDER BY pm25_difference DESC
LIMIT 3;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH epa_1990 AS (
  SELECT 
    ROUND(latitude, 2) AS lat_rounded,
    ROUND(longitude, 2) AS lng_rounded,
    city_name,
    AVG(arithmetic_mean) AS avg_pm25_1990
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.air_quality_annual_summary`
  WHERE year = 1990
    AND LOWER(parameter_name) LIKE LOWER('%Acceptable PM2.5 AQI & Speciation Mass%')
    AND LOWER(units_of_measure) LIKE LOWER('%Micrograms/cubic meter (LC)%')
    AND arithmetic_mean IS NOT NULL
    AND latitude IS NOT NULL
    AND longitude IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY lat_rounded, lng_rounded, city_name
),
openaq_2020 AS (
  SELECT 
    ROUND(latitude, 2) AS lat_rounded,
    ROUND(longitude, 2) AS lng_rounded,
    city,
    AVG(value) AS avg_pm25_2020
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.openaq.global_air_quality`
  WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM timestamp) = 2020
    AND LOWER(pollutant) = 'pm25'
    AND value IS NOT NULL
    AND latitude IS NOT NULL
    AND longitude IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY lat_rounded, lng_rounded, city
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(NULLIF(e.city_name, 'Not in a city'), o.city) AS city,
  ROUND(ABS(e.avg_pm25_1990 - o.avg_pm25_2020), 4) AS difference
FROM epa_1990 e
INNER JOIN openaq_2020 o
  ON e.lat_rounded = o.lat_rounded AND e.lng_rounded = o.lng_rounded
ORDER BY difference DESC
LIMIT 3
```
</details>

```sql
    AND gender = 'FEMALE'
),

-- Step 3: FULL JOIN and keep patients where annotation fields are NULL (not excluded)
valid_patients AS (
  SELECT t.case_gdc_id, t.case_barcode
  FROM target_patients t
  FULL JOIN excluded_patients e ON t.case_gdc_id = e.case_gdc_id
  WHERE e.case_gdc_id IS NULL
)

-- Step 4: Get GDC file URLs from rel14 metadata
SELECT DISTINCT
  vp.case_barcode,
  -- Construct GDC file URL using file_gdc_id from the GCS URL mapping table
  CONCAT('https://api.gdc.cancer.gov/data/', g.file_gdc_id) AS gdc_file_url
FROM valid_patients vp
JOIN `isb-cgc.GDC_metadata.rel14_caseData` cd 
  ON vp.case_gdc_id = cd.case_gdc_id
JOIN `isb-cgc.GDC_metadata.rel14_fileData_current` fdc 
  ON cd.case_gdc_id = fdc.case_gdc_id
JOIN `isb-cgc.GDC_metadata.rel14_GDCfileID_to_GCSurl_NEW` g 
  ON fdc.file_gdc_id = g.file_gdc_id
ORDER BY vp.case_barcode;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH annotations_set AS (

    WHERE entity_type = 'Patient'
      AND (category = 'History of unacceptable prior treatment related to a prior/other malignancy' 
           OR classification = 'Redaction')
),

clinical_set AS (

    ON f.file_gdc_id = u.file_gdc_id;
```

### 13. bq161 (DB: `pancancer_atlas_2`)
**Question**: Calculate the net difference between the number of pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PAAD) patients in TCGA's dataset who are confirmed to have mutations in both KRAS and TP53 genes, and those without mutations in either gene. Utilize patient clinical and follow-up data alongside genomic mutation details from TCGA’s cancer genomics database, focusing specifically on PAAD studies where the mutations have passed quality filters.

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

|               39 |

|-----------------:|
|               40 |

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Get all PAAD patient barcodes from the filtered clinical table
WITH paad_patients AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    bcr_patient_barcode AS patient_barcode
  FROM `isb-cgc-bq.pancancer_atlas.Filtered_clinical_PANCAN_patient_with_followup`
  WHERE acronym = 'PAAD'
),

-- Step 2: For each patient, determine if they have a PASS mutation in KRAS and/or TP53 from MAF
patient_mutations AS (
  SELECT
    p.patient_barcode,
    MAX(CASE WHEN m.Hugo_Symbol = 'KRAS' AND m.FILTER = 'PASS' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS kras_mut,
    MAX(CASE WHEN m.Hugo_Symbol = 'TP53' AND m.FILTER = 'PASS' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS tp53_mut
  FROM paad_patients p
  INNER JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.pancancer_atlas.Filtered_MC3_MAF_V5_one_per_tumor_sample` m
    ON p.patient_barcode = m.ParticipantBarcode
   AND m.Study = 'PAAD'
  GROUP BY p.patient_barcode
),

-- Step 3: Classify patients into categories
classified AS (
  SELECT
    patient_barcode,
    CASE 
      WHEN kras_mut = 1 AND tp53_mut = 1 THEN 'both'
      WHEN kras_mut = 0 AND tp53_mut = 0 THEN 'none'
      ELSE 'other'
    END AS mutation_category
  FROM patient_mutations
)

-- Step 4: Compute net difference: count(both) - count(none)
SELECT
  COUNTIF(mutation_category = 'both') - COUNTIF(mutation_category = 'none') AS net_difference
FROM classified;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Get all PAAD patients from the clinical data
WITH paad_patients AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT bcr_patient_barcode AS patient_barcode
  FROM `isb-cgc-bq.pancancer_atlas.Filtered_clinical_PANCAN_patient_with_followup`
  WHERE acronym = 'PAAD'
),

-- Note: The required mutation data tables (Filtered_MC3_MAF_V5_one_per_tumor_sample) 
-- are not available in the provided schema.
-- Please ensure the mutation data table exists and is accessible.

-- For demonstration, assuming the mutation table exists:
kras_mut AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ParticipantBarcode AS patient_barcode
  FROM `isb-cgc-bq.pancancer_atlas.Filtered_MC3_MAF_V5_one_per_tumor_sample`
  WHERE Study = 'PAAD'
    AND Hugo_Symbol = 'KRAS'
    AND FILTER = 'PASS'
),

tp53_mut AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ParticipantBarcode AS patient_barcode
  FROM `isb-cgc-bq.pancancer_atlas.Filtered_MC3_MAF_V5_one_per_tumor_sample`
  WHERE Study = 'PAAD'
    AND Hugo_Symbol = 'TP53'
    AND FILTER = 'PASS'
),

both_mut AS (
  SELECT patient_barcode FROM kras_mut
  INTERSECT DISTINCT
  SELECT patient_barcode FROM tp53_mut
),

any_mut AS (
  SELECT patient_barcode FROM kras_mut
  UNION DISTINCT
  SELECT patient_barcode FROM tp53_mut
),

neither_mut AS (
  SELECT patient_barcode FROM paad_patients
  EXCEPT DISTINCT
  SELECT patient_barcode FROM any_mut
)

SELECT
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM both_mut) - (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM neither_mut) AS net_difference;
```

### 14. local018 (DB: `California_Traffic_Collision`)
**Question**: For the primary collision factor violation category that was the most common cause of traffic accidents in 2021, how many percentage points did its share of annual road incidents in 2021 decrease compared to its share in 2011?

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

|   MAX(CASE WHEN COLLISION_YEAR = 2011 THEN PERCENTAGE_SHARE END) - MAX(CASE WHEN COLLISION_YEAR = 2021 THEN PERCENTAGE_SHARE END) |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------:|
|                                                                                                                         -0.553654 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

|   percentage_point_decrease |
|----------------------------:|
|                     -0.5537 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

|   decrease_percentage_points |
|-----------------------------:|
|                          nan |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
"yearly_total" AS (
    SELECT 
        c2."db_year",
        COUNT(*) AS "total_accidents"
    FROM "collisions" c
    JOIN "case_ids" c2 ON c."case_id" = c2."case_id"
    WHERE c2."db_year" IN (2011, 2021)
    GROUP BY c2."db_year"
),
"category_counts_2021" AS (
    SELECT 
        c."pcf_violation_category",
        COUNT(*) AS "cnt"
    FROM "collisions" c
    JOIN "case_ids" c2 ON c."case_id" = c2."case_id"
    WHERE c2."db_year" = 2021
      AND c."pcf_violation_category" IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY c."pcf_violation_category"
),
"top_category" AS (
    SELECT 
        "pcf_violation_category"
    FROM "category_counts_2021"
    ORDER BY "cnt" DESC
    LIMIT 1
),
"category_counts" AS (
    SELECT 
        c2."db_year",
        COUNT(*) AS "category_count"
    FROM "collisions" c
    JOIN "case_ids" c2 ON c."case_id" = c2."case_id"
    WHERE c2."db_year" IN (2011, 2021)
      AND c."pcf_violation_category" = (SELECT "pcf_violation_category" FROM "top_category")
    GROUP BY c2."db_year"
)
SELECT 
    ROUND(
        (SELECT "category_count" FROM "category_counts" WHERE "db_year" = 2011) * 100.0 / 
        (SELECT "total_accidents" FROM "yearly_total" WHERE "db_year" = 2011)
        -
        (SELECT "category_count" FROM "category_counts" WHERE "db_year" = 2021) * 100.0 / 
        (SELECT "total_accidents" FROM "yearly_total" WHERE "db_year" = 2021)
        , 4
    ) AS "decrease_percentage_points"
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Total accidents in each year
total_by_year AS (
    SELECT 
        strftime('%Y', "collision_date") AS "year",
        COUNT(*) AS "total_count"
    FROM collisions
    WHERE strftime('%Y', "collision_date") IN ('2011', '2021')
    GROUP BY strftime('%Y', "collision_date")
),
-- Accidents per PCF violation category per year
category_by_year AS (
    SELECT 
        strftime('%Y', "collision_date") AS "year",
        "pcf_violation_category",
        COUNT(*) AS "category_count"
    FROM collisions
    WHERE strftime('%Y', "collision_date") IN ('2011', '2021')
    GROUP BY strftime('%Y', "collision_date"), "pcf_violation_category"
),
-- The most common violation category in 2021
top_category_2021 AS (
    SELECT "pcf_violation_category"
    FROM category_by_year
    WHERE "year" = '2021'
    ORDER BY "category_count" DESC
    LIMIT 1
),
-- Share percentages for that category in both years
shares AS (
    SELECT 
        c."year",
        c."category_count" * 100.0 / t."total_count" AS "share"
    FROM category_by_year c
    JOIN total_by_year t ON c."year" = t."year"
    WHERE c."pcf_violation_category" = (SELECT "pcf_violation_category" FROM top_category_2021)
)
-- Calculate percentage point decrease: share_2011 - share_2021
SELECT 
    ROUND(
        MAX(CASE WHEN "year" = '2011' THEN "share" ELSE 0 END) - 
        MAX(CASE WHEN "year" = '2021' THEN "share" ELSE 0 END),
        4
    ) AS "percentage_point_decrease"
FROM shares;
```
</details>

```sql
-- Compute boundary timestamps in microseconds (UTC)
WITH
  boundaries AS (
    SELECT
      UNIX_MICROS(TIMESTAMP "2021-01-01 00:00:00+00") AS start_7,
      UNIX_MICROS(TIMESTAMP "2021-01-07 23:59:59+00") AS end_7,
      UNIX_MICROS(TIMESTAMP "2021-01-06 00:00:00+00") AS start_2
  ),
  -- Users with positive engagement time in the 7-day window (Jan 1 - Jan 7)
  users_7 AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT user_pseudo_id
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*`, boundaries
    WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20210101' AND '20210110'  -- cover late arrivals up to 3 days
      AND event_timestamp BETWEEN start_7 AND end_7
      AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM UNNEST(event_params) AS p
        WHERE p.key = 'engagement_time_msec'
          AND p.value.int_value > 0
      )
  ),
  -- Users with positive engagement time in the 2-day window (Jan 6 - Jan 7)
  users_2 AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT user_pseudo_id
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*`, boundaries
    WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20210106' AND '20210110'
      AND event_timestamp BETWEEN start_2 AND end_7
      AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM UNNEST(event_params) AS p
        WHERE p.key = 'engagement_time_msec'
          AND p.value.int_value > 0
      )
  )
-- Count users in 7-day window but not in 2-day window
SELECT COUNT(*) AS distinct_users_positive_engagement_7d_not_2d
FROM (
  SELECT user_pseudo_id FROM users_7
  EXCEPT DISTINCT
  SELECT user_pseudo_id FROM users_2
);
```

```sql
  UNNEST(event_params) AS ep

    AND ep.key = 'engagement_time_msec'

SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT user_pseudo_id) AS distinct_users
```

```sql
WITH claims_stats AS (
    -- Combine all claims stats tables
    SELECT * FROM PATENTS_USPTO.USPTO_OCE_CLAIMS.PATENT_CLAIMS_STATS
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM PATENTS_USPTO.USPTO_OCE_CLAIMS.PATENT_CLAIMS_STATS_2014
),
match_tables AS (
    -- Combine all match tables
    SELECT * FROM PATENTS_USPTO.USPTO_OCE_CLAIMS.MATCH
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM PATENTS_USPTO.USPTO_OCE_CLAIMS.MATCH_2014
),
-- Filter independent claims (ind_flg = '1')
independent_claims AS (
    SELECT 
        cs."appl_id",
        cs."claim_no",
        cs."word_ct",
        cs."pat_no"
    FROM claims_stats cs
    WHERE cs."ind_flg" = '1'
),
-- Join with match tables to get publication numbers
claims_with_publications AS (
    SELECT 
        ic."appl_id",
        ic."claim_no",
        ic."word_ct",
        ic."pat_no",
        m."publication_number",
        m."pub_no"
    FROM independent_claims ic
    INNER JOIN match_tables m 
        ON ic."pat_no" = m."pat_no"
),
-- Join with PATENTS.PUBLICATIONS and get earliest publication per claim
ranked_publications AS (
    SELECT 
        cp."appl_id",
        cp."claim_no",
        cp."word_ct",
        cp."pat_no",
        cp."publication_number",
        cp."pub_no",
        p."publication_date",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY cp."pat_no", cp."claim_no"  -- Each claim gets its own earliest publication
            ORDER BY p."publication_date" ASC
        ) AS rn
    FROM claims_with_publications cp
    INNER JOIN PATENTS_USPTO.PATENTS.PUBLICATIONS p 
        ON cp."publication_number" = p."publication_number"
)
-- Final selection: earliest publication per claim, ordered by word count descending, top 100
SELECT 
    "publication_number",
    "appl_id" AS "application_number",
    "claim_no",
    "word_ct"
FROM ranked_publications
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY CAST("word_ct" AS INTEGER) DESC
LIMIT 100;
```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Union all independent claims from claims stats tables
"claims_stats" AS (
    SELECT
        "CS"."pat_no",
        "CS"."appl_id",
        "CS"."claim_no",
        "CS"."word_ct"
    FROM "PATENTS_USPTO"."USPTO_OCE_CLAIMS"."PATENT_CLAIMS_STATS" "CS"
    WHERE "CS"."ind_flg" = '1'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT
        "CS"."pat_no",
        "CS"."appl_id",
        "CS"."claim_no",
        "CS"."word_ct"
    FROM "PATENTS_USPTO"."USPTO_OCE_CLAIMS"."PATENT_CLAIMS_STATS_2014" "CS"
    WHERE "CS"."ind_flg" = '1'
),

-- Step 2: Union all match tables to get publication_number for each patent number
"match_tables" AS (
    SELECT
        "M"."publication_number",
        "M"."pat_no"
    FROM "PATENTS_USPTO"."USPTO_OCE_CLAIMS"."MATCH" "M"
    UNION ALL
    SELECT
        "M"."publication_number",
        "M"."pat_no"
    FROM "PATENTS_USPTO"."USPTO_OCE_CLAIMS"."MATCH_2014" "M"
),

-- Step 3: Join claims stats with match tables on pat_no to get publication numbers
"claims_with_pub" AS (
    SELECT
        "CS"."appl_id",
        "CS"."claim_no",
        "CS"."word_ct",
        "M"."publication_number"
    FROM "claims_stats" "CS"
    INNER JOIN "match_tables" "M"
        ON "CS"."pat_no" = "M"."pat_no"
),

-- Step 4: From PATENTS.PUBLICATIONS, for each application_number,
--         find the earliest publication (smallest publication_date)
"ranked_publications" AS (
    SELECT
        "P"."publication_number",
        "P"."application_number",
        "P"."publication_date",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY "P"."application_number"
            ORDER BY "P"."publication_date" ASC
        ) AS "rn"
    FROM "PATENTS_USPTO"."PATENTS"."PUBLICATIONS" "P"
),

-- Step 5: Keep only the earliest publication per application
"earliest_pubs" AS (
    SELECT
        "publication_number",
        "application_number"
    FROM "ranked_publications"
    WHERE "rn" = 1
)

-- Step 6: Final select - earliest publications with claim details,
--         ordered by highest word count, limited to top 100
SELECT
    "EP"."publication_number",
    "EP"."application_number",
    "CP"."claim_no",
    "CP"."word_ct"
FROM "claims_with_pub" "CP"
INNER JOIN "earliest_pubs" "EP"
    ON "CP"."publication_number" = "EP"."publication_number"
ORDER BY CAST("CP"."word_ct" AS INTEGER) DESC
LIMIT 100;
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Filter users who signed up between Jan 1, 2019 and Apr 30, 2022
filtered_users AS (
    SELECT
        "age",
        "gender",
        "id"
    FROM "THELOOK_ECOMMERCE"."THELOOK_ECOMMERCE"."USERS"
    WHERE
        "gender" IN ('M', 'F')
        AND "created_at" >= 1546300800000000  -- 2019-01-01 00:00:00 UTC in microseconds
        AND "created_at" < 1651363200000000   -- 2022-05-01 00:00:00 UTC in microseconds (exclusive of May 1)
),
-- Step 2: For each gender, get min and max age
gender_age_extremes AS (
    SELECT
        "gender",
        MIN("age") AS "min_age",
        MAX("age") AS "max_age"
    FROM filtered_users
    GROUP BY "gender"
)
-- Step 3: Count users at min age and max age per gender
SELECT
    e."gender",
    e."min_age",
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN f."age" = e."min_age" THEN f."id" END) AS "min_age_count",
    e."max_age",
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN f."age" = e."max_age" THEN f."id" END) AS "max_age_count"
FROM gender_age_extremes e
JOIN filtered_users f
    ON e."gender" = f."gender"
GROUP BY e."gender", e."min_age", e."max_age"
ORDER BY e."gender";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH filtered_users AS (
    SELECT 
        "id",
        "gender",
        "age"
    FROM "THELOOK_ECOMMERCE"."THELOOK_ECOMMERCE"."USERS"
    WHERE "gender" IN ('M', 'F')
      AND TO_TIMESTAMP("created_at" / 1000000) >= '2019-01-01'
      AND TO_TIMESTAMP("created_at" / 1000000) <= '2022-04-30'
),
age_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        "gender",
        MIN("age") AS min_age,
        MAX("age") AS max_age
    FROM filtered_users
    GROUP BY "gender"
),
youngest AS (
    SELECT 
        f."gender",
        'youngest' AS age_group,
        a.min_age AS age,
        COUNT(DISTINCT f."id") AS user_count
    FROM filtered_users f
    JOIN age_stats a 
        ON f."gender" = a."gender" AND f."age" = a.min_age
    GROUP BY f."gender", a.min_age
),
oldest AS (
    SELECT 
        f."gender",
        'oldest' AS age_group,
        a.max_age AS age,
        COUNT(DISTINCT f."id") AS user_count
    FROM filtered_users f
    JOIN age_stats a 
        ON f."gender" = a."gender" AND f."age" = a.max_age
    GROUP BY f."gender", a.max_age
)
SELECT * FROM youngest
UNION ALL
SELECT * FROM oldest
ORDER BY "gender", age_group;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH country_aggregates AS (
```

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
SELECT
    "collection_id",
    "StudyInstanceUID" AS "study_instance_uid",
    "SeriesInstanceUID" AS "series_instance_uid",
    ROUND(SUM("instance_size") / 1024, 2) AS "total_size_kb",
    'https://viewer.imaging.datacommons.cancer.gov/viewer/' || "StudyInstanceUID" AS "viewer_url"
FROM
    "IDC"."IDC_V17"."DICOM_ALL"
WHERE
    "Modality" IN ('SEG', 'RTSTRUCT')
    AND "SOPClassUID" = '1.2.840.10008.5.1.4.1.1.66.4'
    AND (
        "ReferencedSeriesSequence" IS NULL
        OR ARRAY_SIZE("ReferencedSeriesSequence") = 0
    )
    AND (
        "ReferencedImageSequence" IS NULL
        OR ARRAY_SIZE("ReferencedImageSequence") = 0
    )
    AND (
        "SourceImageSequence" IS NULL
        OR ARRAY_SIZE("SourceImageSequence") = 0
    )
GROUP BY
    "collection_id",
    "StudyInstanceUID",
    "SeriesInstanceUID"
ORDER BY
    "total_size_kb" DESC;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH filtered_images AS (
    SELECT
        d."SOPInstanceUID",
        d."StudyInstanceUID",
        d."SeriesInstanceUID",
        d."Modality",
        d."BlobStorageSize",
        d."ReferencedSeriesSequence",
        d."ReferencedStudySequence",
        d."ReferencedImageRealWorldValueMappingSequence",
        d."ReferencedRawDataSequence",
        d."ReferencedPatientSequence",
        d."ReferencedFrameOfReferenceSequence"
    FROM "IDC"."IDC_V17"."DICOM_ALL" d
    WHERE
        d."Modality" IN ('SEG', 'RTSTRUCT')
        -- No references to any other series, study, image, raw data, patient, or frame of reference
        AND (
            d."ReferencedSeriesSequence" IS NULL OR ARRAY_SIZE(d."ReferencedSeriesSequence") = 0
        )
        AND (
            d."ReferencedStudySequence" IS NULL OR ARRAY_SIZE(d."ReferencedStudySequence") = 0
        )
        AND (
            d."ReferencedImageRealWorldValueMappingSequence" IS NULL OR ARRAY_SIZE(d."ReferencedImageRealWorldValueMappingSequence") = 0
        )
        AND (
            d."ReferencedRawDataSequence" IS NULL OR ARRAY_SIZE(d."ReferencedRawDataSequence") = 0
        )
        AND (
            d."ReferencedPatientSequence" IS NULL OR ARRAY_SIZE(d."ReferencedPatientSequence") = 0
        )
        AND (
            d."ReferencedFrameOfReferenceSequence" IS NULL OR ARRAY_SIZE(d."ReferencedFrameOfReferenceSequence") = 0
        )
),
joined_data AS (
    SELECT
        f."StudyInstanceUID",
        f."SeriesInstanceUID",
        f."BlobStorageSize",
        p."source_DOI" AS "Collection",
        p."SOPClassUID"
    FROM filtered_images f
    INNER JOIN "IDC"."IDC_V17"."DICOM_PIVOT" p
        ON f."SOPInstanceUID" = p."SOPInstanceUID"
    WHERE
        p."SOPClassUID" = '1.2.840.10008.5.1.4.1.1.66.4'
)
SELECT
    j."Collection",
    j."StudyInstanceUID",
    j."SeriesInstanceUID",
    ROUND(SUM(j."BlobStorageSize") / 1024.0, 2) AS "TotalSizeKB",
    CONCAT('https://viewer.imaging.datacommons.cancer.gov/viewer/', j."StudyInstanceUID") AS "ViewerURL"
FROM joined_data j
GROUP BY
    j."Collection",
    j."StudyInstanceUID",
    j."SeriesInstanceUID"
ORDER BY
    "TotalSizeKB" DESC;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Calculate per-liter price per transaction, extract year, filter valid records.
price_per_liter AS (
  SELECT
    category_name,
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) AS year,
    state_bottle_retail * 1000.0 / bottle_volume_ml AS calc_price_per_liter
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.iowa_liquor_sales.sales`
  WHERE
    bottle_volume_ml > 0
    AND state_bottle_retail IS NOT NULL
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) IN (2019, 2020, 2021)
),

-- Step 2: Aggregate per category and year.
yearly_avg AS (
  SELECT
    category_name,
    year,
    AVG(calc_price_per_liter) AS avg_price
  FROM price_per_liter
  GROUP BY category_name, year
),

-- Step 3: Identify top 10 categories in 2021 based on their average per-liter price.
top_cats_2021 AS (
  SELECT category_name
  FROM yearly_avg
  WHERE year = 2021
  ORDER BY avg_price DESC
  LIMIT 10
)

-- Step 4: Pivot the yearly averages for the selected categories.
SELECT
  y.category_name,
  ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN y.year = 2019 THEN y.avg_price END), 4) AS avg_price_2019,
  ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN y.year = 2020 THEN y.avg_price END), 4) AS avg_price_2020,
  ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN y.year = 2021 THEN y.avg_price END), 4) AS avg_price_2021
FROM yearly_avg y
INNER JOIN top_cats_2021 t ON y.category_name = t.category_name
GROUP BY y.category_name
ORDER BY avg_price_2021 DESC;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH
  -- Step 1: Compute 2021 average per-liter price for all categories in one scan
  yearly_avg_2021 AS (
    SELECT
      category_name,
      AVG(sale_dollars / volume_sold_liters) AS avg_price_2021
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.iowa_liquor_sales.sales`
    WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) = 2021
      AND volume_sold_liters > 0
      AND sale_dollars > 0
    GROUP BY category_name
  ),

  -- Step 2: Pick top 10 categories by 2021 average price
  top_categories AS (
    SELECT
      category_name,
      avg_price_2021
    FROM yearly_avg_2021
    ORDER BY avg_price_2021 DESC
    LIMIT 10
  ),

  -- Step 3: For those top 10, get averages for 2019, 2020, 2021
  yearly_averages AS (
    SELECT
      s.category_name,
      EXTRACT(YEAR FROM s.date) AS year,
      AVG(s.sale_dollars / s.volume_sold_liters) AS avg_price
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.iowa_liquor_sales.sales` s
    INNER JOIN top_categories tc
      ON s.category_name = tc.category_name
    WHERE s.date BETWEEN '2019-01-01' AND '2021-12-31'
      AND s.volume_sold_liters > 0
      AND s.sale_dollars > 0
    GROUP BY s.category_name, year
  )

-- Step 4: Pivot years into columns
SELECT
  category_name,
  ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN year = 2019 THEN avg_price END), 4) AS avg_price_2019,
  ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN year = 2020 THEN avg_price END), 4) AS avg_price_2020,
  ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN year = 2021 THEN avg_price END), 4) AS avg_price_2021
FROM yearly_averages
GROUP BY category_name
ORDER BY avg_price_2021 DESC;
```

### 7. local007 (DB: `Baseball`)
**Question**: Could you help me calculate the average single career span value in years for all baseball players? Please precise the result as a float number. First, calculate the difference in years, months, and days between the debut and final game dates. For each player, the career span is computed as the sum of the absolute number of years, plus the absolute number of months divided by 12, plus the absolute number of days divided by 365. Round each part to two decimal places before summing. Finally, average the career spans and round the result to a float number.

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Compute absolute day difference for each player (debut to final_game)
WITH player_days AS (
    SELECT 
        "player_id",
        ABS(julianday("final_game") - julianday("debut")) AS total_days
    FROM "player"
    WHERE "debut" IS NOT NULL 
      AND "final_game" IS NOT NULL
),
-- Step 2: Approximate years, months, days using 365-day year and 30-day month
player_parts AS (
    SELECT 
        "player_id",
        CAST("total_days" AS INTEGER) / 365   AS years,
        (CAST("total_days" AS INTEGER) % 365) / 30 AS months,
        (CAST("total_days" AS INTEGER) % 365) % 30 AS days
    FROM player_days
),
-- Step 3: Compute career span per player: years + months/12 + days/365, each rounded to 2 decimals
player_span AS (
    SELECT 
        "player_id",
        ROUND(CAST("years" AS REAL), 2) 
        + ROUND(CAST("months" AS REAL) / 12.0, 2) 
        + ROUND(CAST("days" AS REAL) / 365.0, 2) AS career_span
    FROM player_parts
)
-- Step 4: Average all career spans and round final result to 4 decimal places (float)
SELECT ROUND(AVG("career_span"), 4) AS average_career_span
FROM player_span;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH player_date_diff AS (
    SELECT 
        "player_id",
        ABS(CAST(strftime('%Y', "final_game") AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%Y', "debut") AS INTEGER)) AS year_diff,
        ABS(CAST(strftime('%m', "final_game") AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%m', "debut") AS INTEGER)) AS month_diff,
        ABS(CAST(strftime('%d', "final_game") AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%d', "debut") AS INTEGER)) AS day_diff
    FROM "player"
    WHERE "debut" IS NOT NULL AND "final_game" IS NOT NULL 
      AND "debut" != '' AND "final_game" != ''
),
player_career_span AS (
    SELECT 
        "player_id",
        ROUND(CAST(year_diff AS REAL), 2) + 
        ROUND(CAST(month_diff AS REAL) / 12.0, 2) + 
        ROUND(CAST(day_diff AS REAL) / 365.0, 2) AS career_span
    FROM player_date_diff
)
SELECT ROUND(AVG(career_span), 4) AS avg_career_span_years
FROM player_career_span;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Count home wins for each team
WITH home_wins AS (
    SELECT
        "home_team_api_id" AS team_id,
        COUNT(*) AS wins
    FROM "Match"
    WHERE "home_team_goal" > "away_team_goal"
    GROUP BY "home_team_api_id"
),
-- Step 2: Count away wins for each team
away_wins AS (
    SELECT
        "away_team_api_id" AS team_id,
        COUNT(*) AS wins
    FROM "Match"
    WHERE "away_team_goal" > "home_team_goal"
    GROUP BY "away_team_api_id"
),
-- Step 3: Combine home and away wins per team
total_wins AS (
    SELECT
        team_id,
        SUM(wins) AS total_wins
    FROM (
        SELECT team_id, wins FROM home_wins
        UNION ALL
        SELECT team_id, wins FROM away_wins
    ) AS combined
    GROUP BY team_id
)
-- Step 4: Join with Team table to get the team name and output top 10
SELECT
    t."team_long_name" AS team,
    tw.total_wins AS wins
FROM total_wins tw
JOIN "Team" t ON tw.team_id = t."team_api_id"
ORDER BY tw.total_wins DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- CTE: Count all home wins and away wins separately
WITH team_wins AS (
    -- Home team wins
    SELECT 
        "home_team_api_id" AS team_api_id,
        COUNT(*) AS wins
    FROM "Match"
    WHERE "home_team_goal" > "away_team_goal"
    GROUP BY "home_team_api_id"
    
    UNION ALL
    
    -- Away team wins
    SELECT 
        "away_team_api_id" AS team_api_id,
        COUNT(*) AS wins
    FROM "Match"
    WHERE "away_team_goal" > "home_team_goal"
    GROUP BY "away_team_api_id"
),
-- Aggregate total wins per team
total_wins AS (
    SELECT 
        team_api_id,
        SUM(wins) AS total_wins
    FROM team_wins
    GROUP BY team_api_id
)
-- Final output: top 10 teams with team names
SELECT 
    t."team_long_name" AS team_name
FROM total_wins tw
JOIN "Team" t ON tw.team_api_id = t."team_api_id"
ORDER BY tw.total_wins DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;
```
</details>

```sql
),

-- Actual wind generation (datatypeid 16)
wind_actual_data AS (
    SELECT 
        "DATETIME" AS "datetime",
        "TIMEZONE" AS "timezone",
        "VALUE" AS "wind_gen"
    FROM "YES_ENERGY__SAMPLE_DATA"."YES_ENERGY_SAMPLE"."TS_GEN_SAMPLE"
    WHERE "OBJECTID" = 10000712973
        AND "DATATYPEID" = 16
        AND "DATETIME" >= '2022-10-01 00:00:00'
        AND "DATETIME" < '2022-10-02 00:00:00'
),

-- Actual solar generation (datatypeid 650)
solar_actual_data AS (
    SELECT 
        "DATETIME" AS "datetime",
        "TIMEZONE" AS "timezone",
        "VALUE" AS "solar_gen"
    FROM "YES_ENERGY__SAMPLE_DATA"."YES_ENERGY_SAMPLE"."TS_GEN_SAMPLE"
    WHERE "OBJECTID" = 10000712973
        AND "DATATYPEID" = 650
        AND "DATETIME" >= '2022-10-01 00:00:00'
        AND "DATETIME" < '2022-10-02 00:00:00'
),

-- Actual load (final settlement)
load_actual_data AS (
    SELECT 
        "DATETIME" AS "datetime",
        "TIMEZONE" AS "timezone",
        "RTLOAD" AS "rtload"
    FROM "YES_ENERGY__SAMPLE_DATA"."YES_ENERGY_SAMPLE"."DART_LOADS_SAMPLE"
    WHERE "OBJECTID" = 10000712973
        AND "DATETIME" >= '2022-10-01 00:00:00'
        AND "DATETIME" < '2022-10-02 00:00:00'
        AND "RTFINAL" = 'Y'
),

-- Peak classifications from market times
peak_classification AS (
    SELECT 
        "DATETIME" AS "datetime",
        "TIMEZONE" AS "timezone",
        "ONPEAK" AS "onpeak",
        "OFFPEAK" AS "offpeak",
        "WEPEAK" AS "wepeak",
        "WDPEAK" AS "wdpeak",
        "MARKETDAY" AS "marketday",
        "DATETIME_UTC" AS "datetime_utc"
    FROM "YES_ENERGY__SAMPLE_DATA"."YES_ENERGY_SAMPLE"."ISO_MARKET_TIMES_SAMPLE"
    WHERE "ISO" = 'ERCOT'
        AND "DATETIME" >= '2022-10-01 00:00:00'
        AND "DATETIME" < '2022-10-02 00:00:00'
),

-- Combine all data with the hourly calendar
combined_data AS (
    SELECT
        'ERCOT' AS "iso",
        h."datetime",
        COALESCE(p."timezone", lf."timezone", wf."timezone", sf."timezone",
                 wa."timezone", sa."timezone", la."timezone", pc."timezone", 'CDT') AS "timezone",
        pc."datetime_utc",
        COALESCE(pc."onpeak", 0) AS "onpeak",
        COALESCE(pc."offpeak", 0) AS "offpeak",
        COALESCE(pc."wepeak", 0) AS "wepeak",
        COALESCE(pc."wdpeak", 0) AS "wdpeak",
        pc."marketday",
        pni."price_node_name",
        pni."price_node_id",
        p."dalmp",
        p."rtlmp",
        lzi."load_zone_name",
        lzi."load_zone_id",
        lf."load_forecast",
        lf."load_forecast_publish_date",
        la."rtload",
        wf."wind_gen_forecast",
        wf."wind_gen_forecast_publish_date",
        wa."wind_gen",
        sf."solar_gen_forecast",
        sf."solar_gen_forecast_publish_date",
        sa."solar_gen"
    FROM hourly_slots h
    LEFT JOIN price_data p ON h."datetime" = p."datetime"
    LEFT JOIN load_forecast_data lf ON h."datetime" = lf."datetime"
    LEFT JOIN wind_forecast_data wf ON h."datetime" = wf."datetime"
    LEFT JOIN solar_forecast_data sf ON h."datetime" = sf."datetime"
    LEFT JOIN wind_actual_data wa ON h."datetime" = wa."datetime"
    LEFT JOIN solar_actual_data sa ON h."datetime" = sa."datetime"
    LEFT JOIN load_actual_data la ON h."datetime" = la."datetime"
    LEFT JOIN peak_classification pc ON h."datetime" = pc."datetime"
    CROSS JOIN price_node_info pni
    CROSS JOIN load_zone_info lzi
)

-- Final report with net load calculations
SELECT 
    "iso",
    "datetime",
    "timezone",
    "datetime_utc",
    "onpeak",
    "offpeak",
    "wepeak",
    "wdpeak",
    "marketday",
    "price_node_name",
    "price_node_id",
    ROUND("dalmp", 4) AS "dalmp",
    ROUND("rtlmp", 4) AS "rtlmp",
    "load_zone_name",
    "load_zone_id",
    ROUND("load_forecast", 4) AS "load_forecast",
    "load_forecast_publish_date",
    ROUND("rtload", 4) AS "rtload",
    ROUND("wind_gen_forecast", 4) AS "wind_gen_forecast",
    "wind_gen_forecast_publish_date",
    ROUND("wind_gen", 4) AS "wind_gen",
    ROUND("solar_gen_forecast", 4) AS "solar_gen_forecast",
    "solar_gen_forecast_publish_date",
    ROUND("solar_gen", 4) AS "solar_gen",
    -- Net load forecasts and real-time
    ROUND(COALESCE("load_forecast", 0) - COALESCE("wind_gen_forecast", 0) - COALESCE("solar_gen_forecast", 0), 4) AS "net_load_forecast",
    ROUND(COALESCE("rtload", 0) - COALESCE("wind_gen", 0) - COALESCE("solar_gen", 0), 4) AS "net_load_real_time"
FROM combined_data
ORDER BY "datetime" ASC;
```

```sql
-- Report for ERCOT on October 1, 2022 combining hourly price, load, wind, solar data
-- with time zone alignments, peak classifications, and net load calculations

WITH 
-- Generate all 24 hours for Oct 1, 2022 in America/Chicago (Central Daylight Time)
hours AS (
    SELECT 
        DATEADD('hour', seq, '2022-10-01 00:00:00'::TIMESTAMP_NTZ) AS "datetime",
        'America/Chicago' AS "timezone"
    FROM (
        SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY 1) - 1 AS seq 
        FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 24))
    ) AS seqs
),

-- Price data from DART_PRICES for node 10000697078
prices AS (
    SELECT 
        dp."DATETIME" AS "datetime",
        dp."TIMEZONE" AS "timezone",
        dp."DALMP" AS "dalmp",
        dp."RTLMP" AS "rtlmp",
        pn."PNODENAME" AS "price_node_name",
        dp."OBJECTID" AS "price_node_id"
    FROM YES_ENERGY__SAMPLE_DATA.YES_ENERGY_SAMPLE.DART_PRICES_SAMPLE dp
    JOIN YES_ENERGY__SAMPLE_DATA.YES_ENERGY_SAMPLE.PRICE_NODES_SAMPLE pn
        ON dp."OBJECTID" = pn."OBJECTID"
    WHERE dp."OBJECTID" = 10000697078
        AND dp."DATETIME" BETWEEN '2022-10-01 00:00:00' AND '2022-10-01 23:59:59'
),

-- Load forecast from TS_FORECAST (datatypeid=19060)
load_forecast AS (
    SELECT 
        "DATETIME" AS "datetime",
        "TIMEZONE" AS "timezone",
        "VALUE" AS "load_forecast",
        "PUBLISHDATE" AS "load_forecast_publish_date"
    FROM YES_ENERGY__SAMPLE_DATA.YES_ENERGY_SAMPLE.TS_FORECAST_SAMPLE
    WHERE "OBJECTID" = 10000712973
        AND "DATATYPEID" = 19060
        AND "DATETIME" BETWEEN '2022-10-01 00:00:00' AND '2022-10-01 23:59:59'
),

-- Actual load from DART_LOADS (RTLOAD)
actual_load AS (
    SELECT 
        "DATETIME" AS "datetime",
        "TIMEZONE" AS "timezone",
        "RTLOAD" AS "rtload"
    FROM YES_ENERGY__SAMPLE_DATA.YES_ENERGY_SAMPLE.DART_LOADS_SAMPLE
    WHERE "OBJECTID" = 10000712973
        AND "DATETIME" BETWEEN '2022-10-01 00:00:00' AND '2022-10-01 23:59:59'
),

-- Wind forecast from TS_FORECAST (datatypeid=9285)
wind_forecast AS (
    SELECT 
        "DATETIME" AS "datetime",
        "TIMEZONE" AS "timezone",
        "VALUE" AS "wind_gen_forecast",
        "PUBLISHDATE" AS "wind_gen_forecast_publish_date"
    FROM YES_ENERGY__SAMPLE_DATA.YES_ENERGY_SAMPLE.TS_FORECAST_SAMPLE
    WHERE "OBJECTID" = 10000712973
        AND "DATATYPEID" = 9285
        AND "DATETIME" BETWEEN '2022-10-01 00:00:00' AND '2022-10-01 23:59:59'
),

-- Solar forecast from TS_FORECAST (datatypeid=662)
solar_forecast AS (
    SELECT 
        "DATETIME" AS "datetime",
        "TIMEZONE" AS "timezone",
        "VALUE" AS "solar_gen_forecast",
        "PUBLISHDATE" AS "solar_gen_forecast_publish_date"
    FROM YES_ENERGY__SAMPLE_DATA.YES_ENERGY_SAMPLE.TS_FORECAST_SAMPLE
    WHERE "OBJECTID" = 10000712973
        AND "DATATYPEID" = 662
        AND "DATETIME" BETWEEN '2022-10-01 00:00:00' AND '2022-10-01 23:59:59'
),

-- Actual wind generation from TS_GEN (datatypeid=16), aggregated to hourly
wind_actual AS (
    SELECT 
        DATE_TRUNC('hour', "DATETIME") AS "datetime",
        MODE("TIMEZONE") AS "timezone",
        AVG("VALUE") AS "wind_gen"
    FROM YES_ENERGY__SAMPLE_DATA.YES_ENERGY_SAMPLE.TS_GEN_SAMPLE
    WHERE "OBJECTID" = 10000712973
        AND "DATATYPEID" = 16
        AND "DATETIME" BETWEEN '2022-10-01 00:00:00' AND '2022-10-01 23:59:59'
    GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('hour', "DATETIME")
),

-- Actual solar generation from TS_GEN (datatypeid=650), aggregated to hourly
solar_actual AS (
    SELECT 
        DATE_TRUNC('hour', "DATETIME") AS "datetime",
        MODE("TIMEZONE") AS "timezone",
        AVG("VALUE") AS "solar_gen"
    FROM YES_ENERGY__SAMPLE_DATA.YES_ENERGY_SAMPLE.TS_GEN_SAMPLE
    WHERE "OBJECTID" = 10000712973
        AND "DATATYPEID" = 650
        AND "DATETIME" BETWEEN '2022-10-01 00:00:00' AND '2022-10-01 23:59:59'
    GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('hour', "DATETIME")
),

-- Market times for peak classification
market_times AS (
    SELECT 
        "DATETIME" AS "datetime",
        "TIMEZONE" AS "timezone",
        "ONPEAK",
        "OFFPEAK",
        "WEPEAK",
        "WDPEAK",
        "MARKETDAY"
    FROM YES_ENERGY__SAMPLE_DATA.YES_ENERGY_SAMPLE.ISO_MARKET_TIMES_SAMPLE
    WHERE "ISO" = 'ERCOT'
        AND "MARKETDAY" = '2022-10-01'
),

-- Load zone info from DS_OBJECT_LIST
load_zone_info AS (
    SELECT 
        "OBJECTID" AS "load_zone_id",
        "OBJECTNAME" AS "load_zone_name"
    FROM YES_ENERGY__SAMPLE_DATA.YES_ENERGY_SAMPLE.DS_OBJECT_LIST_SAMPLE
    WHERE "OBJECTID" = 10000712973
)

-- Main report combining all data
SELECT 
    'ERCOT' AS "iso",
    h."datetime",
    h."timezone",
    CONVERT_TIMEZONE(h."timezone", 'UTC', h."datetime"::TIMESTAMP_NTZ) AS "datetime_utc",
    COALESCE(mt."ONPEAK", 0) AS "onpeak",
    COALESCE(mt."OFFPEAK", 0) AS "offpeak",
    COALESCE(mt."WEPEAK", 0) AS "wepeak",
    COALESCE(mt."WDPEAK", 0) AS "wdpeak",
    mt."MARKETDAY",
    p."price_node_name",
    p."price_node_id",
    p."dalmp",
    p."rtlmp",
    lz."load_zone_name",
    lz."load_zone_id",
    lf."load_forecast",
    lf."load_forecast_publish_date",
    al."rtload",
    wf."wind_gen_forecast",
    wf."wind_gen_forecast_publish_date",
    wa."wind_gen",
    sf."solar_gen_forecast",
    sf."solar_gen_forecast_publish_date",
    sa."solar_gen",
    ROUND(lf."load_forecast" - COALESCE(wf."wind_gen_forecast", 0) - COALESCE(sf."solar_gen_forecast", 0), 4) AS "net_load_forecast",
    ROUND(al."rtload" - COALESCE(wa."wind_gen", 0) - COALESCE(sa."solar_gen", 0), 4) AS "net_load_real_time"
FROM hours h
LEFT JOIN prices p ON h."datetime" = p."datetime" AND h."timezone" = p."timezone"
LEFT JOIN load_forecast lf ON h."datetime" = lf."datetime" AND h."timezone" = lf."timezone"
LEFT JOIN actual_load al ON h."datetime" = al."datetime" AND h."timezone" = al."timezone"
LEFT JOIN wind_forecast wf ON h."datetime" = wf."datetime" AND h."timezone" = wf."timezone"
LEFT JOIN solar_forecast sf ON h."datetime" = sf."datetime" AND h."timezone" = sf."timezone"
LEFT JOIN wind_actual wa ON h."datetime" = wa."datetime" AND h."timezone" = wa."timezone"
LEFT JOIN solar_actual sa ON h."datetime" = sa."datetime" AND h."timezone" = sa."timezone"
LEFT JOIN market_times mt ON h."datetime" = mt."datetime" AND h."timezone" = mt."timezone"
CROSS JOIN load_zone_info lz
ORDER BY h."datetime";
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Generate all months from 2008-01 to 2022-12
month_series AS (
    SELECT 
        DATE_TRUNC('month', DATEADD('month', seq, '2008-01-01'::DATE)) AS month_start
    FROM (
        SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY 1) - 1 AS seq
        FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 180))
    )
),

-- Filter US publications with IoT in abstract
iot_publications AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        p."publication_number",
        DATE_TRUNC('month', TO_DATE(p."filing_date"::VARCHAR, 'YYYYMMDD')) AS filing_month
    FROM "PATENTS"."PATENTS"."PUBLICATIONS" p,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => p."abstract_localized") f
    WHERE p."country_code" = 'US'
      AND f.value:"language"::STRING = 'en'
      AND LOWER(f.value:"text"::STRING) LIKE '%internet of things%'
      AND p."filing_date" BETWEEN 20080101 AND 20221231
),

-- Count per month
monthly_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        filing_month,
        COUNT(DISTINCT "publication_number") AS num_publications
    FROM iot_publications
    GROUP BY filing_month
)

-- Final result with zero-fill
SELECT 
    m.month_start AS month,
    COALESCE(mc.num_publications, 0) AS num_publications
FROM month_series m
LEFT JOIN monthly_counts mc
    ON m.month_start = mc.filing_month
ORDER BY m.month_start;
```

```sql
),
"filtered_patents" AS (
    SELECT 
        p."publication_number",
        p."filing_date"
    FROM "PATENTS"."PATENTS"."PUBLICATIONS" p
    WHERE p."country_code" = 'US'
      AND p."filing_date" IS NOT NULL
      AND p."filing_date" >= 20080101
      AND p."filing_date" <= 20221231
),
"iot_patents" AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT p."publication_number"
    FROM "PATENTS"."PATENTS"."PUBLICATIONS" p,
         LATERAL FLATTEN(input => p."abstract_localized") f
    WHERE p."country_code" = 'US'
      AND f.value:"language"::TEXT = 'en'
      AND LOWER(f.value:"text"::TEXT) LIKE '%internet of things%'
),
"monthly_counts" AS (
    SELECT 
        DATE_TRUNC('month', 
            DATE_FROM_PARTS(
                FLOOR(fp."filing_date" / 10000),
                FLOOR(MOD(fp."filing_date", 10000) / 100),
                MOD(fp."filing_date", 100)
            )
        ) AS "month",
        COUNT(DISTINCT fp."publication_number") AS "cnt"
    FROM "filtered_patents" fp
    INNER JOIN "iot_patents" iot ON fp."publication_number" = iot."publication_number"
    GROUP BY "month"
)
SELECT 
    YEAR(m."month_start") AS "year",
    MONTH(m."month_start") AS "month",
    COALESCE(mc."cnt", 0) AS "num_publications"
FROM "month_series" m
LEFT JOIN "monthly_counts" mc ON m."month_start" = mc."month"
ORDER BY m."month_start";
```
</details>

### 2. sf_bq029 (DB: `PATENTS`)
**Question**: Get the average number of inventors per patent and the total count of patent publications in Canada (CA) for each 5-year period from 1960 to 2020, based on publication dates. Only include patents that have at least one inventor listed, and group results by 5-year intervals (1960-1964, 1965-1969, etc.).

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH patent_data AS (
    SELECT 
        p."publication_number",
        ARRAY_SIZE(p."inventor_harmonized") AS inventor_count,
        FLOOR((p."publication_date" / 10000 - 1960) / 5) * 5 + 1960 AS period_start
    FROM PATENTS.PATENTS.PUBLICATIONS p
    WHERE p."country_code" = 'CA'
        AND p."publication_date" >= 19600101
        AND p."publication_date" <= 20201231
        AND p."inventor_harmonized" IS NOT NULL
        AND ARRAY_SIZE(p."inventor_harmonized") > 0
)
SELECT 
    CONCAT(period_start, '-', period_start + 4) AS period,
    COUNT("publication_number") AS total_patents,
    ROUND(AVG(inventor_count), 4) AS avg_inventors_per_patent
FROM patent_data
GROUP BY period_start
ORDER BY period_start;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH patent_data AS (
    -- Filter Canadian patents with at least one inventor and within year range
    SELECT 
        "publication_date",
        ARRAY_SIZE("inventor_harmonized") AS inventor_count
    FROM "PATENTS"."PATENTS"."PUBLICATIONS"
    WHERE 
        "country_code" = 'CA'
        AND "inventor_harmonized" IS NOT NULL
        AND ARRAY_SIZE("inventor_harmonized") > 0
        AND FLOOR("publication_date" / 10000) BETWEEN 1960 AND 2020
),
periods AS (
    -- Assign each patent to a 5-year period based on publication year
    SELECT 
        inventor_count,
        FLOOR(FLOOR("publication_date" / 10000) / 5) * 5 AS period_start,
        FLOOR(FLOOR("publication_date" / 10000) / 5) * 5 + 4 AS period_end
    FROM patent_data
)
SELECT 
    CONCAT(period_start::VARCHAR, '-', period_end::VARCHAR) AS period_label,
    ROUND(AVG(inventor_count), 4) AS avg_inventors_per_patent,
    COUNT(*) AS total_patent_count
FROM periods
GROUP BY period_start, period_end
ORDER BY period_start;
```
</details>
