#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Identify families whose earliest publication is in January 2015
family_earliest AS (
    SELECT 
        "family_id",
        MIN("publication_date") AS "earliest_date"
    FROM PATENTS_GOOGLE.PATENTS_GOOGLE.PUBLICATIONS
    GROUP BY "family_id"
    HAVING MIN("publication_date") BETWEEN 20150101 AND 20150131
),

-- All publications belonging to those target families
target_family_pubs AS (
    SELECT p.*
    FROM PATENTS_GOOGLE.PATENTS_GOOGLE.PUBLICATIONS p
    INNER JOIN family_earliest fe ON p."family_id" = fe."family_id"
),

-- Extract distinct CPC codes from the VARIANT column
cpc_codes AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        tfp."family_id",
        f.value:"code"::VARCHAR AS "cpc_code"
    FROM target_family_pubs tfp,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => tfp."cpc") f
    WHERE f.value:"code" IS NOT NULL
),

-- Extract distinct IPC codes from the VARIANT column
ipc_codes AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        tfp."family_id",
        f.value:"code"::VARCHAR AS "ipc_code"
    FROM target_family_pubs tfp,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => tfp."ipc") f
    WHERE f.value:"code" IS NOT NULL
),

-- Flatten all citations from all publications for finding citing families
all_citations_flattened AS (
    SELECT 
        p."family_id" AS "citing_family_id",
        p."publication_number" AS "citing_publication",
        f.value:"publication_number"::VARCHAR AS "cited_publication_number"
    FROM PATENTS_GOOGLE.PATENTS_GOOGLE.PUBLICATIONS p,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => p."citation") f
    WHERE f.value:"publication_number" IS NOT NULL 
      AND f.value:"publication_number"::VARCHAR <> ''
),

-- Publications cited by the target family (to find families that are cited)
families_cited AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        acf."citing_family_id",
        p2."family_id" AS "cited_family_id"
    FROM all_citations_flattened acf
    INNER JOIN target_family_pubs tfp
        ON acf."citing_family_id" = tfp."family_id"
    INNER JOIN PATENTS_GOOGLE.PATENTS_GOOGLE.PUBLICATIONS p2
        ON acf."cited_publication_number" = p2."publication_number"
    WHERE p2."family_id" != acf."citing_family_id"
),

-- Publications that cite the target family (cited-by)
families_citing AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        tfp."family_id" AS "target_family_id",
        acf."citing_family_id"
    FROM target_family_pubs tfp
    INNER JOIN all_citations_flattened acf
        ON acf."cited_publication_number" = tfp."publication_number"
    WHERE acf."citing_family_id" != tfp."family_id"
),

-- Aggregate publication numbers per family
agg_publications AS (
    SELECT 
        "family_id",
        LISTAGG(DISTINCT "publication_number", ', ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY "publication_number") AS "publication_numbers"
    FROM target_family_pubs
    GROUP BY "family_id"
),

-- Aggregate country codes per family
agg_countries AS (
    SELECT 
        "family_id",
        LISTAGG(DISTINCT "country_code", ', ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY "country_code") AS "country_codes"
    FROM target_family_pubs
    GROUP BY "family_id"
),

-- Aggregate CPC codes per family
agg_cpc AS (
    SELECT 
        "family_id",
        LISTAGG("cpc_code", ', ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY "cpc_code") AS "cpc_codes"
    FROM cpc_codes
    GROUP BY "family_id"
),

-- Aggregate IPC codes per family
agg_ipc AS (
    SELECT 
        "family_id",
        LISTAGG("ipc_code", ', ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY "ipc_code") AS "ipc_codes"
    FROM ipc_codes
    GROUP BY "family_id"
),

-- Aggregate cited family ids per family
agg_cited AS (
    SELECT 
        "citing_family_id" AS "family_id",
        LISTAGG("cited_family_id", ', ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY "cited_family_id") AS "cited_family_ids"
    FROM families_cited
    GROUP BY "citing_family_id"
),

-- Aggregate citing family ids per family
agg_citing AS (
    SELECT 
        "target_family_id" AS "family_id",
        LISTAGG("citing_family_id", ', ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY "citing_family_id") AS "citing_family_ids"
    FROM families_citing
    GROUP BY "target_family_id"
)

-- Final output: one row per family with all aggregated data
SELECT
    fe."family_id",
    fe."earliest_date" AS "earliest_publication_date",
    COALESCE(ap."publication_numbers", '') AS "publication_numbers",
    COALESCE(ac."country_codes", '') AS "country_codes",
    COALESCE(acpc."cpc_codes", '') AS "cpc_codes",
    COALESCE(aipc."ipc_codes", '') AS "ipc_codes",
    COALESCE(acited."cited_family_ids", '') AS "cited_family_ids",
    COALESCE(aciting."citing_family_ids", '') AS "citing_family_ids"
FROM family_earliest fe
LEFT JOIN agg_publications ap ON fe."family_id" = ap."family_id"
LEFT JOIN agg_countries ac ON fe."family_id" = ac."family_id"
LEFT JOIN agg_cpc acpc ON fe."family_id" = acpc."family_id"
LEFT JOIN agg_ipc aipc ON fe."family_id" = aipc."family_id"
LEFT JOIN agg_cited acited ON fe."family_id" = acited."family_id"
LEFT JOIN agg_citing aciting ON fe."family_id" = aciting."family_id"
ORDER BY fe."family_id";
```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
    -- Step 1: Find families whose earliest publication date is in January 2015
    families_of_interest AS (
        SELECT
            "family_id",
            MIN("publication_date") AS "earliest_date"
        FROM PATENTS_GOOGLE.PATENTS_GOOGLE.PUBLICATIONS
        GROUP BY "family_id"
        HAVING MIN("publication_date") >= 20150101
           AND MIN("publication_date") <= 20150131
    ),

    -- Step 2: All publications belonging to those families
    family_pubs AS (
        SELECT
            p."family_id",
            p."publication_date",
            p."publication_number",
            p."country_code",
            p."cpc",
            p."ipc",
            p."citation"
        FROM PATENTS_GOOGLE.PATENTS_GOOGLE.PUBLICATIONS p
        INNER JOIN families_of_interest f
            ON p."family_id" = f."family_id"
    ),

    -- Step 3: Earliest publication date per family
    earliest_dates AS (
        SELECT
            "family_id",
            MIN("publication_date") AS "earliest_date"
        FROM family_pubs
        GROUP BY "family_id"
    ),

    -- Step 4: Distinct publication numbers, comma-separated, sorted alphabetically
    pub_numbers AS (
        SELECT
            "family_id",
            LISTAGG(DISTINCT "publication_number", ', ')
                WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY "publication_number") AS "publication_numbers"
        FROM family_pubs
        GROUP BY "family_id"
    ),

    -- Step 5: Distinct country codes, comma-separated, sorted alphabetically
    country_codes AS (
        SELECT
            "family_id",
            LISTAGG(DISTINCT "country_code", ', ')
                WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY "country_code") AS "country_codes"
        FROM family_pubs
        GROUP BY "family_id"
    ),

    -- Step 6: Distinct CPC codes extracted from the VARIANT array
    cpc_codes AS (
        SELECT
            fp."family_id",
            LISTAGG(DISTINCT c.value:"code"::VARCHAR, ', ')
                WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY c.value:"code"::VARCHAR) AS "cpc_codes"
        FROM family_pubs fp
        CROSS JOIN LATERAL FLATTEN(input => fp."cpc") c
        WHERE c.value:"code" IS NOT NULL
          AND c.value:"code"::VARCHAR != ''
        GROUP BY fp."family_id"
    ),

    -- Step 7: Distinct IPC codes extracted from the VARIANT array
    ipc_codes AS (
        SELECT
            fp."family_id",
            LISTAGG(DISTINCT i.value:"code"::VARCHAR, ', ')
                WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY i.value:"code"::VARCHAR) AS "ipc_codes"
        FROM family_pubs fp
        CROSS JOIN LATERAL FLATTEN(input => fp."ipc") i
        WHERE i.value:"code" IS NOT NULL
          AND i.value:"code"::VARCHAR != ''
        GROUP BY fp."family_id"
    ),

    -- Step 8: Families CITED BY this publication family
    cited_family_ids AS (
        SELECT
            fp."family_id" AS "citing_family_id",
            LISTAGG(DISTINCT cited_p."family_id", ', ')
                WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY cited_p."family_id") AS "cited_family_ids"
        FROM family_pubs fp
        CROSS JOIN LATERAL FLATTEN(input => fp."citation") cit
        LEFT JOIN PATENTS_GOOGLE.PATENTS_GOOGLE.PUBLICATIONS cited_p
            ON cit.value:"publication_number"::VARCHAR = cited_p."publication_number"
        WHERE cit.value:"publication_number" IS NOT NULL
          AND cit.value:"publication_number"::VARCHAR != ''
          AND cited_p."family_id" IS NOT NULL
        GROUP BY fp."family_id"
    ),

    -- Step 9: Families that CITE this publication family
    citing_family_ids AS (
        SELECT
            fpn."family_id" AS "cited_family_id",
            LISTAGG(DISTINCT flat_cit."citing_family_id", ', ')
                WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY flat_cit."citing_family_id") AS "citing_family_ids"
        FROM (
            SELECT DISTINCT "family_id", "publication_number"
            FROM family_pubs
        ) fpn
        INNER JOIN (
            SELECT
                other."family_id" AS "citing_family_id",
                cit.value:"publication_number"::VARCHAR AS "cited_pub_number"
            FROM PATENTS_GOOGLE.PATENTS_GOOGLE.PUBLICATIONS other
            CROSS JOIN LATERAL FLATTEN(input => other."citation") cit
            WHERE cit.value:"publication_number" IS NOT NULL
              AND cit.value:"publication_number"::VARCHAR != ''
        ) flat_cit
            ON flat_cit."cited_pub_number" = fpn."publication_number"
        GROUP BY fpn."family_id"
    )

-- Final SELECT: Combine all pieces per family
SELECT
    ed."family_id",
    ed."earliest_date",
    pn."publication_numbers",
    cc."country_codes",
    COALESCE(cpc."cpc_codes", '') AS "cpc_codes",
    COALESCE(ipc."ipc_codes", '') AS "ipc_codes",
    COALESCE(citing."citing_family_ids", '') AS "citing_family_ids",
    COALESCE(cited."cited_family_ids", '') AS "cited_family_ids"
FROM earliest_dates ed
INNER JOIN families_of_interest foi
    ON ed."family_id" = foi."family_id"
LEFT JOIN pub_numbers pn
    ON ed."family_id" = pn."family_id"
LEFT JOIN country_codes cc
    ON ed."family_id" = cc."family_id"
LEFT JOIN cpc_codes cpc
    ON ed."family_id" = cpc."family_id"
LEFT JOIN ipc_codes ipc
    ON ed."family_id" = ipc."family_id"
LEFT JOIN citing_family_ids citing
    ON ed."family_id" = citing."cited_family_id"
LEFT JOIN cited_family_ids cited
    ON ed."family_id" = cited."citing_family_id"
ORDER BY ed."family_id";
```
</details>

```sql
WITH file_depth AS (
    SELECT 
        "path",
        CASE 
            WHEN LOWER("path") LIKE '%.py' THEN '.py'
            WHEN LOWER("path") LIKE '%.c' THEN '.c'
            WHEN LOWER("path") LIKE '%.ipynb' THEN '.ipynb'
            WHEN LOWER("path") LIKE '%.java' THEN '.java'
            WHEN LOWER("path") LIKE '%.js' THEN '.js'
        END AS "file_type",
        LENGTH("path") - LENGTH(REPLACE("path", '/', '')) AS "depth"
    FROM GITHUB_REPOS.GITHUB_REPOS.SAMPLE_FILES
    WHERE LOWER("path") LIKE '%.py'
       OR LOWER("path") LIKE '%.c'
       OR LOWER("path") LIKE '%.ipynb'
       OR LOWER("path") LIKE '%.java'
       OR LOWER("path") LIKE '%.js'
)
SELECT 
    "file_type",
    COUNT(*) AS "file_count"
FROM file_depth
WHERE "depth" > 10
  AND "file_type" IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY "file_type"
ORDER BY "file_count" DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH file_depth AS (
    SELECT 
        "path",
        LOWER(SPLIT_PART("path", '.', -1)) AS "extension",
        LENGTH("path") - LENGTH(REPLACE("path", '/', '')) AS "directory_depth"
    FROM "GITHUB_REPOS"."GITHUB_REPOS"."SAMPLE_FILES"
    WHERE "path" LIKE '%.%'
      AND LOWER(SPLIT_PART("path", '.', -1)) IN ('py', 'c', 'ipynb', 'java', 'js')
)
SELECT 
    "extension",
    COUNT(*) AS "file_count"
FROM file_depth
WHERE "directory_depth" > 10
GROUP BY "extension"
ORDER BY "file_count" DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Calculate total claim counts per drug in New York State (2014)
WITH ny_drug_totals AS (
  SELECT
    drug_name,
    SUM(total_claim_count) AS total_claims_ny
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.part_d_prescriber_2014`
  WHERE nppes_provider_state = 'NY'
  GROUP BY drug_name
),

-- Step 2: Identify the drug with the highest total claims in NY
top_drug_ny AS (
  SELECT drug_name
  FROM ny_drug_totals
  ORDER BY total_claims_ny DESC
  LIMIT 1
),

-- Step 3: For that drug, aggregate claim counts and drug costs by state nationwide
state_totals AS (
  SELECT
    nppes_provider_state AS state,
    SUM(total_claim_count) AS total_claim_count,
    SUM(total_drug_cost) AS total_drug_cost
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.part_d_prescriber_2014`
  WHERE drug_name IN (SELECT drug_name FROM top_drug_ny)
  GROUP BY nppes_provider_state
)

-- Step 4: Retrieve top 5 states by total claim count
SELECT
  state,
  total_claim_count,
  total_drug_cost
FROM state_totals
ORDER BY total_claim_count DESC
LIMIT 5;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Find the drug with the highest total claim count in NY state (2014)
WITH ny_drug_totals AS (
  SELECT 
    drug_name,
    SUM(total_claim_count) AS total_ny_claims
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.part_d_prescriber_2014`
  WHERE nppes_provider_state = 'NY'
  GROUP BY drug_name
  ORDER BY total_ny_claims DESC
  LIMIT 1
),
-- Step 2: For that drug, aggregate total claims and costs by state
state_aggregates AS (
  SELECT 
    p.nppes_provider_state AS state,
    SUM(p.total_claim_count) AS total_claim_count,
    SUM(p.total_drug_cost) AS total_drug_cost
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.part_d_prescriber_2014` p
  INNER JOIN ny_drug_totals t
    ON p.drug_name = t.drug_name
  GROUP BY p.nppes_provider_state
)
-- Step 3: Get the top 5 states with highest total claim counts
SELECT 
  state,
  total_claim_count,
  ROUND(total_drug_cost, 4) AS total_drug_cost
FROM state_aggregates
ORDER BY total_claim_count DESC
LIMIT 5;
```
</details>

```sql
  SELECT latitude, longitude, year, month, day, wind_speed / 10
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_2015`
  WHERE wind_speed IS NOT NULL
),
daily_averages AS (
  SELECT
    latitude,
    longitude,
    DATE(year, month, day) AS observation_date,
    AVG(wind_speed_ms) AS daily_avg_wind_speed
  FROM all_records
  GROUP BY latitude, longitude, observation_date
)
SELECT
  latitude,
  longitude,
  observation_date
FROM daily_averages
ORDER BY daily_avg_wind_speed DESC
LIMIT 5;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Combine ICOADS core data from 2010 to 2014, filtering out NULL/NaN values
WITH combined AS (
  SELECT
    year,
    month,
    air_temperature,
    wetbulb_temperature,
    dewpoint_temperature,
    sea_surface_temp
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_*`
  WHERE
    _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2010' AND '2014'
    -- Exclude nulls and NaN (NaN is not equal to itself)
    AND air_temperature IS NOT NULL AND air_temperature = air_temperature
    AND wetbulb_temperature IS NOT NULL AND wetbulb_temperature = wetbulb_temperature
    AND dewpoint_temperature IS NOT NULL AND dewpoint_temperature = dewpoint_temperature
    AND sea_surface_temp IS NOT NULL AND sea_surface_temp = sea_surface_temp
),
-- Compute monthly averages for each temperature variable
monthly_avg AS (
  SELECT
    year,
    month,
    AVG(air_temperature) AS avg_air,
    AVG(wetbulb_temperature) AS avg_wet,
    AVG(dewpoint_temperature) AS avg_dew,
    AVG(sea_surface_temp) AS avg_sst
  FROM combined
  GROUP BY year, month
),
-- Calculate sum of absolute differences among the four averages
diff AS (
  SELECT
    year,
    month,
    ABS(avg_air - avg_wet) + ABS(avg_air - avg_dew) + ABS(avg_air - avg_sst) +
    ABS(avg_wet - avg_dew) + ABS(avg_wet - avg_sst) + ABS(avg_dew - avg_sst) AS sum_abs_diff
  FROM monthly_avg
)
-- Select the top 3 months with smallest sum
SELECT
  year,
  month,
  ROUND(sum_abs_diff, 4) AS sum_abs_diff
FROM diff
ORDER BY sum_abs_diff ASC
LIMIT 3;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH monthly_aggregates AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM timestamp) AS year,
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM timestamp) AS month,
    AVG(air_temperature) AS avg_air_temp,
    AVG(wetbulb_temperature) AS avg_wetbulb_temp,
    AVG(dewpoint_temperature) AS avg_dewpoint_temp,
    AVG(sea_surface_temp) AS avg_sst
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_*`
  WHERE
    _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2010' AND '2014'
    AND air_temperature IS NOT NULL
    AND wetbulb_temperature IS NOT NULL
    AND dewpoint_temperature IS NOT NULL
    AND sea_surface_temp IS NOT NULL
    AND NOT IS_NAN(air_temperature)
    AND NOT IS_NAN(wetbulb_temperature)
    AND NOT IS_NAN(dewpoint_temperature)
    AND NOT IS_NAN(sea_surface_temp)
    AND timestamp >= '2010-01-01'
    AND timestamp < '2015-01-01'
  GROUP BY year, month
)
SELECT
  year,
  month,
  ROUND(
    ABS(avg_air_temp - avg_wetbulb_temp) +
    ABS(avg_air_temp - avg_dewpoint_temp) +
    ABS(avg_air_temp - avg_sst) +
    ABS(avg_wetbulb_temp - avg_dewpoint_temp) +
    ABS(avg_wetbulb_temp - avg_sst) +
    ABS(avg_dewpoint_temp - avg_sst),
    4
  ) AS sum_abs_diff
FROM monthly_aggregates
ORDER BY sum_abs_diff ASC
LIMIT 3
```
</details>

```sql
)
```

**Question**: Based on the most recent 1km population grid data in Singapore before January 2023, using ST_CONVEXHULL to aggregate all population grid centroids into a bounding region and ST_INTERSECTS to identify hospitals from OpenStreetMap’s planet layer (layer_code in (2110, 2120)) that fall within this region, then calculating the distance from each grid cell to its nearest hospital, what is the total population of the grid cell that is farthest from any hospital?

**Status**: Baseline ✅ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

|   population |
|-------------:|
|      12723.2 |

**OR**

|            0 |

|   population |
|-------------:|

<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

|----------------------:|

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH recent_date AS (
    SELECT MAX("last_updated") AS "max_date"
    FROM "GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_WORLDPOP"."WORLDPOP"."POPULATION_GRID_1KM"
    WHERE "alpha_3_code" = 'SGP'
      AND "last_updated" < '2023-01-01'
),
sg_grid AS (
    SELECT "population", "longitude_centroid", "latitude_centroid", "geo_id"
    FROM "GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_WORLDPOP"."WORLDPOP"."POPULATION_GRID_1KM"
    WHERE "alpha_3_code" = 'SGP'
      AND "last_updated" = (SELECT "max_date" FROM recent_date)
),
bounding_region AS (
    SELECT 
        ST_GEOGRAPHYFROMWKT(
            'POLYGON((' ||
            MIN("longitude_centroid") || ' ' || MIN("latitude_centroid") || ', ' ||
            MAX("longitude_centroid") || ' ' || MIN("latitude_centroid") || ', ' ||
            MAX("longitude_centroid") || ' ' || MAX("latitude_centroid") || ', ' ||
            MIN("longitude_centroid") || ' ' || MAX("latitude_centroid") || ', ' ||
            MIN("longitude_centroid") || ' ' || MIN("latitude_centroid") || '))'
        ) AS "bbox_region"
    FROM sg_grid
),
hospitals AS (
    SELECT pl."geometry" AS "hospital_geom_wkb"
    FROM "GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_WORLDPOP"."GEO_OPENSTREETMAP"."PLANET_LAYERS" pl
    CROSS JOIN bounding_region br
    WHERE pl."layer_code" IN (2110, 2120)
      AND ST_INTERSECTS(br."bbox_region", ST_GEOGFROMWKB(pl."geometry"))
)
SELECT "population" AS "population_farthest"
FROM (
    SELECT 
        sg."geo_id",
        sg."population",
        MIN(ST_DISTANCE(
            ST_POINT(sg."longitude_centroid", sg."latitude_centroid"), 
            ST_GEOGFROMWKB(h."hospital_geom_wkb")
        )) AS "min_dist_to_hospital"
    FROM sg_grid sg
    CROSS JOIN hospitals h
    GROUP BY sg."geo_id", sg."population"
)
ORDER BY "min_dist_to_hospital" DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Get all Singapore population grid records before Jan 2023
sg_population AS (
    SELECT
        p."population",
        p."longitude_centroid",
        p."latitude_centroid",
        p."last_updated",
        ST_MAKEPOINT(p."longitude_centroid", p."latitude_centroid") AS "centroid_geom"
    FROM "GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_WORLDPOP"."WORLDPOP"."POPULATION_GRID_1KM" p
    WHERE p."alpha_3_code" = 'SGP'
      AND p."last_updated" < '2023-01-01'
),

-- Step 2: Find the single most recent update date
most_recent_date AS (
    SELECT MAX("last_updated") AS "max_date"
    FROM sg_population
),

-- Step 3: Keep only the most recent snapshot of population data
latest_sg_population AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM sg_population
    WHERE "last_updated" = (SELECT "max_date" FROM most_recent_date)
),

-- Step 4: Build the bounding box (envelope) encompassing all grid centroids
bounding_region AS (
    SELECT ST_ENVELOPE(ST_COLLECT("centroid_geom")) AS "bounding_box"
    FROM latest_sg_population
),

-- Step 5: Identify hospitals (layer_code 2110) and doctors (layer_code 2120)
-- that intersect the bounding box
hospitals AS (
    SELECT
        l."geometry",
        l."layer_code"
    FROM "GEO_OPENSTREETMAP_WORLDPOP"."GEO_OPENSTREETMAP"."PLANET_LAYERS" l,
         bounding_region b
    WHERE l."layer_code" IN (2110, 2120)
      AND ST_INTERSECTS(ST_GEOGFROMWKB(l."geometry"), b."bounding_box")
),

-- Step 6: For each grid cell, compute the minimum distance to any hospital
grid_hospital_distances AS (
    SELECT
        p."population",
        p."longitude_centroid",
        p."latitude_centroid",
        MIN(ST_DISTANCE(p."centroid_geom", ST_GEOGFROMWKB(h."geometry"))) AS "min_distance_to_hospital"
    FROM latest_sg_population p
    CROSS JOIN hospitals h
    GROUP BY p."population", p."longitude_centroid", p."latitude_centroid"
)

-- Step 7: Return the population of the grid cell farthest from any hospital
SELECT "population"
FROM grid_hospital_distances
ORDER BY "min_distance_to_hospital" DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH "dates" AS (
    SELECT DATEADD('day', seq, '2018-08-30'::DATE) AS "dt"
    FROM (
        SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY (SELECT NULL)) - 1 AS seq
        FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 32))
    )
),
"daily_counts" AS (
    SELECT
        TO_DATE(TO_TIMESTAMP(t."block_timestamp" / 1000000)) AS "day",
        COUNT_IF(t."trace_address" IS NULL) AS "external_created",
        COUNT_IF(t."trace_address" IS NOT NULL) AS "internal_created"
    FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TRACES t
    WHERE t."trace_type" = 'create'
      AND t."status" = 1
      AND t."block_timestamp" >= 1535587200000000
      AND t."block_timestamp" < 1538352000000000
    GROUP BY "day"
),
"cumulative" AS (
    SELECT
        d."dt",
        COALESCE(dc."external_created", 0) AS "external_created",
        COALESCE(dc."internal_created", 0) AS "internal_created",
        SUM(COALESCE(dc."external_created", 0)) OVER (ORDER BY d."dt" ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS "cum_external",
        SUM(COALESCE(dc."internal_created", 0)) OVER (ORDER BY d."dt" ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS "cum_internal"
    FROM "dates" d
    LEFT JOIN "daily_counts" dc ON d."dt" = dc."day"
)
SELECT
    "dt" AS "date",
    "cum_external" AS "cumulative_external_created",
    "cum_internal" AS "cumulative_internal_created"
FROM "cumulative"
ORDER BY "dt";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH date_spine AS (
    SELECT
        DATEADD('day', seq.seq, '2018-08-30'::DATE) AS "date"
    FROM (
        SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY 0) - 1 AS seq
        FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 32))
    ) AS seq
),

contract_creations AS (
    SELECT
        TO_DATE(TO_TIMESTAMP("block_timestamp" / 1000000)) AS "date",
        CASE
            WHEN "trace_address" IS NULL THEN 'external_user'
            ELSE 'contract'
        END AS "creator_type",
        1 AS "cnt"
    FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TRACES
    WHERE "trace_type" = 'create'
      AND "status" = 1
      AND "block_timestamp" >= 1535587200000000   -- Aug 30, 2018 00:00:00 UTC in microseconds
      AND "block_timestamp" < 1538352000000000    -- Oct 1, 2018 00:00:00 UTC in microseconds (exclusive)
),

daily_counts AS (
    SELECT
        ds."date",
        COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN cc."creator_type" = 'external_user' THEN cc."cnt" ELSE 0 END), 0) AS "ext_user_created",
        COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN cc."creator_type" = 'contract' THEN cc."cnt" ELSE 0 END), 0) AS "contract_created"
    FROM date_spine ds
    LEFT JOIN contract_creations cc
        ON ds."date" = cc."date"
    GROUP BY ds."date"
)

SELECT
    "date",
    SUM("ext_user_created") OVER (ORDER BY "date" ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS "cumulative_ext_user_created",
    SUM("contract_created") OVER (ORDER BY "date" ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS "cumulative_contract_created"
FROM daily_counts
ORDER BY "date";
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH RECURSIVE date_series AS (
    SELECT '2017-01-01'::DATE AS dt
    UNION ALL
    SELECT DATEADD(DAY, 1, dt)
    FROM date_series
    WHERE dt < '2021-12-31'
),
daily_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        TO_DATE(TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(CAST("block_timestamp" AS BIGINT) / 1000000)) AS creation_date,
        CASE 
            WHEN "trace_address" IS NULL THEN 'external'
            ELSE 'internal'
        END AS creator_type,
        COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM "CRYPTO"."CRYPTO_ETHEREUM"."TRACES"
    WHERE "trace_type" = 'create'
      AND "status" = 1
      AND "block_timestamp" >= 1483228800000000  -- 2017-01-01 in microseconds
      AND "block_timestamp" <  1640995200000000  -- 2022-01-01 in microseconds
    GROUP BY creation_date, creator_type
),
pivoted AS (
    SELECT 
        ds.dt,
        COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN dc.creator_type = 'external' THEN dc.cnt END), 0) AS external_created,
        COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN dc.creator_type = 'internal' THEN dc.cnt END), 0) AS internal_created
    FROM date_series ds
    LEFT JOIN daily_counts dc ON ds.dt = dc.creation_date
    GROUP BY ds.dt
)
SELECT 
    dt AS date,
    SUM(external_created) OVER (ORDER BY dt ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS cumulative_external,
    SUM(internal_created) OVER (ORDER BY dt ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS cumulative_internal
FROM pivoted
ORDER BY dt;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH "date_series" AS (
    -- Generate all dates from 2017-01-01 to 2021-12-31 using a cross join method
    SELECT DATEADD(DAY, "seq"."index", DATE('2017-01-01')) AS "date"
    FROM (
        SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY 1) - 1 AS "index"
        FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 1826))  -- 5 years * 365 days + 1 leap day
    ) "seq"
    WHERE DATEADD(DAY, "seq"."index", DATE('2017-01-01')) <= DATE('2021-12-31')
),
"creations" AS (
    SELECT 
        DATE(TO_TIMESTAMP(t."block_timestamp" / 1000000)) AS "creation_date",
        CASE 
            WHEN t."trace_address" IS NULL THEN 'external'
            ELSE 'contract'
        END AS "creator_type"
    FROM "CRYPTO"."CRYPTO_ETHEREUM"."TRACES" t
    WHERE t."trace_type" = 'create'
      AND t."status" = 1
      AND t."block_timestamp" >= 1483228800000000      -- 2017-01-01 00:00:00 UTC
      AND t."block_timestamp" < 1640995200000000       -- 2022-01-01 00:00:00 UTC
),
"daily_counts" AS (
    SELECT 
        "creation_date",
        COUNT(CASE WHEN "creator_type" = 'external' THEN 1 END) AS "external_created",
        COUNT(CASE WHEN "creator_type" = 'contract' THEN 1 END) AS "contract_created"
    FROM "creations"
    GROUP BY "creation_date"
)
SELECT 
    d."date",
    SUM(COALESCE(dc."external_created", 0)) OVER (ORDER BY d."date") AS "external_created_cumulative",
    SUM(COALESCE(dc."contract_created", 0)) OVER (ORDER BY d."date") AS "contract_created_cumulative"
FROM "date_series" d
LEFT JOIN "daily_counts" dc 
    ON d."date" = dc."creation_date"
ORDER BY d."date";
```

### 14. sf_bq187 (DB: `ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN`)
**Question**: Calculate the total circulating supply of 'BNB' tokens (in units divided by 10^18) by summing balances of all non-zero addresses, where each address’s balance equals its total received BNB minus sent BNB. Exclude transactions involving the zero address (0x000...) for both senders and receivers.

**Status**: Baseline ✅ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
    -- Step 1: Get the BNB token contract address and decimals (handle NULL decimals)
    bnb_token_info AS (
        SELECT 
            t."address" AS token_address,
            COALESCE(TRY_CAST(t."decimals" AS NUMBER), 18) AS decimals
        FROM ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.TOKENS t
        WHERE UPPER(t."symbol") = 'BNB'
        LIMIT 1
    ),

    -- Step 2: Calculate total BNB received per address (exclude zero addresses)
    received AS (
        SELECT 
            tt."to_address" AS address,
            SUM(COALESCE(TRY_CAST(tt."value" AS NUMBER(38,0)), 0)) AS total_received
        FROM ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.TOKEN_TRANSFERS tt
        INNER JOIN bnb_token_info bti ON tt."token_address" = bti.token_address
        WHERE 
            tt."to_address" != '0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000'
            AND tt."from_address" != '0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000'
        GROUP BY tt."to_address"
    ),

    -- Step 3: Calculate total BNB sent per address (exclude zero addresses)
    sent AS (
        SELECT 
            tt."from_address" AS address,
            SUM(COALESCE(TRY_CAST(tt."value" AS NUMBER(38,0)), 0)) AS total_sent
        FROM ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.TOKEN_TRANSFERS tt
        INNER JOIN bnb_token_info bti ON tt."token_address" = bti.token_address
        WHERE 
            tt."to_address" != '0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000'
            AND tt."from_address" != '0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000'
        GROUP BY tt."from_address"
    ),

    -- Step 4: Compute net balance per address
    balances AS (
        SELECT 
            COALESCE(r.address, s.address) AS address,
            COALESCE(r.total_received, 0) - COALESCE(s.total_sent, 0) AS balance
        FROM received r
        FULL OUTER JOIN sent s ON r.address = s.address
    )

-- Step 5: Sum balances of all non-zero addresses and divide by 10^decimals
SELECT 
    ROUND(SUM(COALESCE(balance, 0)) / POWER(10, (SELECT decimals FROM bnb_token_info)), 4) AS total_circulating_supply_BNB
FROM balances
WHERE balance > 0;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify the BNB token contract address
WITH bnb_token AS (
    SELECT "address"
    FROM ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.TOKENS
    WHERE LOWER("symbol") = LOWER('BNB')
    LIMIT 1
),

-- Step 2: Get all token transfers for BNB, excluding zero-address transactions
valid_transfers AS (
    SELECT
        "from_address",
        "to_address",
        TRY_CAST("value" AS DOUBLE) AS "transfer_value"
    FROM ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.ETHEREUM_BLOCKCHAIN.TOKEN_TRANSFERS
    WHERE "token_address" = (SELECT "address" FROM bnb_token)
      -- Exclude transactions where sender or receiver is the zero address
      AND "from_address" != '0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000'
      AND "to_address"   != '0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000'
),

-- Step 3: Compute total received per address
received AS (
    SELECT "to_address" AS "address", SUM("transfer_value") AS "total_received"
    FROM valid_transfers
    GROUP BY "to_address"
),

-- Step 4: Compute total sent per address
sent AS (
    SELECT "from_address" AS "address", SUM("transfer_value") AS "total_sent"
    FROM valid_transfers
    GROUP BY "from_address"
),

-- Step 5: Combine to get net balance per address
balances AS (
    SELECT
        COALESCE(r."address", s."address") AS "address",
        COALESCE(r."total_received", 0) - COALESCE(s."total_sent", 0) AS "balance"
    FROM received r
    FULL OUTER JOIN sent s
        ON r."address" = s."address"
)

-- Step 6: Sum all positive (non-zero) balances, divide by 10^18 for decimal adjustment
SELECT SUM("balance") / 1e18 AS "total_circulating_supply"
FROM balances
WHERE "balance" > 0;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH session_durations AS (
    SELECT 
        e."browser",
        e."session_id",
        (MAX(e."created_at") - MIN(e."created_at")) / 1000000.0 AS session_duration_seconds
    FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.EVENTS e
    GROUP BY e."browser", e."session_id"
)
SELECT 
    s."browser",
    ROUND(AVG(s.session_duration_seconds), 4) AS avg_session_duration
FROM session_durations s
GROUP BY s."browser"
HAVING COUNT(*) > 10
ORDER BY avg_session_duration ASC
LIMIT 3;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH "session_durations" AS (
    -- Step 1: Calculate duration (in seconds) for each session within each browser
    -- Using the difference in microseconds, then converting to seconds
    SELECT 
        "browser",
        "session_id",
        (MAX("created_at") - MIN("created_at")) / 1000000.0 AS "session_duration_seconds"
    FROM "THELOOK_ECOMMERCE"."THELOOK_ECOMMERCE"."EVENTS"
    GROUP BY "browser", "session_id"
),
"browser_stats" AS (
    -- Step 2: Aggregate by browser: average session duration + session count
    SELECT 
        "browser",
        AVG("session_duration_seconds") AS "avg_session_duration",
        COUNT("session_id") AS "total_sessions"
    FROM "session_durations"
    GROUP BY "browser"
    HAVING COUNT("session_id") > 10   -- Only browsers with more than 10 sessions
)
-- Step 3: Get the 3 browsers with the shortest average session duration
SELECT 
    "browser",
    ROUND("avg_session_duration", 4) AS "avg_session_duration"
FROM "browser_stats"
ORDER BY "avg_session_duration" ASC
LIMIT 3;
```
</details>

```sql
      COALESCE(population_age_16, 0) + COALESCE(population_age_17, 0) + 
      COALESCE(population_age_18, 0) + COALESCE(population_age_19, 0) + 
      COALESCE(population_age_20, 0) + COALESCE(population_age_21, 0) + 
      COALESCE(population_age_22, 0) + COALESCE(population_age_23, 0) + 
      COALESCE(population_age_24, 0)
    ) AS population_under_25
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.midyear_population_age_sex`
  WHERE year = 2017
  GROUP BY country_name, year
),
total_pop AS (
  -- Get total midyear population for each country in 2017
  SELECT 
    country_name,
    year,
    midyear_population AS total_population
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.midyear_population`
  WHERE year = 2017
)
SELECT 
  u.country_name
FROM under_25 u
JOIN total_pop t 
  ON u.country_name = t.country_name AND u.year = t.year
ORDER BY 
  (u.population_under_25 / t.total_population) * 100 DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH county_data AS (
  SELECT 
    SAFE_CAST(symptom_anosmia AS FLOAT64) AS anosmia_value,
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM DATE(date)) AS year
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_symptom_search.symptom_search_sub_region_2_weekly`
  WHERE sub_region_1 = 'New York'
    AND sub_region_2 IN ('Bronx County', 'Queens County', 'Kings County', 'New York County', 'Richmond County')
    AND date BETWEEN '2019-01-01' AND '2020-12-31'
    AND symptom_anosmia IS NOT NULL
    AND symptom_anosmia != 'None'
)
SELECT 
  ROUND(
    (AVG(CASE WHEN year = 2020 THEN anosmia_value END) - 
     AVG(CASE WHEN year = 2019 THEN anosmia_value END)) 
    / AVG(CASE WHEN year = 2019 THEN anosmia_value END) * 100, 
    4
  ) AS percentage_change
FROM county_data;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
  -- Extract all weekly anosmia values for the 5 NYC counties in 2019-2020
  nyc_symptom_data AS (
    SELECT 
      SAFE_CAST(symptom_anosmia AS FLOAT64) AS anosmia_value,
      date
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_symptom_search.symptom_search_sub_region_2_weekly`
    WHERE sub_region_1 = 'New York'
      AND sub_region_2 IN (
        'Bronx County', 
        'Queens County', 
        'Kings County', 
        'New York County', 
        'Richmond County'
      )
      AND date BETWEEN '2019-01-01' AND '2020-12-31'
  ),
  -- Average weekly search frequency across all 5 counties for 2019
  period_2019 AS (
    SELECT AVG(anosmia_value) AS avg_2019
    FROM nyc_symptom_data
    WHERE date BETWEEN '2019-01-01' AND '2019-12-31'
  ),
  -- Average weekly search frequency across all 5 counties for 2020
  period_2020 AS (
    SELECT AVG(anosmia_value) AS avg_2020
    FROM nyc_symptom_data
    WHERE date BETWEEN '2020-01-01' AND '2020-12-31'
  )
-- Calculate overall percentage change: ((2020 avg - 2019 avg) / 2019 avg) * 100
SELECT 
  ROUND(
    ((avg_2020 - avg_2019) / ABS(avg_2019)) * 100, 
    4
  ) AS percentage_change
FROM period_2019, period_2020;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

```sql
-- Count vaccine sites per California county from the all-facilities table
WITH vaccine_counts AS (
  SELECT
    facility_sub_region_2_code AS county_fips,
    COUNT(DISTINCT facility_place_id) AS site_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_vaccination_access.facility_boundary_us_all`

    AND facility_sub_region_1_code = 'US-CA'        -- Only California

),

-- Get population estimates for California counties from the 2018 5-year ACS
california_pop AS (
  SELECT
    geo_id,
    total_pop
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.county_2018_5yr`
  WHERE geo_id LIKE '06%'             -- California FIPS codes start with '06'
    AND total_pop IS NOT NULL
)

SELECT
  b.county_name,
  -- Compute sites per 1,000 people, rounded to 4 decimal places
  ROUND(COALESCE(v.site_count, 0) / p.total_pop * 1000, 4) AS sites_per_1000
FROM california_pop p
INNER JOIN vaccine_counts v
  ON p.geo_id = v.county_fips
-- Get the county name from the vaccine table (ensuring we use California rows)
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT DISTINCT facility_sub_region_2_code, facility_sub_region_2 AS county_name
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_vaccination_access.facility_boundary_us_all`
  WHERE facility_sub_region_1_code = 'US-CA'
) b
  ON p.geo_id = b.facility_sub_region_2_code
ORDER BY county_name;
```

```sql
WITH vaccine_sites AS (
  -- Count distinct vaccination sites per county in California
  SELECT
    facility_sub_region_2_code AS county_fips,
    ANY_VALUE(facility_sub_region_2) AS county_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT facility_place_id) AS site_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_vaccination_access.facility_boundary_us_all`
  WHERE facility_sub_region_1 = 'California'
  GROUP BY facility_sub_region_2_code
),
county_population AS (
  -- Get 2018 5-year ACS population estimates for California counties
  SELECT
    geo_id,
    total_pop
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.county_2018_5yr`
  WHERE geo_id LIKE '06%'  -- California FIPS state code prefix
)
SELECT
  vs.county_name,
  ROUND(vs.site_count / cp.total_pop * 1000, 4) AS sites_per_1000_people
FROM vaccine_sites vs
INNER JOIN county_population cp
  ON vs.county_fips = cp.geo_id
ORDER BY vs.county_name
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- CTE to get median income per census tract in 2015 (5-year ACS)
WITH income_2015 AS (
  SELECT
    geo_id,
    median_income AS income_2015
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.censustract_2015_5yr`
  WHERE median_income = median_income  -- filter out NaN
),

-- CTE to get median income per census tract in 2018 (5-year ACS)
income_2018 AS (
  SELECT
    geo_id,
    median_income AS income_2018
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.censustract_2018_5yr`
  WHERE median_income = median_income
),

-- Join 2015 and 2018 incomes, compute increase, keep only California tracts
income_change AS (
  SELECT
    i15.geo_id,
    i15.income_2015,
    i18.income_2018,
    i18.income_2018 - i15.income_2015 AS increase
  FROM income_2015 i15
  INNER JOIN income_2018 i18
    USING (geo_id)
  WHERE i15.geo_id LIKE '06%'  -- California state FIPS code is '06'
)

-- Get the tract with the largest increase and retrieve its tract_ce
SELECT
  ct.tract_ce AS tract_code
FROM income_change ic
INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.geo_census_tracts.census_tracts_california` ct
  ON ic.geo_id = ct.geo_id
ORDER BY ic.increase DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Get 2015 median income for California tracts
income_2015 AS (
  SELECT 
    geo_id,
    median_income AS median_income_2015
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.censustract_2015_5yr`
  WHERE LOWER(geo_id) LIKE '06%' -- California state FIPS code is 06
    AND median_income IS NOT NULL
),

-- Get 2018 median income for California tracts
income_2018 AS (
  SELECT 
    geo_id,
    median_income AS median_income_2018
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.censustract_2018_5yr`
  WHERE LOWER(geo_id) LIKE '06%'
    AND median_income IS NOT NULL
),

-- Join and compute increase
income_change AS (
  SELECT 
    i15.geo_id,
    i15.median_income_2015,
    i18.median_income_2018,
    ROUND(i18.median_income_2018 - i15.median_income_2015, 4) AS income_increase
  FROM income_2015 i15
  INNER JOIN income_2018 i18 ON i15.geo_id = i18.geo_id
)

-- Get the tract code (last part of geo_id, e.g., after the county code)
SELECT 
  SUBSTR(geo_id, -11) AS tract_code
FROM income_change
ORDER BY income_increase DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

### 22. bq113 (DB: `bls`)
**Question**: Which county in Utah experienced the greatest percentage increase in construction employment from 2000 to 2018, calculated by averaging the employment levels during the third month of each quarter in those years? What is the corresponding percentage increase?

**Status**: Baseline ✅ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

| county_name   |   AVG_CONSTRUCTION_2000 |   AVG_CONSTRUCTION_2018 |   PERCENTAGE_INCREASE |
|:--------------|------------------------:|------------------------:|----------------------:|
| Utah          |                 10466.2 |                 24692.2 |                135.92 |

**OR**

| COUNTY_NAME   |   AVG_CONSTRUCTION_EMPL_2000 |   AVG_CONSTRUCTION_EMPL_2018 |   PERCENTAGE_INCREASE |
|:--------------|-----------------------------:|-----------------------------:|----------------------:|
| Utah County   |                      10466.2 |                      24692.2 |                135.92 |

**OR**

| county            |   pct_increase |
|:------------------|---------------:|
| Utah County, Utah |         135.92 |

<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

| county   |   percentage_increase |
|:---------|----------------------:|
| Utah     |               135.923 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

| county_name   |   pct_increase |
|:--------------|---------------:|
| Utah          |        135.923 |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Get Utah counties
utah_counties AS (
  SELECT 
    county_fips_code,
    county_name
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.counties`
  WHERE state_fips_code = '49'
),

-- Get 2000 construction employment data (average of month3 across all 4 quarters)
empl_2000 AS (
  SELECT 
    area_fips,
    AVG(month3_emplvl_23_construction) AS avg_empl_2000
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.bls_qcew.2000_*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN 'q1' AND 'q4'
    AND month3_emplvl_23_construction IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY area_fips
),

-- Get 2018 construction employment data (average of month3 across all 4 quarters)
empl_2018 AS (
  SELECT 
    area_fips,
    AVG(month3_emplvl_23_construction) AS avg_empl_2018
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.bls_qcew.2018_*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN 'q1' AND 'q4'
    AND month3_emplvl_23_construction IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY area_fips
)

-- Join and calculate percentage increase
SELECT 
  c.county_name,
  ROUND(((e18.avg_empl_2018 - e00.avg_empl_2000) / e00.avg_empl_2000) * 100, 4) AS pct_increase
FROM utah_counties c
JOIN empl_2000 e00 ON c.county_fips_code = e00.area_fips
JOIN empl_2018 e18 ON c.county_fips_code = e18.area_fips
WHERE e00.avg_empl_2000 > 0  -- Avoid division by zero
ORDER BY pct_increase DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Extract construction employment data for 2000 and 2018 quarters, filtered to Utah counties
qcew_data AS (
  SELECT
    area_fips,
    _TABLE_SUFFIX AS table_suffix,
    month3_emplvl_23_construction
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.bls_qcew.*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX IN ('2000_q1', '2000_q2', '2000_q3', '2000_q4',
                          '2018_q1', '2018_q2', '2018_q3', '2018_q4')
    AND area_fips LIKE '49%'  -- Utah county FIPS codes start with '49'
),

-- Step 2: Average the employment across the 4 quarters for each county per year
yearly_avg AS (
  SELECT
    area_fips,
    CASE
      WHEN table_suffix LIKE '2000_%' THEN 2000
      WHEN table_suffix LIKE '2018_%' THEN 2018
    END AS year,
    AVG(month3_emplvl_23_construction) AS avg_construction_empl
  FROM qcew_data
  GROUP BY area_fips, year
),

-- Step 3: Pair each county's 2000 and 2018 averages side by side
county_comparison AS (
  SELECT
    y2000.area_fips,
    y2000.avg_construction_empl AS avg_2000,
    y2018.avg_construction_empl AS avg_2018
  FROM yearly_avg y2000
  JOIN yearly_avg y2018
    ON y2000.area_fips = y2018.area_fips
  WHERE y2000.year = 2000
    AND y2018.year = 2018
    AND y2000.avg_construction_empl > 0  -- Avoid division by zero
)

-- Step 4 & 5: Join with county names and find the top percentage increase
SELECT
  c.county_name AS county,
  ROUND(((cc.avg_2018 - cc.avg_2000) / cc.avg_2000) * 100, 4) AS percentage_increase
FROM county_comparison cc
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.counties` c
  ON cc.area_fips = c.county_fips_code
WHERE c.state_fips_code = '49'
ORDER BY percentage_increase DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

### 23. sf_bq078 (DB: `OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM_2`)
**Question**: Retrieve the approved symbol of target genes with the highest overall score that are associated with the disease 'EFO_0000676' from the data source 'IMPC'.

**Status**: Baseline ✅ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

| approvedSymbol   |
|:-----------------|
| CARD14           |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

| approvedSymbol   |
|:-----------------|
| CARD14           |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

| approvedSymbol   |
|:-----------------|
| CARD14           |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH ranked_targets AS (
    SELECT 
        t."approvedSymbol",
        a."score"
    FROM OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM_2.OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM.ASSOCIATIONBYOVERALLDIRECT a
    INNER JOIN OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM_2.OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM.TARGETS t
        ON a."targetId" = t."id"
    WHERE a."diseaseId" = 'EFO_0000676'
),
max_score AS (
    SELECT MAX("score") AS "max_score"
    FROM ranked_targets
)
SELECT DISTINCT r."approvedSymbol"
FROM ranked_targets r
CROSS JOIN max_score m
WHERE r."score" = m."max_score";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
    -- Step 1: Identify targets with evidence from IMPC (case-insensitive)
    impc_evidence_targets AS (
        SELECT DISTINCT e."targetId"
        FROM OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM_2.OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM.EVIDENCE e
        WHERE e."diseaseId" = 'EFO_0000676'
          AND LOWER(e."datasourceId") = 'impc'
    ),
    -- Step 2: Get overall direct and indirect scores for those targets
    combined_scores AS (
        SELECT 
            COALESCE(d."targetId", ind."targetId") AS "targetId",
            COALESCE(d."score", 0) AS "direct_score",
            COALESCE(ind."score", 0) AS "indirect_score",
            ROUND(GREATEST(COALESCE(d."score", 0), COALESCE(ind."score", 0)), 4) AS "overall_score"
        FROM impc_evidence_targets t
        LEFT JOIN OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM_2.OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM.ASSOCIATIONBYOVERALLDIRECT d
            ON t."targetId" = d."targetId" AND d."diseaseId" = 'EFO_0000676'
        LEFT JOIN OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM_2.OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM.ASSOCIATIONBYOVERALLINDIRECT ind
            ON t."targetId" = ind."targetId" AND ind."diseaseId" = 'EFO_0000676'
    ),
    -- Step 3: Find the maximum overall score
    max_score AS (
        SELECT MAX("overall_score") AS "max_overall_score"
        FROM combined_scores
    ),
    -- Step 4: Identify the target(s) with that maximum score
    top_targets AS (
        SELECT "targetId"
        FROM combined_scores
        WHERE "overall_score" = (SELECT "max_overall_score" FROM max_score)
    )
-- Step 5: Retrieve the approved symbol from the TARGETS table
SELECT t."approvedSymbol"
FROM OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM_2.OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM.TARGETS t
INNER JOIN top_targets tt ON t."id" = tt."targetId"
WHERE t."approvedSymbol" IS NOT NULL;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH monthly_total AS (
  SELECT 
    FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m', creation_date) AS month,
    COUNT(*) AS total
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
  WHERE 
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM creation_date) = 2022
    AND post_type_id = 1
  GROUP BY month
),
monthly_python AS (
  SELECT 
    FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m', creation_date) AS month,
    COUNT(*) AS python_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
  WHERE 
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM creation_date) = 2022
    AND post_type_id = 1
    AND REGEXP_CONTAINS(tags, r'(^|\|)python($|\|)')
  GROUP BY month
)
SELECT 
  t.month,
  ROUND(COALESCE(SAFE_DIVIDE(p.python_count, t.total), 0), 4) AS proportion
FROM monthly_total t
LEFT JOIN monthly_python p ON t.month = p.month
ORDER BY t.month;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
SELECT
  FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m', creation_date) AS month,
  ROUND(
    COUNTIF(REGEXP_CONTAINS(tags, r'(^|\|)python(\||$)')) / COUNT(*),
    4
  ) AS proportion
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM creation_date) = 2022
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify living patients whose last names start with 'A'
WITH living_A_patients AS (
  SELECT p.id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.fhir_synthea.patient` p
  WHERE (p.deceased IS NULL OR p.deceased.boolean = FALSE)
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM UNNEST(p.name) AS n
      WHERE n.family LIKE 'A%'
    )
),

-- Step 2: Patients with exactly one distinct condition (by condition code)
single_condition_patients AS (
  SELECT c.subject.patientId AS patient_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.fhir_synthea.condition` c,
       UNNEST(c.code.coding) AS coding
  GROUP BY c.subject.patientId
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT coding.code) = 1
),

-- Step 3: Intersection of the above two sets
eligible_patients AS (
  SELECT p.id
  FROM living_A_patients p
  INNER JOIN single_condition_patients sc ON p.id = sc.patient_id
),

-- Step 4: For each eligible patient, count distinct active medications
patient_med_count AS (
  SELECT mr.subject.patientId AS patient_id,
         COUNT(DISTINCT mc.code) AS active_med_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.fhir_synthea.medication_request` mr,
       UNNEST(mr.medication.codeableConcept.coding) AS mc
  WHERE mr.status = 'active'
    AND mr.subject.patientId IN (SELECT id FROM eligible_patients)
  GROUP BY mr.subject.patientId
),

-- Step 5: Get the unique condition code for each eligible patient
patient_condition AS (
  SELECT c.subject.patientId AS patient_id,
         coding.code AS condition_code,
         coding.display AS condition_display
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.fhir_synthea.condition` c,
       UNNEST(c.code.coding) AS coding
  WHERE c.subject.patientId IN (SELECT id FROM eligible_patients)
),

-- Step 6: Combine medication count with condition (left join to include patients with zero meds)
condition_med AS (
  SELECT pc.condition_code,
         pc.condition_display,
         COALESCE(pmc.active_med_count, 0) AS med_count
  FROM patient_condition pc
  LEFT JOIN patient_med_count pmc ON pc.patient_id = pmc.patient_id
),

-- Step 7: For each condition, find the maximum number of active medications across patients
condition_max AS (
  SELECT condition_code,
         condition_display,
         MAX(med_count) AS max_med_count
  FROM condition_med
  GROUP BY condition_code, condition_display
)

-- Step 8: Return the top 8 conditions with highest max medication count
SELECT condition_code, condition_display
FROM condition_max
ORDER BY max_med_count DESC
LIMIT 8;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Living patients whose last name begins with 'A' (using EXISTS to avoid DISTINCT)
living_patients_with_A AS (
  SELECT p.id AS patient_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.fhir_synthea.patient` p
  WHERE 
    (p.deceased IS NULL OR p.deceased.boolean = FALSE)
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM UNNEST(p.name) AS name_entry
      WHERE STARTS_WITH(name_entry.family, 'A')
    )
),

-- Step 2: Among them, patients with exactly one distinct condition code (efficient HAVING)
patients_with_one_condition AS (
  SELECT c.subject.patientId AS patient_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.fhir_synthea.condition` c,
       UNNEST(c.code.coding) AS cond_code
  WHERE c.subject.patientId IN (SELECT patient_id FROM living_patients_with_A)
  GROUP BY patient_id
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT cond_code.code) = 1
),

-- Step 3: The single condition each qualifying patient has (use LEFT JOIN LATERAL? Not needed. Direct join with patients_with_one_condition)
patient_conditions AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    c.subject.patientId AS patient_id,
    cond_code.code AS condition_code,
    cond_code.display AS condition_display
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.fhir_synthea.condition` c,
       UNNEST(c.code.coding) AS cond_code
  WHERE c.subject.patientId IN (SELECT patient_id FROM patients_with_one_condition)
),

-- Step 4: Active medications for those patients (use INNER JOIN to avoid scanning non-matching rows)
patient_medications AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    mr.subject.patientId AS patient_id,
    med_code.code AS medication_code
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.fhir_synthea.medication_request` mr,
       UNNEST(mr.medication.codeableConcept.coding) AS med_code
  WHERE 
    mr.subject.patientId IN (SELECT patient_id FROM patients_with_one_condition)
    AND mr.status = 'active'
),

-- Step 5: Count distinct medications per patient per condition (change LEFT to INNER because patients with no meds won't affect top conditions)
patient_condition_med_count AS (
  SELECT 
    pc.condition_code,
    pc.condition_display,
    pc.patient_id,
    COUNT(DISTINCT pm.medication_code) AS medication_count
  FROM patient_conditions pc
  INNER JOIN patient_medications pm ON pc.patient_id = pm.patient_id
  GROUP BY pc.condition_code, pc.condition_display, pc.patient_id
),

-- Step 6: For each condition, find the max meds for any single patient
condition_max_meds AS (
  SELECT 
    condition_code,
    condition_display,
    MAX(medication_count) AS max_medications_for_single_patient
  FROM patient_condition_med_count
  GROUP BY condition_code, condition_display
)

-- Step 7: Top 8 conditions by highest medication count
SELECT 
  condition_display AS condition_name,
  condition_code
FROM condition_max_meds
ORDER BY max_medications_for_single_patient DESC
LIMIT 8;
```
</details>

```sql
-- CTE for each pollutant: compute monthly average of daily arithmetic_mean
-- For SO2 and Lead, apply scaling factor before averaging.
WITH pm10_monthly AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date_local) AS month,
    ROUND(AVG(arithmetic_mean), 4) AS avg_pm10
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.pm10_daily_summary`
  WHERE state_name = 'California'
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 2020
  GROUP BY month
),
pm25_frm_monthly AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date_local) AS month,
    ROUND(AVG(arithmetic_mean), 4) AS avg_pm25_frm
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.pm25_frm_daily_summary`
  WHERE state_name = 'California'
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 2020
  GROUP BY month
),
pm25_nonfrm_monthly AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date_local) AS month,
    ROUND(AVG(arithmetic_mean), 4) AS avg_pm25_nonfrm
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.pm25_nonfrm_daily_summary`
  WHERE state_name = 'California'
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 2020
  GROUP BY month
),
voc_monthly AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date_local) AS month,
    ROUND(AVG(arithmetic_mean), 4) AS avg_voc
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.voc_daily_summary`
  WHERE state_name = 'California'
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 2020
  GROUP BY month
),
so2_monthly AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date_local) AS month,
    ROUND(AVG(arithmetic_mean * 10), 4) AS avg_so2_scaled
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.so2_daily_summary`
  WHERE state_name = 'California'
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 2020
  GROUP BY month
),
lead_monthly AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date_local) AS month,
    ROUND(AVG(arithmetic_mean * 100), 4) AS avg_lead_scaled
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.lead_daily_summary`
  WHERE state_name = 'California'
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 2020
  GROUP BY month
)
-- Full outer join all monthly summaries on month to produce one row per month
SELECT
  COALESCE(pm10.month, pm25_frm.month, pm25_nonfrm.month, voc.month, so2.month, lead.month) AS month,
  pm10.avg_pm10,
  pm25_frm.avg_pm25_frm,
  pm25_nonfrm.avg_pm25_nonfrm,
  voc.avg_voc,
  so2.avg_so2_scaled,
  lead.avg_lead_scaled
FROM pm10_monthly pm10
FULL OUTER JOIN pm25_frm_monthly pm25_frm
  ON pm10.month = pm25_frm.month
FULL OUTER JOIN pm25_nonfrm_monthly pm25_nonfrm
  ON COALESCE(pm10.month, pm25_frm.month) = pm25_nonfrm.month
FULL OUTER JOIN voc_monthly voc
  ON COALESCE(pm10.month, pm25_frm.month, pm25_nonfrm.month) = voc.month
FULL OUTER JOIN so2_monthly so2
  ON COALESCE(pm10.month, pm25_frm.month, pm25_nonfrm.month, voc.month) = so2.month
FULL OUTER JOIN lead_monthly lead
  ON COALESCE(pm10.month, pm25_frm.month, pm25_nonfrm.month, voc.month, so2.month) = lead.month
ORDER BY month;
```
</details>

### 29. sf_bq219 (DB: `IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES`)
**Question**: In the Iowa Liquor Sales dataset, starting from January 1, 2022 through the last fully completed month, which two liquor categories, each contributing an average of at least 1% to the monthly sales volume over at least 24 months of available data, have the lowest Pearson correlation coefficient when comparing their monthly percentages of total liquor sales across those months, and what are their names?

**Status**: Baseline ✅ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

| CATEGORY1               | CATEGORY2      |
|:------------------------|:---------------|
| AMERICAN FLAVORED VODKA | CREAM LIQUEURS |

**OR**

| output                  |
|:------------------------|
| AMERICAN FLAVORED VODKA |
| CREAM LIQUEURS          |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

| CATEGORY_1              | CATEGORY_2     |   PEARSON_CORRELATION |
|:------------------------|:---------------|----------------------:|
| AMERICAN FLAVORED VODKA | CREAM LIQUEURS |             -0.737908 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

| CAT_A                   | CAT_B          |
|:------------------------|:---------------|
| AMERICAN FLAVORED VODKA | CREAM LIQUEURS |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Determine the date range: from Jan 1, 2022 through the last fully completed month
WITH date_range AS (
    SELECT 
        '2022-01-01'::DATE AS start_date,
        -- last fully completed month
        LAST_DAY(
            CASE 
                WHEN MAX("date") = LAST_DAY(MAX("date")) THEN MAX("date")
                ELSE DATEADD('month', -1, MAX("date"))
            END
        ) AS end_date
    FROM "IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES"."IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES"."SALES"
),

-- Step 2: Filter sales to the date range and compute monthly volumes per category
monthly_category_volume AS (
    SELECT 
        DATE_TRUNC('month', s."date") AS month,
        s."category_name",
        SUM(s."volume_sold_liters") AS cat_volume
    FROM "IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES"."IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES"."SALES" s
    CROSS JOIN date_range dr
    WHERE s."date" >= dr.start_date
      AND s."date" <= dr.end_date
    GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', s."date"), s."category_name"
),

-- Step 3: Compute total monthly volume across all categories
monthly_total_volume AS (
    SELECT 
        month,
        SUM(cat_volume) AS total_volume
    FROM monthly_category_volume
    GROUP BY month
),

-- Step 4: Compute monthly percentage for each category
category_monthly_pct AS (
    SELECT 
        mcv.month,
        mcv."category_name",
        mcv.cat_volume / NULLIF(mtv.total_volume, 0) AS monthly_pct
    FROM monthly_category_volume mcv
    INNER JOIN monthly_total_volume mtv ON mcv.month = mtv.month
),

-- Step 5: Filter categories with at least 24 months and average monthly percentage >= 1%
qualified_categories AS (
    SELECT 
        "category_name",
        COUNT(*) AS num_months,
        AVG(monthly_pct) AS avg_pct
    FROM category_monthly_pct
    GROUP BY "category_name"
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 24
       AND AVG(monthly_pct) >= 0.01
),

-- Step 6: Keep monthly percentage series for qualified categories
cat_series AS (
    SELECT 
        c."category_name",
        cmp.month,
        cmp.monthly_pct
    FROM category_monthly_pct cmp
    INNER JOIN qualified_categories c ON cmp."category_name" = c."category_name"
),

-- Step 7: Compute Pearson correlation for every pair of qualified categories
pair_corr AS (
    SELECT 
        a."category_name" AS cat_a,
        b."category_name" AS cat_b,
        CORR(a.monthly_pct, b.monthly_pct) AS pearson_r
    FROM cat_series a
    INNER JOIN cat_series b 
        ON a.month = b.month 
        AND a."category_name" < b."category_name"
    GROUP BY a."category_name", b."category_name"
)

-- Step 8: Return the two category names with the lowest correlation
SELECT cat_a, cat_b
FROM pair_corr
ORDER BY pearson_r ASC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: Define the date range: from 2022-01-01 to the end of the last fully completed month.
-- The last fully completed month is the month before the current month (no partial current month data).
date_range AS (
    SELECT 
        '2022-01-01'::DATE AS start_date,
        DATE_TRUNC('month', CURRENT_DATE) AS end_of_last_complete_month  -- this is the first day of current month, so all dates < this are in completed months
),
-- Step 2: Compute total monthly sales volume (in liters) for all categories.
monthly_total AS (
    SELECT 
        DATE_TRUNC('month', s."date") AS month_start,
        SUM(s."volume_sold_liters") AS total_vol
    FROM "IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES"."IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES"."SALES" s
    WHERE s."date" >= (SELECT start_date FROM date_range)
      AND s."date" <  (SELECT end_of_last_complete_month FROM date_range)
    GROUP BY month_start
),
-- Step 3: Compute monthly sales volume per category.
monthly_category AS (
    SELECT 
        DATE_TRUNC('month', s."date") AS month_start,
        s."category_name",
        SUM(s."volume_sold_liters") AS cat_vol
    FROM "IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES"."IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES"."SALES" s
    WHERE s."date" >= (SELECT start_date FROM date_range)
      AND s."date" <  (SELECT end_of_last_complete_month FROM date_range)
    GROUP BY month_start, s."category_name"
    HAVING cat_vol > 0  -- exclude months where the category had no sales (though they won't appear anyway)
),
-- Step 4: Calculate the percentage contribution of each category to the total monthly volume.
category_pct AS (
    SELECT 
        mc.month_start,
        mc."category_name",
        mc.cat_vol / mt.total_vol AS pct
    FROM monthly_category mc
    JOIN monthly_total mt ON mc.month_start = mt.month_start
),
-- Step 5: For each category, compute the average percentage and the number of months with sales (available data).
-- Only keep categories that have at least 24 months of data and an average percentage >= 1%.
category_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        cp."category_name",
        COUNT(DISTINCT cp.month_start) AS num_months,
        AVG(cp.pct) AS avg_pct
    FROM category_pct cp
    GROUP BY cp."category_name"
    HAVING num_months >= 24 AND avg_pct >= 0.01
),
-- Step 6: Get the list of qualifying categories.
qualifying_categories AS (
    SELECT cs."category_name" FROM category_stats cs
),
-- Step 7: Restrict the monthly percentages to only qualifying categories.
qual_pct AS (
    SELECT cp.*
    FROM category_pct cp
    WHERE cp."category_name" IN (SELECT qc."category_name" FROM qualifying_categories qc)
)
-- Step 8: For each unordered pair of qualifying categories, compute the Pearson correlation coefficient
-- of their monthly percentage time series, using only months where both categories have data.
SELECT 
    a."category_name" AS category_1,
    b."category_name" AS category_2,
    CORR(a.pct, b.pct) AS pearson_correlation
FROM qual_pct a
JOIN qual_pct b ON a.month_start = b.month_start
WHERE a."category_name" < b."category_name"  -- ensure each pair only once, and avoid self-joins
GROUP BY a."category_name", b."category_name"
-- Step 9: Order by the smallest (lowest) correlation coefficient.
ORDER BY pearson_correlation ASC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

```sql
-- Step 1: Filter sales to Dubuque County, 2022, Bourbon Whiskey
WITH bourbon_sales AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(REGEXP_EXTRACT(zip_code, r'^\d+') AS INT64) AS zip_int,
    sale_dollars,
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date) AS sale_month
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.iowa_liquor_sales.sales`
  WHERE
    LOWER(county) = 'dubuque'
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) = 2022
    AND LOWER(category_name) LIKE '%bourbon%'
),

-- Step 2: Rank zip codes by total 2022 Bourbon sales
zip_ranking AS (
  SELECT
    zip_int,
    SUM(sale_dollars) AS total_sales,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(sale_dollars) DESC) AS rn
  FROM bourbon_sales
  GROUP BY zip_int
),

-- Step 3: Identify the 3rd ranked zip code
target_zip AS (
  SELECT zip_int
  FROM zip_ranking
  WHERE rn = 3
),

-- Step 4: Compute monthly sales for that zip code
monthly_sales AS (
  SELECT
    sale_month,
    SUM(sale_dollars) AS monthly_total
  FROM bourbon_sales
  WHERE zip_int = (SELECT zip_int FROM target_zip)
  GROUP BY sale_month
),

-- Step 5: Get population aged 21+ for that zip code from 2010 census
population_21plus AS (
  SELECT
    SUM(population) AS adult_population
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_usa.population_by_zip_2010`
  WHERE
    zipcode = CAST((SELECT zip_int FROM target_zip) AS STRING)
    AND gender IN ('male', 'female')
    AND minimum_age >= 21
)

-- Final: Compute monthly per capita Bourbon sales
SELECT
  sale_month,
  ROUND(monthly_total / adult_population, 4) AS per_capita_sales
FROM monthly_sales, population_21plus
ORDER BY sale_month;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
  -- Step 1: Filter Bourbon Whiskey sales in Dubuque County 2022, extract 5-digit zip
  bourbon_sales AS (
    SELECT
      SPLIT(zip_code, '.')[OFFSET(0)] AS zip5,
      date,
      sale_dollars
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.iowa_liquor_sales.sales`
    WHERE
      county = 'DUBUQUE'
      AND date BETWEEN '2022-01-01' AND '2022-12-31'
      AND LOWER(category_name) LIKE '%bourbon%'
  ),

  -- Step 2: Total sales per zip code and rank them
  zip_totals AS (
    SELECT
      zip5,
      SUM(sale_dollars) AS total_sales
    FROM bourbon_sales
    GROUP BY zip5
  ),
  ranked_zips AS (
    SELECT
      zip5,
      total_sales,
      RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total_sales DESC) AS rnk
    FROM zip_totals
  ),

  -- Step 3: Pick the zip code ranked 3rd
  target_zip AS (
    SELECT zip5
    FROM ranked_zips
    WHERE rnk = 3
  ),

  -- Step 4: Population aged 21+ for the target zip (only fetch the needed zip)
  population_21plus AS (
    SELECT
      zipcode,
      SUM(population) AS pop_21plus
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_usa.population_by_zip_2010`
    WHERE
      gender IN ('male', 'female')
      AND minimum_age IS NOT NULL
      AND minimum_age >= 21
      AND zipcode IN (SELECT zip5 FROM target_zip)
    GROUP BY zipcode
  )

-- Step 5: Monthly per capita sales for the target zip
SELECT
  FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m', bs.date) AS month,
  ROUND(SUM(bs.sale_dollars) / pop.pop_21plus, 4) AS per_capita_sales
FROM bourbon_sales bs
JOIN target_zip tz ON bs.zip5 = tz.zip5
JOIN population_21plus pop ON tz.zip5 = pop.zipcode
GROUP BY month, pop.pop_21plus
ORDER BY month;
```
</details>

```sql
    FROM "TCGA"."TCGA_VERSIONED"."PER_SAMPLE_FILE_METADATA_HG38_GDC_R39_V2" m
    JOIN "TCGA"."TCGA_VERSIONED"."RNASEQ_HG38_GDC_R35" r
        ON m."sample_barcode" = r."sample_barcode"  -- or appropriate join key
    WHERE m."project_short_name" = 'TCGA-BRCA'
      AND r."gene_type" = 'protein_coding'
),
cases_with_multiple_types AS (
    SELECT "case_barcode"
    FROM rnaseq_genes
    GROUP BY "case_barcode"
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT "sample_type_name") >= 2
       AND SUM(CASE WHEN "sample_type_name" = 'Solid Tissue Normal' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
)
SELECT DISTINCT "case_barcode"
FROM cases_with_multiple_types
ORDER BY "case_barcode";
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Define cytoband region for 15q11 on chromosome 15
WITH cytoband_15q11 AS (
    SELECT 
        "chromosome",
        MIN("hg38_start") AS "region_start",
        MAX("hg38_stop")  AS "region_end"
    FROM TCGA_MITELMAN.PROD.CYTOBANDS_HG38
    WHERE "chromosome" = 'chr15'
      AND "cytoband_name" LIKE '15q11%'
    GROUP BY "chromosome"
),

-- Step 2: Get copy number segments for TCGA-LAML on chromosome 15
segments_laml_chr15 AS (
    SELECT 
        "case_barcode",
        "chromosome",
        "start_pos",
        "end_pos",
        "copy_number"
    FROM TCGA_MITELMAN.TCGA_VERSIONED.COPY_NUMBER_SEGMENT_ALLELIC_HG38_GDC_R23
    WHERE "project_short_name" = 'TCGA-LAML'
      AND "chromosome" = 'chr15'
),

-- Step 3: Compute overlap between segments and cytoband region
overlap AS (
    SELECT 
        s."case_barcode",
        s."copy_number",
        -- length of overlap
        GREATEST(0, 
            LEAST(s."end_pos", c."region_end") - GREATEST(s."start_pos", c."region_start") + 1
        ) AS "overlap_length"
    FROM segments_laml_chr15 s
    CROSS JOIN cytoband_15q11 c
    WHERE s."start_pos" <= c."region_end" 
      AND s."end_pos"   >= c."region_start"
),

-- Step 4: Weighted average copy number per case
per_case AS (
    SELECT 
        "case_barcode",
        SUM("copy_number" * "overlap_length") / NULLIF(SUM("overlap_length"), 0) AS "weighted_avg_cn"
    FROM overlap
    WHERE "overlap_length" > 0
    GROUP BY "case_barcode"
),

-- Step 5: Rank cases by weighted average copy number descending
ranked AS (
    SELECT 
        "case_barcode",
        "weighted_avg_cn",
        RANK() OVER (ORDER BY "weighted_avg_cn" DESC) AS "rnk"
    FROM per_case
)

-- Step 6: Output the case barcode(s) with the highest value
SELECT "case_barcode"
FROM ranked
WHERE "rnk" = 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH cytoband_15q11 AS (
  -- Get cytoband boundaries for 15q11 (convert 0-based start to 1-based)
  SELECT 
    "chromosome",
    "cytoband_name",
    "hg38_start" + 1 AS "cb_start_1based",  -- UCSC-style 0-based start -> 1-based
    "hg38_stop" AS "cb_end_1based"         -- already 1-based
  FROM "TCGA_MITELMAN"."PROD"."CYTOBANDS_HG38"
  WHERE "chromosome" = 'chr15'
    AND "cytoband_name" = '15q11'
),
overlap_segments AS (
  -- Join copy number segments with cytoband, compute overlap length
  SELECT 
    seg."case_barcode",
    seg."copy_number",
    -- Compute overlapping interval (1-based inclusive)
    GREATEST(seg."start_pos", cb."cb_start_1based") AS "overlap_start",
    LEAST(seg."end_pos", cb."cb_end_1based") AS "overlap_end",
    -- Overlap length (0 if no overlap)
    GREATEST(LEAST(seg."end_pos", cb."cb_end_1based") - GREATEST(seg."start_pos", cb."cb_start_1based") + 1, 0) AS "overlap_length"
  FROM "TCGA_MITELMAN"."TCGA_VERSIONED"."COPY_NUMBER_SEGMENT_ALLELIC_HG38_GDC_R23" seg
  CROSS JOIN cytoband_15q11 cb
  WHERE seg."project_short_name" = 'TCGA-LAML'
    AND seg."chromosome" = 'chr15'
    AND seg."start_pos" <= cb."cb_end_1based"
    AND seg."end_pos" >= cb."cb_start_1based"
),
case_weighted_avg AS (
  -- Compute weighted average copy number per case
  SELECT 
    "case_barcode",
    SUM("copy_number" * "overlap_length") / NULLIF(SUM("overlap_length"), 0) AS "weighted_avg_cn"
  FROM overlap_segments
  WHERE "overlap_length" > 0
  GROUP BY "case_barcode"
),
ranked AS (
  -- Rank cases by weighted average descending
  SELECT 
    "case_barcode",
    "weighted_avg_cn",
    RANK() OVER (ORDER BY "weighted_avg_cn" DESC) AS "rnk"
  FROM case_weighted_avg
)
-- Return case(s) with highest weighted average
SELECT "case_barcode"
FROM ranked
WHERE "rnk" = 1
ORDER BY "case_barcode";
```
</details>
