#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Filter variants on chromosome 12 and flatten the call array
WITH variant_calls AS (
    SELECT 
        V."start",
        V."end",
        V."call" AS call_data
    FROM "_1000_GENOMES"."_1000_GENOMES"."VARIANTS" V
    WHERE V."reference_name" = '12'
),

-- Step 2: Unnest the call array to get individual sample genotypes
flattened_calls AS (
    SELECT
        VC."start",
        VC."end",
        f.value:"call_set_name"::STRING AS sample_id,
        f.value:"genotype"::ARRAY AS genotype_array
    FROM variant_calls VC,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => VC.call_data) f
),

-- Step 3: Unnest the genotype array to get individual alleles (0 or 1)
alleles AS (
    SELECT
        FC."start",
        FC."end",
        FC.sample_id,
        g.value::INTEGER AS allele
    FROM flattened_calls FC,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => FC.genotype_array) g
),

-- Step 4: Join with SAMPLE_INFO to get super population
allele_with_pop AS (
    SELECT
        a."start",
        a."end",
        a.allele,
        CASE WHEN si."Super_Population" = 'EAS' THEN 'case' ELSE 'control' END AS group_type
    FROM alleles a
    JOIN "_1000_GENOMES"."_1000_GENOMES"."SAMPLE_INFO" si 
      ON a.sample_id = si."Sample"
),

-- Step 5: Aggregate per variant: counts for each cell in 2x2 table
counts AS (
    SELECT
        "start",
        "end",
        SUM(CASE WHEN group_type = 'case' AND allele = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS case_ref,
        SUM(CASE WHEN group_type = 'case' AND allele = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS case_alt,
        SUM(CASE WHEN group_type = 'control' AND allele = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS control_ref,
        SUM(CASE WHEN group_type = 'control' AND allele = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS control_alt
    FROM allele_with_pop
    GROUP BY "start", "end"
),

-- Step 6: Compute row, column totals and expected values
expected_values AS (
    SELECT
        c.*,
        (c.case_ref + c.case_alt)::FLOAT AS case_total,
        (c.control_ref + c.control_alt)::FLOAT AS control_total,
        (c.case_ref + c.control_ref)::FLOAT AS ref_total,
        (c.case_alt + c.control_alt)::FLOAT AS alt_total,
        (c.case_ref + c.case_alt + c.control_ref + c.control_alt)::FLOAT AS grand_total
    FROM counts c
    WHERE (c.case_ref + c.case_alt + c.control_ref + c.control_alt) > 0
),

-- Step 7: Filter variants where all expected counts >= 5
valid_variants AS (
    SELECT
        e.*,
        (e.case_total * e.ref_total) / NULLIF(e.grand_total, 0) AS exp_case_ref,
        (e.case_total * e.alt_total) / NULLIF(e.grand_total, 0) AS exp_case_alt,
        (e.control_total * e.ref_total) / NULLIF(e.grand_total, 0) AS exp_control_ref,
        (e.control_total * e.alt_total) / NULLIF(e.grand_total, 0) AS exp_control_alt
    FROM expected_values e
    WHERE (e.case_total * e.ref_total) / NULLIF(e.grand_total, 0) >= 5
      AND (e.case_total * e.alt_total) / NULLIF(e.grand_total, 0) >= 5
      AND (e.control_total * e.ref_total) / NULLIF(e.grand_total, 0) >= 5
      AND (e.control_total * e.alt_total) / NULLIF(e.grand_total, 0) >= 5
),

-- Step 8: Compute chi-squared with Yates's correction
chi_sq AS (
    SELECT
        "start",
        "end",
        ROUND(
            CASE WHEN ABS(case_ref - exp_case_ref) > 0.5
                 THEN POWER(ABS(case_ref - exp_case_ref) - 0.5, 2) / NULLIF(exp_case_ref, 0)
                 ELSE 0 END +
            CASE WHEN ABS(case_alt - exp_case_alt) > 0.5
                 THEN POWER(ABS(case_alt - exp_case_alt) - 0.5, 2) / NULLIF(exp_case_alt, 0)
                 ELSE 0 END +
            CASE WHEN ABS(control_ref - exp_control_ref) > 0.5
                 THEN POWER(ABS(control_ref - exp_control_ref) - 0.5, 2) / NULLIF(exp_control_ref, 0)
                 ELSE 0 END +
            CASE WHEN ABS(control_alt - exp_control_alt) > 0.5
                 THEN POWER(ABS(control_alt - exp_control_alt) - 0.5, 2) / NULLIF(exp_control_alt, 0)
                 ELSE 0 END,
            4
        ) AS chi_squared
    FROM valid_variants
)

-- Step 9: Return top variants with chi_squared >= threshold
SELECT "start", "end", chi_squared
FROM chi_sq
WHERE chi_squared >= 29.71679
ORDER BY chi_squared DESC;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Flatten call array to extract per-individual allele counts for variants on chr12
per_variant_ind AS (
  SELECT
    v."start",
    v."end",
    v."reference_name",
    f.value:"call_set_name"::STRING AS "individual_id",
    (f.value:"genotype"[0]::INT + f.value:"genotype"[1]::INT) AS "alt_allele_count"
  FROM "_1000_GENOMES"."_1000_GENOMES"."VARIANTS" v,
  LATERAL FLATTEN(input => v."call") f
  WHERE v."reference_name" = '12'
),

-- Step 2: Join with sample info to get super population
ind_info AS (
  SELECT
    p."individual_id",
    p."alt_allele_count",
    p."start",
    p."end",
    s."Super_Population"
  FROM per_variant_ind p
  JOIN "_1000_GENOMES"."_1000_GENOMES"."SAMPLE_INFO" s
    ON p."individual_id" = s."Sample"
),

-- Step 3: Aggregate allele counts for cases (EAS) and controls (all others)
grouped AS (
  SELECT
    "start",
    "end",
    SUM(CASE WHEN "Super_Population" = 'EAS' THEN "alt_allele_count" ELSE 0 END) AS "alt_cases",
    SUM(CASE WHEN "Super_Population" != 'EAS' THEN "alt_allele_count" ELSE 0 END) AS "alt_controls",
    COUNT(CASE WHEN "Super_Population" = 'EAS' THEN 1 END) * 2 AS "total_cases_alleles",
    COUNT(CASE WHEN "Super_Population" != 'EAS' THEN 1 END) * 2 AS "total_controls_alleles"
  FROM ind_info
  GROUP BY "start", "end"
)

-- Step 4: Compute chi-squared with Yates correction and filter
SELECT
  "start",
  "end",
  ROUND(
    -- Yates chi-squared = (|ad - bc| - N/2)^2 * N / ( (a+b)(c+d)(a+c)(b+d) )
    (
      POW(
        ABS(
          "alt_cases" * ("total_controls_alleles" - "alt_controls")
          - "alt_controls" * ("total_cases_alleles" - "alt_cases")
        ) - ("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles") / 2.0,
        2
      ) * ("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles")
    ) / (
      ("alt_cases" + "alt_controls")
      * (("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles") - ("alt_cases" + "alt_controls"))
      * "total_cases_alleles"
      * "total_controls_alleles"
    ),
    4
  ) AS "chi_squared"
FROM grouped
WHERE
  -- Ensure all expected cell counts are >= 5
  ("alt_cases" + "alt_controls") * "total_cases_alleles" / ("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles") >= 5
  AND ("alt_cases" + "alt_controls") * "total_controls_alleles" / ("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles") >= 5
  AND (("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles") - ("alt_cases" + "alt_controls")) * "total_cases_alleles" / ("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles") >= 5
  AND (("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles") - ("alt_cases" + "alt_controls")) * "total_controls_alleles" / ("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles") >= 5
  AND ROUND(
    (
      POW(
        ABS(
          "alt_cases" * ("total_controls_alleles" - "alt_controls")
          - "alt_controls" * ("total_cases_alleles" - "alt_cases")
        ) - ("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles") / 2.0,
        2
      ) * ("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles")
    ) / (
      ("alt_cases" + "alt_controls")
      * (("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles") - ("alt_cases" + "alt_controls"))
      * "total_cases_alleles"
      * "total_controls_alleles"
    ),
    4
  ) >= 29.71679
ORDER BY "chi_squared" DESC;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH station_trip_years AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT start_station_id AS station_id, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM start_time) AS year

  s.status,

  ON sy.station_id = s.station_id
```

```sql
WITH trips_by_year AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM start_time) AS year,
    start_station_id AS station_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_trips`
  WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM start_time) IN (2013, 2014)
  GROUP BY year, station_id
)
SELECT
  t.year,
  LOWER(s.status) AS status,
  COUNT(DISTINCT t.station_id) AS station_count
FROM trips_by_year t
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_stations` s
  ON t.station_id = s.station_id
WHERE LOWER(s.status) IN ('active', 'closed')
GROUP BY year, status
ORDER BY year, status;
```

```sql
    WHERE "status" = 'active'
),
-- Step 2: For each active station, compute total starting trips and average duration
"trips_summary" AS (
    SELECT 
        t."start_station_id" AS "station_id",
        COUNT(t."trip_id") AS "total_trips",
        AVG(t."duration_minutes") AS "avg_duration"
    FROM "AUSTIN"."AUSTIN_BIKESHARE"."BIKESHARE_TRIPS" t
    INNER JOIN "active_stations" a ON t."start_station_id" = a."station_id"
    GROUP BY t."start_station_id"
),
-- Step 3: Compute the overall total trips from active stations (needed for percentage)
"overall_total" AS (
    SELECT SUM("total_trips") AS "overall_trips"
    FROM "trips_summary"
),
-- Step 4: Rank stations by total trips descending (using RANK to include ties)
"ranked" AS (
    SELECT 
        s."station_id",
        s."total_trips",
        s."avg_duration",
        o."overall_trips",
        RANK() OVER (ORDER BY s."total_trips" DESC) AS "rank"
    FROM "trips_summary" s
    CROSS JOIN "overall_total" o
)
-- Step 5: Select top 15 (including ties) and compute percentage
SELECT 
    "station_id",
    "total_trips",
    ROUND(("total_trips" / "overall_trips") * 100, 4) AS "percentage",
    ROUND("avg_duration", 4) AS "avg_duration_minutes"
FROM "ranked"
WHERE "rank" <= 15
ORDER BY "rank";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Join active stations with their starting trips
active_station_trips AS (
    SELECT 
        s."station_id",
        t."duration_minutes"
    FROM "AUSTIN"."AUSTIN_BIKESHARE"."BIKESHARE_STATIONS" s
    INNER JOIN "AUSTIN"."AUSTIN_BIKESHARE"."BIKESHARE_TRIPS" t
        ON s."station_id" = t."start_station_id"
    WHERE LOWER(s."status") = 'active'
),

-- Step 2: Aggregate per station: total trips and avg duration
station_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        "station_id",
        COUNT(*) AS "total_trips",
        ROUND(AVG("duration_minutes"), 4) AS "avg_duration_minutes"
    FROM active_station_trips
    GROUP BY "station_id"
),

-- Step 3: Compute the grand total of trips from all active stations
overall_total AS (
    SELECT SUM("total_trips") AS "grand_total"
    FROM station_stats
),

-- Step 4: Rank stations by total trips (DENSE_RANK includes ties)
ranked_stations AS (
    SELECT 
        "station_id",
        "total_trips",
        "avg_duration_minutes",
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY "total_trips" DESC) AS "rank"
    FROM station_stats
)

-- Step 5: Final selection of top 15 stations (including ties)
SELECT 
    "station_id",
    "total_trips",
    ROUND("total_trips" * 100.0 / (SELECT "grand_total" FROM overall_total), 4) AS "percentage",
    "avg_duration_minutes"
FROM ranked_stations
WHERE "rank" <= 15
ORDER BY "rank";
```
</details>

```sql
WITH

    SELECT
      category,

    FROM `bigquery-public-data.bbc_news.fulltext`
    GROUP BY category
  ),
  education_counts AS (

      COUNT(*) AS education_articles
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.bbc_news.fulltext`
    WHERE
      LOWER(body) LIKE '%education%'
      OR LOWER(title) LIKE '%education%'
    GROUP BY category
  )
SELECT
  ct.category,
  ct.total_articles,
  ROUND(IFNULL(ec.education_articles, 0) * 100.0 / ct.total_articles, 4) AS percentage_mention_education
FROM category_totals ct
LEFT JOIN education_counts ec
  ON ct.category = ec.category
ORDER BY ct.category;
```

```sql
    COUNT(*) AS total_articles,
    COUNTIF(LOWER(title) LIKE '%education%' OR LOWER(body) LIKE '%education%') AS education_articles
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.bbc_news.fulltext` TABLESAMPLE SYSTEM (1 PERCENT)
  GROUP BY category
)
SELECT
  category,
  total_articles,
  ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(education_articles, total_articles) * 100, 4) AS education_percentage
FROM category_stats
ORDER BY total_articles DESC;
```

### 38. sf_bq423 (DB: `GOOGLE_ADS`)
**Question**: Between January 1, 2023, and January 1, 2024, which image-type advertisement on the topic of Health, published by a verified advertiser located in Cyprus, was shown in Croatia, has times_shown_availability_date as NULL (meaning the times shown data is available), utilized demographic information, geo-location targeting, contextual signals, customer lists, and topics of interest without any of these selection methods being unused, and additionally had its first shown date strictly after January 1, 2023, and last shown date strictly before January 1, 2024? Among such ads, provide the page URL of the one with the highest upper bound of times shown.

**Status**: Baseline ✅ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

| creative_page_url                                                                                    |
|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| https://adstransparency.google.com/advertiser/AR03023670995157254145/creative/CR14007923720077705217 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

| creative_page_url                                                                                    |
|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| https://adstransparency.google.com/advertiser/AR03023670995157254145/creative/CR14007923720077705217 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

| creative_page_url                                                                                    |
|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| https://adstransparency.google.com/advertiser/AR03023670995157254145/creative/CR14007923720077705217 |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: Filter ads based on core criteria
filtered_ads AS (
    SELECT 
        cs."creative_page_url",
        cs."region_stats",
        cs."audience_selection_approach_info"
    FROM "GOOGLE_ADS"."GOOGLE_ADS_TRANSPARENCY_CENTER"."CREATIVE_STATS" cs
    WHERE 
        cs."ad_format_type" = 'IMAGE'
        AND cs."topic" = 'Health'
        AND cs."advertiser_verification_status" = 'VERIFIED'
        AND cs."advertiser_location" = 'CY'
        -- All five audience selection methods must be used (not 'CRITERIA_UNUSED')
        AND cs."audience_selection_approach_info":"demographic_info"::STRING != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
        AND cs."audience_selection_approach_info":"geo_location"::STRING != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
        AND cs."audience_selection_approach_info":"contextual_signals"::STRING != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
        AND cs."audience_selection_approach_info":"customer_lists"::STRING != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
        AND cs."audience_selection_approach_info":"topics_of_interest"::STRING != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
),
-- Step 2: Unnest region_stats and restrict to Croatia (HR)
croatia_region AS (
    SELECT 
        fa."creative_page_url",
        reg.value:"first_shown"::DATE AS "first_shown",
        reg.value:"last_shown"::DATE AS "last_shown",
        reg.value:"times_shown_availability_date"::DATE AS "times_shown_availability_date",
        reg.value:"times_shown_upper_bound"::NUMBER AS "times_shown_upper_bound"
    FROM filtered_ads fa,
         LATERAL FLATTEN(input => fa."region_stats") reg
    WHERE reg.value:"region_code"::STRING = 'HR'
)
-- Step 3: Apply remaining filters, sort by upper bound descending, and pick top URL
SELECT 
    cr."creative_page_url"
FROM croatia_region cr
WHERE 
    cr."times_shown_availability_date" IS NULL          -- times shown data is available
    AND cr."first_shown" > '2023-01-01'                 -- strictly after Jan 1, 2023
    AND cr."last_shown" < '2024-01-01'                  -- strictly before Jan 1, 2024
ORDER BY cr."times_shown_upper_bound" DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH "flattened" AS (
    SELECT 
        cs."creative_page_url",
        cs."ad_format_type",
        cs."topic",
        cs."advertiser_verification_status",
        cs."advertiser_location",
        cs."audience_selection_approach_info",
        r.value AS "region_entry"
    FROM GOOGLE_ADS.GOOGLE_ADS_TRANSPARENCY_CENTER.CREATIVE_STATS cs,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => cs."region_stats") r
)
SELECT 
    f."creative_page_url"
FROM "flattened" f
WHERE f."ad_format_type" = 'IMAGE'
  AND f."topic" = 'Health'
  AND f."advertiser_verification_status" = 'VERIFIED'
  AND f."advertiser_location" = 'CY'
  AND f."region_entry":"region_code"::TEXT = 'HR'
  AND f."region_entry":"times_shown_availability_date" IS NULL
  AND f."region_entry":"first_shown"::DATE > '2023-01-01'
  AND f."region_entry":"last_shown"::DATE < '2024-01-01'
  AND f."audience_selection_approach_info":"demographic_info"::TEXT != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
  AND f."audience_selection_approach_info":"geo_location"::TEXT != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
  AND f."audience_selection_approach_info":"contextual_signals"::TEXT != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
  AND f."audience_selection_approach_info":"customer_lists"::TEXT != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
  AND f."audience_selection_approach_info":"topics_of_interest"::TEXT != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
ORDER BY f."region_entry":"times_shown_upper_bound"::INTEGER DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Total 2022 production (bushels for corn) for each U.S. state.
-- Includes corn from 'FIELD CROPS' (unit = BU) and mushrooms from 'HORTICULTURE'.
-- Uses conditional aggregation to yield one row per state with both totals.

SELECT
  state_name,
  ROUND(SUM(CASE
      WHEN commodity_desc = 'CORN'
       AND group_desc = 'FIELD CROPS'
       AND unit_desc = 'BU'
       THEN value
    END), 4) AS corn_production_bu,
  ROUND(SUM(CASE
      WHEN commodity_desc = 'MUSHROOMS'
       AND group_desc = 'HORTICULTURE'
       THEN value
    END), 4) AS mushroom_production
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.usda_nass_agriculture.crops`
WHERE
  year = 2022
  AND statisticcat_desc = 'PRODUCTION'
  AND agg_level_desc = 'STATE'
  AND value IS NOT NULL
  AND (
    (commodity_desc = 'CORN' AND group_desc = 'FIELD CROPS' AND unit_desc = 'BU')
    OR (commodity_desc = 'MUSHROOMS' AND group_desc = 'HORTICULTURE')
  )
GROUP BY
  state_name
ORDER BY
  state_name;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH corn_data AS (
  -- Aggregate 2022 corn production from FIELD CROPS, measured in bushels (BU)
  SELECT 
    state_name,
    ROUND(SUM(value), 4) AS corn_production
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.usda_nass_agriculture.crops`
  WHERE year = 2022
    AND LOWER(commodity_desc) = 'corn'
    AND group_desc = 'FIELD CROPS'
    AND statisticcat_desc = 'PRODUCTION'
    AND agg_level_desc = 'STATE'
    AND unit_desc = 'BU'
    AND value IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY state_name
),
mushroom_data AS (
  -- Aggregate 2022 mushroom production from HORTICULTURE
  SELECT 
    state_name,
    ROUND(SUM(value), 4) AS mushroom_production
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.usda_nass_agriculture.crops`
  WHERE year = 2022
    AND LOWER(commodity_desc) = 'mushrooms'
    AND group_desc = 'HORTICULTURE'
    AND statisticcat_desc = 'PRODUCTION'
    AND agg_level_desc = 'STATE'
    AND value IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY state_name
)
-- FULL OUTER JOIN preserves all states from both datasets
SELECT 
  COALESCE(c.state_name, m.state_name) AS state_name,
  c.corn_production,
  m.mushroom_production
FROM corn_data c
FULL OUTER JOIN mushroom_data m
  ON c.state_name = m.state_name
ORDER BY state_name;
```
</details>

```sql
-- Step 1: Find the forum ID for "General"
WITH general_forum AS (
    SELECT "Id"
    FROM META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMS
    WHERE LOWER("Title") = 'general'
),

-- Step 2: Find all sub-forums under General (forums whose ParentForumId = General's Id)
sub_forums AS (
    SELECT f."Id" AS "sub_forum_id",
           f."Title" AS "sub_forum_title"
    FROM META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMS f
    JOIN general_forum g ON f."ParentForumId" = g."Id"
),

-- Step 3: Get the earliest five topics in those sub-forums
topics AS (
    SELECT t."Id" AS "topic_id",
           t."CreationDate",
           t."Title" AS "topic_title",
           t."ForumId",
           t."TotalViews"
    FROM META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMTOPICS t
    JOIN sub_forums s ON t."ForumId" = s."sub_forum_id"
    ORDER BY t."CreationDate" ASC
    LIMIT 5
),

-- Step 4: Compute per-topic message counts and distinct users
message_stats AS (
    SELECT m."ForumTopicId",
           COUNT(*) AS "reply_count",
           COUNT(DISTINCT m."PostUserId") AS "distinct_user_replies_count"
    FROM META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMMESSAGES m
    JOIN topics t ON m."ForumTopicId" = t."topic_id"
    GROUP BY m."ForumTopicId"
),

-- Step 5: Compute total upvotes per topic (each vote is an upvote)
vote_stats AS (
    SELECT m."ForumTopicId",
           COUNT(v."Id") AS "total_upvotes"
    FROM META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMMESSAGES m
    JOIN META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMMESSAGEVOTES v
         ON m."Id" = v."ForumMessageId"
    JOIN topics t ON m."ForumTopicId" = t."topic_id"
    GROUP BY m."ForumTopicId"
)

-- Step 6: Final selection with coalesce for missing values
SELECT
    t."CreationDate",
    t."topic_title" AS "Title",
    s."sub_forum_title" AS "Parent Forum Title",
    COALESCE(ms."reply_count", 0) AS "Reply count",
    COALESCE(ms."distinct_user_replies_count", 0) AS "Distinct user replies count",
    COALESCE(vs."total_upvotes", 0) AS "Total upvotes",
    COALESCE(t."TotalViews", 0) AS "Total views"
FROM topics t
LEFT JOIN sub_forums s ON t."ForumId" = s."sub_forum_id"
LEFT JOIN message_stats ms ON t."topic_id" = ms."ForumTopicId"
LEFT JOIN vote_stats vs ON t."topic_id" = vs."ForumTopicId"
ORDER BY t."CreationDate" ASC;
```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
    "general_forum" AS (
        -- Step 1: Find the Id of the parent forum titled 'General'
        SELECT "Id"
        FROM META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMS
        WHERE "Title" = 'General'
    ),
    "sub_forums" AS (
        -- Step 2: Find all sub-forums under 'General' (where ParentForumId matches any General Id)
        SELECT "Id"
        FROM META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMS
        WHERE "ParentForumId" IN (SELECT "Id" FROM "general_forum")
    ),
    "topic_base" AS (
        -- Step 3: Get all topics that belong to any sub-forum under General
        SELECT
            ft."Id" AS "topic_id",
            ft."CreationDate",
            ft."Title" AS "topic_title",
            ft."TotalViews",
            ft."ForumId"
        FROM META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMTOPICS ft
        WHERE ft."ForumId" IN (SELECT "Id" FROM "sub_forums")
    ),
    "message_aggregates" AS (
        -- Step 4 & 5: Count total messages (reply count) and distinct users per topic
        SELECT
            fm."ForumTopicId",
            COUNT(fm."Id") AS "reply_count",
            COUNT(DISTINCT fm."PostUserId") AS "distinct_user_replies_count"
        FROM META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMMESSAGES fm
        WHERE fm."ForumTopicId" IN (SELECT "topic_id" FROM "topic_base")
        GROUP BY fm."ForumTopicId"
    ),
    "upvote_aggregates" AS (
        -- Step 6: Count total upvotes on all messages within each topic
        SELECT
            fm."ForumTopicId",
            COUNT(fmv."Id") AS "total_upvotes"
        FROM META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMMESSAGES fm
        LEFT JOIN META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMMESSAGEVOTES fmv
            ON fm."Id" = fmv."ForumMessageId"
        WHERE fm."ForumTopicId" IN (SELECT "topic_id" FROM "topic_base")
        GROUP BY fm."ForumTopicId"
    )
-- Step 7: Assemble final output with earliest 5 topics
SELECT
    TO_TIMESTAMP(tb."CreationDate" / 1000000) AS "CreationDate",
    tb."topic_title" AS "Title",
    f."Title" AS "ParentForumTitle",
    COALESCE(ma."reply_count", 0) AS "ReplyCount",
    COALESCE(ma."distinct_user_replies_count", 0) AS "DistinctUserRepliesCount",
    COALESCE(ua."total_upvotes", 0) AS "TotalUpvotes",
    tb."TotalViews"
FROM "topic_base" tb
LEFT JOIN "message_aggregates" ma
    ON tb."topic_id" = ma."ForumTopicId"
LEFT JOIN "upvote_aggregates" ua
    ON tb."topic_id" = ua."ForumTopicId"
JOIN META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMS f
    ON tb."ForumId" = f."Id"
ORDER BY tb."CreationDate" ASC
LIMIT 5;
```

### 42. bq402 (DB: `ecommerce`)
**Question**: Calculate the conversion rate from unique visitors to purchasers by using data exclusively from the `web_analytics` table in the `data-to-insights.ecommerce` dataset. A visitor is defined as a unique `fullVisitorId` present in the table, while a purchaser is a visitor who has at least one transaction recorded (`totals.transactions` is not null). The conversion rate is computed by dividing the number of unique purchasers by the total number of unique visitors. Additionally, calculate the average number of transactions per purchaser, considering only those visitors who have made at least one transaction.

**Status**: Baseline ✅ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

**OR**

|   TOTAL_UNIQUE_VISITORS |   UNIQUE_PURCHASERS |   TOTAL_TRANSACTIONS |   CONVERSION_RATE_PERCENTAGE |   AVG_TRANSACTIONS_PER_PURCHASER |
|------------------------:|--------------------:|---------------------:|-----------------------------:|---------------------------------:|
|                  741721 |               20015 |                24901 |                          2.7 |                             1.24 |

</details>

|   unique_visitors |   unique_purchasers |   conversion_rate |   avg_transactions_per_purchaser |
|------------------:|--------------------:|------------------:|---------------------------------:|
|            741721 |               20015 |             0.027 |                           1.2441 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

|   conversion_rate |   avg_transactions_per_purchaser |
|------------------:|---------------------------------:|
|             0.027 |                           1.2441 |

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Calculate conversion rate and average transactions per purchaser
-- from the web_analytics table only
WITH visitor_stats AS (
  SELECT
    COUNT(DISTINCT fullVisitorId) AS total_visitors,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN totals.transactions IS NOT NULL THEN fullVisitorId END) AS total_purchasers,
    SUM(CASE WHEN totals.transactions IS NOT NULL THEN totals.transactions ELSE 0 END) AS total_transactions
  FROM `data-to-insights.ecommerce.web_analytics`
)
SELECT
  ROUND(total_purchasers / total_visitors, 4) AS conversion_rate,
  ROUND(total_transactions / total_purchasers, 4) AS avg_transactions_per_purchaser
FROM visitor_stats;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
  -- Total unique visitors across all sessions
  visitor_stats AS (
    SELECT
      COUNT(DISTINCT fullVisitorId) AS total_visitors
    FROM `data-to-insights.ecommerce.web_analytics`
  ),

  -- Purchasers: visitors with at least one transaction,
  -- along with their total transaction count across all sessions
  purchaser_stats AS (
    SELECT
      fullVisitorId,
      SUM(totals.transactions) AS total_transactions_per_visitor
    FROM `data-to-insights.ecommerce.web_analytics`
    WHERE totals.transactions IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY fullVisitorId
  ),

  -- Aggregate purchaser-level data
  aggregated AS (
    SELECT
      (SELECT total_visitors FROM visitor_stats) AS unique_visitors,
      COUNT(DISTINCT fullVisitorId)                AS unique_purchasers,
      AVG(total_transactions_per_visitor)          AS avg_transactions_per_purchaser
    FROM purchaser_stats
  )

-- Final output: conversion rate and average transactions per purchaser
SELECT
  unique_visitors,
  unique_purchasers,
  ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(unique_purchasers, unique_visitors), 4) AS conversion_rate,
  ROUND(avg_transactions_per_purchaser, 4)                  AS avg_transactions_per_purchaser
FROM aggregated;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
    -- Step 1: Identify race codes that describe 'black' (case-insensitive)
    black_race_codes AS (
        SELECT "Code"
        FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."RACE"
        WHERE LOWER("Description") LIKE '%black%'
    ),

    -- Step 2: Identify ICD-10 codes whose description contains 'vehicle'
    vehicle_icd_codes AS (
        SELECT "Code"
        FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."ICD10CODE"
        WHERE LOWER("Description") LIKE '%vehicle%'
    ),

    -- Step 3: Identify ICD-10 codes whose description contains 'firearm'
    firearm_icd_codes AS (
        SELECT "Code"
        FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."ICD10CODE"
        WHERE LOWER("Description") LIKE '%firearm%'
    ),

    -- Step 4: Find all death records associated with at least one vehicle ICD code
    vehicle_death_records AS (
        SELECT DISTINCT "DeathRecordId"
        FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."ENTITYAXISCONDITIONS"
        WHERE "Icd10Code" IN (SELECT "Code" FROM vehicle_icd_codes)
    ),

    -- Step 5: Find all death records associated with at least one firearm ICD code
    firearm_death_records AS (
        SELECT DISTINCT "DeathRecordId"
        FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."ENTITYAXISCONDITIONS"
        WHERE "Icd10Code" IN (SELECT "Code" FROM firearm_icd_codes)
    ),

    -- Step 6: Combine both causes into a single list with a cause label
    all_death_ids AS (
        SELECT "DeathRecordId", 'Vehicle' AS "cause"
        FROM vehicle_death_records
        UNION ALL
        SELECT "DeathRecordId", 'Firearm' AS "cause"
        FROM firearm_death_records
    ),

    -- Step 7: Attach age and race information, restrict to ages 12-18 (in years)
    deaths_with_cause AS (
        SELECT
            d."Id",
            d."Age",
            d."Race",
            a."cause"
        FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."DEATHRECORDS" d
        INNER JOIN all_death_ids a ON d."Id" = a."DeathRecordId"
        WHERE d."AgeType" = 1           -- Age is in years
          AND d."Age" BETWEEN 12 AND 18
    ),

    -- Step 8: Generate all ages 12 through 18 inclusive
    age_series AS (
        SELECT 12 AS "age"
        UNION ALL SELECT 13
        UNION ALL SELECT 14
        UNION ALL SELECT 15
        UNION ALL SELECT 16
        UNION ALL SELECT 17
        UNION ALL SELECT 18
    ),

    -- Step 9: Create all combinations of age and cause (Vehicle / Firearm)
    cause_list AS (
        SELECT 'Vehicle' AS "cause"
        UNION ALL
        SELECT 'Firearm'
    ),
    age_cause_grid AS (
        SELECT a."age", c."cause"
        FROM age_series a
        CROSS JOIN cause_list c
    ),

    -- Step 10: Aggregate counts per age and cause
    aggregated AS (
        SELECT
            d."Age" AS "age",
            d."cause",
            COUNT(DISTINCT d."Id") AS "total_deaths",
            COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN d."Race" IN (SELECT "Code" FROM black_race_codes)
                                THEN d."Id" END) AS "black_deaths"
        FROM deaths_with_cause d
        GROUP BY d."Age", d."cause"
    )

-- Step 11: Final output with missing combinations filled as zero
SELECT
    g."age",
    g."cause",
    COALESCE(a."total_deaths", 0) AS "total_deaths",
    COALESCE(a."black_deaths", 0) AS "black_deaths"
FROM age_cause_grid g
LEFT JOIN aggregated a ON g."age" = a."age" AND g."cause" = a."cause"
ORDER BY g."age", g."cause";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH vehicle_icd_codes AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT "Code"
    FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."ICD10CODE"
    WHERE LOWER("Description") LIKE '%vehicle%'
),
firearm_icd_codes AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT "Code"
    FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."ICD10CODE"
    WHERE LOWER("Description") LIKE '%firearm%'
),
vehicle_death_ids AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT eac."DeathRecordId"
    FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."ENTITYAXISCONDITIONS" eac
    INNER JOIN vehicle_icd_codes vic ON eac."Icd10Code" = vic."Code"
),
firearm_death_ids AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT eac."DeathRecordId"
    FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."ENTITYAXISCONDITIONS" eac
    INNER JOIN firearm_icd_codes fic ON eac."Icd10Code" = fic."Code"
),
vehicle_stats AS (
    SELECT
        dr."Age",
        COUNT(DISTINCT dr."Id") AS total_deaths,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN LOWER(r."Description") LIKE '%black%' THEN dr."Id" END) AS black_deaths
    FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."DEATHRECORDS" dr
    INNER JOIN vehicle_death_ids vdi ON dr."Id" = vdi."DeathRecordId"
    LEFT JOIN "DEATH"."DEATH"."RACE" r ON dr."Race" = r."Code"
    WHERE dr."AgeType" = 1
      AND dr."Age" BETWEEN 12 AND 18
    GROUP BY dr."Age"
),
firearm_stats AS (
    SELECT
        dr."Age",
        COUNT(DISTINCT dr."Id") AS total_deaths,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN LOWER(r."Description") LIKE '%black%' THEN dr."Id" END) AS black_deaths
    FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."DEATHRECORDS" dr
    INNER JOIN firearm_death_ids fdi ON dr."Id" = fdi."DeathRecordId"
    LEFT JOIN "DEATH"."DEATH"."RACE" r ON dr."Race" = r."Code"
    WHERE dr."AgeType" = 1
      AND dr."Age" BETWEEN 12 AND 18
    GROUP BY dr."Age"
)
SELECT
    "Age",
    'vehicle' AS cause,
    total_deaths,
    black_deaths
FROM vehicle_stats
UNION ALL
SELECT
    "Age",
    'firearm' AS cause,
    total_deaths,
    black_deaths
FROM firearm_stats
ORDER BY "Age", cause;
```
</details>

### 44. local019 (DB: `WWE`)
**Question**: For the NXT title that had the shortest match (excluding titles with "title change"), what were the names of the two wrestlers involved?

**Status**: Baseline ✅ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

|:--------------|:-------------|
| Bron Breakker | Duke Hudson  |

<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

|:--------------|:-------------|
| Bron Breakker | Duke Hudson  |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Find the NXT championship belt with the shortest match (excluding title changes),
-- then retrieve the names of the winner and loser from that match.

WITH
  -- Step 1: Get the promotion ID for NXT
  nxt_promotion AS (
    SELECT id
    FROM "Promotions"
    WHERE name = 'NXT'
  ),
  -- Step 2: Filter matches that belong to NXT events, are for an NXT belt,
  --         have a non‑empty duration, and are not title changes
  nxt_matches AS (
    SELECT m.id, m.winner_id, m.loser_id, m.duration, m.title_id, m.title_change
    FROM "Matches" m
    JOIN "Cards" c ON m.card_id = c.id
    JOIN nxt_promotion p ON c.promotion_id = p.id
    JOIN "Belts" b ON m.title_id = b.id
    WHERE m.title_change = 0                     -- exclude title changes
      AND m.duration != ''                       -- exclude missing durations
      AND LOWER(b.name) LIKE '%nxt%'            -- only NXT championships
  ),
  -- Step 3: Convert the duration (MM:SS) to total seconds for comparison
  match_durations AS (
    SELECT m.*,
           CAST(SUBSTR(m.duration, 1, INSTR(m.duration, ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 60 +
           CAST(SUBSTR(m.duration, INSTR(m.duration, ':') + 1) AS INTEGER) AS duration_seconds
    FROM nxt_matches m
  ),
  -- Step 4: Pick the match with the smallest duration (shortest)
  shortest_match AS (
    SELECT * FROM match_durations
    ORDER BY duration_seconds ASC
    LIMIT 1
  )
-- Step 5: Retrieve the names of the two wrestlers involved
SELECT w1.name AS winner_name,
       w2.name AS loser_name
FROM shortest_match sm
JOIN "Wrestlers" w1 ON sm.winner_id = w1.id
JOIN "Wrestlers" w2 ON sm.loser_id = w2.id;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Find the NXT promotion ID
WITH nxt_promotion AS (
    SELECT id
    FROM Promotions
    WHERE name = 'NXT'
),

-- Step 2: Find all card IDs belonging to NXT shows
nxt_cards AS (
    SELECT id
    FROM Cards
    WHERE promotion_id IN (SELECT id FROM nxt_promotion)
),

-- Step 3: Get all NXT title matches (excluding title changes) with parsed durations
nxt_title_matches AS (
    SELECT 
        m.id AS match_id,
        m.winner_id,
        m.loser_id,
        b.name AS title_name,
        -- Convert duration from 'MM:SS' format to total seconds
        CAST(SUBSTR(m.duration, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) * 60 + 
        CAST(SUBSTR(m.duration, 4, 2) AS INTEGER) AS duration_seconds
    FROM Matches m
    INNER JOIN Cards c ON m.card_id = c.id
    INNER JOIN Belts b ON m.title_id = b.id
    WHERE c.id IN (SELECT id FROM nxt_cards)
      AND m.title_change = 0          -- Exclude matches where title changed hands
      AND m.duration != ''             -- Only consider matches with recorded duration
      AND b.name LIKE '%NXT%'         -- Only consider NXT-branded titles
),

-- Step 4: Identify the match with the shortest duration
shortest_match AS (
    SELECT 
        winner_id,
        loser_id
    FROM nxt_title_matches
    ORDER BY duration_seconds ASC
    LIMIT 1
)

-- Step 5: Retrieve the names of the two wrestlers involved
SELECT 
    w_winner.name AS winner_name,
    w_loser.name AS loser_name
FROM shortest_match sm
INNER JOIN Wrestlers w_winner ON CAST(sm.winner_id AS INTEGER) = w_winner.id
INNER JOIN Wrestlers w_loser ON CAST(sm.loser_id AS INTEGER) = w_loser.id;
```
</details>

### 45. local031 (DB: `Brazilian_E_Commerce`)
**Question**: What is the highest monthly delivered orders volume in the year with the lowest annual delivered orders volume among 2016, 2017, and 2018?

**Status**: Baseline ✅ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

|------------------------------------------:|

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Extract year and month from delivery dates for delivered orders in 2016-2018
WITH delivered_orders AS (
    SELECT 
        "order_id",
        CAST(strftime('%Y', "order_delivered_customer_date") AS INTEGER) AS "year",
        CAST(strftime('%m', "order_delivered_customer_date") AS INTEGER) AS "month"
    FROM "olist_orders"
    WHERE "order_status" = 'delivered'
      AND "order_delivered_customer_date" IS NOT NULL
      AND CAST(strftime('%Y', "order_delivered_customer_date") AS INTEGER) IN (2016, 2017, 2018)
),

-- Step 2: Compute annual delivered orders volume
annual_volumes AS (
    SELECT 
        "year",
        COUNT("order_id") AS "annual_volume"
    FROM delivered_orders
    GROUP BY "year"
),

-- Step 3: Identify the year with the lowest annual volume
lowest_year AS (
    SELECT "year"
    FROM annual_volumes
    ORDER BY "annual_volume" ASC
    LIMIT 1
),

-- Step 4: Compute monthly volumes for that year
monthly_volumes AS (
    SELECT 
        "month",
        COUNT("order_id") AS "monthly_volume"
    FROM delivered_orders
    WHERE "year" = (SELECT "year" FROM lowest_year)
    GROUP BY "month"
)

-- Step 5: Get the highest monthly volume
SELECT MAX("monthly_volume") AS "highest_monthly_delivered_orders_volume"
FROM monthly_volumes;
```
</details>

<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Extract year and month for delivered orders in 2016-2018
delivered_orders AS (
    SELECT 
        order_id,
        SUBSTR(order_delivered_customer_date, 1, 4) AS year,
        SUBSTR(order_delivered_customer_date, 6, 2) AS month
    FROM olist_orders
    WHERE order_status = 'delivered'
      AND order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
      AND SUBSTR(order_delivered_customer_date, 1, 4) IN ('2016', '2017', '2018')
),
-- Count annual delivered orders volume
annual_volumes AS (
    SELECT 
        year,
        COUNT(*) AS annual_count
    FROM delivered_orders
    GROUP BY year
),
-- Identify the year with the lowest annual volume
lowest_volume_year AS (
    SELECT year
    FROM annual_volumes
    ORDER BY annual_count ASC
    LIMIT 1
),
-- Count monthly delivered orders for that specific year
monthly_volumes AS (
    SELECT 
        year,
        month,
        COUNT(*) AS monthly_count
    FROM delivered_orders
    WHERE year = (SELECT year FROM lowest_volume_year)
    GROUP BY year, month
)
-- Return the highest monthly volume
SELECT MAX(monthly_count) AS highest_monthly_delivered_orders_volume
FROM monthly_volumes;
```
</details>

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify films matching all criteria: English language, Children category, rating G or PG, length <= 120, release year between 2000 and 2010.
-- Step 2: Join film_actor and actor to count appearances per actor.
-- Step 3: Order by count descending and take the top actor. Provide full name.

WITH qualified_films AS (
    SELECT f.film_id
    FROM "film" f
    JOIN "language" l ON f.language_id = l.language_id
    JOIN "film_category" fc ON f.film_id = fc.film_id
    JOIN "category" c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id
    WHERE l.name = 'English'
      AND c.name = 'Children'
      AND f.rating IN ('G', 'PG')
      AND f.length <= 120
      AND CAST(f.release_year AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 2000 AND 2010
),
actor_counts AS (
    SELECT fa.actor_id,
           COUNT(*) AS film_count
    FROM "film_actor" fa
    JOIN qualified_films qf ON fa.film_id = qf.film_id
    GROUP BY fa.actor_id
)
SELECT a.first_name || ' ' || a.last_name AS actor_full_name
FROM actor_counts ac
JOIN "actor" a ON ac.actor_id = a.actor_id
ORDER BY ac.film_count DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
    -- Identify the English language ID from the language lookup table
    english_language AS (
        SELECT language_id 
        FROM language 
        WHERE name = 'English'
    ),
    -- Films satisfying: English language, G or PG rating, ≤120 minutes, released 2000-2010
    base_films AS (
        SELECT f.film_id
        FROM film f
        CROSS JOIN english_language el
        WHERE f.language_id = el.language_id
          AND f.rating IN ('G', 'PG')
          AND f.length <= 120
          AND CAST(f.release_year AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 2000 AND 2010
    ),
    -- Films belonging to the 'Children' category
    children_films AS (
        SELECT fc.film_id
        FROM film_category fc
        JOIN category c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id
        WHERE c.name = 'Children'
    ),
    -- Intersection: English-language children's films meeting all criteria
    qualified_films AS (
        SELECT bf.film_id
        FROM base_films bf
        INNER JOIN children_films cf ON bf.film_id = cf.film_id
    ),
    -- Count how many qualified films each actor appeared in
    actor_appearances AS (
        SELECT fa.actor_id, COUNT(*) AS appearance_count
        FROM film_actor fa
        INNER JOIN qualified_films qf ON fa.film_id = qf.film_id
        GROUP BY fa.actor_id
    ),
    -- Select the actor with the highest appearance count
    top_actor AS (
        SELECT actor_id
        FROM actor_appearances
        ORDER BY appearance_count DESC
        LIMIT 1
    )
-- Return the full name of the top actor
SELECT a.first_name || ' ' || a.last_name AS actor_full_name
FROM actor a
INNER JOIN top_actor ta ON a.actor_id = ta.actor_id;
```
</details>

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify unicorn companies with their founding year and industry
WITH unicorn_companies AS (
    SELECT
        cd.company_id,
        cd.date_joined,
        ci.industry
    FROM companies_dates cd
    JOIN companies_funding cf ON cd.company_id = cf.company_id
    JOIN companies_industries ci ON cd.company_id = ci.company_id
    WHERE cf.valuation >= 1000000000  -- Unicorn threshold: $1B
      AND strftime('%Y', cd.date_joined) BETWEEN '2019' AND '2021'
),
-- Step 2: Count new unicorns per industry per year
counts_per_industry_year AS (
    SELECT
        industry,
        strftime('%Y', date_joined) AS year,
        COUNT(DISTINCT company_id) AS cnt
    FROM unicorn_companies
    GROUP BY industry, year
),
-- Step 3: Sum counts across 2019-2021 for each industry to find the top
total_counts_per_industry AS (
    SELECT
        industry,
        SUM(cnt) AS total_count
    FROM counts_per_industry_year
    GROUP BY industry
),
-- Step 4: Identify the top industry (highest total count; if tie, pick alphabetically)
top_industry AS (
    SELECT industry
    FROM total_counts_per_industry
    ORDER BY total_count DESC, industry ASC
    LIMIT 1
)
-- Step 5: Compute average new unicorns per year for the top industry (2019-2021)
SELECT ROUND(SUM(cnt) / 3.0, 4) AS avg_new_unicorns_per_year
FROM counts_per_industry_year
WHERE industry = (SELECT industry FROM top_industry)
  AND year BETWEEN '2019' AND '2021';
```

```sql
WITH unicorn_yearly AS (
    SELECT 
        ci.industry,
        SUBSTR(cd.date_joined, 1, 4) AS year,
        COUNT(DISTINCT cd.company_id) AS cnt
    FROM companies_dates cd
    JOIN companies_industries ci ON cd.company_id = ci.company_id
    WHERE SUBSTR(cd.date_joined, 1, 4) BETWEEN '2019' AND '2021'
    GROUP BY ci.industry, SUBSTR(cd.date_joined, 1, 4)
),
industry_total AS (
    SELECT 
        industry,
        SUM(cnt) AS total_unicorns,
        COUNT(DISTINCT year) AS num_years
    FROM unicorn_yearly
    GROUP BY industry
),
top_industry AS (
    SELECT industry
    FROM industry_total
    ORDER BY total_unicorns DESC NULLS LAST
    LIMIT 1
)
SELECT 
    ROUND(AVG(cnt), 4) AS avg_new_unicorns_per_year
FROM unicorn_yearly
WHERE industry IN (SELECT industry FROM top_industry);
```

### 49. local050 (DB: `complex_oracle`)
**Question**: What is the median of the average monthly projected sales in USD for France in 2021, calculated by using the monthly sales data from 2019 and 2020 (filtered by promo_total_id=1 and channel_total_id=1), applying the growth rate from 2019 to 2020 to project 2021, converting to USD based on the currency table, and then determining the monthly averages before finding their median?

**Status**: Baseline ✅ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

|   OUTPUT |
|---------:|
|   2552.7 |

**OR**

|   median_monthly_avg_projected_sales_usd |
|-----------------------------------------:|
|                                  2077.39 |

**OR**

|   median_avg_monthly_projected_sales_usd_2021 |
|----------------------------------------------:|
|                                       2014.66 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

|   median_val |
|-------------:|
|       2552.7 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

|   median_of_monthly_avg_projected_sales_usd |
|--------------------------------------------:|
|                                     2552.69 |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Filter sales for France, promo_total_id=1, channel_total_id=1, years 2019/2020
WITH filtered_sales AS (
    SELECT
        s."prod_id",
        t."calendar_month_number" AS "month",
        t."calendar_year" AS "year",
        s."amount_sold"
    FROM "sales" AS s
    JOIN "times" AS t ON s."time_id" = t."time_id"
    JOIN "customers" AS c ON s."cust_id" = c."cust_id"
    JOIN "countries" AS co ON c."country_id" = co."country_id"
    JOIN "promotions" AS p ON s."promo_id" = p."promo_id"
    JOIN "channels" AS ch ON s."channel_id" = ch."channel_id"
    WHERE LOWER(co."country_name") = LOWER('France')
      AND p."promo_total_id" = 1
      AND ch."channel_total_id" = 1
      AND t."calendar_year" IN (2019, 2020)
),
-- Step 2: Aggregate sales per product, month, year
agg_sales AS (
    SELECT
        "prod_id",
        "month",
        "year",
        SUM("amount_sold") AS "total_sales"
    FROM filtered_sales
    GROUP BY "prod_id", "month", "year"
),
-- Step 3: Pivot to get sales for 2019 and 2020 per product-month
pivot_sales AS (
    SELECT
        "prod_id",
        "month",
        MAX(CASE WHEN "year" = 2019 THEN "total_sales" END) AS "sales_2019",
        MAX(CASE WHEN "year" = 2020 THEN "total_sales" END) AS "sales_2020"
    FROM agg_sales
    GROUP BY "prod_id", "month"
),
-- Step 4: Project 2021 sales using the given growth formula
projected AS (
    SELECT
        "prod_id",
        "month",
        CASE
            WHEN "sales_2019" IS NOT NULL AND "sales_2019" > 0
            THEN ((("sales_2020" - "sales_2019") / "sales_2019") * "sales_2020") + "sales_2020"
            ELSE NULL
        END AS "projected_sales_local"
    FROM pivot_sales
),
-- Step 5: Convert to USD using currency rates for France, year=2021
projected_usd AS (
    SELECT
        pr."prod_id",
        pr."month",
        ROUND(pr."projected_sales_local" * COALESCE(cr."to_us", 1), 2) AS "projected_sales_usd"
    FROM projected AS pr
    LEFT JOIN "currency" AS cr
        ON cr."month" = pr."month"
        AND cr."year" = 2021
        AND LOWER(cr."country") = LOWER('France')
    WHERE pr."projected_sales_local" IS NOT NULL  -- exclude invalid projections (division by zero)
),
-- Step 6: Compute monthly averages across all products
monthly_avg AS (
    SELECT
        "month",
        ROUND(AVG("projected_sales_usd"), 2) AS "avg_monthly_sales"
    FROM projected_usd
    GROUP BY "month"
),
-- Step 7: Calculate median of the twelve monthly averages
median_calc AS (
    SELECT
        "avg_monthly_sales",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY "avg_monthly_sales") AS "rn",
        COUNT(*) OVER () AS "cnt"
    FROM monthly_avg
)
SELECT ROUND(AVG("avg_monthly_sales"), 2) AS "median_of_monthly_avg_projected_sales_usd"
FROM median_calc
WHERE "rn" IN (("cnt" + 1) / 2, ("cnt" + 2) / 2);
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Monthly sales in 2019 (France, promo_total_id=1, channel_total_id=1)
WITH sales_2019 AS (
    SELECT 
        s.prod_id,
        t.calendar_month_number AS month,
        SUM(s.amount_sold) AS total_sales
    FROM sales s
    JOIN times t ON s.time_id = t.time_id
    JOIN promotions p ON s.promo_id = p.promo_id
    JOIN channels ch ON s.channel_id = ch.channel_id
    JOIN customers c ON s.cust_id = c.cust_id
    JOIN countries co ON c.country_id = co.country_id
    WHERE t.calendar_year = 2019
        AND p.promo_total_id = 1
        AND ch.channel_total_id = 1
        AND co.country_name = 'France'
    GROUP BY s.prod_id, t.calendar_month_number
),
-- Step 2: Monthly sales in 2020 (same filters)
sales_2020 AS (
    SELECT 
        s.prod_id,
        t.calendar_month_number AS month,
        SUM(s.amount_sold) AS total_sales
    FROM sales s
    JOIN times t ON s.time_id = t.time_id
    JOIN promotions p ON s.promo_id = p.promo_id
    JOIN channels ch ON s.channel_id = ch.channel_id
    JOIN customers c ON s.cust_id = c.cust_id
    JOIN countries co ON c.country_id = co.country_id
    WHERE t.calendar_year = 2020
        AND p.promo_total_id = 1
        AND ch.channel_total_id = 1
        AND co.country_name = 'France'
    GROUP BY s.prod_id, t.calendar_month_number
),
-- Step 3: Project 2021 sales per product/month using growth rate from 2019->2020
projected AS (
    SELECT 
        a.prod_id,
        a.month,
        -- Formula: ((2020sales - 2019sales) / 2019sales) * 2020sales + 2020sales = 2020sales^2 / 2019sales
        CASE 
            WHEN a.total_sales IS NOT NULL AND a.total_sales != 0 
                 AND b.total_sales IS NOT NULL AND b.total_sales != 0 
            THEN (b.total_sales * b.total_sales) / a.total_sales
            ELSE NULL
        END AS projected_sales
    FROM sales_2019 a
    JOIN sales_2020 b ON a.prod_id = b.prod_id AND a.month = b.month
),
-- Step 4: Convert projected sales to USD using currency table (2021 rates)
converted AS (
    SELECT 
        p.month,
        p.projected_sales * COALESCE(cur.to_us, 1) AS projected_usd
    FROM projected p
    LEFT JOIN currency cur ON cur.country = 'France' 
        AND cur.year = 2021 
        AND cur.month = p.month
    WHERE p.projected_sales IS NOT NULL
),
-- Step 5: Average projected sales per month (across products)
monthly_avg AS (
    SELECT 
        month,
        AVG(projected_usd) AS avg_projected
    FROM converted
    GROUP BY month
),
-- Step 6: Compute median of the 12 monthly averages
median AS (
    SELECT 
        AVG(avg_projected) AS median_val
    FROM (
        SELECT 
            avg_projected,
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY avg_projected) AS rn,
            COUNT(*) OVER () AS cnt
        FROM monthly_avg
    )
    WHERE rn IN ((cnt + 1) / 2, (cnt + 2) / 2)
)
SELECT median_val FROM median;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Compute per-state alien statistics (total, friendly, hostile, average age)
WITH state_stats AS (
    SELECT
        "state",
        COUNT(*) AS total_aliens,
        SUM(CASE WHEN "aggressive" = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS friendly_count,
        SUM(CASE WHEN "aggressive" = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS hostile_count,
        AVG("age") AS avg_age
    FROM "alien_data"
    GROUP BY "state"
),
-- Step 2: Rank states by total alien population descending
ranked_states AS (
    SELECT
        "state",
        total_aliens,
        friendly_count,
        hostile_count,
        avg_age,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY total_aliens DESC) AS rn
    FROM state_stats
)
-- Step 3 & 4: Filter top 10, apply conditions, count matching states
SELECT COUNT(*) AS matching_states_count
FROM ranked_states
WHERE rn <= 10
  AND friendly_count > hostile_count   -- friendly percentage > hostile percentage
  AND avg_age > 200;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH "top_states" AS (
    SELECT
        "state",
        COUNT(*) AS "alien_population"
    FROM "alien_data"
    GROUP BY "state"
    ORDER BY "alien_population" DESC
    LIMIT 10
),
"state_stats" AS (
    SELECT
        ad."state",
        AVG(ad."age") AS "avg_age",
        CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN ad."aggressive" = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / COUNT(*) AS "friendly_pct",
        CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN ad."aggressive" = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / COUNT(*) AS "hostile_pct"
    FROM "alien_data" ad
    INNER JOIN "top_states" ts ON ad."state" = ts."state"
    GROUP BY ad."state"
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS "result"
FROM "state_stats"
WHERE "friendly_pct" > "hostile_pct"
  AND "avg_age" > 200;
```
</details>

```sql
    FROM "skills_job_dim" sjd
    INNER JOIN filtered_jobs fj ON sjd.job_id = fj.job_id
    GROUP BY sjd.skill_id
),
top_skills AS (
    SELECT skill_id
    FROM skill_counts
    ORDER BY job_count DESC
    LIMIT 3
),
final_jobs AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT fj.job_id, fj.salary_year_avg
    FROM filtered_jobs fj
    INNER JOIN "skills_job_dim" sjd ON fj.job_id = sjd.job_id
    INNER JOIN top_skills ts ON sjd.skill_id = ts.skill_id
)
SELECT ROUND(AVG(salary_year_avg), 4) AS overall_average_salary
FROM final_jobs;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Filter to remote Data Analyst jobs with non-null annual salary
qualified_jobs AS (
    SELECT
        job_id,
        salary_year_avg
    FROM job_postings_fact
    WHERE job_title_short = 'Data Analyst'
      AND salary_year_avg IS NOT NULL
      AND job_work_from_home = 1
),
-- Step 2: Count how many qualified job postings demand each skill
skill_frequencies AS (
    SELECT
        sjd.skill_id,
        sd.skills,
        COUNT(*) AS freq
    FROM qualified_jobs qj
    JOIN skills_job_dim sjd ON qj.job_id = sjd.job_id
    JOIN skills_dim sd ON sjd.skill_id = sd.skill_id
    GROUP BY sjd.skill_id, sd.skills
),
-- Step 3: Identify the top 3 most frequently demanded skills
top_skills AS (
    SELECT skill_id
    FROM skill_frequencies
    ORDER BY freq DESC NULLS LAST
    LIMIT 3
),
-- Step 4: Find all qualified jobs that require at least one of the top 3 skills
jobs_with_top_skills AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT qj.job_id, qj.salary_year_avg
    FROM qualified_jobs qj
    JOIN skills_job_dim sjd ON qj.job_id = sjd.job_id
    JOIN top_skills ts ON sjd.skill_id = ts.skill_id
)
-- Step 5: Calculate the overall average salary across these positions
SELECT ROUND(AVG(salary_year_avg), 4) AS overall_avg_salary
FROM jobs_with_top_skills;
```

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

|   avg_loss_rate |   items_below_1std |   items_within_1std |   items_above_1std |
|----------------:|-------------------:|--------------------:|-------------------:|
|          9.4267 |                 35 |                 187 |                 29 |

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Get distinct wholesale item loss rates
wholesale_loss_rates AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT lr."item_code", lr."loss_rate_%"
    FROM "veg_loss_rate_df" lr
    INNER JOIN "veg_whsle_df" w ON lr."item_code" = w."item_code"
),
-- Compute average and variance (population variance)
stats AS (
    SELECT 
        AVG(lr."loss_rate_%") AS avg_loss_rate,
        AVG((lr."loss_rate_%" - avg_calc.avg_val) * (lr."loss_rate_%" - avg_calc.avg_val)) AS variance_loss_rate
    FROM wholesale_loss_rates lr
    CROSS JOIN (SELECT AVG("loss_rate_%") AS avg_val FROM wholesale_loss_rates) avg_calc
),
-- Categorize each item relative to 1 standard deviation (using variance instead of std dev)
categorized AS (
    SELECT 
        lr."item_code",
        lr."loss_rate_%",
        (lr."loss_rate_%" - s.avg_loss_rate) AS dev,
        CASE 
            WHEN (lr."loss_rate_%" - s.avg_loss_rate) * (lr."loss_rate_%" - s.avg_loss_rate) <= s.variance_loss_rate THEN 'Within'
            WHEN (lr."loss_rate_%" - s.avg_loss_rate) > 0 THEN 'Above'
            ELSE 'Below'
        END AS deviation_category
    FROM wholesale_loss_rates lr
    CROSS JOIN stats s
)
-- Final summary: average loss rate + counts per category
SELECT 
    ROUND((SELECT avg_loss_rate FROM stats), 4) AS avg_loss_rate,
    SUM(CASE WHEN deviation_category = 'Below' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS items_below_1std,
    SUM(CASE WHEN deviation_category = 'Within' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS items_within_1std,
    SUM(CASE WHEN deviation_category = 'Above' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS items_above_1std
FROM categorized;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Identify items that appear in veg wholesale data
whsle_items AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT "item_code"
    FROM veg_whsle_df
),

-- Loss rates only for wholesale items
loss_data AS (
    SELECT l."loss_rate_%" AS loss_rate
    FROM veg_loss_rate_df l
    WHERE l."item_code" IN (SELECT "item_code" FROM whsle_items)
),

-- Compute average loss rate and population variance
stats AS (
    SELECT
        AVG(loss_rate)                                         AS avg_loss_rate,
        AVG(loss_rate * loss_rate) - AVG(loss_rate) * AVG(loss_rate) AS variance_loss_rate
    FROM loss_data
),

-- Newton's method to compute square root of variance (standard deviation)
-- Uses 10 iterations, enough for double precision
sqrt_iter(guess, iteration) AS (
    SELECT
        CASE
            WHEN variance_loss_rate > 0 THEN variance_loss_rate
            ELSE 1e-12
        END,
        0
    FROM stats
    UNION ALL
    SELECT
        (guess + (SELECT variance_loss_rate FROM stats) / guess) / 2.0,
        iteration + 1
    FROM sqrt_iter
    WHERE iteration < 10  -- stop after generating iteration 10
),

-- Combine average, standard deviation, and variance for final classification
final_stats AS (
    SELECT
        s.avg_loss_rate,
        (SELECT guess FROM sqrt_iter WHERE iteration = 10) AS stddev_loss_rate,
        s.variance_loss_rate
    FROM stats s
)

-- Classify each loss rate using squared difference instead of sqrt
SELECT
    ROUND(f.avg_loss_rate, 4)    AS avg_loss_rate,
    ROUND(f.stddev_loss_rate, 4) AS stddev_loss_rate,
    SUM(CASE
        WHEN ld.loss_rate < f.avg_loss_rate
             AND (ld.loss_rate - f.avg_loss_rate) * (ld.loss_rate - f.avg_loss_rate) > f.variance_loss_rate
        THEN 1 ELSE 0
    END)                         AS items_below_1std,
    SUM(CASE
        WHEN (ld.loss_rate - f.avg_loss_rate) * (ld.loss_rate - f.avg_loss_rate) <= f.variance_loss_rate
        THEN 1 ELSE 0
    END)                         AS items_within_1std,
    SUM(CASE
        WHEN ld.loss_rate > f.avg_loss_rate
             AND (ld.loss_rate - f.avg_loss_rate) * (ld.loss_rate - f.avg_loss_rate) > f.variance_loss_rate
        THEN 1 ELSE 0
    END)                         AS items_above_1std
FROM loss_data ld
CROSS JOIN final_stats f;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Generate summary of monthly closing balances per customer
-- Includes months with no activity by filling the full date range

WITH
-- Step 1: Determine overall date range from transaction table
date_range AS (
  SELECT
    date(MIN(txn_date), 'start of month') AS first_month,
    date(MAX(txn_date), 'start of month') AS last_month
  FROM customer_transactions
),
-- Step 2: Recursively generate all months in the range
months AS (
  SELECT first_month AS month_start FROM date_range
  UNION ALL
  SELECT date(month_start, '+1 month')
  FROM months
  WHERE month_start < (SELECT last_month FROM date_range)
),
-- Step 3: Unique customers who have at least one transaction
customers AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id
  FROM customer_transactions
),
-- Step 4: Cartesian product to ensure every customer has a row for every month
customer_months AS (
  SELECT c.customer_id, m.month_start
  FROM customers c
  CROSS JOIN months m
),
-- Step 5: Compute net change per customer per month (deposits positive, others negative)
monthly_net AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(txn_date, 'start of month') AS txn_month,
    SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE -txn_amount END) AS net_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
  GROUP BY customer_id, txn_month
)
-- Step 6: Final output with cumulative closing balance
SELECT
  cm.customer_id,
  cm.month_start,
  COALESCE(mn.net_amount, 0) AS monthly_change,
  SUM(COALESCE(mn.net_amount, 0)) OVER (
    PARTITION BY cm.customer_id
    ORDER BY cm.month_start
  ) AS closing_balance
FROM customer_months cm
LEFT JOIN monthly_net mn
  ON cm.customer_id = mn.customer_id AND cm.month_start = mn.txn_month
ORDER BY cm.customer_id, cm.month_start;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: All distinct year-month periods present in the transaction data
all_months AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT strftime('%Y-%m', txn_date) AS month
    FROM customer_transactions
),

-- Step 2: Convert each transaction to a signed amount
-- deposit: +txn_amount ; purchase/withdrawal: -txn_amount
signed_txns AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        txn_date,
        CASE 
            WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount
            ELSE -txn_amount
        END AS signed_amount
    FROM customer_transactions
),

-- Step 3: Aggregate net change per customer per month
monthly_changes AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        strftime('%Y-%m', txn_date) AS month,
        SUM(signed_amount) AS net_change
    FROM signed_txns
    GROUP BY customer_id, month
),

-- Step 4: Build a complete grid of all customers × all months
-- This ensures months with no customer activity are still included
customer_month_grid AS (
    SELECT 
        c.customer_id,
        m.month
    FROM (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transactions) c
    CROSS JOIN all_months m
),

-- Step 5: Left join the actual changes onto the grid, filling NULLs with 0
filled_data AS (
    SELECT 
        cmg.customer_id,
        cmg.month,
        COALESCE(mc.net_change, 0) AS net_change
    FROM customer_month_grid cmg
    LEFT JOIN monthly_changes mc 
        ON cmg.customer_id = mc.customer_id AND cmg.month = mc.month
)

-- Step 6: Compute cumulative running balance using a window function
-- The cumulative balance represents the closing balance at month-end
SELECT 
    customer_id,
    month,
    net_change AS monthly_change,
    SUM(net_change) OVER (
        PARTITION BY customer_id 
        ORDER BY month
        ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS cumulative_balance
FROM filled_data
ORDER BY customer_id, month;
```
</details>

```sql
-- Step 1: Compute total orders and late orders per employee
WITH employee_order_stats AS (
    SELECT
        "employeeid",
        COUNT(*) AS total_orders,
        SUM(
            CASE
                WHEN "shippeddate" IS NOT NULL AND "shippeddate" >= "requireddate" THEN 1
                ELSE 0
            END
        ) AS late_orders
    FROM "orders"
    GROUP BY "employeeid"
)
-- Step 2: Filter employees with >50 total orders, calculate percentage, and get top 3
SELECT
    "employeeid",
    "late_orders",
    ROUND(CAST("late_orders" AS REAL) / CAST("total_orders" AS REAL) * 100, 4) AS late_percentage

ORDER BY "late_percentage" DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 3;
```

```sql
    FROM "orders"

    HAVING COUNT(*) > 50
)
SELECT

    "late_orders",
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Calculate per-track duration in minutes
WITH track_duration AS (
    SELECT
        "TrackId",
        "Milliseconds" / 60000.0 AS duration
    FROM "Track"
),
-- Step 2: Global statistics (min, avg, max duration)
global_stats AS (
    SELECT
        MIN(duration) AS min_dur,
        AVG(duration) AS avg_dur,
        MAX(duration) AS max_dur
    FROM track_duration
),
-- Step 3: Classify each track using the external length definitions
track_category AS (
    SELECT
        td."TrackId",
        td.duration,
        CASE
            WHEN td.duration < (gs.min_dur + gs.avg_dur) / 2 THEN 'short'
            WHEN td.duration < (gs.avg_dur + gs.max_dur) / 2 THEN 'medium'
            ELSE 'long'
        END AS category
    FROM track_duration td
    CROSS JOIN global_stats gs
),
-- Step 4: Compute total revenue per track from sales (InvoiceLine)
track_revenue AS (
    SELECT
        "TrackId",
        SUM("Quantity" * "UnitPrice") AS revenue
    FROM "InvoiceLine"
    GROUP BY "TrackId"
)
-- Step 5: Aggregate by category
SELECT
    tc.category,
    ROUND(MIN(tc.duration), 4) AS min_minutes,
    ROUND(MAX(tc.duration), 4) AS max_minutes,
    ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(tr.revenue), 0), 4) AS total_revenue
FROM track_category tc
LEFT JOIN track_revenue tr ON tc."TrackId" = tr."TrackId"
GROUP BY tc.category
ORDER BY tc.category;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- CTE 1: Calculate duration in minutes for every track
WITH track_durations AS (
    SELECT 
        "TrackId",
        "Milliseconds" / 60000.0 AS duration_minutes
    FROM "Track"
),

-- CTE 2: Compute global min, avg, max durations
stats AS (
    SELECT
        MIN(duration_minutes) AS min_dur,
        AVG(duration_minutes) AS avg_dur,
        MAX(duration_minutes) AS max_dur
    FROM track_durations
),

-- CTE 3: Classify each track into Short / Medium / Long
classified_tracks AS (
    SELECT
        t."TrackId",
        t.duration_minutes,
        CASE
            WHEN t.duration_minutes >= s.min_dur 
                 AND t.duration_minutes < (s.min_dur + s.avg_dur) / 2.0 
            THEN 'Short'
            WHEN t.duration_minutes >= (s.min_dur + s.avg_dur) / 2.0 
                 AND t.duration_minutes < (s.avg_dur + s.max_dur) / 2.0 
            THEN 'Medium'
            WHEN t.duration_minutes >= (s.avg_dur + s.max_dur) / 2.0 
                 AND t.duration_minutes <= s.max_dur 
            THEN 'Long'
        END AS category
    FROM track_durations t
    CROSS JOIN stats s
)

-- Final: Aggregate by category
SELECT
    ct.category,
    ROUND(MIN(ct.duration_minutes), 4) AS min_time_minutes,
    ROUND(MAX(ct.duration_minutes), 4) AS max_time_minutes,
    ROUND(SUM(COALESCE(il."UnitPrice", 0) * COALESCE(il."Quantity", 0)), 4) AS total_revenue
FROM classified_tracks ct
LEFT JOIN "InvoiceLine" il ON ct."TrackId" = il."TrackId"
WHERE ct.category IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY ct.category
ORDER BY ct.category;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Define the Magnificent 7 tickers
magnificent_tickers AS (
    SELECT 'AAPL' AS "ticker"
    UNION ALL SELECT 'MSFT'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'GOOGL'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'AMZN'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'META'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'NVDA'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'TSLA'
),

-- Get all post-market close prices for these tickers in the first half of 2024
post_market_prices AS (
    SELECT
        sp."TICKER",
        sp."DATE",
        sp."VALUE"
    FROM FINANCE__ECONOMICS.CYBERSYN.STOCK_PRICE_TIMESERIES sp
    WHERE sp."VARIABLE" = 'post-market_close'
      AND sp."TICKER" IN (SELECT "ticker" FROM magnificent_tickers)
      AND sp."DATE" >= '2024-01-01'
      AND sp."DATE" <= '2024-06-30'
),

-- Find the first and last trading day in the period for each ticker
start_end_dates AS (
    SELECT
        "TICKER" AS "ticker",
        MIN("DATE") AS "start_date",
        MAX("DATE") AS "end_date"
    FROM post_market_prices
    GROUP BY "TICKER"
),

-- Get the actual price values on those dates
start_prices AS (
    SELECT
        se."ticker",
        se."start_date",
        p."VALUE" AS "start_value"
    FROM start_end_dates se
    JOIN post_market_prices p
        ON se."ticker" = p."TICKER" AND se."start_date" = p."DATE"
),

end_prices AS (
    SELECT
        se."ticker",
        se."end_date",
        p."VALUE" AS "end_value"
    FROM start_end_dates se
    JOIN post_market_prices p
        ON se."ticker" = p."TICKER" AND se."end_date" = p."DATE"
)

-- Compute percentage change: ((end - start) / start) * 100
SELECT
    sp."ticker",
    sp."start_date",
    sp."start_value",
    ep."end_date",
    ep."end_value",
    ROUND((ep."end_value" - sp."start_value") / NULLIF(sp."start_value", 0) * 100, 4) AS "percentage_change"
FROM start_prices sp
JOIN end_prices ep ON sp."ticker" = ep."ticker"
ORDER BY sp."ticker";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
  -- Prices at the start of the period (first trading day of 2024)
  start_prices AS (
    SELECT
      "TICKER",
      "VALUE" AS "start_price"
    FROM "FINANCE__ECONOMICS"."CYBERSYN"."STOCK_PRICE_TIMESERIES"
    WHERE
      "VARIABLE" = 'post-market_close'
      AND "TICKER" IN ('AAPL', 'MSFT', 'GOOGL', 'AMZN', 'NVDA', 'META', 'TSLA')
      AND "DATE" = '2024-01-02'
  ),
  -- Prices at the end of the period (last trading day of June 2024)
  end_prices AS (
    SELECT
      "TICKER",
      "VALUE" AS "end_price"
    FROM "FINANCE__ECONOMICS"."CYBERSYN"."STOCK_PRICE_TIMESERIES"
    WHERE
      "VARIABLE" = 'post-market_close'
      AND "TICKER" IN ('AAPL', 'MSFT', 'GOOGL', 'AMZN', 'NVDA', 'META', 'TSLA')
      AND "DATE" = '2024-06-28'
  )
SELECT
  s."TICKER",
  ROUND(100.0 * (e."end_price" - s."start_price") / NULLIF(s."start_price", 0), 4) AS "percentage_change"
FROM start_prices s
JOIN end_prices e
  ON s."TICKER" = e."TICKER"
ORDER BY s."TICKER";
```
</details>

```sql
-- Analyze push notification engagement on June 1, 2023 between 08:00 and 09:00 UTC
-- using Unix timestamp filter on the TIME column for consistency across all event tables.
WITH send_events AS (
    SELECT 
        "APP_GROUP_ID",
        "CAMPAIGN_ID",
        "USER_ID",
        "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
        "PLATFORM",
        "AD_TRACKING_ENABLED",
        CAST(NULL AS TEXT) AS "CARRIER",
        CAST(NULL AS TEXT) AS "BROWSER",
        CAST(NULL AS TEXT) AS "DEVICE_MODEL",
        'send' AS event_type
    FROM BRAZE_USER_EVENT_DEMO_DATASET.PUBLIC.USERS_MESSAGES_PUSHNOTIFICATION_SEND_VIEW
    WHERE "TIME" >= 1685606400 AND "TIME" < 1685610000  -- 2023-06-01 08:00:00 UTC to 09:00:00 UTC
),
bounce_events AS (
    SELECT 
        "APP_GROUP_ID",
        "CAMPAIGN_ID",
        "USER_ID",
        "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
        "PLATFORM",
        "AD_TRACKING_ENABLED",
        CAST(NULL AS TEXT) AS "CARRIER",
        CAST(NULL AS TEXT) AS "BROWSER",
        CAST(NULL AS TEXT) AS "DEVICE_MODEL",
        'bounce' AS event_type
    FROM BRAZE_USER_EVENT_DEMO_DATASET.PUBLIC.USERS_MESSAGES_PUSHNOTIFICATION_BOUNCE_VIEW
    WHERE "TIME" >= 1685606400 AND "TIME" < 1685610000
),
open_events AS (
    SELECT 
        "APP_GROUP_ID",
        "CAMPAIGN_ID",
        "USER_ID",
        "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
        "PLATFORM",
        "AD_TRACKING_ENABLED",
        "CARRIER",
        "BROWSER",
        "DEVICE_MODEL",
        'open' AS event_type
    FROM BRAZE_USER_EVENT_DEMO_DATASET.PUBLIC.USERS_MESSAGES_PUSHNOTIFICATION_OPEN_VIEW
    WHERE "TIME" >= 1685606400 AND "TIME" < 1685610000
),
influenced_open_events AS (
    SELECT 
        "APP_GROUP_ID",
        "CAMPAIGN_ID",
        "USER_ID",
        "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
        "PLATFORM",
        CAST(NULL AS BOOLEAN) AS "AD_TRACKING_ENABLED",  -- column not present in this table
        "CARRIER",
        "BROWSER",
        "DEVICE_MODEL",
        'influenced_open' AS event_type
    FROM BRAZE_USER_EVENT_DEMO_DATASET.PUBLIC.USERS_MESSAGES_PUSHNOTIFICATION_INFLUENCEDOPEN_VIEW
    WHERE "TIME" >= 1685606400 AND "TIME" < 1685610000
),
combined AS (
    SELECT * FROM send_events
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM bounce_events
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM open_events
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM influenced_open_events
)
SELECT
    "APP_GROUP_ID",
    "CAMPAIGN_ID",
    "USER_ID",
    "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
    "PLATFORM",
    "AD_TRACKING_ENABLED",
    "CARRIER",
    "BROWSER",
    "DEVICE_MODEL",
    COUNT(CASE WHEN event_type = 'send' THEN 1 END) AS push_notification_sends,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN event_type = 'send' THEN "USER_ID" END) AS unique_push_notification_sends,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN event_type = 'bounce' THEN 1 END) AS push_notification_bounced,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN event_type = 'bounce' THEN "USER_ID" END) AS unique_push_notification_bounced,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN event_type = 'open' THEN 1 END) AS push_notification_open,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN event_type = 'open' THEN "USER_ID" END) AS unique_push_notification_opened,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN event_type = 'influenced_open' THEN 1 END) AS push_notification_influenced_open,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN event_type = 'influenced_open' THEN "USER_ID" END) AS unique_push_notification_influenced_open
FROM combined
GROUP BY 
    "APP_GROUP_ID",
    "CAMPAIGN_ID",
    "USER_ID",
    "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID",
    "PLATFORM",
    "AD_TRACKING_ENABLED",
    "CARRIER",
    "BROWSER",
    "DEVICE_MODEL"
ORDER BY 
    "APP_GROUP_ID", "CAMPAIGN_ID", "USER_ID", "MESSAGE_VARIATION_ID";
```

```sql
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN "event_type" = 'open' THEN "USER_ID" END) AS "unique_push_notification_opened",
    COUNT(CASE WHEN "event_type" = 'influenced_open' THEN 1 END)    AS "push_notification_influenced_open",
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN "event_type" = 'influenced_open' THEN "USER_ID" END) AS "unique_push_notification_influenced_open"
FROM all_events
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8
ORDER BY 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8;
```

```sql
),
tract_totals AS (

    FROM
```
