```sql
WITH 
-- Extract page title and page_location for each event
page_info AS (
  SELECT
    e.user_pseudo_id,
    e.event_date,
    (SELECT value.string_value FROM UNNEST(e.event_params) WHERE key = 'page_title') AS page_title,
    (SELECT value.string_value FROM UNNEST(e.event_params) WHERE key = 'page_location') AS page_url
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_20210102` e
  WHERE e.event_date = '20210102'
    AND e.event_name = 'page_view'
    AND e.user_pseudo_id = '1402138.5184246691'
),

-- Parse URL segments for classification
classified_pages AS (
  SELECT
    page_title,
    page_url,
    SPLIT(page_url, '/') AS url_parts
  FROM page_info
)

-- Final output with adjusted page names
SELECT DISTINCT
  CASE
    WHEN ARRAY_LENGTH(url_parts) >= 5 THEN
      CASE
        -- PDP: last segment contains '+' and category in 4th or 5th
        WHEN url_parts[SAFE_ORDINAL(5)] LIKE '%+%' 
             AND (LOWER(IFNULL(url_parts[SAFE_ORDINAL(4)], '')) IN ('accessories','apparel','brands','campus collection','drinkware','electronics','google redesign','lifestyle','nest','new 2015 logo','notebooks journals','office','shop by brand','small goods','stationery','wearables')
                  OR LOWER(IFNULL(url_parts[SAFE_ORDINAL(5)], '')) IN ('accessories','apparel','brands','campus collection','drinkware','electronics','google redesign','lifestyle','nest','new 2015 logo','notebooks journals','office','shop by brand','small goods','stationery','wearables'))
          THEN 'PDP'
        -- PLP: category in 4th or 5th but no '+' in those positions
        WHEN (LOWER(IFNULL(url_parts[SAFE_ORDINAL(4)], '')) IN ('accessories','apparel','brands','campus collection','drinkware','electronics','google redesign','lifestyle','nest','new 2015 logo','notebooks journals','office','shop by brand','small goods','stationery','wearables')
              OR LOWER(IFNULL(url_parts[SAFE_ORDINAL(5)], '')) IN ('accessories','apparel','brands','campus collection','drinkware','electronics','google redesign','lifestyle','nest','new 2015 logo','notebooks journals','office','shop by brand','small goods','stationery','wearables'))
             AND (url_parts[SAFE_ORDINAL(4)] NOT LIKE '%+%' AND url_parts[SAFE_ORDINAL(5)] NOT LIKE '%+%')
          THEN 'PLP'
        ELSE page_title
      END
    ELSE page_title
  END AS adjusted_page_name
FROM classified_pages;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Optimized query to reduce bytes scanned by using a single UNNEST for both parameters
WITH page_data AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    user_pseudo_id,
    -- Extract page_title and page_location in a single pass
    MAX(CASE WHEN p.key = 'page_title' THEN p.value.string_value END) AS page_title,
    MAX(CASE WHEN p.key = 'page_location' THEN p.value.string_value END) AS page_location
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_20210102`,
    UNNEST(event_params) AS p
  WHERE user_pseudo_id = '1402138.5184246691'
    AND event_name = 'page_view'
    AND p.key IN ('page_title', 'page_location')
  GROUP BY user_pseudo_id, -- Group by event-level identifiers to avoid duplicate rows
    (SELECT value.string_value FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'page_title') -- not needed, group by user only
  -- Actually, DISTINCT is safer; we can keep DISTINCT with the two extracted fields
),
parsed_urls AS (
  SELECT
    page_title,
    page_location,
    SPLIT(page_location, '/') AS url_segments,
    ARRAY_LENGTH(SPLIT(page_location, '/')) AS num_segments
  FROM page_data
  WHERE page_location IS NOT NULL
),
classified AS (
  SELECT
    page_title,
    page_location,
    num_segments,
    -- Category present in 4th or 5th segment (0-indexed: 3 and 4)
    num_segments >= 5 AND (
      LOWER(url_segments[SAFE_OFFSET(3)]) IN (
        'accessories','apparel','brands','campus+collection','drinkware',
        'electronics','google+redesign','lifestyle','nest','new+2015+logo',
        'notebooks+journals','office','shop+by+brand','small+goods',
        'stationery','wearables'
      )
      OR LOWER(url_segments[SAFE_OFFSET(4)]) IN (
        'accessories','apparel','brands','campus+collection','drinkware',
        'electronics','google+redesign','lifestyle','nest','new+2015+logo',
        'notebooks+journals','office','shop+by+brand','small+goods',
        'stationery','wearables'
      )
    ) AS has_category,
    -- Last segment contains '+' for PDP
    url_segments[SAFE_OFFSET(num_segments - 1)] LIKE '%+%' AS last_segment_has_plus
  FROM parsed_urls
)
SELECT
  CASE
    WHEN has_category AND NOT last_segment_has_plus THEN 'PLP'
    WHEN has_category AND last_segment_has_plus THEN 'PDP'
    ELSE COALESCE(page_title, page_location)
  END AS page_name
FROM classified
ORDER BY page_name;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH session_hits AS (
  -- 1. Extract all hits for sessions in Jan 2017 with campaign containing 'Data Share'
  SELECT
    fullVisitorId,
    visitId,
    hit.hitNumber,
    hit.time AS hit_time,
    hit.page.pagePath AS current_page,
    hit.type AS hit_type
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*` AS s,
    UNNEST(hits) AS hit
  WHERE
    _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170101' AND '20170131'
    AND s.trafficSource.campaign LIKE '%Data Share%'
    AND hit.type = 'PAGE'
),
home_hits_with_next AS (
  -- 2. For each hit, get the next hit in the same session using LEAD
  SELECT
    fullVisitorId,
    visitId,
    hitNumber,
    hit_time,
    current_page,
    LEAD(current_page) OVER (
      PARTITION BY fullVisitorId, visitId
      ORDER BY hitNumber
    ) AS next_page,
    LEAD(hit_time) OVER (
      PARTITION BY fullVisitorId, visitId
      ORDER BY hitNumber
    ) AS next_hit_time
  FROM session_hits
)
-- 3. Filter for '/home' hits that have a next page, compute time_on_home
SELECT
  next_page,
  MAX(ROUND((next_hit_time - hit_time) / 1000.0, 4)) AS max_time_on_home_seconds
FROM home_hits_with_next
WHERE
  current_page LIKE '/home%'
  AND next_page IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY next_page
ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH january_sessions AS (
  -- Step 1: Get all January 2017 sessions with campaign containing 'Data Share'
  SELECT
    fullVisitorId,
    visitId,
    visitStartTime,
    trafficSource.campaign AS campaign,
    hits
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170101' AND '20170131'
    AND LOWER(trafficSource.campaign) LIKE '%data share%'
),
-- Step 2: Unnest hits and use LEAD to find the next page in each session
hit_sequences AS (
  SELECT
    s.fullVisitorId,
    s.visitId,
    h.hitNumber,
    h.time AS hit_time_ms,
    h.page.pagePath AS current_page,
    LEAD(h.page.pagePath) OVER (
      PARTITION BY s.fullVisitorId, s.visitId
      ORDER BY h.hitNumber
    ) AS next_page,
    LEAD(h.time) OVER (
      PARTITION BY s.fullVisitorId, s.visitId
      ORDER BY h.hitNumber
    ) AS next_hit_time_ms
  FROM january_sessions s
  CROSS JOIN UNNEST(s.hits) AS h
  WHERE h.type = 'PAGE'  -- Only consider page hits
)
-- Step 3: Filter for '/home' pages, find most common next page and max time
SELECT
  next_page AS most_common_next_page,
  ROUND(MAX((next_hit_time_ms - hit_time_ms) / 1000.0), 4) AS max_time_on_home_seconds
FROM hit_sequences
WHERE current_page LIKE '/home%'
  AND next_page IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY next_page
ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH filtered AS (
    SELECT
        p."publication_number",
        p."citation"
    FROM "PATENTS"."PATENTS"."PUBLICATIONS" p
    WHERE p."country_code" = 'US'
      AND p."kind_code" = 'B2'
      AND p."grant_date" BETWEEN 20150101 AND 20181231
),
cited_pats AS (
    SELECT
        f."publication_number" AS focal_pub,
        cit.value:"publication_number"::VARCHAR AS cited_pub_number
    FROM filtered f,
         LATERAL FLATTEN(input => f."citation") cit
    WHERE cit.value:"publication_number" IS NOT NULL
),
cited_ipc AS (
    SELECT
        cp.focal_pub,
        SUBSTR(ipc.value:"code"::VARCHAR, 1, 4) AS ipc4
    FROM cited_pats cp
    INNER JOIN "PATENTS"."PATENTS"."PUBLICATIONS" cited_pub
        ON cp.cited_pub_number = cited_pub."publication_number",
     LATERAL FLATTEN(input => cited_pub."ipc") ipc
    WHERE ipc.value:"code" IS NOT NULL
),
ipc_counts AS (
    SELECT
        focal_pub,
        ipc4,
        COUNT(*) AS cnt_ipc4
    FROM cited_ipc
    GROUP BY focal_pub, ipc4
),
total_and_sq AS (
    SELECT
        c.focal_pub,
        SUM(c.cnt_ipc4) AS total_occurrences,
        SUM(c.cnt_ipc4 * c.cnt_ipc4) AS sum_squares
    FROM ipc_counts c
    GROUP BY c.focal_pub
    HAVING total_occurrences > 0
)
SELECT
    ts.focal_pub AS "publication_number",
    ROUND(1 - (ts.sum_squares / (ts.total_occurrences * ts.total_occurrences)), 4) AS "originality_score"
FROM total_and_sq ts
ORDER BY "originality_score" DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: US patents with B2 kind and grant date 2015-2018
target_pats AS (
    SELECT 
        "publication_number",
        "citation"
    FROM "PATENTS"."PATENTS"."PUBLICATIONS"
    WHERE "country_code" = 'US'
      AND "kind_code" = 'B2'
      AND "grant_date" BETWEEN 20150101 AND 20181231
),

-- Step 2: Flatten backward citations
citations_flattened AS (
    SELECT 
        tp."publication_number" AS patent_number,
        f.value:"publication_number"::STRING AS cited_pub
    FROM target_pats tp,
         LATERAL FLATTEN(input => tp."citation") f
    WHERE f.value:"publication_number" IS NOT NULL
),

-- Step 3: Join to cited publications and flatten their IPC codes
cited_ipc AS (
    SELECT 
        cf.patent_number,
        SUBSTR(ipc_u.value:"code"::STRING, 1, 4) AS ipc4
    FROM citations_flattened cf
    JOIN "PATENTS"."PATENTS"."PUBLICATIONS" p2
        ON cf.cited_pub = p2."publication_number",
         LATERAL FLATTEN(input => p2."ipc") ipc_u
    WHERE ipc_u.value:"code" IS NOT NULL
),

-- Step 4: Compute total occurrences of IPC codes per patent
total_occurrences AS (
    SELECT 
        patent_number,
        COUNT(*) AS total_occ
    FROM cited_ipc
    GROUP BY patent_number
),

-- Step 5: Compute count per distinct 4-digit IPC per patent
ipc_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        patent_number,
        ipc4,
        COUNT(*) AS ipc_count
    FROM cited_ipc
    GROUP BY patent_number, ipc4
),

-- Step 6: Compute originality score
pat_originality AS (
    SELECT 
        ic.patent_number,
        ROUND(
            1 - SUM(POWER(ic.ipc_count * 1.0 / tot.total_occ, 2)),
            4
        ) AS originality_score
    FROM ipc_counts ic
    JOIN total_occurrences tot
        ON ic.patent_number = tot.patent_number
    GROUP BY ic.patent_number, tot.total_occ
)

-- Step 7: Return the patent with the highest originality
SELECT 
    patent_number,
    originality_score
FROM pat_originality
ORDER BY originality_score DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

The query should focus on specific CPC categories, sort results by backward citations in descending order, and return the patent with the most backward citations, limiting to one result.

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: CTE to get base U.S. patents with application dates
WITH base AS (
    SELECT p."id" AS "patent_id",
           a."date" AS "app_date"
    FROM PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.PATENT p
    JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.APPLICATION a ON p."id" = a."patent_id"
    WHERE p."country" = 'US'
),

-- Step 2: Filter patents that belong to the specified CPC categories
-- Using broader CPC sections
cpc_filtered AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT c."patent_id"
    FROM PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.CPC_CURRENT c
    WHERE c."section_id" IN ('A', 'C', 'G', 'H')
),

-- Step 3: Compute backward citations count (within 1 year before app_date)
backward AS (
    SELECT b."patent_id",
           COUNT(*) AS "backward_1yr"
    FROM base b
    JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.USPATENTCITATION uc ON b."patent_id" = uc."patent_id"
    JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.PATENT cited ON cited."id" = uc."citation_id"
    JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.APPLICATION cited_app ON cited_app."patent_id" = cited."id"
    WHERE cited_app."date" >= TO_CHAR(DATEADD(YEAR, -1, TO_DATE(b."app_date", 'YYYY-MM-DD')), 'YYYY-MM-DD')
      AND cited_app."date" < b."app_date"
    GROUP BY b."patent_id"
),

-- Step 4: Compute forward citations count within 1 year after app_date
forward_1yr AS (
    SELECT b."patent_id",
           COUNT(*) AS "forward_1yr"
    FROM base b
    JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.USPATENTCITATION uc ON b."patent_id" = uc."citation_id"
    JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.PATENT citing ON citing."id" = uc."patent_id"
    JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.APPLICATION citing_app ON citing_app."patent_id" = citing."id"
    WHERE citing_app."date" > b."app_date"
      AND citing_app."date" <= TO_CHAR(DATEADD(YEAR, 1, TO_DATE(b."app_date", 'YYYY-MM-DD')), 'YYYY-MM-DD')
    GROUP BY b."patent_id"
),

-- Step 5: Compute forward citations count within 3 years after app_date
forward_3yr AS (
    SELECT b."patent_id",
           COUNT(*) AS "forward_3yr"
    FROM base b
    JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.USPATENTCITATION uc ON b."patent_id" = uc."citation_id"
    JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.PATENT citing ON citing."id" = uc."patent_id"
    JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.APPLICATION citing_app ON citing_app."patent_id" = citing."id"
    WHERE citing_app."date" > b."app_date"
      AND citing_app."date" <= TO_CHAR(DATEADD(YEAR, 3, TO_DATE(b."app_date", 'YYYY-MM-DD')), 'YYYY-MM-DD')
    GROUP BY b."patent_id"
),

-- Step 6: Calculate backward citations for final ordering
backward_with_citations AS (
    SELECT b."patent_id",
           COUNT(*) AS "backward_count"
    FROM base b
    JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.USPATENTCITATION uc ON b."patent_id" = uc."patent_id"
    JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.PATENT cited ON cited."id" = uc."citation_id"
    JOIN PATENTSVIEW.PATENTSVIEW.APPLICATION cited_app ON cited_app."patent_id" = cited."id"
    WHERE cited_app."date" >= TO_CHAR(DATEADD(YEAR, -1, TO_DATE(b."app_date", 'YYYY-MM-DD')), 'YYYY-MM-DD')
      AND cited_app."date" < b."app_date"
    GROUP BY b."patent_id"
)

-- Step 7: Final selection with proper ordering
SELECT b."patent_id",
       COALESCE(f3."forward_3yr", 0) AS "forward_citations_3yr"
FROM base b
JOIN cpc_filtered cf ON b."patent_id" = cf."patent_id"
JOIN backward_with_citations bw ON b."patent_id" = bw."patent_id"
LEFT JOIN forward_1yr f1 ON b."patent_id" = f1."patent_id"
LEFT JOIN forward_3yr f3 ON b."patent_id" = f3."patent_id"
WHERE COALESCE(f1."forward_1yr", 0) > 0
ORDER BY bw."backward_count" DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- CTE: Get U.S. patents with their application dates (safely cast dates)
WITH "patent_app" AS (
    SELECT 
        p."id" AS "patent_id",
        p."country",
        TRY_CAST(a."date" AS DATE) AS "app_date"
    FROM "PATENTSVIEW"."PATENTSVIEW"."PATENT" p
    JOIN "PATENTSVIEW"."PATENTSVIEW"."APPLICATION" a 
        ON p."id" = a."patent_id"
    WHERE p."country" = 'US'
),

-- CTE: Count backward citations within 1 year before application date
"backward_citations" AS (
    SELECT 
        uc."patent_id" AS "citing_patent_id",
        COUNT(*) AS "backward_count"
    FROM "PATENTSVIEW"."PATENTSVIEW"."USPATENTCITATION" uc
    JOIN "patent_app" pa 
        ON uc."patent_id" = pa."patent_id"
    WHERE TRY_CAST(uc."date" AS DATE) >= DATEADD(day, -365, pa."app_date")
      AND TRY_CAST(uc."date" AS DATE) < pa."app_date"
      AND pa."app_date" IS NOT NULL
      AND TRY_CAST(uc."date" AS DATE) IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY uc."patent_id"
),

-- CTE: Count forward citations (within 1 year and within 3 years after application date)
"forward_citations" AS (
    SELECT 
        uc."citation_id" AS "cited_patent_id",
        COUNT(CASE 
            WHEN TRY_CAST(uc."date" AS DATE) >= pa."app_date" 
             AND TRY_CAST(uc."date" AS DATE) < DATEADD(day, 365, pa."app_date") 
            THEN 1 
        END) AS "forward_1yr_count",
        COUNT(CASE 
            WHEN TRY_CAST(uc."date" AS DATE) >= pa."app_date" 
             AND TRY_CAST(uc."date" AS DATE) < DATEADD(day, 365*3, pa."app_date") 
            THEN 1 
        END) AS "forward_3yr_count"
    FROM "PATENTSVIEW"."PATENTSVIEW"."USPATENTCITATION" uc
    JOIN "patent_app" pa 
        ON uc."citation_id" = pa."patent_id"
    WHERE pa."app_date" IS NOT NULL
      AND TRY_CAST(uc."date" AS DATE) IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY uc."citation_id"
),

-- CTE: Patents that have at least one CPC classification
"cpc_patents" AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT "patent_id"
    FROM "PATENTSVIEW"."PATENTSVIEW"."CPC_CURRENT"
)

-- Final query: Combine all conditions and return the patent with most backward citations
SELECT 
    pa."patent_id",
    bc."backward_count",
    fc."forward_3yr_count" AS "forward_citations_within_3_years"
FROM "patent_app" pa
JOIN "backward_citations" bc 
    ON pa."patent_id" = bc."citing_patent_id"
JOIN "forward_citations" fc 
    ON pa."patent_id" = fc."cited_patent_id"
JOIN "cpc_patents" cpc 
    ON pa."patent_id" = cpc."patent_id"
WHERE bc."backward_count" > 0 
  AND fc."forward_1yr_count" > 0
ORDER BY bc."backward_count" DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH months AS (
    -- Generate all 12 months of 2016
    SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', '2016-01-01'::DATE) AS "month_start"
    UNION ALL
    SELECT DATEADD('month', 1, "month_start")
    FROM months
    WHERE "month_start" < '2016-12-01'
),
python_repos AS (
    -- Identify repositories that contain Python code
    SELECT DISTINCT l."repo_name"
    FROM GITHUB_REPOS.GITHUB_REPOS.LANGUAGES l,
         LATERAL FLATTEN(input => l."language") f
    WHERE f.value::TEXT = 'Python'
),
commits_per_month AS (
    -- Count commits per month for Python repos in 2016
    SELECT
        DATE_TRUNC('month', TO_TIMESTAMP(c."committer":"date"::NUMBER / 1000000)) AS "month",
        COUNT(*) AS "commit_count"
    FROM GITHUB_REPOS.GITHUB_REPOS.SAMPLE_COMMITS c
    JOIN python_repos pr ON c."repo_name" = pr."repo_name"
    WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM TO_TIMESTAMP(c."committer":"date"::NUMBER / 1000000)) = 2016
    GROUP BY "month"
)
-- Compute average monthly commits across all 12 months
SELECT ROUND(AVG(COALESCE(cpm."commit_count", 0)), 4) AS "avg_monthly_commits"
FROM months m
LEFT JOIN commits_per_month cpm ON m."month_start" = cpm."month";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify repositories that contain Python code (have at least one file with .py extension)
WITH python_repos AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT "repo_name"
    FROM "GITHUB_REPOS"."GITHUB_REPOS"."SAMPLE_FILES"
    WHERE LOWER("path") LIKE '%.py'
),

-- Step 2: Count commits made in 2016 for those repositories
commits_2016 AS (
    SELECT c."commit"
    FROM "GITHUB_REPOS"."GITHUB_REPOS"."SAMPLE_COMMITS" c
    INNER JOIN python_repos p
        ON c."repo_name" = p."repo_name"
    -- Extract year from the committer's date (stored as microseconds since epoch)
    WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM TO_TIMESTAMP(c."committer":"date"::NUMBER / 1000000)) = 2016
)

-- Step 3: Calculate average commits per month (total commits / 12 months)
SELECT ROUND(COUNT(*) / 12.0, 4) AS "avg_commits_per_month"
FROM commits_2016;
```

| JavaScript         |                14 |

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Count PullRequestEvents per repository on January 18, 2023
event_counts AS (
    SELECT
        e."repo":"name"::STRING AS "repo_name",
        COUNT(*) AS "event_count"
    FROM "GITHUB_REPOS_DATE"."DAY"."_20230118" e
    WHERE e."type" = 'PullRequestEvent'
    GROUP BY e."repo":"name"::STRING
),

-- Determine primary programming language for each repository
-- (language with the highest byte count per repository)
primary_langs AS (
    SELECT
        l."repo_name",
        f.value:"language"::STRING AS "language",
        f.value:"bytes"::NUMBER AS "bytes"
    FROM "GITHUB_REPOS_DATE"."GITHUB_REPOS"."LANGUAGES" l,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => l."language") f
    QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
        PARTITION BY l."repo_name"
        ORDER BY f.value:"bytes"::NUMBER DESC
    ) = 1
)

-- Aggregate event counts by primary language and filter those with >= 100 events
SELECT
    p."language" AS "primary_language"
FROM primary_langs p
JOIN event_counts e ON p."repo_name" = e."repo_name"
GROUP BY p."language"
HAVING SUM(e."event_count") >= 100
ORDER BY p."language";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH primary_lang AS (
    SELECT
        l."repo_name",
        f.value:"language"::STRING AS "language",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY l."repo_name"
            ORDER BY f.value:"bytes"::NUMBER DESC
        ) AS "rn"
    FROM "GITHUB_REPOS_DATE"."GITHUB_REPOS"."LANGUAGES" l,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => l."language") f
),
repo_primary AS (
    SELECT "repo_name", "language"
    FROM primary_lang
    WHERE "rn" = 1
),
events AS (
    SELECT
        e."repo":"name"::STRING AS "repo_name"
    FROM "GITHUB_REPOS_DATE"."DAY"."_20230118" e
    WHERE e."type" = 'PullRequestEvent'
)
SELECT
    rp."language"
FROM repo_primary rp
JOIN events e ON rp."repo_name" = e."repo_name"
GROUP BY rp."language"
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 100;
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH hurricane_points AS (
    -- Convert hurricane lat/lon to geography points, normalizing longitude to [-180,180]
    SELECT 
        h."name",
        ST_POINT(
            CASE 
                WHEN h."longitude" > 180 THEN h."longitude" - 360
                WHEN h."longitude" < -180 THEN h."longitude" + 360
                ELSE h."longitude"
            END,
            h."latitude"
        ) AS "hurricane_point"
    FROM "NOAA_DATA_PLUS"."NOAA_HURRICANES"."HURRICANES" h
    WHERE h."name" IS NOT NULL 
      AND TRIM(h."name") != ''
      AND h."latitude" IS NOT NULL 
      AND h."longitude" IS NOT NULL
      AND ABS(h."latitude") <= 90
),
zip_hurricanes AS (
    -- Spatial join: find which hurricanes fall within which zip code boundaries
    SELECT DISTINCT
        z."city",
        z."zip_code",
        z."state_code",
        hp."name"
    FROM "NOAA_DATA_PLUS"."GEO_US_BOUNDARIES"."ZIP_CODES" z
    JOIN hurricane_points hp
        ON ST_WITHIN(hp."hurricane_point", ST_GEOGFROMWKB(z."zip_code_geom"))
)
-- Aggregate results by city, zip code, and state
SELECT 
    zh."city",
    zh."zip_code",
    zh."state_code" AS "state",
    COUNT(zh."name") AS "count_of_hurricanes",
    LISTAGG(zh."name", ', ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY zh."name") AS "list_of_hurricanes"
FROM zip_hurricanes zh
GROUP BY zh."city", zh."zip_code", zh."state_code"
ORDER BY COUNT(zh."name") DESC;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH "hurricane_points" AS (
    -- Get distinct hurricanes (by name) that are Category 1-5 on Saffir-Simpson scale
    -- and have a non-empty name (exclude unnamed hurricanes)
    SELECT DISTINCT
        "name",
        ST_MAKEPOINT("longitude", "latitude") AS "point_geom"
    FROM "NOAA_DATA_PLUS"."NOAA_HURRICANES"."HURRICANES"
    WHERE "usa_sshs" >= 1
      AND "name" IS NOT NULL
      AND TRIM("name") != ''
),
"zip_hurricane_links" AS (
    -- Spatial join: find which zip codes contain hurricane track points
    -- Using internal_point_geom (WKB point) as the zip location
    SELECT DISTINCT
        z."zip_code",
        z."city",
        z."state_name",
        hp."name"
    FROM "NOAA_DATA_PLUS"."GEO_US_BOUNDARIES"."ZIP_CODES" z
    INNER JOIN "hurricane_points" hp
        ON ST_WITHIN(
            hp."point_geom",
            ST_GEOMFROMWKB(z."internal_point_geom")
        )
)
-- Aggregate: count hurricanes and list their names per city/zip/state
SELECT
    "city",
    "zip_code",
    "state_name" AS "state",
    COUNT(DISTINCT "name") AS "count_of_hurricanes",
    LISTAGG(DISTINCT "name", ', ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY "name") AS "list_of_hurricanes"
FROM "zip_hurricane_links"
GROUP BY "city", "zip_code", "state_name"
ORDER BY "count_of_hurricanes" DESC, "city", "zip_code";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Get the geometry of zip code 10019 in NY
zip_geom AS (
    SELECT "zip_code_geom"
    FROM "NEW_YORK_CITIBIKE_1"."GEO_US_BOUNDARIES"."ZIP_CODES"
    WHERE "zip_code" = '10019'
      AND "state_code" = 'NY'
    LIMIT 1
),

-- Weather data for 2018 from the New York Central Park station (WMO ID 725030)
weather_2018 AS (
    SELECT 
        TO_DATE('2018-' || "mo" || '-' || "da") AS "weather_date",
        "temp",
        "prcp",
        CAST("wdsp" AS FLOAT) AS "wdsp"
    FROM "NEW_YORK_CITIBIKE_1"."NOAA_GSOD"."GSOD2018"
    WHERE "stn" = '725030'
      AND "temp" != 9999.9
      AND "prcp" != 99.99
      AND "wdsp" != 999.9
),

-- Trips in 2018 that start and end within the polygon of zip code 10019
trips_in_10019 AS (
    SELECT 
        t."usertype",
        DATE(TO_TIMESTAMP(t."starttime" / 1000000)) AS "trip_date"
    FROM "NEW_YORK_CITIBIKE_1"."NEW_YORK_CITIBIKE"."CITIBIKE_TRIPS" t
    CROSS JOIN zip_geom z
    WHERE DATE(TO_TIMESTAMP(t."starttime" / 1000000)) BETWEEN '2018-01-01' AND '2018-12-31'
      AND ST_WITHIN(
          ST_MAKEPOINT(t."start_station_longitude", t."start_station_latitude"),
          ST_GEOGFROMWKB(z."zip_code_geom")
      )
      AND ST_WITHIN(
          ST_MAKEPOINT(t."end_station_longitude", t."end_station_latitude"),
          ST_GEOGFROMWKB(z."zip_code_geom")
      )
)

-- Final aggregation: average weather metrics per user type, ordered by avg temp
SELECT 
    t."usertype" AS "user_type",
    ROUND(AVG(w."temp"), 4) AS "avg_temperature",
    ROUND(AVG(w."prcp"), 4) AS "avg_precipitation",
    ROUND(AVG(w."wdsp"), 4) AS "avg_wind_speed"
FROM trips_in_10019 t
JOIN weather_2018 w ON t."trip_date" = w."weather_date"
GROUP BY t."usertype"
ORDER BY AVG(w."temp") DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH zip_geo AS (
    SELECT ST_GEOGFROMWKB("zip_code_geom") AS "geom"
    FROM "NEW_YORK_CITIBIKE_1"."GEO_US_BOUNDARIES"."ZIP_CODES"
    WHERE "zip_code" = '10019'
      AND "state_name" = 'New York'
),

weather AS (
    SELECT
        CAST("temp" AS FLOAT) AS "temp",
        CAST("prcp" AS FLOAT) AS "prcp",
        CAST("wdsp" AS FLOAT) AS "wdsp",
        TO_DATE('2018' || '-' || "mo" || '-' || "da", 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS "date"
    FROM "NEW_YORK_CITIBIKE_1"."NOAA_GSOD"."GSOD2018"
    WHERE "STN" = '725033'
      AND CAST("temp" AS FLOAT) < 9999.0
      AND CAST("prcp" AS FLOAT) < 99.99
      AND CAST("wdsp" AS FLOAT) < 999.0
),

trips_in_zip AS (
    SELECT
        "usertype",
        TO_DATE(TO_TIMESTAMP("starttime" / 1000000)) AS "trip_date"
    FROM "NEW_YORK_CITIBIKE_1"."NEW_YORK_CITIBIKE"."CITIBIKE_TRIPS"
    WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM TO_TIMESTAMP("starttime" / 1000000)) = 2018
      AND ST_WITHIN(
              ST_GEOMPOINT("start_station_longitude", "start_station_latitude"),
              (SELECT "geom" FROM zip_geo)
          )
      AND ST_WITHIN(
              ST_GEOMPOINT("end_station_longitude", "end_station_latitude"),
              (SELECT "geom" FROM zip_geo)
          )
)

SELECT
    t."usertype",
    ROUND(AVG(w."temp"), 4) AS "avg_temperature",
    ROUND(AVG(w."prcp"), 4) AS "avg_precipitation",
    ROUND(AVG(w."wdsp"), 4) AS "avg_wind_speed"
FROM trips_in_zip t
JOIN weather w ON t."trip_date" = w."date"
GROUP BY t."usertype"
ORDER BY AVG(w."temp") DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: First check what creation_times exist in the table for July 2019
creation_time_check AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        TO_TIMESTAMP("creation_time" / 1000000) AS creation_ts
    FROM "NOAA_GLOBAL_FORECAST_SYSTEM"."NOAA_GLOBAL_FORECAST_SYSTEM"."NOAA_GFS0P25"
    WHERE TO_TIMESTAMP("creation_time" / 1000000) BETWEEN '2019-07-01' AND '2019-07-31'
    LIMIT 10
),

-- Step 2: Sample geography data for the target area
sample_geography AS (
    SELECT
        "geography",
        "creation_time"
    FROM "NOAA_GLOBAL_FORECAST_SYSTEM"."NOAA_GLOBAL_FORECAST_SYSTEM"."NOAA_GFS0P25"
    WHERE TO_TIMESTAMP("creation_time" / 1000000) BETWEEN '2019-07-01' AND '2019-07-31'
    LIMIT 5
),

-- Step 3: Try without the geography filter first to see if any data exists
all_july_forecasts AS (
    SELECT
        "creation_time",
        "forecast"
    FROM "NOAA_GLOBAL_FORECAST_SYSTEM"."NOAA_GLOBAL_FORECAST_SYSTEM"."NOAA_GFS0P25"
    WHERE TO_TIMESTAMP("creation_time" / 1000000) BETWEEN '2019-07-01' AND '2019-07-31'
),

-- Step 4: Explode the forecast array
exploded AS (
    SELECT
        f.value:"time"::NUMBER                       AS forecast_time_micro,
        f.value:"temperature_2m_above_ground"::FLOAT  AS temperature_celsius,
        f.value:"total_cloud_cover_entire_atmosphere"::FLOAT AS cloud_cover_pct,
        f.value:"total_precipitation_surface"::FLOAT  AS precipitation_mm,
        fg."creation_time"
    FROM all_july_forecasts fg,
         LATERAL FLATTEN(input => fg."forecast") f
    WHERE f.value:"time"::NUMBER IS NOT NULL
)

-- Step 5: Daily aggregation
SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('day', TO_TIMESTAMP(forecast_time_micro / 1000000)) AS forecast_date,
    ROUND(MAX(temperature_celsius), 4)           AS max_temp_celsius,
    ROUND(MIN(temperature_celsius), 4)           AS min_temp_celsius,
    ROUND(AVG(temperature_celsius), 4)           AS avg_temp_celsius,
    ROUND(SUM(precipitation_mm), 4)              AS total_precipitation_mm,
    ROUND(
        AVG(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(HOUR FROM TO_TIMESTAMP(forecast_time_micro / 1000000)) >= 10
                      AND EXTRACT(HOUR FROM TO_TIMESTAMP(forecast_time_micro / 1000000)) < 17
                 THEN cloud_cover_pct END),
        4
    )                                             AS avg_cloud_cover_10am_5pm_pct,
    CASE
        WHEN AVG(temperature_celsius) < 0
        THEN ROUND(SUM(precipitation_mm), 4)
        ELSE 0
    END                                           AS total_snowfall_mm,
    CASE
        WHEN AVG(temperature_celsius) >= 0
        THEN ROUND(SUM(precipitation_mm), 4)
        ELSE 0
    END                                           AS total_rainfall_mm
FROM exploded
WHERE
    TO_TIMESTAMP(forecast_time_micro / 1000000) BETWEEN '2019-07-01' AND '2019-07-31'
    AND DATE_TRUNC('day', TO_TIMESTAMP(forecast_time_micro / 1000000)) = 
        DATE_TRUNC('day', TO_TIMESTAMP("creation_time" / 1000000)) + INTERVAL '1 day'
GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('day', TO_TIMESTAMP(forecast_time_micro / 1000000))
ORDER BY forecast_date;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Filter forecasts created in July 2019 and spatially within 5 km of target point
filtered_data AS (
    SELECT
        f."geography",
        f."creation_time",
        TO_TIMESTAMP(f."creation_time"::NUMBER) AS creation_utc,
        fc.value AS forecast_hour_element
    FROM "NOAA_GLOBAL_FORECAST_SYSTEM"."NOAA_GLOBAL_FORECAST_SYSTEM"."NOAA_GFS0P25" f,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => f."forecast") fc
    WHERE
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM TO_TIMESTAMP(f."creation_time"::NUMBER)) = 2019
        AND EXTRACT(MONTH FROM TO_TIMESTAMP(f."creation_time"::NUMBER)) = 7
        AND ST_DWITHIN(
            ST_GEOGFROMWKB(f."geography"),
            ST_GEOGRAPHYFROMTEXT('POINT(51.5 26.75)'),
            5000
        )
),

-- Step 2: Extract hourly values, convert to local time (+3 UTC), keep only "following day" rows
hourly_data AS (
    SELECT
        DATE(creation_utc + INTERVAL '1 day') AS target_date,
        forecast_hour_element:"temperature_2m_above_ground"::FLOAT AS temp_c,
        forecast_hour_element:"total_precipitation_surface"::FLOAT AS precip,
        forecast_hour_element:"total_cloud_cover_entire_atmosphere"::FLOAT AS cloud_cover,
        TO_TIMESTAMP(forecast_hour_element:"time"::NUMBER) + INTERVAL '3 hours' AS fc_dt_local
    FROM filtered_data
    WHERE
        DATE(TO_TIMESTAMP(forecast_hour_element:"time"::NUMBER) + INTERVAL '3 hours') = DATE(creation_utc + INTERVAL '1 day')
),

-- Step 3: Aggregate per forecast date (only July 2019)
daily_aggregates AS (
    SELECT
        target_date AS forecast_date,
        MAX(temp_c * 9/5 + 32) AS max_temp_f,
        MIN(temp_c * 9/5 + 32) AS min_temp_f,
        AVG(temp_c * 9/5 + 32) AS avg_temp_f,
        SUM(precip) AS total_precip,
        AVG(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(HOUR FROM fc_dt_local) BETWEEN 10 AND 16 THEN cloud_cover END) AS avg_cloud_cover_10_16
    FROM hourly_data
    WHERE EXTRACT(MONTH FROM target_date) = 7 AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM target_date) = 2019
    GROUP BY target_date
)

-- Step 4: Final selection with rounding and conditional columns
SELECT
    forecast_date,
    ROUND(max_temp_f, 4) AS max_temperature,
    ROUND(min_temp_f, 4) AS min_temperature,
    ROUND(avg_temp_f, 4) AS avg_temperature,
    ROUND(total_precip, 4) AS total_precipitation,
    ROUND(avg_cloud_cover_10_16, 4) AS avg_cloud_cover_10am_5pm,
    CASE WHEN avg_temp_f < 32 THEN ROUND(total_precip, 4) ELSE 0 END AS total_snowfall,
    CASE WHEN avg_temp_f >= 32 THEN ROUND(total_precip, 4) ELSE 0 END AS total_rainfall
FROM daily_aggregates
ORDER BY forecast_date;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Extract trips for 2015-01-01 with valid pickup coordinates
WITH trips_jan1 AS (
  SELECT
    pickup_datetime,
    pickup_latitude,
    pickup_longitude
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tlc_yellow_trips_2015`
  WHERE
    pickup_datetime >= TIMESTAMP('2015-01-01 00:00:00')
    AND pickup_datetime < TIMESTAMP('2015-01-02 00:00:00')
    AND pickup_latitude IS NOT NULL
    AND pickup_longitude IS NOT NULL
    -- Exclude common invalid values like 0,0
    AND ABS(pickup_latitude) > 0.001
    AND ABS(pickup_longitude) > 0.001
),

-- Step 2: Map each trip to a NYC zip code using ST_CONTAINS
trips_with_zip AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    t.pickup_datetime,
    z.zip_code
  FROM trips_jan1 t
  INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.zip_codes` z
    ON ST_CONTAINS(z.zip_code_geom, ST_GEOGPOINT(t.pickup_longitude, t.pickup_latitude))
),

-- Step 3: Aggregate trips per zip code and hour (0–23)
agg_by_zip_hour AS (
  SELECT
    zip_code,
    EXTRACT(HOUR FROM pickup_datetime) AS hour,
    COUNT(*) AS trips
  FROM trips_with_zip
  GROUP BY zip_code, hour
),

-- Step 4: Create all combinations of distinct zip codes and all hours
all_zip_hours AS (
  SELECT
    z.zip_code,
    h.hour
  FROM (SELECT DISTINCT zip_code FROM agg_by_zip_hour) z
  CROSS JOIN (SELECT hour FROM UNNEST(GENERATE_ARRAY(0, 23)) AS hour) h
)

-- Step 5: Final selection with time-based metrics and moving statistics
SELECT
  ah.zip_code,
  ah.hour,
  COALESCE(az.trips, 0) AS total_trips,
  -- Count of trips from 1 hour ago (same day)
  COALESCE(LAG(az.trips, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY ah.zip_code ORDER BY ah.hour), 0) AS trips_1h_ago,
  -- Count of trips from 24 hours ago (previous day, may be NULL)
  COALESCE(LAG(az.trips, 24) OVER (PARTITION BY ah.zip_code ORDER BY ah.hour), 0) AS trips_24h_ago,
  -- Count of trips from 168 hours ago (7 days)
  COALESCE(LAG(az.trips, 168) OVER (PARTITION BY ah.zip_code ORDER BY ah.hour), 0) AS trips_168h_ago,
  -- Count of trips from 336 hours ago (14 days)
  COALESCE(LAG(az.trips, 336) OVER (PARTITION BY ah.zip_code ORDER BY ah.hour), 0) AS trips_336h_ago,
  -- 14-day moving average (excluding current hour)
  AVG(az.trips) OVER (
    PARTITION BY ah.zip_code
    ORDER BY ah.hour
    ROWS BETWEEN 336 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
  ) AS moving_avg_14d,
  -- 14-day moving standard deviation
  STDDEV(az.trips) OVER (
    PARTITION BY ah.zip_code
    ORDER BY ah.hour
    ROWS BETWEEN 336 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
  ) AS moving_stddev_14d,
  -- 21-day moving average
  AVG(az.trips) OVER (
    PARTITION BY ah.zip_code
    ORDER BY ah.hour
    ROWS BETWEEN 504 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
  ) AS moving_avg_21d,
  -- 21-day moving standard deviation
  STDDEV(az.trips) OVER (
    PARTITION BY ah.zip_code
    ORDER BY ah.hour
    ROWS BETWEEN 504 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
  ) AS moving_stddev_21d
FROM all_zip_hours ah
LEFT JOIN agg_by_zip_hour az
  ON ah.zip_code = az.zip_code AND ah.hour = az.hour
ORDER BY total_trips DESC
LIMIT 5;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
  -- 1. Identify NYC ZIP codes (five boroughs)
  nyc_zip_codes AS (
    SELECT
      zip_code,
      zip_code_geom
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.zip_codes`
    WHERE county IN ('New York County', 'Kings County', 'Queens County', 'Bronx County', 'Richmond County')
  ),

  -- 2. Generate all hours (0-23) for Jan 1, 2015
  hours AS (
    SELECT hour
    FROM UNNEST(GENERATE_ARRAY(0, 23)) AS hour
  ),

  -- 3. Cross join: all NYC ZIPs � all hours
  all_combos AS (
    SELECT zip_code, hour
    FROM nyc_zip_codes
    CROSS JOIN hours
  ),

  -- 4. Aggregate actual trip counts for each (zip, hour) on Jan 1, 2015
  trip_counts_raw AS (
    SELECT
      z.zip_code,
      EXTRACT(HOUR FROM t.pickup_datetime) AS hour,
      COUNT(*) AS trip_count
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tlc_yellow_trips_2015` t
    JOIN nyc_zip_codes z
      ON ST_CONTAINS(z.zip_code_geom, ST_GEOGPOINT(t.pickup_longitude, t.pickup_latitude))
    WHERE DATE(t.pickup_datetime) = '2015-01-01'
      AND t.pickup_latitude IS NOT NULL
      AND t.pickup_longitude IS NOT NULL
      AND t.pickup_latitude != 0
      AND t.pickup_longitude != 0
    GROUP BY z.zip_code, hour
  ),

  -- 5. Fill missing (zip, hour) with zero trips
  complete_counts AS (
    SELECT
      a.zip_code,
      a.hour,
      COALESCE(tr.trip_count, 0) AS trip_count
    FROM all_combos a
    LEFT JOIN trip_counts_raw tr
      ON a.zip_code = tr.zip_code AND a.hour = tr.hour
  ),

  -- 6. Compute lookback and moving window metrics
  with_metrics AS (
    SELECT
      zip_code,
      hour,
      trip_count,
      COALESCE(LAG(trip_count, 1)  OVER (PARTITION BY zip_code ORDER BY hour), 0) AS trips_1_hour_ago,
      COALESCE(LAG(trip_count, 24) OVER (PARTITION BY zip_code ORDER BY hour), 0) AS trips_24_hours_ago,
      COALESCE(LAG(trip_count, 168) OVER (PARTITION BY zip_code ORDER BY hour), 0) AS trips_168_hours_ago,
      COALESCE(LAG(trip_count, 336) OVER (PARTITION BY zip_code ORDER BY hour), 0) AS trips_336_hours_ago,
      -- 14-day moving average and stddev (excluding current hour)
      AVG(trip_count) OVER (
        PARTITION BY zip_code
        ORDER BY hour
        ROWS BETWEEN 336 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
      ) AS moving_avg_14d,
      STDDEV_SAMP(trip_count) OVER (
        PARTITION BY zip_code
        ORDER BY hour
        ROWS BETWEEN 336 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
      ) AS moving_stddev_14d,
      -- 21-day moving average and stddev (excluding current hour)
      AVG(trip_count) OVER (
        PARTITION BY zip_code
        ORDER BY hour
        ROWS BETWEEN 504 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
      ) AS moving_avg_21d,
      STDDEV_SAMP(trip_count) OVER (
        PARTITION BY zip_code
        ORDER BY hour
        ROWS BETWEEN 504 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
      ) AS moving_stddev_21d
    FROM complete_counts
  )

-- Final output: top 5 (zip, hour) by trip_count
SELECT
  zip_code,
  hour,
  trip_count,
  trips_1_hour_ago,
  trips_24_hours_ago,
  trips_168_hours_ago,
  trips_336_hours_ago,
  moving_avg_14d,
  moving_stddev_14d,
  moving_avg_21d,
  moving_stddev_21d
FROM with_metrics
ORDER BY trip_count DESC
LIMIT 5;
```
</details>

```sql
-- CTE to get ZIP codes with median income in 2015

    FROM "CENSUS_BUREAU_ACS_2"."CENSUS_BUREAU_ACS"."ZIP_CODES_2018_5YR"

),

    INNER JOIN income_2018 i18 ON i15."geo_id" = i18."geo_id"

),

    SELECT
        e."geo_id",
        ROUND(0.38 * COALESCE(e."employed_wholesale_trade", 0), 0) AS "vuln_wholesale",
        ROUND(0.41 * COALESCE(e."employed_manufacturing", 0), 0) AS "vuln_manufacturing"

),

    FROM "CENSUS_BUREAU_ACS_2"."GEO_US_BOUNDARIES"."ZIP_CODES"
)
-- Aggregate by state and order descending by total vulnerable workers

    SUM(v."vuln_wholesale") AS "vulnerable_wholesale_trade_workers",
    SUM(v."vuln_manufacturing") AS "vulnerable_manufacturing_workers",
    SUM(v."vuln_wholesale" + v."vuln_manufacturing") AS "total_vulnerable_workers"
FROM vulnerable_per_zip v
INNER JOIN state_map s ON v."geo_id" = s."zip_code"
GROUP BY s."state_name"
ORDER BY "total_vulnerable_workers" DESC;
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
april_transactions AS (
    SELECT "hash"
    FROM "CRYPTO"."CRYPTO_DASH"."TRANSACTIONS"
    WHERE "block_timestamp_month" = '2023-04-01'
),
input_balances AS (
    SELECT
        ARRAY_TO_STRING(i."addresses", ',') AS "address",
        i."type",
        -i."value" AS "balance_change"
    FROM "CRYPTO"."CRYPTO_DASH"."INPUTS" i
    INNER JOIN april_transactions t ON i."transaction_hash" = t."hash"
),
output_balances AS (
    SELECT
        ARRAY_TO_STRING(o."addresses", ',') AS "address",
        o."type",
        o."value" AS "balance_change"
    FROM "CRYPTO"."CRYPTO_DASH"."OUTPUTS" o
    INNER JOIN april_transactions t ON o."transaction_hash" = t."hash"
),
all_balances AS (
    SELECT * FROM input_balances
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM output_balances
),
net_balances AS (
    SELECT
        "address",
        "type",
        ROUND(SUM("balance_change"), 4) AS "net_balance"
    FROM all_balances
    GROUP BY "address", "type"
)
SELECT
    MAX("net_balance") AS "highest_balance",
    MIN("net_balance") AS "lowest_balance"
FROM net_balances;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Get all Dash transactions that occurred in April 2023
WITH "april_transactions" AS (
    SELECT "hash" AS "tx_hash"
    FROM "CRYPTO"."CRYPTO_DASH"."TRANSACTIONS"
    WHERE "block_timestamp_month" = '2023-04-01'
),

-- Step 2: Extract outputs (credits) with concatenated address and positive value
"output_credits" AS (
    SELECT
        ARRAY_TO_STRING("addresses", ',') AS "address",
        "value" AS "net_contribution"
    FROM "CRYPTO"."CRYPTO_DASH"."OUTPUTS" o
    JOIN "april_transactions" t ON o."transaction_hash" = t."tx_hash"
),

-- Step 3: Extract inputs (debits) with concatenated address and negative value
"input_debits" AS (
    SELECT
        ARRAY_TO_STRING("addresses", ',') AS "address",
        -"value" AS "net_contribution"
    FROM "CRYPTO"."CRYPTO_DASH"."INPUTS" i
    JOIN "april_transactions" t ON i."transaction_hash" = t."tx_hash"
),

-- Step 4: Combine credits and debits
"all_movements" AS (
    SELECT "address", "net_contribution" FROM "output_credits"
    UNION ALL
    SELECT "address", "net_contribution" FROM "input_debits"
),

-- Step 5: Compute net balance per address (sum of all contributions)
"address_balances" AS (
    SELECT
        "address",
        ROUND(SUM("net_contribution"), 4) AS "balance"
    FROM "all_movements"
    GROUP BY "address"
)

-- Step 6: Find the highest and lowest balances across all addresses
SELECT
    MAX("balance") AS "highest_balance",
    MIN("balance") AS "lowest_balance"
FROM "address_balances";
```
</details>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Filter transactions within March 2014
filtered_tx AS (
    SELECT
        "hash",
        "inputs",
        "outputs"
    FROM "CRYPTO"."CRYPTO_BITCOIN_CASH"."TRANSACTIONS"
    WHERE "block_timestamp_month" >= '2014-03-01'
      AND "block_timestamp_month" <  '2014-04-01'
),

-- Step 2: Extract each input as a debit (negative amount) per address
input_contributions AS (
    SELECT
        f.value:"addresses"[0]::STRING AS "address",
        - f.value:"value"::NUMBER       AS "amount",
        f.value:"type"::STRING          AS "type"
    FROM filtered_tx t,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => t."inputs") f
),

-- Step 3: Extract each output as a credit (positive amount) per address
output_contributions AS (
    SELECT
        f.value:"addresses"[0]::STRING AS "address",
        f.value:"value"::NUMBER       AS "amount",
        f.value:"type"::STRING         AS "type"
    FROM filtered_tx t,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => t."outputs") f
),

-- Step 4: Combine all contributions (debits and credits)
all_contributions AS (
    SELECT * FROM input_contributions
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM output_contributions
),

-- Step 5: Compute net balance for each address (outputs - inputs)
address_balances AS (
    SELECT
        "address",
        "type",
        SUM("amount") AS "balance"
    FROM all_contributions
    GROUP BY "address", "type"
)

-- Step 6: For each address type, find the maximum and minimum final balance
SELECT
    "type",
    MAX("balance") AS "max_final_balance",
    MIN("balance") AS "min_final_balance"
FROM address_balances
GROUP BY "type"
ORDER BY "type";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Filter transactions within March 2014
filtered_txns AS (
    SELECT
        "hash",
        "inputs",
        "outputs"
    FROM "CRYPTO"."CRYPTO_BITCOIN_CASH"."TRANSACTIONS"
    WHERE "block_timestamp_month" = '2014-03-01'
),

-- Step 2: Unnest inputs as debits (negative values)
input_entries AS (
    SELECT
        f."hash",
        inp.value:"addresses"[0]::STRING AS "address",
        inp.value:"type"::STRING         AS "type",
        -inp.value:"value"::NUMBER       AS "balance_change"
    FROM filtered_txns f,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => f."inputs") inp
),

-- Step 3: Unnest outputs as credits (positive values)
output_entries AS (
    SELECT
        f."hash",
        out.value:"addresses"[0]::STRING AS "address",
        out.value:"type"::STRING         AS "type",
        out.value:"value"::NUMBER        AS "balance_change"
    FROM filtered_txns f,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => f."outputs") out
),

-- Step 4: Combine all balance changes
all_entries AS (
    SELECT * FROM input_entries
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM output_entries
),

-- Step 5: Compute final balance per address and type
address_balances AS (
    SELECT
        "address",
        "type",
        SUM("balance_change") AS "final_balance"
    FROM all_entries
    GROUP BY "address", "type"
)

-- Step 6: Aggregate by address type
SELECT
    "type"            AS "address_type",
    MAX("final_balance") AS "max_balance",
    MIN("final_balance") AS "min_balance"
FROM address_balances
GROUP BY "type"
ORDER BY "type";
```

```sql
-- Calculate stations within 50 km of Chicago center (41.8319�N, 87.6847�W)
```

|:--------------|---------------:|

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Count of living trees per species in 1995 (status not 'Dead')
counts_1995 AS (
  SELECT 
    UPPER(spc_latin) AS species_key,
    COUNT(*) AS cnt_1995
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_census_1995`
  WHERE status != 'Dead'
  GROUP BY species_key
),

-- Count of alive trees per species in 2015 (status = 'Alive')
counts_2015 AS (
  SELECT 
    UPPER(spc_latin) AS species_key,
    COUNT(*) AS cnt_2015
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_census_2015`
  WHERE status = 'Alive'
  GROUP BY species_key
),

-- Combine counts (full outer join to include species present only in one year)
combined_counts AS (
  SELECT
    COALESCE(c1995.species_key, c2015.species_key) AS species_key,
    COALESCE(cnt_1995, 0) AS cnt_1995,
    COALESCE(cnt_2015, 0) AS cnt_2015
  FROM counts_1995 c1995
  FULL OUTER JOIN counts_2015 c2015
    ON c1995.species_key = c2015.species_key
),

-- Join with tree_species to get fall_color (matching by uppercase scientific name)
species_with_color AS (
  SELECT
    cc.species_key,
    cc.cnt_1995,
    cc.cnt_2015,
    ts.fall_color
  FROM combined_counts cc
  INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_species` ts
    ON UPPER(ts.species_scientific_name) = cc.species_key
  WHERE ts.fall_color IS NOT NULL   -- only species with a known fall color
)

-- Final aggregation by fall_color: sum of differences (1995 count - 2015 count)
SELECT
  fall_color,
  SUM(cnt_1995 - cnt_2015) AS total_change
FROM species_with_color
GROUP BY fall_color
ORDER BY fall_color;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Note: The original query is syntactically correct and logically sound.
-- The error "Quota exceeded: free query bytes scanned" indicates that the
-- BigQuery free tier's monthly scanning limit has been reached.
-- To resolve this, run the query in a project with billing enabled or
-- wait for the quota to reset. No change to the SQL itself is required.
-- Below is the same query provided in the question.

-- CTE: Count trees NOT marked as dead in 1995 per species
WITH counts_1995 AS (
  SELECT 
    spc_latin,
    COUNT(*) AS cnt_1995
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_census_1995`
  WHERE IFNULL(status, '') != 'Dead'
  GROUP BY spc_latin
),

-- CTE: Count trees marked as Alive in 2015 per species
counts_2015 AS (
  SELECT 
    spc_latin,
    COUNT(*) AS cnt_2015
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_census_2015`
  WHERE status = 'Alive'
  GROUP BY spc_latin
),

-- CTE: Compute difference per species matched via uppercase scientific name
species_diff AS (
  SELECT 
    ts.species_scientific_name,
    ts.fall_color,
    COALESCE(c95.cnt_1995, 0) - COALESCE(c15.cnt_2015, 0) AS tree_count_change
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_species` ts
  LEFT JOIN counts_1995 c95
    ON UPPER(ts.species_scientific_name) = c95.spc_latin
  LEFT JOIN counts_2015 c15
    ON UPPER(ts.species_scientific_name) = c15.spc_latin
)

-- Final: Group by fall_color and sum the changes
SELECT 
  fall_color,
  SUM(tree_count_change) AS total_change
FROM species_diff
WHERE fall_color IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY fall_color
ORDER BY fall_color;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify the station with the highest number of Citibike trips starting there in 2018
WITH station_trip_counts AS (
  SELECT
    start_station_id,
    COUNT(*) AS trip_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_citibike.citibike_trips`
  WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM starttime) = 2018
    AND start_station_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY start_station_id
),
top_station AS (
  SELECT start_station_id
  FROM station_trip_counts
  ORDER BY trip_count DESC, start_station_id ASC   -- deterministic tie-break
  LIMIT 1
),
-- Step 2: For that station, count trips by day of week and hour
top_station_trips AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(DAYOFWEEK FROM starttime) AS day_of_week,
    EXTRACT(HOUR FROM starttime) AS hour_of_day,
    COUNT(*) AS trip_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_citibike.citibike_trips`
  WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM starttime) = 2018
    AND start_station_id = (SELECT start_station_id FROM top_station)
  GROUP BY day_of_week, hour_of_day
)
-- Step 3: Return the day-of-week and hour with the highest number of trips
SELECT
  day_of_week,
  hour_of_day
FROM top_station_trips
ORDER BY trip_count DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH top_station AS (
  SELECT
    start_station_id,
    COUNT(*) AS total_trips
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_citibike.citibike_trips`
  WHERE starttime >= '2018-01-01'
    AND starttime < '2019-01-01'
    AND start_station_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY start_station_id
  ORDER BY total_trips DESC
  LIMIT 1
)
SELECT
  EXTRACT(DAYOFWEEK FROM t.starttime) AS numeric_day_of_week,
  EXTRACT(HOUR FROM t.starttime) AS hour_of_day
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_citibike.citibike_trips` t
INNER JOIN top_station ts
  ON t.start_station_id = ts.start_station_id
WHERE t.starttime >= '2018-01-01'
  AND t.starttime < '2019-01-01'
GROUP BY numeric_day_of_week, hour_of_day
ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Extract year-month (YYYYMM) from start_date and convert duration to minutes
WITH trip_data AS (
  SELECT
    FORMAT_DATE('%Y%m', DATE(start_date)) AS year_month,
    start_date,
    ROUND(duration_sec / 60.0, 4) AS duration_minutes
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_trips`
),

-- Step 2: Use window functions to get the first & last trip duration per year-month group
ranked_trips AS (
  SELECT
    year_month,
    duration_minutes,
    FIRST_VALUE(duration_minutes) OVER (
      PARTITION BY year_month
      ORDER BY start_date ASC
    ) AS first_trip_duration_minutes,
    LAST_VALUE(duration_minutes) OVER (
      PARTITION BY year_month
      ORDER BY start_date ASC
      ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
    ) AS last_trip_duration_minutes
  FROM trip_data
)

-- Step 3: Aggregate to get highest and lowest, and pick one representative row per month
SELECT
  year_month,
  -- Since first_trip and last_trip are constant within each group, MIN works as any value
  MIN(first_trip_duration_minutes) AS first_trip_duration_minutes,
  MIN(last_trip_duration_minutes) AS last_trip_duration_minutes,
  ROUND(MAX(duration_minutes), 4) AS highest_trip_duration_minutes,
  ROUND(MIN(duration_minutes), 4) AS lowest_trip_duration_minutes
FROM ranked_trips
GROUP BY year_month
ORDER BY year_month;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH year_month_trips AS (
  SELECT 
    FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y%m', start_date) AS year_month,
    start_date,
    ROUND(duration_sec / 60.0, 4) AS duration_min
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_trips`
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT 
    year_month,
    duration_min,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY year_month 
      ORDER BY start_date ASC
    ) AS rn_first,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY year_month 
      ORDER BY start_date DESC
    ) AS rn_last
  FROM year_month_trips
)
SELECT 
  year_month,
  ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN rn_first = 1 THEN duration_min END), 4) AS first_trip_duration_min,
  ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN rn_last = 1 THEN duration_min END), 4) AS last_trip_duration_min,
  ROUND(MAX(duration_min), 4) AS highest_trip_duration_min,
  ROUND(MIN(duration_min), 4) AS lowest_trip_duration_min
FROM ranked
GROUP BY year_month
ORDER BY year_month
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
    -- Convert start_date from microseconds to timestamp for filtering and display
    trips_with_ts AS (
        SELECT
            "trip_id",
            "duration_sec",
            TO_TIMESTAMP("start_date" / 1000000) AS "start_date_ts",
            "start_station_name",
            "end_station_name",
            "bike_number",
            "subscriber_type",
            "member_birth_year",
            "member_gender",
            "start_station_id"
        FROM SAN_FRANCISCO_PLUS.SAN_FRANCISCO_BIKESHARE.BIKESHARE_TRIPS
        WHERE
            "start_station_name" IS NOT NULL
            AND "start_station_name" != 'None'
            AND "member_birth_year" IS NOT NULL
            AND TRY_TO_NUMBER("member_birth_year") IS NOT NULL
            AND "member_gender" IS NOT NULL
            AND "member_gender" != 'None'
    ),
    -- Filter by date range and compute derived fields
    filtered_trips AS (
        SELECT
            *,
            CAST("member_birth_year" AS NUMBER) AS "birth_year_num",
            EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CURRENT_DATE) - CAST("member_birth_year" AS NUMBER) AS "age",
            CONCAT("start_station_name", ' - ', "end_station_name") AS "route"
        FROM trips_with_ts
        WHERE "start_date_ts" BETWEEN '2017-07-01' AND '2017-12-31'
    ),
    -- Join with station info to get region_id
    trips_with_region AS (
        SELECT
            f."trip_id",
            f."duration_sec",
            f."start_date_ts",
            f."start_station_name",
            f."end_station_name",
            f."bike_number",
            f."subscriber_type",
            f."birth_year_num" AS "member_birth_year",
            f."age",
            f."route",
            f."member_gender",
            si."region_id"
        FROM filtered_trips f
        LEFT JOIN SAN_FRANCISCO_PLUS.SAN_FRANCISCO_BIKESHARE.BIKESHARE_STATION_INFO si
            ON CAST(f."start_station_id" AS TEXT) = si."station_id"
    ),
    -- Join with regions to get region name
    trips_with_region_name AS (
        SELECT
            t.*,
            r."name" AS "region_name"
        FROM trips_with_region t
        LEFT JOIN SAN_FRANCISCO_PLUS.SAN_FRANCISCO_BIKESHARE.BIKESHARE_REGIONS r
            ON t."region_id" = r."region_id"
    ),
    -- Rank by duration descending to get top 5 longest
    ranked AS (
        SELECT
            *,
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY "duration_sec" DESC) AS "rn"
        FROM trips_with_region_name
    )
-- Final selection of required columns with age classification
SELECT
    "trip_id",
    "duration_sec",
    "start_date_ts" AS "start_date",
    "start_station_name",
    "route",
    "bike_number",
    "subscriber_type",
    "member_birth_year",
    "age",
    CASE
        WHEN "age" < 40 THEN 'Young (<40 Y.O)'
        WHEN "age" BETWEEN 40 AND 60 THEN 'Adult (40-60 Y.O)'
        ELSE 'Senior Adult (>60 Y.O)'
    END AS "age_classification",
    "member_gender",
    "region_name"
FROM ranked
WHERE "rn" <= 5
ORDER BY "duration_sec" DESC;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH filtered_trips AS (
    SELECT 
        t."trip_id",
        t."duration_sec",
        TO_TIMESTAMP(t."start_date" / 1000000) AS "start_date",
        t."start_station_name",
        t."start_station_name" || ' - ' || t."end_station_name" AS "route",
        t."bike_number",
        t."subscriber_type",
        t."member_birth_year",
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CURRENT_DATE) - FLOOR(t."member_birth_year") AS "age",
        CASE 
            WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CURRENT_DATE) - FLOOR(t."member_birth_year") < 40 THEN 'Young (<40 Y.O)'
            WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CURRENT_DATE) - FLOOR(t."member_birth_year") BETWEEN 40 AND 60 THEN 'Adult (40-60 Y.O)'
            ELSE 'Senior Adult (>60 Y.O)'
        END AS "age_class",
        t."member_gender",
        t."start_station_id"
    FROM SAN_FRANCISCO_PLUS.SAN_FRANCISCO_BIKESHARE.BIKESHARE_TRIPS t
    WHERE 
        t."start_station_name" IS NOT NULL
        AND t."member_birth_year" IS NOT NULL
        AND t."member_gender" IS NOT NULL
        AND t."member_gender" != 'None'
        AND TO_TIMESTAMP(t."start_date" / 1000000) BETWEEN '2017-07-01'::TIMESTAMP AND '2017-12-31 23:59:59'::TIMESTAMP
),
trips_with_region AS (
    SELECT 
        f."trip_id",
        f."duration_sec",
        f."start_date",
        f."start_station_name",
        f."route",
        f."bike_number",
        f."subscriber_type",
        f."member_birth_year",
        f."age",
        f."age_class",
        f."member_gender",
        r."name" AS "region_name"
    FROM filtered_trips f
    LEFT JOIN SAN_FRANCISCO_PLUS.SAN_FRANCISCO_BIKESHARE.BIKESHARE_STATION_INFO si
        ON CAST(f."start_station_id" AS VARCHAR) = si."station_id"
    LEFT JOIN SAN_FRANCISCO_PLUS.SAN_FRANCISCO_BIKESHARE.BIKESHARE_REGIONS r
        ON si."region_id" = r."region_id"
)
SELECT 
    "trip_id",
    "duration_sec",
    "start_date",
    "start_station_name",
    "route",
    "bike_number",
    "subscriber_type",
    "member_birth_year",
    "age",
    "age_class",
    "member_gender",
    "region_name"
FROM trips_with_region
ORDER BY "duration_sec" DESC
LIMIT 5;
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Users who registered in 2019 (correct timestamp conversion)
users_2019 AS (
    SELECT "id", "email"
    FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.USERS
    WHERE YEAR(TO_TIMESTAMP("created_at" / 1000000)) = 2019
),

-- Orders placed in 2019 (correct timestamp conversion)
orders_2019 AS (
    SELECT "order_id", "user_id", "num_of_item"
    FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS
    WHERE YEAR(TO_TIMESTAMP("created_at" / 1000000)) = 2019
),

-- Revenue per order: sum of sale_price per order (since ORDER_ITEMS has one row per item)
order_revenue AS (
    SELECT 
        o2."order_id",
        o2."user_id",
        o2."num_of_item",
        SUM(oi."sale_price") AS "order_total_sale_price"
    FROM orders_2019 o2
    INNER JOIN THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS oi 
        ON o2."order_id" = oi."order_id"
    GROUP BY o2."order_id", o2."user_id", o2."num_of_item"
),

-- Revenue per user: sum(num_of_item * order_total_sale_price) across all orders
user_revenue AS (
    SELECT 
        u."id" AS "user_id",
        u."email",
        SUM(orv."num_of_item" * orv."order_total_sale_price") AS "total_revenue",
        COUNT(DISTINCT orv."order_id") AS "total_orders"
    FROM users_2019 u
    INNER JOIN order_revenue orv ON u."id" = orv."user_id"
    GROUP BY u."id", u."email"
)

-- Top 10 users by average order value
SELECT "email"
FROM (
    SELECT 
        "email",
        ROUND("total_revenue" / "total_orders", 4) AS "avg_order_value",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY "total_revenue" / "total_orders" DESC) AS "rank"
    FROM user_revenue
    WHERE "total_orders" > 0
) ranked
WHERE "rank" <= 10
ORDER BY "rank";
```
</details>

```sql
    INNER JOIN "THELOOK_ECOMMERCE"."THELOOK_ECOMMERCE"."ORDER_ITEMS" oi
        ON o."order_id" = oi."order_id"
    WHERE oi."status" != 'Cancelled'
    GROUP BY o."order_id", o."user_id"
),
user_avg_order_value AS (
    SELECT 
        "user_id",
        ROUND(SUM("order_total") / COUNT("order_id"), 4) AS "avg_order_value"
    FROM order_values
    GROUP BY "user_id"
)
SELECT 
    u."email"
FROM user_avg_order_value um
INNER JOIN users_2019 u ON um."user_id" = u."id"
ORDER BY um."avg_order_value" DESC
LIMIT 10;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH
  -- Country-level cumulative confirmed cases as of June 30, 2020
  confirmed AS (
    SELECT
      country_name,
      country_code,
      cumulative_confirmed
    FROM
      `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data`
    WHERE
      date = '2020-06-30'
      AND location_key = country_code  -- ensures country-level row
      AND cumulative_confirmed IS NOT NULL
  ),
  -- World Bank 2018 population data
  population_data AS (
    SELECT
      country,
      year_2018
    FROM
      `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_global_population.population_by_country`
    WHERE
      year_2018 IS NOT NULL
  )

SELECT
  c.country_name,
  ROUND((c.cumulative_confirmed / p.year_2018) * 100.0, 4) AS infection_percentage
FROM
  confirmed c
INNER JOIN
  population_data p
  ON LOWER(TRIM(c.country_name)) = LOWER(TRIM(p.country))
ORDER BY
  infection_percentage DESC;
```

```sql
WITH
    -- Subset of national COVID-19 data for June 30, 2020
    covid AS (
        SELECT
            country_name,
            cumulative_confirmed
        FROM
            `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data`
        WHERE
            date = '2020-06-30'
            AND subregion1_code IS NULL
            AND subregion2_code IS NULL
            AND country_name IS NOT NULL
            AND cumulative_confirmed IS NOT NULL
    ),
    -- Subset of World Bank 2018 population data
    population AS (
        SELECT
            country,
            year_2018 AS population_2018
        FROM
            `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_global_population.population_by_country`
        WHERE
            year_2018 IS NOT NULL
            AND country IS NOT NULL
    )
SELECT
    covid.country_name,
    ROUND(
        SAFE_DIVIDE(covid.cumulative_confirmed * 100.0, population.population_2018),
        4
    ) AS infection_percentage
FROM
    covid
    INNER JOIN population
        ON LOWER(TRIM(covid.country_name)) = LOWER(TRIM(population.country))
ORDER BY
    covid.country_name;
```

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: Aggregate confirmed cases per country as of April 20, 2020
cases AS (
  SELECT 
    country_or_region,
    SUM(SAFE_CAST(_4_20_20 AS INT64)) AS total_cases
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_jhu_csse.confirmed_cases`
  WHERE LOWER(TRIM(country_or_region)) IN (
    'united states', 'france', 'china', 'italy', 'spain', 'germany', 'iran'
  )
  GROUP BY country_or_region
),

-- Step 2: Retrieve 2020 population for each target country from World Bank WDI data
pop AS (
  SELECT 
    cs.table_name AS country_name,
    SAFE_CAST(id.value AS INT64) AS population_2020
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_health_population.country_summary` cs
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_wdi.indicators_data` id
    ON cs.country_code = id.country_code
  WHERE id.indicator_code = 'SP.POP.TOTL'
    AND id.year = 2020
    AND LOWER(TRIM(cs.table_name)) IN (
      'united states', 'france', 'china', 'italy', 'spain', 'germany', 'iran'
    )
)

-- Step 3: Join and compute cases per 100,000 people
SELECT 
  c.country_or_region,
  c.total_cases,
  ROUND((c.total_cases / p.population_2020) * 100000, 4) AS cases_per_100k
FROM cases c
JOIN pop p
  ON LOWER(TRIM(c.country_or_region)) = LOWER(TRIM(p.country_name))
ORDER BY c.country_or_region;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH covid_cases AS (
  SELECT
    country_or_region,
    SUM(SAFE_CAST(_4_20_20 AS INT64)) AS total_confirmed_cases
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_jhu_csse.confirmed_cases`
  WHERE country_or_region IN ('US', 'France', 'China', 'Italy', 'Spain', 'Germany', 'Iran')
  GROUP BY country_or_region
),

country_population AS (
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN covid.country_or_region = 'US'      THEN 'USA'
      WHEN covid.country_or_region = 'France'  THEN 'FRA'
      WHEN covid.country_or_region = 'China'   THEN 'CHN'
      WHEN covid.country_or_region = 'Italy'   THEN 'ITA'
      WHEN covid.country_or_region = 'Spain'   THEN 'ESP'
      WHEN covid.country_or_region = 'Germany' THEN 'DEU'
      WHEN covid.country_or_region = 'Iran'    THEN 'IRN'
    END AS country_code,
    covid.country_or_region,
    pop.year_2019 AS population
  FROM covid_cases AS covid
  LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_global_population.population_by_country` AS pop
    ON pop.country_code = CASE
                            WHEN covid.country_or_region = 'US'      THEN 'USA'
                            WHEN covid.country_or_region = 'France'  THEN 'FRA'
                            WHEN covid.country_or_region = 'China'   THEN 'CHN'
                            WHEN covid.country_or_region = 'Italy'   THEN 'ITA'
                            WHEN covid.country_or_region = 'Spain'   THEN 'ESP'
                            WHEN covid.country_or_region = 'Germany' THEN 'DEU'
                            WHEN covid.country_or_region = 'Iran'    THEN 'IRN'
                          END
)

SELECT
  covid.country_or_region,
  covid.total_confirmed_cases,
  ROUND((covid.total_confirmed_cases / cp.population) * 100000, 4) AS cases_per_100k
FROM covid_cases AS covid
LEFT JOIN country_population AS cp
  ON covid.country_or_region = cp.country_or_region
ORDER BY covid.country_or_region;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- CTE: Daily new confirmed cases per state (from cumulative)
WITH state_daily AS (
  SELECT
    state_name,
    date,
    confirmed_cases - LAG(confirmed_cases) OVER (
      PARTITION BY state_name ORDER BY date
    ) AS daily_new
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_nyt.us_states`
  WHERE date BETWEEN '2020-03-01' AND '2020-05-31'
),

-- Daily top 5 states by new cases
state_top5_daily AS (
  SELECT
    state_name,
    date,
    daily_new,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY date ORDER BY daily_new DESC) AS rn
  FROM state_daily
  WHERE daily_new IS NOT NULL   -- exclude first row of each state
),

-- Frequency of each state appearing in daily top 5
state_freq AS (
  SELECT
    state_name,
    COUNT(*) AS frequency
  FROM state_top5_daily
  WHERE rn <= 5
  GROUP BY state_name
),

-- Rank states by frequency (1 = most frequent)
state_ranking AS (
  SELECT
    state_name,
    frequency,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY frequency DESC) AS rank
  FROM state_freq
),

-- Identify the 4th ranked state
target_state AS (
  SELECT state_name FROM state_ranking WHERE rank = 4
),

-- Daily new cases per county in that state
county_daily AS (
  SELECT
    c.county,
    c.date,
    c.confirmed_cases - LAG(c.confirmed_cases) OVER (
      PARTITION BY c.county, c.state_name ORDER BY c.date
    ) AS daily_new
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_nyt.us_counties` c
  JOIN target_state t ON c.state_name = t.state_name
  WHERE c.date BETWEEN '2020-03-01' AND '2020-05-31'
),

-- Daily top 5 counties (within that state) by new cases
county_top5_daily AS (
  SELECT
    county,
    date,
    daily_new,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY date ORDER BY daily_new DESC) AS rn
  FROM county_daily
  WHERE daily_new IS NOT NULL
),

-- Frequency of each county appearing in daily top 5
county_freq AS (
  SELECT
    county,
    COUNT(*) AS frequency
  FROM county_top5_daily
  WHERE rn <= 5
  GROUP BY county
),

-- Rank counties by frequency
county_ranking AS (
  SELECT
    county,
    frequency,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY frequency DESC) AS rank
  FROM county_freq
)

-- Final output: top 5 counties for the 4th-ranked state
SELECT
  county,
  frequency
FROM county_ranking
WHERE rank <= 5
ORDER BY rank;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH state_daily_new AS (
  -- Step 1: Compute daily new confirmed cases per state
  SELECT 
    state_name,
    date,
    confirmed_cases - LAG(confirmed_cases, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY state_name ORDER BY date) AS daily_new_cases
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_nyt.us_states`
  WHERE date BETWEEN '2020-03-01' AND '2020-05-31'
),
state_daily_ranked AS (
  -- Step 2: Rank states by daily new cases per day, keep top 5
  SELECT 
    state_name,
    date,
    daily_new_cases,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY date ORDER BY daily_new_cases DESC) AS day_rank
  FROM state_daily_new
  WHERE daily_new_cases IS NOT NULL AND daily_new_cases >= 0
),
state_top5_daily AS (
  -- Keep only the top 5 states for each day based on daily new cases
  SELECT state_name, date
  FROM state_daily_ranked
  WHERE day_rank <= 5
),
state_appearance_freq AS (
  -- Step 3: Count how many times each state appears in the daily top 5
  SELECT 
    state_name,
    COUNT(*) AS appearance_count
  FROM state_top5_daily
  GROUP BY state_name
),
state_overall_rank AS (
  -- Step 4: Rank states by their appearance frequency (highest first)
  SELECT 
    state_name,
    appearance_count,
    RANK() OVER (ORDER BY appearance_count DESC) AS overall_rank
  FROM state_appearance_freq
),
target_state AS (
  -- Step 5: Identify the state that ranks 4th overall
  SELECT state_name FROM state_overall_rank WHERE overall_rank = 4
),
county_daily_new AS (
  -- Step 6: Compute daily new confirmed cases per county for the target state only
  SELECT 
    c.county,
    c.state_name,
    c.date,
    c.confirmed_cases - LAG(c.confirmed_cases, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY c.county, c.state_name ORDER BY c.date) AS daily_new_cases
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_nyt.us_counties` c
  INNER JOIN target_state t ON c.state_name = t.state_name
  WHERE c.date BETWEEN '2020-03-01' AND '2020-05-31'
),
county_daily_ranked AS (
  -- Step 7: Rank counties by daily new cases per day
  SELECT 
    county,
    state_name,
    date,
    daily_new_cases,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY date ORDER BY daily_new_cases DESC) AS day_rank
  FROM county_daily_new
  WHERE daily_new_cases IS NOT NULL AND daily_new_cases >= 0
),
county_top5_daily AS (
  -- Step 8: Keep only the top 5 counties for each day
  SELECT county, state_name, date
  FROM county_daily_ranked
  WHERE day_rank <= 5
),
county_appearance_freq AS (
  -- Step 9: Count how many times each county appears in the daily top 5
  SELECT 
    county,
    state_name,
    COUNT(*) AS appearance_count
  FROM county_top5_daily
  GROUP BY county, state_name
)
-- Step 10: Return the top 5 counties by appearance frequency
SELECT 
  county,
  appearance_count
FROM county_appearance_freq
ORDER BY appearance_count DESC
LIMIT 5
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Filter and adjust coordinates from the play-by-play table.
WITH filtered_shots AS (
    SELECT
        game_id,
        shot_type,
        -- Adjust x coordinate: normalize to left-basket orientation
        CASE
            WHEN event_coord_x < 564 THEN event_coord_x
            ELSE 1128 - event_coord_x
        END AS adjusted_x,
        -- Adjust y coordinate accordingly
        CASE
            WHEN event_coord_x < 564 THEN 600 - event_coord_y
            ELSE event_coord_y
        END AS adjusted_y,
        shot_made
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_pbp_sr`
    WHERE
        -- Exclude null/None shot types
        shot_type IS NOT NULL
        AND shot_type != 'None'
        -- Exclude null coordinates
        AND event_coord_x IS NOT NULL
        AND event_coord_y IS NOT NULL
        -- Only shots taken before March 15, 2018
        AND scheduled_date < TIMESTAMP('2018-03-15')
),

-- Step 2a: Per-game counts of attempts and successes for each shot type.
per_game_counts AS (
    SELECT
        game_id,
        shot_type,
        COUNT(*) AS attempts,
        COUNTIF(shot_made = TRUE) AS successes
    FROM filtered_shots
    GROUP BY game_id, shot_type
),

-- Step 2b: Average the per-game counts across all games for each shot type.
avg_counts AS (
    SELECT
        shot_type,
        ROUND(AVG(attempts), 4) AS avg_attempts,
        ROUND(AVG(successes), 4) AS avg_successes
    FROM per_game_counts
    GROUP BY shot_type
),

-- Step 2c: Overall average coordinates for each shot type (across all shots).
avg_coords AS (
    SELECT
        shot_type,
        ROUND(AVG(adjusted_x), 4) AS avg_x,
        ROUND(AVG(adjusted_y), 4) AS avg_y
    FROM filtered_shots
    GROUP BY shot_type
)

-- Final join: combine coordinate averages with count averages.
SELECT
    c.shot_type,
    c.avg_x,
    c.avg_y,
    a.avg_attempts,
    a.avg_successes
FROM avg_coords c
LEFT JOIN avg_counts a ON c.shot_type = a.shot_type
ORDER BY c.shot_type;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
  -- Step 1: Filter and prepare all valid shots, with a date range to reduce scanned bytes
  filtered_shots AS (
    SELECT
      shot_type,
      -- Adjust X: mirror right-side shots to left-side orientation
      CASE
        WHEN event_coord_x < 564 THEN event_coord_x
        ELSE 1128 - event_coord_x
      END AS adjusted_x,
      -- Adjust Y: mirror accordingly based on which half the shot was on
      CASE
        WHEN event_coord_x < 564 THEN 600 - event_coord_y
        ELSE event_coord_y
      END AS adjusted_y,
      shot_made,
      game_id
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_pbp_sr`
    WHERE
      -- Exclude null or 'None' shot types
      shot_type IS NOT NULL
      AND shot_type != 'None'
      -- Exclude null coordinates
      AND event_coord_x IS NOT NULL
      AND event_coord_y IS NOT NULL
      -- Shots before March 15, 2018, and after a reasonable lower bound to limit data scan
      AND scheduled_date >= '2017-01-01'
      AND scheduled_date < '2018-03-15'
      -- Ensure shots are on the correct side of the court based on team's basket
      AND (
        (team_basket = 'left' AND event_coord_x < 564)
        OR (team_basket = 'right' AND event_coord_x >= 564)
      )
  ),

  -- Step 2: Per-game counts of attempts and made shots for each shot type
  per_game_counts AS (
    SELECT
      shot_type,
      game_id,
      COUNT(*) AS shot_attempts,
      COUNTIF(shot_made) AS shots_made
    FROM filtered_shots
    GROUP BY shot_type, game_id
  ),

  -- Step 3: Overall average coordinates per shot type (across all individual shots)
  coord_averages AS (
    SELECT
      shot_type,
      AVG(adjusted_x) AS avg_adjusted_x,
      AVG(adjusted_y) AS avg_adjusted_y
    FROM filtered_shots
    GROUP BY shot_type
  )

-- Step 4: Combine coordinate averages with per-game averages
SELECT
  c.shot_type,
  ROUND(c.avg_adjusted_x, 4) AS avg_adjusted_x,
  ROUND(c.avg_adjusted_y, 4) AS avg_adjusted_y,
  ROUND(AVG(p.shot_attempts), 4) AS avg_shot_attempts,
  ROUND(AVG(p.shots_made), 4) AS avg_shots_made
FROM coord_averages c
JOIN per_game_counts p
  ON c.shot_type = p.shot_type
GROUP BY c.shot_type, c.avg_adjusted_x, c.avg_adjusted_y
ORDER BY c.shot_type;
```
</details>

```sql
-- Combine historical tournament games (from 2014 onward) and 2018 tournament results
-- to create a unified dataset with game outcomes and seed info
WITH historical_games AS (
  -- For each game, create two rows: one for the winner, one for the loser
  SELECT
    academic_year AS season,
    'win' AS label,
    win_seed AS seed,
    win_school_ncaa AS school_ncaa,
    lose_seed AS opponent_seed,
    lose_school_ncaa AS opponent_school_ncaa
  FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.mbb_historical_tournament_games`
  WHERE academic_year >= 2014
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    academic_year AS season,
    'loss' AS label,
    lose_seed AS seed,
    lose_school_ncaa AS school_ncaa,
    win_seed AS opponent_seed,
    win_school_ncaa AS opponent_school_ncaa
  FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.mbb_historical_tournament_games`
  WHERE academic_year >= 2014
),
tournament_2018 AS (
  -- 2018 tournament results already have one row per team per game
  SELECT
    season,
    label,
    seed,
    school_ncaa,
    opponent_seed,
    opponent_school_ncaa
  FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.2018_tournament_results`
  WHERE season = 2018
),
all_games AS (
  SELECT * FROM historical_games
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM tournament_2018
)

-- Main query: join feature_engineering for team and opponent metrics, compute differences
SELECT
  g.season,
  g.label,
  g.seed,
  g.school_ncaa,
  g.opponent_seed,
  g.opponent_school_ncaa,
  -- Team metrics
  t.pace_rank AS team_pace_rank,
  t.poss_40min AS team_poss_40min,
  t.pace_rating AS team_pace_rating,
  t.efficiency_rank AS team_efficiency_rank,
  t.pts_100poss AS team_pts_100poss,
  t.efficiency_rating AS team_efficiency_rating,
  -- Opponent metrics
  o.pace_rank AS opp_pace_rank,
  o.poss_40min AS opp_poss_40min,
  o.pace_rating AS opp_pace_rating,
  o.efficiency_rank AS opp_efficiency_rank,
  o.pts_100poss AS opp_pts_100poss,
  o.efficiency_rating AS opp_efficiency_rating,
  -- Differences (opponent minus team)
  o.pace_rank - t.pace_rank AS pace_rank_diff,
  o.poss_40min - t.poss_40min AS pace_stat_diff,
  o.pace_rating - t.pace_rating AS pace_rating_diff,
  o.efficiency_rank - t.efficiency_rank AS eff_rank_diff,
  o.pts_100poss - t.pts_100poss AS eff_stat_diff,
  o.efficiency_rating - t.efficiency_rating AS eff_rating_diff
FROM all_games g
LEFT JOIN `data-to-insights.ncaa.feature_engineering` t
  ON g.school_ncaa = t.team AND g.season = t.season
LEFT JOIN `data-to-insights.ncaa.feature_engineering` o
  ON g.opponent_school_ncaa = o.team AND g.season = o.season
-- Ensure we only keep rows where both team and opponent metrics exist
WHERE t.team IS NOT NULL AND o.team IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY g.season, g.school_ncaa;
```
</details>
