```sql
WITH historical_games AS (
  SELECT 
    academic_year AS season,
    'win' AS label,
    win_seed AS seed,
    win_school_ncaa AS school_ncaa,
    lose_seed AS opponent_seed,
    lose_school_ncaa AS opponent_school_ncaa
  FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.mbb_historical_tournament_games`
  WHERE academic_year BETWEEN 2014 AND 2017
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 
    academic_year AS season,
    'loss' AS label,
    lose_seed AS seed,
    lose_school_ncaa AS school_ncaa,
    win_seed AS opponent_seed,
    win_school_ncaa AS opponent_school_ncaa
  FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.mbb_historical_tournament_games`
  WHERE academic_year BETWEEN 2014 AND 2017
),

games_2018 AS (
  SELECT 
    season,
    label,
    seed,
    school_ncaa,
    opponent_seed,
    opponent_school_ncaa
  FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.2018_tournament_results`
  WHERE season = 2018
),

all_games AS (
  SELECT * FROM historical_games
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM games_2018
),

-- Pre-filter feature_engineering to relevant seasons only
filtered_features AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.feature_engineering`
  WHERE season >= 2014
)

SELECT 
  g.season,
  g.label,
  g.seed,
  g.school_ncaa,
  g.opponent_seed,
  g.opponent_school_ncaa,
  tm.pace_rank,
  tm.poss_40min,
  tm.pace_rating,
  tm.efficiency_rank,
  tm.pts_100poss,
  tm.efficiency_rating,
  opp.pace_rank AS opp_pace_rank,
  opp.poss_40min AS opp_poss_40min,
  opp.pace_rating AS opp_pace_rating,
  opp.efficiency_rank AS opp_efficiency_rank,
  opp.pts_100poss AS opp_pts_100poss,
  opp.efficiency_rating AS opp_efficiency_rating,
  opp.pace_rank - tm.pace_rank AS pace_rank_diff,
  opp.poss_40min - tm.poss_40min AS pace_stat_diff,
  opp.pace_rating - tm.pace_rating AS pace_rating_diff,
  opp.efficiency_rank - tm.efficiency_rank AS eff_rank_diff,
  opp.pts_100poss - tm.pts_100poss AS eff_stat_diff,
  opp.efficiency_rating - tm.efficiency_rating AS eff_rating_diff
FROM all_games g
LEFT JOIN filtered_features tm
  ON g.school_ncaa = tm.team AND g.season = tm.season
LEFT JOIN filtered_features opp
  ON g.opponent_school_ncaa = opp.team AND g.season = opp.season
ORDER BY g.season, g.school_ncaa;
```

```sql
WITH
  -- Google overall workforce hiring in 2021 (non-intersectional, overall)
  google_hiring AS (
    SELECT
      race_asian,
      race_black,
      race_hispanic_latinx,
      race_white,
      gender_us_women,
      gender_us_men
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_dei.dar_non_intersectional_hiring`
    WHERE report_year = 2021
      AND workforce = 'overall'
    LIMIT 1  -- assume one row per year
  ),

  -- Google overall workforce representation in 2021
  google_representation AS (
    SELECT
      race_asian,
      race_black,
      race_hispanic_latinx,
      race_white,
      gender_us_women,
      gender_us_men
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_dei.dar_non_intersectional_representation`
    WHERE report_year = 2021
      AND workforce = 'overall'
    LIMIT 1
  ),

  -- BLS data for the specified technology sectors in 2021
  bls_tech AS (
    SELECT
      -- Weighted averages for each demographic group
      SAFE_DIVIDE(
        SUM(percent_asian * total_employed_in_thousands),
        SUM(total_employed_in_thousands)
      ) AS race_asian,
      SAFE_DIVIDE(
        SUM(percent_black_or_african_american * total_employed_in_thousands),
        SUM(total_employed_in_thousands)
      ) AS race_black,
      SAFE_DIVIDE(
        SUM(percent_hispanic_or_latino * total_employed_in_thousands),
        SUM(total_employed_in_thousands)
      ) AS race_hispanic_latinx,
      SAFE_DIVIDE(
        SUM(percent_white * total_employed_in_thousands),
        SUM(total_employed_in_thousands)
      ) AS race_white,
      SAFE_DIVIDE(
        SUM(percent_women * total_employed_in_thousands),
        SUM(total_employed_in_thousands)
      ) AS gender_women
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_dei.full_csv-latest-data-is-2023`
    WHERE year = 2021
      AND (
        LOWER(subsector) LIKE '%internet publishing%'
        OR LOWER(subsector) LIKE '%web search%'
        OR LOWER(subsector) LIKE '%computer systems design%'
      )
  )

-- Combine into a unified report
SELECT
  'Asian' AS metric,
  ROUND(h.race_asian, 4) AS hiring_pct,
  ROUND(r.race_asian, 4) AS representation_pct,
  ROUND(b.race_asian, 4) AS bls_pct
FROM google_hiring h, google_representation r, bls_tech b
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'Black',
  ROUND(h.race_black, 4),
  ROUND(r.race_black, 4),
  ROUND(b.race_black, 4)
FROM google_hiring h, google_representation r, bls_tech b
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'Hispanic/Latinx',
  ROUND(h.race_hispanic_latinx, 4),
  ROUND(r.race_hispanic_latinx, 4),
  ROUND(b.race_hispanic_latinx, 4)
FROM google_hiring h, google_representation r, bls_tech b
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'White',
  ROUND(h.race_white, 4),
  ROUND(r.race_white, 4),
  ROUND(b.race_white, 4)
FROM google_hiring h, google_representation r, bls_tech b
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'U.S. Women',
  ROUND(h.gender_us_women, 4),
  ROUND(r.gender_us_women, 4),
  ROUND(b.gender_women, 4)  -- BLS gives percent women
FROM google_hiring h, google_representation r, bls_tech b
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'U.S. Men',
  ROUND(h.gender_us_men, 4),
  ROUND(r.gender_us_men, 4),
  ROUND(1 - b.gender_women, 4)  -- men = 1 - women
FROM google_hiring h, google_representation r, bls_tech b
ORDER BY metric;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Combined 2021 Report: Google Hiring, Google Representation, and BLS Tech Sectors
-- Fixed BLS table reference using wildcard to locate the correct 2021 table

WITH google_hiring AS (
  SELECT
    'Google Hiring' AS source,
    ROUND(race_asian, 4) AS race_asian,
    ROUND(race_black, 4) AS race_black,
    ROUND(race_hispanic_latinx, 4) AS race_hispanic_latinx,
    ROUND(race_white, 4) AS race_white,
    ROUND(gender_us_women, 4) AS gender_us_women,
    ROUND(gender_us_men, 4) AS gender_us_men
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_dei.dar_non_intersectional_hiring`
  WHERE report_year = 2021
    AND workforce = 'overall'
),

google_representation AS (
  SELECT
    'Google Representation' AS source,
    ROUND(race_asian, 4) AS race_asian,
    ROUND(race_black, 4) AS race_black,
    ROUND(race_hispanic_latinx, 4) AS race_hispanic_latinx,
    ROUND(race_white, 4) AS race_white,
    ROUND(gender_us_women, 4) AS gender_us_women,
    ROUND(gender_us_men, 4) AS gender_us_men
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_dei.dar_non_intersectional_representation`
  WHERE report_year = 2021
    AND workforce = 'overall'
),

bls_tech_raw AS (
  -- Use wildcard table with _TABLE_SUFFIX to find the correct 2021 BLS table
  SELECT
    percent_asian,
    percent_black_or_african_american AS percent_black,
    percent_hispanic_or_latino AS percent_hispanic_latinx,
    percent_white,
    percent_women,
    total_employed_in_thousands
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.bls.cpsaat*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX LIKE '%21%'
    AND year = 2021
    AND (
      LOWER(sector) LIKE '%internet publishing%'
      OR LOWER(sector) LIKE '%web search portals%'
      OR LOWER(sector) LIKE '%computer systems design%'
      OR LOWER(sector) LIKE '%related services%'
    )
),

-- Aggregate BLS sectors into one row; convert percentages (0-100) to proportions
bls_tech AS (
  SELECT
    'BLS Tech Sectors' AS source,
    ROUND(AVG(percent_asian) / 100, 4) AS race_asian,
    ROUND(AVG(percent_black) / 100, 4) AS race_black,
    ROUND(AVG(percent_hispanic_latinx) / 100, 4) AS race_hispanic_latinx,
    ROUND(AVG(percent_white) / 100, 4) AS race_white,
    ROUND(AVG(percent_women) / 100, 4) AS gender_us_women,
    ROUND(1 - (AVG(percent_women) / 100), 4) AS gender_us_men
  FROM bls_tech_raw
)

-- Final combined report
SELECT * FROM google_hiring
UNION ALL
SELECT * FROM google_representation
UNION ALL
SELECT * FROM bls_tech
ORDER BY source;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH transfer_logs AS (
    SELECT
        "block_number",
        PARSE_JSON("topics")[1]::STRING AS "from_hex",
        PARSE_JSON("topics")[2]::STRING AS "to_hex",
        SUBSTR("data", 3) AS "raw_hex"
    FROM "GOOG_BLOCKCHAIN"."GOOG_BLOCKCHAIN_TRON_MAINNET_US"."LOGS"
    WHERE "address" = '0xa614f803b6fd780986a42c78ec9c7f77e6ded13c'
      AND PARSE_JSON("topics")[0]::STRING = '0xddf252ad1be2c89b69c2b068fc378daa952ba7f163c4a11628f55a4df523b3ef'
)
SELECT
    "block_number",
    "from_hex" AS "source_address",
    "to_hex"   AS "destination_address",
    ROUND(
        TO_NUMBER(RIGHT("raw_hex", 16), 'XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX') / 1000000,
        4
    ) AS "transfer_amount"
FROM transfer_logs
ORDER BY TO_NUMBER(RIGHT("raw_hex", 16), 'XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX') DESC
LIMIT 3;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH parsed_logs AS (
    SELECT
        "block_number",
        "data",
        TRY_PARSE_JSON("topics") AS topics_json
    FROM "GOOG_BLOCKCHAIN"."GOOG_BLOCKCHAIN_TRON_MAINNET_US"."LOGS"
    WHERE "address" = '0xa614f803b6fd780986a42c78ec9c7f77e6ded13c'
      AND TRY_PARSE_JSON("topics")[0]::STRING = '0xddf252ad1be2c89b69c2b068fc378daa952ba7f163c4a11628f55a4df523b3ef'
      AND "removed" = FALSE
),

extracted AS (
    SELECT
        "block_number",
        '0x' || RIGHT(SUBSTRING(topics_json[1]::STRING, 3), 40) AS "source_hex",
        '0x' || RIGHT(SUBSTRING(topics_json[2]::STRING, 3), 40) AS "dest_hex",
        LTRIM(SUBSTRING("data", 3), '0') AS "raw_amount_hex"
    FROM parsed_logs
),

converted AS (
    SELECT
        "block_number",
        "source_hex",
        "dest_hex",
        ROUND(
            TRY_CAST('0x' || COALESCE(NULLIF("raw_amount_hex", ''), '0') AS DOUBLE) / 1000000,
            4
        ) AS "transfer_amount"
    FROM extracted
)

SELECT
    "block_number",
    "source_hex" AS "source_address",
    "dest_hex" AS "destination_address",
    "transfer_amount"
FROM converted
WHERE "transfer_amount" IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY "transfer_amount" DESC
LIMIT 3;
```

```sql
  SELECT 
    DATE_TRUNC(date, MONTH) AS month,
    COUNT(*) AS monthly_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.chicago_crime.crime`
  WHERE date BETWEEN '2016-01-01' AND '2016-12-31'
    AND primary_type = 'MOTOR VEHICLE THEFT'
  GROUP BY month
)
SELECT MAX(monthly_count) AS max_motor_vehicle_theft_monthly
FROM monthly_counts;
```

<details>

```sql
WITH relevant_drugs AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        kda."drugId"
    FROM 
        "OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM_1"."PLATFORM"."KNOWNDRUGSAGGREGATED" kda,
        LATERAL FLATTEN(input => kda."tradeNames":"list") t
    WHERE 
        LOWER(t.value:"element") IN ('keytruda', 'vioxx', 'premarin', 'humira')
)
SELECT DISTINCT
    m."id" AS "drugId",
    m."drugType",
    m."hasBeenWithdrawn" AS "withdrawalStatus"
FROM 
    "OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM_1"."PLATFORM"."MOLECULE" m
    INNER JOIN relevant_drugs rd
        ON m."id" = rd."drugId"
WHERE 
    m."isApproved" = TRUE
    AND m."blackBoxWarning" = TRUE
    AND m."drugType" IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY 
    m."id";
```

```sql
WITH drug_ids AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT k."drugId" AS "drugId"
  FROM OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM_1.PLATFORM.KNOWNDRUGSAGGREGATED k,
  LATERAL FLATTEN(input => k."tradeNames":"list") f
  WHERE k."tradeNames" IS NOT NULL
    AND LOWER(TRIM(f.value:"element"::STRING)) IN ('keytruda', 'vioxx', 'premarin', 'humira')
)
SELECT
  m."id" AS "drug_id",
  m."drugType" AS "drug_type",
  m."hasBeenWithdrawn" AS "withdrawal_status"
FROM OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM_1.PLATFORM.MOLECULE m
WHERE m."id" IN (SELECT "drugId" FROM drug_ids)
  AND m."blackBoxWarning" = TRUE
  AND m."isApproved" = TRUE
  AND m."drugType" IS NOT NULL;
```

```sql
    left_chrom,
    left_pos,
    left_ref,
    left_alt
  FROM `open-targets-genetics.genetics.variant_disease_coloc`
  WHERE 
    right_gene_id = 'ENSG00000169174'
    AND coloc_h4 > 0.8
    AND coloc_h3 < 0.02
    AND right_bio_feature = 'IPSC'
    AND left_chrom = '1'
    AND left_pos = 55029009
    AND left_ref = 'C'
    AND left_alt = 'T'
    AND left_study IN (
      SELECT study_id 
      FROM `open-targets-genetics.genetics.studies` 
      WHERE LOWER(trait_reported) LIKE '%lesterol%levels%'
    )
),
stats AS (
  SELECT
    ROUND(AVG(coloc_log2_h4_h3), 4) AS avg_log2h4h3,
    ROUND(VAR_POP(coloc_log2_h4_h3), 4) AS variance_log2h4h3,
    ROUND(MAX(coloc_log2_h4_h3) - MIN(coloc_log2_h4_h3), 4) AS max_min_diff,
    MAX(coloc_log2_h4_h3) AS max_value
  FROM filtered_data
),
max_study AS (
  SELECT right_study AS qtl_source
  FROM filtered_data
  WHERE coloc_log2_h4_h3 = (SELECT max_value FROM stats)
  LIMIT 1
)
SELECT
  s.avg_log2h4h3 AS average,
  s.variance_log2h4h3 AS variance,
  s.max_min_diff,
  ms.qtl_source
FROM stats s
CROSS JOIN max_study ms;
```

```sql
max_row AS (
```

```sql
WITH per_study_best_variant AS (
    -- For each gene within each study, identify the best p-value
    SELECT 
        "gene_id",
        "study_id",
        MIN("pval") AS "best_study_pval"
    FROM OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS_2.OPEN_TARGETS_GENETICS.DISEASE_VARIANT_GENE
    GROUP BY "gene_id", "study_id"
),
gene_overall_best AS (
    -- For each gene, find the smallest p-value across all studies
    SELECT 
        "gene_id",
        MIN("best_study_pval") AS "overall_best_pval"
    FROM per_study_best_variant
    GROUP BY "gene_id"
),
ranked_genes AS (
    -- Rank genes by their overall best p-value
    SELECT 
        "gene_id",
        "overall_best_pval",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY "overall_best_pval" ASC) AS "rank"
    FROM gene_overall_best
)
-- Return top 10 genes with smallest p-values
SELECT "gene_id"
FROM ranked_genes
WHERE "rank" <= 10
ORDER BY "rank";
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: UNNEST the Sides array to extract LONG trades and strategy information
WITH long_trades AS (
  SELECT
    t.TradeReportID,
    side.Side AS trade_side,
    t.StrikePrice,
    t.LastPx,
    t.Quantity,
    LOWER(t.TargetCompID) AS strategy
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.cymbal_investments.trade_capture_report` t,
    UNNEST(t.Sides) AS side
  WHERE
    side.Side = 'LONG'
),

-- Step 2: Categorize trades by strategy based on TargetCompID
strategy_trades AS (
  SELECT
    *,
    CASE
      WHEN strategy LIKE '%feeling%lucky%' OR strategy LIKE '%lucky%' THEN 'feeling-lucky'
      WHEN strategy LIKE '%momo%' OR strategy LIKE '%momentum%' THEN 'momentum'
      ELSE 'other'
    END AS strategy_group,
    -- Intrinsic value for long: (StrikePrice - LastPx), focused on per-unit value as asked
    t.StrikePrice - t.LastPx AS per_unit_intrinsic_value
  FROM long_trades t
),

-- Step 3: Calculate average intrinsic value per strategy
avg_by_strategy AS (
  SELECT
    strategy_group,
    AVG(per_unit_intrinsic_value) AS avg_intrinsic_value
  FROM strategy_trades
  WHERE strategy_group IN ('feeling-lucky', 'momentum')
  GROUP BY strategy_group
)

-- Step 4: Calculate the difference
SELECT
  ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN strategy_group = 'feeling-lucky' THEN avg_intrinsic_value END) -
        MAX(CASE WHEN strategy_group = 'momentum' THEN avg_intrinsic_value END), 4) AS avg_intrinsic_value_difference
FROM avg_by_strategy;
```
</details>

<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH long_trades AS (
  SELECT
    t.StrikePrice,
    t.LastPx,
    t.StrikePrice - t.LastPx AS intrinsic_value,
    CASE
      WHEN t.TargetCompID LIKE '%MOMOES%' THEN 'momentum'
      WHEN t.TargetCompID LIKE '%LUCKY%' THEN 'feeling-lucky'
      ELSE NULL
    END AS strategy
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cymbal_investments.trade_capture_report` AS t,
  UNNEST(t.Sides) AS side
  WHERE side.Side = 'LONG'
    AND (t.TargetCompID LIKE '%MOMOES%' OR t.TargetCompID LIKE '%LUCKY%')
),
avg_intrinsic AS (
  SELECT
    strategy,
    ROUND(AVG(intrinsic_value), 4) AS avg_value
  FROM long_trades
  WHERE strategy IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY strategy
)
SELECT
  ROUND(
    (SELECT avg_value FROM avg_intrinsic WHERE strategy = 'feeling-lucky') -
    (SELECT avg_value FROM avg_intrinsic WHERE strategy = 'momentum'),
    4
  ) AS difference;
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH us_states AS (
  -- All US state geometries (including DC; territories like PR are also present but we accept them)
  SELECT state_geom
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.states`
  WHERE state_geom IS NOT NULL
),

us_ports AS (
  -- Ports with region number '6585' that lie inside a US state boundary
  SELECT p.port_name, p.port_geom
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.geo_international_ports.world_port_index` p
  WHERE p.region_number = '6585'
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM us_states s
      WHERE ST_WITHIN(p.port_geom, s.state_geom)
    )
),

relevant_storms AS (
  -- Named tropical storms in North Atlantic basin with wind speed >= 35 kt
  -- Compute the maximum 34‑kt wind radius among the four quadrants (in nautical miles)
  SELECT
    sid,
    latitude,
    longitude,
    GREATEST(
      COALESCE(usa_r34_ne, 0),
      COALESCE(usa_r34_se, 0),
      COALESCE(usa_r34_sw, 0),
      COALESCE(usa_r34_nw, 0)
    ) AS max_r34_nm
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes`
  WHERE basin = 'NA'
    AND name != 'NOT_NAMED'
    AND usa_wind >= 35
    AND usa_wind IS NOT NULL
    AND latitude IS NOT NULL AND longitude IS NOT NULL
    AND latitude BETWEEN -90 AND 90
    AND longitude BETWEEN -180 AND 180
    -- At least one quadrant radius must be positive (storm has a measurable area)
    AND (usa_r34_ne IS NOT NULL OR usa_r34_se IS NOT NULL OR usa_r34_sw IS NOT NULL OR usa_r34_nw IS NOT NULL)
)

SELECT p.port_name
FROM us_ports p
CROSS JOIN relevant_storms s
WHERE ST_DISTANCE(
        p.port_geom,
        ST_GEOGPOINT(s.longitude, s.latitude)
      ) <= s.max_r34_nm * 1852  -- 1 nautical mile = 1852 meters
GROUP BY p.port_name
ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Define temporary functions as required
CREATE TEMP FUNCTION nautical_miles_conversion(input_nautical_miles FLOAT64)
RETURNS FLOAT64
AS (
  input_nautical_miles * 1.15078
);

CREATE TEMP FUNCTION azimuth_to_geog_point(input_lat FLOAT64, input_lon FLOAT64, azimuth FLOAT64, distance FLOAT64)
RETURNS GEOGRAPHY
AS (
  ST_GEOGPOINT(
    57.2958 * (
      input_lon * (3.14159 / 180) + ATAN2(
        SIN(azimuth * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(distance * 1.61 / 6378.1) * COS(input_lat * (3.14159 / 180)),
        COS(distance * 1.61 / 6378.1) - SIN(input_lat * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(
          57.2958 * ASIN(
            SIN(input_lat * (3.14159 / 180)) * COS(distance * 1.61 / 6378.1) +
            COS(input_lat * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(distance * 1.61 / 6378.1) * COS(azimuth * (3.14159 / 180))
          )
        )
      )
    ),
    57.2958 * ASIN(
      SIN(input_lat * (3.14159 / 180)) * COS(distance * 1.61 / 6378.1) +
      COS(input_lat * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(distance * 1.61 / 6378.1) * COS(azimuth * (3.14159 / 180))
    )
  )
);

WITH
  -- Filter hurricanes: North Atlantic, named, wind >= 35 kt, non-null quadrant radii
  hurricane_obs AS (
    SELECT
      sid,
      name,
      latitude,
      longitude,
      usa_wind,
      usa_r34_ne,
      usa_r34_se,
      usa_r34_sw,
      usa_r34_nw
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes`
    WHERE basin = 'NA'
      AND name != 'NOT_NAMED'
      AND usa_wind >= 35
      AND usa_r34_ne IS NOT NULL
      AND usa_r34_se IS NOT NULL
      AND usa_r34_sw IS NOT NULL
      AND usa_r34_nw IS NOT NULL
  ),
  -- Build polygons representing the 34-kt wind field (four quadrant points)
  storm_polygons AS (
    SELECT
      sid,
      name,
      latitude,
      longitude,
      usa_wind,
      ST_MAKEPOLYGON(
        -- Build a closed linestring: p1 -> p2 -> p3 -> p4 -> p1
        ST_MAKELINE(
          ST_MAKELINE(
            azimuth_to_geog_point(latitude, longitude, 45, usa_r34_ne),
            azimuth_to_geog_point(latitude, longitude, 135, usa_r34_se)
          ),
          ST_MAKELINE(
            azimuth_to_geog_point(latitude, longitude, 225, usa_r34_sw),
            ST_MAKELINE(
              azimuth_to_geog_point(latitude, longitude, 315, usa_r34_nw),
              azimuth_to_geog_point(latitude, longitude, 45, usa_r34_ne)  -- close the loop
            )
          )
        )
      ) AS storm_area
    FROM hurricane_obs
  ),
  -- U.S. states (50 states + DC)
  us_states AS (
    SELECT state_geom
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.states`
    WHERE state_name IN (
      'Alabama','Alaska','Arizona','Arkansas','California','Colorado','Connecticut','Delaware',
      'Florida','Georgia','Hawaii','Idaho','Illinois','Indiana','Iowa','Kansas','Kentucky',
      'Louisiana','Maine','Maryland','Massachusetts','Michigan','Minnesota','Mississippi',
      'Missouri','Montana','Nebraska','Nevada','New Hampshire','New Jersey','New Mexico',
      'New York','North Carolina','North Dakota','Ohio','Oklahoma','Oregon','Pennsylvania',
      'Rhode Island','South Carolina','South Dakota','Tennessee','Texas','Utah','Vermont',
      'Virginia','Washington','West Virginia','Wisconsin','Wyoming','District of Columbia'
    )
  ),
  -- Ports with region_number '6585' that lie within a U.S. state boundary
  ports_in_us AS (
    SELECT
      p.port_name,
      ANY_VALUE(p.port_geom) AS port_geom
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.geo_international_ports.world_port_index` p
    CROSS JOIN us_states s
    WHERE p.region_number = '6585'
      AND ST_WITHIN(p.port_geom, s.state_geom)
    GROUP BY p.port_name
  ),
  -- Count how many storm polygons contain each port
  port_storm_counts AS (
    SELECT
      p.port_name,
      COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM ports_in_us p
    JOIN storm_polygons sp
      ON ST_WITHIN(p.port_geom, sp.storm_area)
    GROUP BY p.port_name
  )
-- Return the port with the highest count
SELECT port_name
FROM port_storm_counts
ORDER BY cnt DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

```sql
-- Step 1: Aggregate census tract solar data by state
WITH tract_agg AS (
    SELECT
        state_name,
        COUNT(region_name)                                              AS tract_count,
        SUM(count_qualified)                                            AS tract_total_qualified_buildings,
        AVG(percent_covered)                                            AS tract_avg_pct_covered,
        AVG(percent_qualified)                                          AS tract_avg_pct_qualified,
        SUM(number_of_panels_total)                                     AS tract_total_panels,
        SUM(kw_total)                                                   AS tract_total_kw,
        SUM(yearly_sunlight_kwh_total)                                  AS tract_total_kwh,
        SUM(carbon_offset_metric_tons)                                  AS tract_total_co2_offset,
        SUM(existing_installs_count)                                    AS tract_existing_installs,
        ROUND(
            SUM(count_qualified * percent_covered / 100.0 * percent_qualified / 100.0)
            - SUM(existing_installs_count), 4
        )                                                               AS tract_installation_gap
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.sunroof_solar.solar_potential_by_censustract`
    GROUP BY state_name
),

-- Step 2: Aggregate postal code solar data by state
postal_agg AS (
    SELECT
        state_name,
        COUNT(region_name)                                              AS postal_count,
        SUM(count_qualified)                                            AS postal_total_qualified_buildings,
        AVG(percent_covered)                                            AS postal_avg_pct_covered,
        AVG(percent_qualified)                                          AS postal_avg_pct_qualified,
        SUM(number_of_panels_total)                                     AS postal_total_panels,
        SUM(kw_total)                                                   AS postal_total_kw,
        SUM(yearly_sunlight_kwh_total)                                  AS postal_total_kwh,
        SUM(carbon_offset_metric_tons)                                  AS postal_total_co2_offset,
        SUM(existing_installs_count)                                    AS postal_existing_installs,
        ROUND(
            SUM(count_qualified * percent_covered / 100.0 * percent_qualified / 100.0)
            - SUM(existing_installs_count), 4
        )                                                               AS postal_installation_gap
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.sunroof_solar.solar_potential_by_postal_code`
    GROUP BY state_name
)

-- Step 3: Build final state-level comparison
SELECT
    COALESCE(t.state_name, p.state_name)                                AS state_name,
    -- Census tract level columns
    t.tract_count,
    t.tract_total_qualified_buildings,
    ROUND(t.tract_avg_pct_covered, 4)                                   AS tract_avg_pct_covered,
    ROUND(t.tract_avg_pct_qualified, 4)                                 AS tract_avg_pct_qualified,
    t.tract_total_panels,
    ROUND(t.tract_total_kw, 4)                                          AS tract_total_kw,
    ROUND(t.tract_total_kwh, 4)                                         AS tract_total_kwh,
    ROUND(t.tract_total_co2_offset, 4)                                  AS tract_total_co2_offset,
    t.tract_existing_installs,
    t.tract_installation_gap,
    -- Postal code level columns
    p.postal_count,
    p.postal_total_qualified_buildings,
    ROUND(p.postal_avg_pct_covered, 4)                                  AS postal_avg_pct_covered,
    ROUND(p.postal_avg_pct_qualified, 4)                                AS postal_avg_pct_qualified,
    p.postal_total_panels,
    ROUND(p.postal_total_kw, 4)                                         AS postal_total_kw,
    ROUND(p.postal_total_kwh, 4)                                        AS postal_total_kwh,
    ROUND(p.postal_total_co2_offset, 4)                                 AS postal_total_co2_offset,
    p.postal_existing_installs,
    p.postal_installation_gap
FROM tract_agg t
FULL OUTER JOIN postal_agg p
    ON t.state_name = p.state_name
ORDER BY state_name;
```

<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Aggregate solar potential data at the state level from postal code regions
postal_agg AS (
  SELECT
    state_name,
    -- Derive total buildings in Google Maps: count_qualified represents buildings that are
    -- both covered AND suitable. So total = count_qualified / (pct_qualified) / (pct_covered)
    SUM(count_qualified / NULLIF(percent_qualified / 100, 0) / NULLIF(percent_covered / 100, 0)) 
      AS total_buildings,
    AVG(percent_covered) AS avg_percent_covered,
    AVG(percent_qualified) AS avg_percent_qualified,
    SUM(number_of_panels_total) AS total_panel_count,
    SUM(kw_total) AS total_kw_capacity,
    SUM(yearly_sunlight_kwh_total) AS total_energy_kwh,
    SUM(carbon_offset_metric_tons) AS total_carbon_offset_tons,
    SUM(existing_installs_count) AS total_existing_installs,
    SUM(count_qualified) AS total_qualified
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.sunroof_solar.solar_potential_by_postal_code`
  WHERE percent_covered > 0 AND percent_qualified > 0
  GROUP BY state_name
),

-- Aggregate solar potential data at the state level from census tract regions
census_agg AS (
  SELECT
    state_name,
    SUM(count_qualified / NULLIF(percent_qualified / 100, 0) / NULLIF(percent_covered / 100, 0)) 
      AS total_buildings,
    AVG(percent_covered) AS avg_percent_covered,
    AVG(percent_qualified) AS avg_percent_qualified,
    SUM(number_of_panels_total) AS total_panel_count,
    SUM(kw_total) AS total_kw_capacity,
    SUM(yearly_sunlight_kwh_total) AS total_energy_kwh,
    SUM(carbon_offset_metric_tons) AS total_carbon_offset_tons,
    SUM(existing_installs_count) AS total_existing_installs,
    SUM(count_qualified) AS total_qualified
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.sunroof_solar.solar_potential_by_censustract`
  WHERE percent_covered > 0 AND percent_qualified > 0
  GROUP BY state_name
)

-- Compare postal code vs census tract metrics side-by-side per state
SELECT
  COALESCE(p.state_name, c.state_name) AS state,

  -- ===== Postal Code Level Metrics =====
  ROUND(p.total_buildings, 4)          AS pc_total_buildings,
  ROUND(p.avg_percent_covered, 4)      AS pc_avg_pct_covered,
  ROUND(p.avg_percent_qualified, 4)    AS pc_avg_pct_qualified,
  p.total_panel_count                  AS pc_total_panels,
  ROUND(p.total_kw_capacity, 4)        AS pc_total_kw_capacity,
  ROUND(p.total_energy_kwh, 4)         AS pc_energy_kwh,
  ROUND(p.total_carbon_offset_tons, 4) AS pc_co2_offset_tons,
  p.total_existing_installs            AS pc_existing_installs,
  -- Gap = total qualified (suitable) buildings minus current installations
  p.total_qualified - p.total_existing_installs AS pc_potential_gap,

  -- ===== Census Tract Level Metrics =====
  ROUND(c.total_buildings, 4)          AS ct_total_buildings,
  ROUND(c.avg_percent_covered, 4)      AS ct_avg_pct_covered,
  ROUND(c.avg_percent_qualified, 4)    AS ct_avg_pct_qualified,
  c.total_panel_count                  AS ct_total_panels,
  ROUND(c.total_kw_capacity, 4)        AS ct_total_kw_capacity,
  ROUND(c.total_energy_kwh, 4)         AS ct_energy_kwh,
  ROUND(c.total_carbon_offset_tons, 4) AS ct_co2_offset_tons,
  c.total_existing_installs            AS ct_existing_installs,
  c.total_qualified - c.total_existing_installs AS ct_potential_gap

FROM postal_agg p
FULL OUTER JOIN census_agg c 
  ON p.state_name = c.state_name
ORDER BY state;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Compute summary statistics for genetic variants on chromosome 1 in the specified region
-- from gnomAD v3 (genomes). The region spans positions 55039447-55064852.
-- Note: The table does not contain VEP annotations, so distinct_gene_symbols is reported as NULL.
WITH region_variants AS (
  SELECT
    start_position,
    AN
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.gnomAD.v3_genomes__chr1`
  WHERE
    reference_name = 'chr1'
    AND start_position BETWEEN 55039447 AND 55064852
)
SELECT
  COUNT(DISTINCT start_position) AS number_of_variants,
  SUM(AN) AS total_allele_count,
  SUM(AN) AS total_number_of_alleles,
  -- VEP gene annotations are not available in the gnomAD v3 genomes tables.
  CAST(NULL AS INT64) AS distinct_gene_symbols,
  ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(55064852 - 55039447, COUNT(DISTINCT start_position)), 4) AS density
FROM
  region_variants;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
  region_variants AS (
    SELECT
      AN
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.gnomAD.v3_genomes__chr1`
    WHERE reference_name = 'chr1'
      AND start_position BETWEEN 55039447 AND 55064852
  )
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS number_of_variants,
  SUM(AN) AS total_allele_count,
  SUM(AN) AS total_number_of_alleles,
  NULL AS distinct_gene_symbols,  -- VEP annotations not available in v3 schema
  ROUND(
    (55064852 - 55039447 + 1) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0),
    4
  ) AS density_mutations_per_base
FROM region_variants;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH
  -- Extract state code from consecutive_number and count distracted crashes for 2015
  distracted_2015 AS (
    SELECT
      SUBSTR(SAFE_CAST(d.consecutive_number AS STRING), 1, 2) AS state_code,
      COUNT(DISTINCT d.consecutive_number) AS crash_count
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.nhtsa_traffic_fatalities.distract_2015` d
    WHERE LOWER(d.driver_distracted_by_name) NOT IN (
      'not distracted', 'unknown if distracted', 'not reported'
    )
    GROUP BY state_code
  ),

  -- Same for 2016
  distracted_2016 AS (
    SELECT
      SUBSTR(SAFE_CAST(d.consecutive_number AS STRING), 1, 2) AS state_code,
      COUNT(DISTINCT d.consecutive_number) AS crash_count
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.nhtsa_traffic_fatalities.distract_2016` d
    WHERE LOWER(d.driver_distracted_by_name) NOT IN (
      'not distracted', 'unknown if distracted', 'not reported'
    )
    GROUP BY state_code
  ),

  -- Map state_code to state_name (using us_states_area)
  state_mapping AS (
    SELECT
      state_geo_id AS state_code,
      state_name
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.utility_us.us_states_area`
    WHERE state_name IS NOT NULL AND state_name != ''
  ),

  -- Combine to get crash counts per state name
  crashes_per_state_2015 AS (
    SELECT
      m.state_name,
      d.crash_count
    FROM distracted_2015 d
    JOIN state_mapping m ON d.state_code = m.state_code
  ),

  crashes_per_state_2016 AS (
    SELECT
      m.state_name,
      d.crash_count
    FROM distracted_2016 d
    JOIN state_mapping m ON d.state_code = m.state_code
  ),

  -- Get state-level population from 2010 census (using zipcode-area mapping)
  state_population AS (
    SELECT
      z.state_name,
      SUM(SAFE_CAST(p.population AS INT64)) AS total_population
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_usa.population_by_zip_2010` p
    JOIN `bigquery-public-data.utility_us.zipcode_area` z
      ON p.zipcode = z.zipcode
    WHERE z.state_name IS NOT NULL
      AND z.state_name != ''
    GROUP BY z.state_name
  ),

  -- Calculate rate per 100k for 2015
  rates_2015 AS (
    SELECT
      c.state_name,
      c.crash_count,
      sp.total_population,
      ROUND((c.crash_count * 100000.0) / NULLIF(sp.total_population, 0), 2) AS rate_per_100k,
      '2015' AS year
    FROM crashes_per_state_2015 c
    JOIN state_population sp ON c.state_name = sp.state_name
  ),

  -- Calculate rate per 100k for 2016
  rates_2016 AS (
    SELECT
      c.state_name,
      c.crash_count,
      sp.total_population,
      ROUND((c.crash_count * 100000.0) / NULLIF(sp.total_population, 0), 2) AS rate_per_100k,
      '2016' AS year
    FROM crashes_per_state_2016 c
    JOIN state_population sp ON c.state_name = sp.state_name
  ),

  -- Combine both years and rank
  all_rates AS (
    SELECT * FROM rates_2015
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM rates_2016
  ),

  ranked AS (
    SELECT
      state_name,
      year,
      rate_per_100k,
      DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY rate_per_100k DESC) AS rank
    FROM all_rates
  )

-- Select top 5 states per year
SELECT
  state_name,
  year,
  rate_per_100k
FROM ranked
WHERE rank <= 5
ORDER BY year, rank;
```

```sql
-- Count weekend accidents per state with rainy and clear conditions

    state_name,
    COUNTIF(LOWER(TRIM(atmospheric_conditions_1_name)) = 'rain') AS rainy_count,
```

```sql
      WHEN atmospheric_conditions_1_name = 'Clear' THEN 'Clear'
    END AS weather_type

  WHERE 
    EXTRACT(DAYOFWEEK FROM timestamp_of_crash) IN (1, 7)   -- Sunday=1, Saturday=7
    AND atmospheric_conditions_1_name IN ('Rain', 'Clear')
```

<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Aggregate unsheltered homeless individuals by state for 2015
state_2015 AS (
  SELECT 
    SPLIT(CoC_Number, '-')[OFFSET(0)] AS state_abbr,
    SUM(Unsheltered_Homeless_Individuals) AS total_2015
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.sdoh_hud_pit_homelessness.hud_pit_by_coc`
  WHERE Count_Year = 2015
  GROUP BY state_abbr
),
-- Aggregate unsheltered homeless individuals by state for 2018
state_2018 AS (
  SELECT 
    SPLIT(CoC_Number, '-')[OFFSET(0)] AS state_abbr,
    SUM(Unsheltered_Homeless_Individuals) AS total_2018
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.sdoh_hud_pit_homelessness.hud_pit_by_coc`
  WHERE Count_Year = 2018
  GROUP BY state_abbr
),
-- Join 2015 and 2018 data and compute percentage change per state
state_pct_change AS (
  SELECT 
    a.state_abbr,
    ROUND(((b.total_2018 - a.total_2015) / a.total_2015) * 100, 4) AS pct_change
  FROM state_2015 a
  INNER JOIN state_2018 b ON a.state_abbr = b.state_abbr
  WHERE a.total_2015 > 0  -- exclude states with zero unsheltered in 2015 to avoid division by zero
),
-- Compute the national average of state percentage changes
national_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(pct_change) AS avg_pct_change
  FROM state_pct_change
)
-- Select the 5 states whose percentage change is closest to the national average
SELECT state_abbr
FROM state_pct_change
CROSS JOIN national_avg
ORDER BY ABS(pct_change - avg_pct_change) ASC
LIMIT 5;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH state_year_totals AS (
  -- Step 1: Sum unsheltered homeless individuals by state and year
  SELECT 
    SUBSTR(CoC_Number, 1, 2) AS state_abbr,
    Count_Year,
    SUM(Unsheltered_Homeless_Individuals) AS total_unsheltered
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.sdoh_hud_pit_homelessness.hud_pit_by_coc`
  WHERE Count_Year IN (2015, 2018)
  GROUP BY state_abbr, Count_Year
),
state_pivot AS (
  -- Step 2: Pivot to get 2015 and 2018 values side by side per state
  SELECT 
    state_abbr,
    MAX(CASE WHEN Count_Year = 2015 THEN total_unsheltered END) AS val_2015,
    MAX(CASE WHEN Count_Year = 2018 THEN total_unsheltered END) AS val_2018
  FROM state_year_totals
  GROUP BY state_abbr
  -- Only keep states that have data in both years and a non-zero 2015 baseline
  HAVING val_2015 IS NOT NULL AND val_2018 IS NOT NULL AND val_2015 > 0
),
state_pct_change AS (
  -- Step 3: Calculate percentage change for each state from 2015 to 2018
  SELECT 
    state_abbr,
    ROUND(((val_2018 - val_2015) / val_2015) * 100, 4) AS pct_change
  FROM state_pivot
),
national_avg AS (
  -- Step 4: Calculate the national average of all state percentage changes
  SELECT 
    ROUND(AVG(pct_change), 4) AS avg_pct_change
  FROM state_pct_change
)
-- Step 5: Find the 5 states whose percentage change is closest to the national average
SELECT 
  s.state_abbr
FROM state_pct_change s
CROSS JOIN national_avg n
ORDER BY ABS(s.pct_change - n.avg_pct_change)
LIMIT 5;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>

```sql
-- CTE: count mentions per Stack Overflow question from Hacker News comments on or after 2014
WITH comment_mentions AS (
    SELECT
        "post_id",
        COUNT(*) AS mention_count
    FROM (
        SELECT "post_id", "id", "time"
        FROM "STACKOVERFLOW_PLUS"."HACKERNEWS"."COMMENTS_CONVOLUTION"
        WHERE "time" >= 1388534400  -- Unix timestamp for 2014-01-01 00:00:00 UTC
        UNION ALL
        SELECT "post_id", "id", "time"
        FROM "STACKOVERFLOW_PLUS"."HACKERNEWS"."FULL_PARTITION_EXTRA"
        WHERE "time" >= 1388534400
    ) c
    GROUP BY "post_id"
),

-- join with Stack Overflow questions to get tag strings
question_tags AS (
    SELECT
        q."id",
        q."tags",
        COALESCE(m.mention_count, 0) AS mention_count
    FROM "STACKOVERFLOW_PLUS"."STACKOVERFLOW"."POSTS_QUESTIONS" q
    INNER JOIN comment_mentions m ON q."id" = m."post_id"
    WHERE q."tags" IS NOT NULL AND q."tags" != ''
),

-- split pipe-delimited tags into rows, preserving question mention count
tag_splits AS (
    SELECT
        q."id",
        TRIM(f.value) AS tag,
        q.mention_count
    FROM question_tags q,
    LATERAL SPLIT_TO_TABLE(q."tags", '|') f
)

-- aggregate mention counts by tag and rank top 10
SELECT
    tag,
    SUM(mention_count) AS total_mentions
FROM tag_splits
GROUP BY tag
ORDER BY total_mentions DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- CTE to count mentions per Stack Overflow question from Hacker News comments on or after 2014
WITH question_mentions AS (
    SELECT 
        c."post_id",
        COUNT(*) AS "mention_count"
    FROM "STACKOVERFLOW_PLUS"."HACKERNEWS"."COMMENTS_CONVOLUTION" c
    WHERE c."post_id" IS NOT NULL
      -- Unix timestamp for 2014-01-01 00:00:00 UTC
      AND c."time" >= 1388534400
    GROUP BY c."post_id"
),

-- Join with Stack Overflow questions, split tags, and aggregate counts per tag
tag_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        f.value::STRING AS "tag",
        SUM(m."mention_count") AS "total_mentions"
    FROM question_mentions m
    JOIN "STACKOVERFLOW_PLUS"."STACKOVERFLOW"."POSTS_QUESTIONS" q
      ON m."post_id" = q."id"
    -- Split the pipe-delimited tags and flatten into individual tag rows
    , LATERAL FLATTEN(INPUT => SPLIT(q."tags", '|')) f
    WHERE q."tags" IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY f.value
)

-- Rank tags by total mention count and return top 10
SELECT 
    RANK() OVER (ORDER BY "total_mentions" DESC) AS "rank",
    "tag",
    "total_mentions"
FROM tag_counts
ORDER BY "rank"
LIMIT 10;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: Identify all gold badges (class=1) and assign row number per user ordered by date
first_gold AS (
    SELECT 
        b."user_id",
        b."name",
        b."date",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY b."user_id" ORDER BY b."date") AS rn
    FROM STACKOVERFLOW.STACKOVERFLOW.BADGES b
    WHERE b."class" = 1
),
-- Step 2: Keep only the first gold badge per user and join with user creation date
user_first_gold AS (
    SELECT 
        f."user_id",
        f."name",
        f."date",
        u."creation_date"
    FROM first_gold f
    JOIN STACKOVERFLOW.STACKOVERFLOW.USERS u ON f."user_id" = u."id"
    WHERE f.rn = 1
)
-- Step 3: Aggregate by badge name to get count and average days
SELECT 
    ug."name" AS "badge_name",
    COUNT(DISTINCT ug."user_id") AS "num_users",
    ROUND(AVG((ug."date" - ug."creation_date") / 86400000000.0), 4) AS "avg_days"
FROM user_first_gold ug
GROUP BY ug."name"
ORDER BY "num_users" DESC
LIMIT 10;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH "gold_badges" AS (
    SELECT 
        b."user_id",
        b."name",
        b."date" AS "badge_date"
    FROM "STACKOVERFLOW"."STACKOVERFLOW"."BADGES" b
    WHERE b."class" = 1
),
"first_gold_badge" AS (
    SELECT 
        gb."user_id",
        gb."name",
        gb."badge_date"
    FROM "gold_badges" gb
    QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY gb."user_id" ORDER BY gb."badge_date" ASC) = 1
),
"badge_stats" AS (
    SELECT 
        fgb."name",
        fgb."user_id",
        (fgb."badge_date" - u."creation_date") / 86400000000 AS "days_to_badge"
    FROM "first_gold_badge" fgb
    JOIN "STACKOVERFLOW"."STACKOVERFLOW"."USERS" u 
        ON fgb."user_id" = u."id"
)
SELECT 
    "name" AS "badge_name",
    COUNT(DISTINCT "user_id") AS "user_count",
    ROUND(AVG("days_to_badge"), 4) AS "avg_days_to_badge"
FROM "badge_stats"
GROUP BY "name"
ORDER BY "user_count" DESC
LIMIT 10;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH combined_data AS (
  SELECT 
    gameId, pitcherId, pitcherFirstName, pitcherLastName, pitchSpeed,
    homeTeamName, awayTeamName,
    homeFielder1, homeFielder2, homeFielder3, homeFielder4, homeFielder5, 
    homeFielder6, homeFielder7, homeFielder8, homeFielder9, homeFielder10, 
    homeFielder11, homeFielder12,
    awayFielder1, awayFielder2, awayFielder3, awayFielder4, awayFielder5, 
    awayFielder6, awayFielder7, awayFielder8, awayFielder9, awayFielder10, 
    awayFielder11, awayFielder12
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.baseball.games_wide`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 
    gameId, pitcherId, pitcherFirstName, pitcherLastName, pitchSpeed,
    homeTeamName, awayTeamName,
    homeFielder1, homeFielder2, homeFielder3, homeFielder4, homeFielder5, 
    homeFielder6, homeFielder7, homeFielder8, homeFielder9, homeFielder10, 
    homeFielder11, homeFielder12,
    awayFielder1, awayFielder2, awayFielder3, awayFielder4, awayFielder5, 
    awayFielder6, awayFielder7, awayFielder8, awayFielder9, awayFielder10, 
    awayFielder11, awayFielder12
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.baseball.games_post_wide`
),
validated_pitches AS (
  SELECT *,
    CASE
      WHEN pitcherId IN (
        homeFielder1, homeFielder2, homeFielder3, homeFielder4, homeFielder5, 
        homeFielder6, homeFielder7, homeFielder8, homeFielder9, homeFielder10, 
        homeFielder11, homeFielder12
      ) THEN homeTeamName
      WHEN pitcherId IN (
        awayFielder1, awayFielder2, awayFielder3, awayFielder4, awayFielder5, 
        awayFielder6, awayFielder7, awayFielder8, awayFielder9, awayFielder10, 
        awayFielder11, awayFielder12
      ) THEN awayTeamName
      ELSE NULL
    END AS team_name
  FROM combined_data
  WHERE pitchSpeed > 0
),
ranked_pitches AS (
  SELECT 
    team_name,
    CONCAT(pitcherFirstName, ' ', pitcherLastName) AS pitcher_full_name,
    pitchSpeed,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY team_name 
      ORDER BY pitchSpeed DESC, pitcherLastName, pitcherFirstName
    ) AS rn
  FROM validated_pitches
  WHERE team_name IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  team_name,
  pitcher_full_name,
  pitchSpeed AS max_pitch_speed
FROM ranked_pitches
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY team_name;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH combined AS (
  -- Step 1: Combine regular season and post-season pitch data with non-zero speed
  -- Select only the columns needed to reduce bytes scanned
  SELECT
    pitcherId,
    pitcherFirstName,
    pitcherLastName,
    pitchSpeed,
    homeFielder1, homeFielder2, homeFielder3, homeFielder4,
    homeFielder5, homeFielder6, homeFielder7, homeFielder8,
    homeFielder9, homeFielder10, homeFielder11, homeFielder12,
    awayFielder1, awayFielder2, awayFielder3, awayFielder4,
    awayFielder5, awayFielder6, awayFielder7, awayFielder8,
    awayFielder9, awayFielder10, awayFielder11, awayFielder12,
    homeTeamName, awayTeamName
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.baseball.games_wide`
  WHERE pitchSpeed IS NOT NULL AND pitchSpeed > 0
    AND pitcherId IS NOT NULL AND pitcherId != ''
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    pitcherId,
    pitcherFirstName,
    pitcherLastName,
    pitchSpeed,
    homeFielder1, homeFielder2, homeFielder3, homeFielder4,
    homeFielder5, homeFielder6, homeFielder7, homeFielder8,
    homeFielder9, homeFielder10, homeFielder11, homeFielder12,
    awayFielder1, awayFielder2, awayFielder3, awayFielder4,
    awayFielder5, awayFielder6, awayFielder7, awayFielder8,
    awayFielder9, awayFielder10, awayFielder11, awayFielder12,
    homeTeamName, awayTeamName
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.baseball.games_post_wide`
  WHERE pitchSpeed IS NOT NULL AND pitchSpeed > 0
    AND pitcherId IS NOT NULL AND pitcherId != ''
),
pitcher_team AS (
  -- Step 2: Determine which team the pitcher actually played for in each game
  -- by checking if pitcherId exists in the home or away fielder lists
  SELECT
    pitcherId,
    pitcherFirstName,
    pitcherLastName,
    pitchSpeed,
    CASE
      WHEN pitcherId IN (
        homeFielder1, homeFielder2, homeFielder3, homeFielder4,
        homeFielder5, homeFielder6, homeFielder7, homeFielder8,
        homeFielder9, homeFielder10, homeFielder11, homeFielder12
      ) THEN homeTeamName
      WHEN pitcherId IN (
        awayFielder1, awayFielder2, awayFielder3, awayFielder4,
        awayFielder5, awayFielder6, awayFielder7, awayFielder8,
        awayFielder9, awayFielder10, awayFielder11, awayFielder12
      ) THEN awayTeamName
      ELSE NULL
    END AS team_name
  FROM combined
),
pitcher_team_max AS (
  -- Step 3: For each pitcher & team combination, compute max valid pitch speed
  SELECT
    pitcherFirstName,
    pitcherLastName,
    team_name,
    MAX(pitchSpeed) AS max_speed
  FROM pitcher_team
  WHERE team_name IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY pitcherFirstName, pitcherLastName, team_name
),
ranked AS (
  -- Step 4: Rank pitchers within each team by descending max_speed
  SELECT
    team_name,
    pitcherFirstName,
    pitcherLastName,
    max_speed,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY team_name ORDER BY max_speed DESC) AS rn
  FROM pitcher_team_max
)
-- Step 5: Return the top pitcher (highest valid speed) for each team
SELECT
  team_name,
  CONCAT(pitcherFirstName, ' ', pitcherLastName) AS pitcher_full_name,
  max_speed
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY team_name;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: Tokenize all articles using SPLIT_TO_TABLE (more efficient than REGEXP_EXTRACT_ALL + FLATTEN)
token_rows AS (
    SELECT 
        n."id",
        n."title",
        n."date",
        LOWER(f.VALUE::STRING) AS token
    FROM "WORD_VECTORS_US"."WORD_VECTORS_US"."NATURE" n,
    TABLE(SPLIT_TO_TABLE(REGEXP_REPLACE(n."body", '[^a-zA-Z0-9]+', ' '), ' ')) f
    WHERE LOWER(f.VALUE) NOT IN (
        'a','about','above','after','again','against','ain','all','am','an','and','any','are','aren','arent',
        'as','at','be','because','been','before','being','below','between','both','but','by','can','couldn',
        'couldnt','d','did','didn','didnt','do','does','doesn','doesnt','doing','don','dont','down','during',
        'each','few','for','from','further','had','hadn','hadnt','has','hasn','hasnt','have','haven','havent',
        'having','he','her','here','hers','herself','him','himself','his','how','i','if','in','into','is','isn',
        'isnt','it','its','itself','just','ll','m','ma','me','mightn','mightnt','more','most','mustn','mustnt',
        'my','myself','needn','neednt','no','nor','not','now','o','of','off','on','once','only','or','other',
        'our','ours','ourselves','out','over','own','re','s','same','shan','shant','she','shes','should',
        'shouldn','shouldnt','shouldve','so','some','such','t','than','that','thatll','the','their','theirs',
        'them','themselves','then','there','these','they','this','those','through','to','too','under','until',
        'up','ve','very','was','wasn','wasnt','we','were','weren','werent','what','when','where','which','while',
        'who','whom','why','will','with','won','wont','wouldn','wouldnt','y','you','youd','youll','your',
        'youre','yours','yourself','yourselves','youve'
    )
),

-- Step 2: Join with vectors and frequencies, and flatten vector to get weighted contributions per dimension
vector_parts AS (
    SELECT 
        tr."id",
        tr."title",
        tr."date",
        fv.seq AS idx,
        fv.value::FLOAT / POWER(wf."frequency", 0.4) AS contribution
    FROM token_rows tr
    JOIN "WORD_VECTORS_US"."WORD_VECTORS_US"."GLOVE_VECTORS" gv 
        ON tr.token = gv."word"
    JOIN "WORD_VECTORS_US"."WORD_VECTORS_US"."WORD_FREQUENCIES" wf 
        ON tr.token = wf."word",
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => gv."vector"::ARRAY) fv
),

-- Step 3: Aggregate per article per dimension to get weighted sum vectors
aggregated AS (
    SELECT 
        "id",
        "title",
        "date",
        idx,
        SUM(contribution) AS weighted_sum
    FROM vector_parts
    GROUP BY "id", "title", "date", idx
),

-- Step 4: Compute Euclidean norm for each article's aggregate vector
norms AS (
    SELECT 
        "id",
        SQRT(SUM(weighted_sum * weighted_sum)) AS norm
    FROM aggregated
    GROUP BY "id"
),

-- Step 5: Get the target article's normalized vector
target AS (
    SELECT 
        a.idx,
        a.weighted_sum / n.norm AS norm_val
    FROM aggregated a
    JOIN norms n ON a."id" = n."id"
    WHERE a."id" = '8a78ef2d-d5f7-4d2d-9b47-5adb25cbd373'
),

-- Step 6: Compute cosine similarity with all other articles
similarities AS (
    SELECT 
        a."id" AS article_id,
        MAX(a."title") AS "title",
        MAX(a."date") AS "date",
        ROUND(SUM(a.weighted_sum * t.norm_val) / MAX(n.norm), 4) AS cosine_similarity
    FROM aggregated a
    JOIN norms n ON a."id" = n."id"
    JOIN target t ON a.idx = t.idx
    WHERE a."id" != '8a78ef2d-d5f7-4d2d-9b47-5adb25cbd373'
    GROUP BY a."id"
)

-- Step 7: Return top 10 most similar articles
SELECT 
    article_id AS "id",
    "date",
    "title",
    cosine_similarity
FROM similarities
ORDER BY cosine_similarity DESC
LIMIT 10;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH filtered_images AS (
    SELECT 
        "PatientID",

series_aggregated AS (
    SELECT

        "SeriesInstanceUID",
        "StudyDate",
        SUM("BlobStorageSize") AS total_bytes
    FROM filtered_images
    GROUP BY

        "StudyInstanceUID",
        "SeriesInstanceUID",
        "StudyDate"
)
SELECT 
    "PatientID",
    "PatientName",
    "StudyInstanceUID",
    "SeriesInstanceUID",
    "StudyDate",
    's3://idc-open-data/' || "SeriesInstanceUID" || '/*' AS "SeriesAWSURL",
    ROUND(total_bytes / 1000000.0, 2) AS "TotalSizeMB"
FROM series_aggregated
ORDER BY "StudyDate", "PatientID";
```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH filtered_images AS (
    SELECT
        "PatientID",
        "PatientSex",
        "PatientAge",
        "StudyInstanceUID",
        "StudyDate",
        "StudyDescription",
        "SeriesInstanceUID",
        "SeriesDescription",
        "SeriesNumber",
        "Rows",
        "Columns",
        "BitsAllocated",
        CAST("NumberOfFrames" AS NUMBER) AS "NumFrames"
    FROM "IDC"."IDC_V17"."DICOM_ALL"
    WHERE
        "BodyPartExamined" = 'MEDIASTINUM'
        AND "PatientSex" = 'M'
        AND "StudyDate" > '2014-09-01'
        AND TRY_CAST(REGEXP_SUBSTR("PatientAge", '\\d+') AS INT) = 18
        AND "NumberOfFrames" IS NOT NULL  -- Ensure we can compute size
),
computed_size AS (
    SELECT
        "PatientID",
        "StudyInstanceUID",
        "StudyDate",
        "StudyDescription",
        "SeriesInstanceUID",
        "SeriesDescription",
        "SeriesNumber",
        ROUND(SUM("Rows" * "Columns" * ("BitsAllocated" / 8.0) * "NumFrames") / 1000000.0, 2) AS "TotalSizeMB"
    FROM filtered_images
    GROUP BY
        "PatientID",
        "StudyInstanceUID",
        "StudyDate",
        "StudyDescription",
        "SeriesInstanceUID",
        "SeriesDescription",
        "SeriesNumber"
)
SELECT
    "PatientID",
    "StudyInstanceUID",
    "StudyDate",
    "StudyDescription",
    "SeriesInstanceUID",
    "SeriesDescription",
    "SeriesNumber",
    -- Storage location not available � will be NULL or can be constructed if base URL known
    NULL AS "StorageLocation",
    "TotalSizeMB"
FROM computed_size
ORDER BY
    "PatientID",
    "StudyDate",
    "SeriesInstanceUID";
```
</details>

```sql
WITH

    AND provider_business_practice_location_address_state_name = 'CA'
),

-- Unpivot all 15 specialization columns into rows
unpivoted AS (
  SELECT npi, specialization FROM (
    SELECT npi, healthcare_provider_taxonomy_1_specialization AS specialization FROM mountain_view_providers UNION ALL
    SELECT npi, healthcare_provider_taxonomy_2_specialization FROM mountain_view_providers UNION ALL
    SELECT npi, healthcare_provider_taxonomy_3_specialization FROM mountain_view_providers UNION ALL
    SELECT npi, healthcare_provider_taxonomy_4_specialization FROM mountain_view_providers UNION ALL
    SELECT npi, healthcare_provider_taxonomy_5_specialization FROM mountain_view_providers UNION ALL
    SELECT npi, healthcare_provider_taxonomy_6_specialization FROM mountain_view_providers UNION ALL
    SELECT npi, healthcare_provider_taxonomy_7_specialization FROM mountain_view_providers UNION ALL

    SELECT npi, healthcare_provider_taxonomy_11_specialization FROM mountain_view_providers UNION ALL
    SELECT npi, healthcare_provider_taxonomy_12_specialization FROM mountain_view_providers UNION ALL
    SELECT npi, healthcare_provider_taxonomy_13_specialization FROM mountain_view_providers UNION ALL
    SELECT npi, healthcare_provider_taxonomy_14_specialization FROM mountain_view_providers UNION ALL
    SELECT npi, healthcare_provider_taxonomy_15_specialization FROM mountain_view_providers
  )
  WHERE specialization IS NOT NULL AND specialization != ''
),

-- Count distinct NPIs per specialization
specialization_counts AS (
  SELECT specialization, COUNT(DISTINCT npi) AS distinct_npi_count
  FROM unpivoted
  GROUP BY specialization
),

-- Top 10 specializations by distinct NPI count
top_10 AS (
  SELECT specialization, distinct_npi_count
  FROM specialization_counts
  ORDER BY distinct_npi_count DESC
  LIMIT 10
),

-- Calculate average across top 10
with_average AS (
  SELECT 
    specialization,
    distinct_npi_count,
    AVG(distinct_npi_count) OVER() AS avg_count
  FROM top_10
)

-- Find specialization closest to the average
SELECT specialization, distinct_npi_count
FROM with_average
ORDER BY ABS(distinct_npi_count - avg_count)
LIMIT 1;
```

```sql
    healthcare_provider_taxonomy_11_specialization,
    healthcare_provider_taxonomy_12_specialization,
    healthcare_provider_taxonomy_13_specialization,
    healthcare_provider_taxonomy_14_specialization,
    healthcare_provider_taxonomy_15_specialization
  ]) AS specialization
  WHERE specialization IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(specialization) != ''
),
specialization_counts AS (
  -- Step 3: Count distinct NPIs per specialization and keep top 10
  SELECT 
    specialization,
    COUNT(DISTINCT npi) AS npi_count
  FROM unpivoted_specializations
  GROUP BY specialization
  ORDER BY npi_count DESC
  LIMIT 10
),
avg_and_distance AS (
  -- Step 4: Compute the average count across the top 10,
  --          then calculate absolute distance from that average for each
  SELECT 
    specialization,
    npi_count,
    ROUND(npi_count - AVG(npi_count) OVER(), 4) AS distance_from_avg
  FROM specialization_counts
)
-- Step 5: Return the specialization with count closest to the average
SELECT 
  specialization,
  npi_count
FROM avg_and_distance
ORDER BY ABS(distance_from_avg) ASC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

```sql
-- Step 1: Get CCRCC proteome data with sample type info
WITH proteome_data AS (
  SELECT 
    p.gene_symbol,
    p.aliquot_submitter_id,
    p.protein_abundance_log2ratio,
    m.sample_type
  FROM `isb-cgc-bq.CPTAC.quant_proteome_CPTAC_CCRCC_discovery_study_pdc_current` p
  JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.CPTAC.per_sample_file_metadata_CPTAC3_discovery_and_confirmatory_pdc_current` m
    ON p.sample_id = m.sample_id
  WHERE m.sample_type IN ('Primary Tumor', 'Solid Tissue Normal')
    AND p.protein_abundance_log2ratio IS NOT NULL
),

-- Step 2: Get RNAseq data with log-transformed FPKM
rnaseq_data AS (
  SELECT 
    r.gene_name,
    r.sample_gdc_id,
    r.case_barcode,
    r.sample_type_name,
    LOG(r.fpkm_unstranded + 1) AS log_fpkm
  FROM `isb-cgc-bq.CPTAC.RNAseq_hg38_gdc_current` r
  WHERE r.sample_type_name IN ('Primary Tumor', 'Solid Tissue Normal')
    AND r.fpkm_unstranded IS NOT NULL
    AND r.fpkm_unstranded >= 0
),

-- Step 3: Join proteomics and RNAseq on gene symbol
joined_data AS (
  SELECT 
    p.gene_symbol,
    p.sample_type,
    p.protein_abundance_log2ratio,
    r.log_fpkm,
    -- Assign a unique sample identifier for pairing
    CONCAT(p.aliquot_submitter_id, '_', r.sample_gdc_id) AS join_key
  FROM proteome_data p
  JOIN rnaseq_data r
    ON LOWER(p.gene_symbol) = LOWER(r.gene_name)
  WHERE p.protein_abundance_log2ratio IS NOT NULL
    AND r.log_fpkm IS NOT NULL
),

-- Step 4: Calculate correlation per gene per sample type
correlations AS (
  SELECT 
    gene_symbol,
    sample_type,
    CORR(protein_abundance_log2ratio, log_fpkm) AS correlation
  FROM joined_data
  GROUP BY gene_symbol, sample_type
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3  -- Minimum observations for meaningful correlation
)

-- Step 5: Filter and compute average
SELECT 
  sample_type,
  ROUND(AVG(correlation), 4) AS avg_correlation_abs_gt_05
FROM correlations
WHERE ABS(correlation) > 0.5
GROUP BY sample_type
ORDER BY sample_type;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: Get proteomics data with sample type and case submitter ID
proteomics_samples AS (
  SELECT
    p.gene_symbol,
    p.protein_abundance_log2ratio,
    m.sample_submitter_id,
    m.case_submitter_id,
    m.sample_type
  FROM `isb-cgc-bq.CPTAC.quant_proteome_CPTAC_CCRCC_discovery_study_pdc_current` AS p
  INNER JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.CPTAC.per_sample_file_metadata_CPTAC3_discovery_and_confirmatory_pdc_current` AS m
    ON p.sample_id = m.sample_id
  WHERE m.sample_type IN ('Primary Tumor', 'Solid Tissue Normal')
),

-- Step 2: Collect distinct case IDs from proteomics to limit RNAseq scan
relevant_cases AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT case_submitter_id
  FROM proteomics_samples
),

-- Step 3: Filter RNAseq to only relevant cases and sample types, and restrict project to reduce scan
rnaseq_filtered AS (
  SELECT
    gene_name,
    fpkm_unstranded,
    case_barcode,
    sample_type_name
  FROM `isb-cgc-bq.CPTAC.RNAseq_hg38_gdc_current`
  WHERE sample_type_name IN ('Primary Tumor', 'Solid Tissue Normal')
    AND project_short_name = 'CPTAC-3'
    AND case_barcode IN (SELECT case_submitter_id FROM relevant_cases)
),

-- Step 4: Join proteomics and RNAseq on case, gene symbol, and sample type
joined AS (
  SELECT
    p.case_submitter_id,
    p.sample_type,
    p.gene_symbol,
    p.protein_abundance_log2ratio,
    r.fpkm_unstranded,
    LN(1 + r.fpkm_unstranded) AS log_fpkm
  FROM proteomics_samples AS p
  INNER JOIN rnaseq_filtered AS r
    ON p.case_submitter_id = r.case_barcode
      AND UPPER(p.gene_symbol) = UPPER(r.gene_name)
      AND p.sample_type = r.sample_type_name
),

-- Step 5: Compute correlation per gene and sample type
correlations AS (
  SELECT
    sample_type,
    gene_symbol,
    CORR(protein_abundance_log2ratio, log_fpkm) AS corr
  FROM joined
  GROUP BY sample_type, gene_symbol
),

-- Step 6: Filter to |corr| > 0.5
filtered_correlations AS (
  SELECT
    sample_type,
    corr
  FROM correlations
  WHERE ABS(corr) > 0.5
)

-- Step 7: Average correlation per sample type
SELECT
  sample_type,
  ROUND(AVG(corr), 4) AS avg_correlation
FROM filtered_correlations
GROUP BY sample_type
ORDER BY sample_type;
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH expression AS (
    SELECT
        "case_barcode",
        LOG(10, AVG("normalized_count")) AS log_expression
    FROM TCGA_HG19_DATA_V0.TCGA_HG19_DATA_V0.RNASEQ_GENE_EXPRESSION_UNC_RSEM
    WHERE "HGNC_gene_symbol" = 'TP53'
      AND "project_short_name" = 'TCGA-BRCA'
      AND "normalized_count" > 0
    GROUP BY "case_barcode"
),

mutations AS (
    SELECT
        "case_barcode",
        "Variant_Classification"
    FROM TCGA_HG19_DATA_V0.TCGA_HG19_DATA_V0.SOMATIC_MUTATION_MC3
    WHERE "Hugo_Symbol" = 'TP53'
      AND "project_short_name" = 'TCGA-BRCA'
),

combined AS (
    SELECT
        m."Variant_Classification" AS variant_type,
        e.log_expression
    FROM mutations m
    INNER JOIN expression e
        ON m."case_barcode" = e."case_barcode"
),

grand_stats AS (
    SELECT
        COUNT(*) AS total_n,
        AVG(log_expression) AS grand_mean
    FROM combined
),

group_stats AS (
    SELECT
        variant_type,
        COUNT(*) AS n_j,
        AVG(log_expression) AS group_mean
    FROM combined
    GROUP BY variant_type
),

ss_within AS (
    SELECT
        c.variant_type,
        SUM(POWER(c.log_expression - gs.group_mean, 2)) AS ss_within
    FROM combined c
    JOIN group_stats gs ON c.variant_type = gs.variant_type
    GROUP BY c.variant_type
),

anova_components AS (
    SELECT
        (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM group_stats) AS k,
        MAX(grand_stats.total_n) AS N,
        SUM(group_stats.n_j * POWER(group_stats.group_mean - grand_stats.grand_mean, 2)) AS SSB,
        SUM(ss_within.ss_within) AS SSW
    FROM group_stats, grand_stats, ss_within
    WHERE group_stats.variant_type = ss_within.variant_type
)

SELECT
    N AS "total_number_of_samples",
    k AS "number_of_mutation_types",
    ROUND(SSB / (k - 1), 4) AS "mean_square_between",
    ROUND(SSW / (N - k), 4) AS "mean_square_within",
    ROUND((SSB / (k - 1)) / NULLIF(SSW / (N - k), 0), 4) AS "F_statistic"
FROM anova_components;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Get TP53 expression for TCGA-BRCA (positive counts only, one value per case)
tp53_expression AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        e."case_barcode",
        e."normalized_count"
    FROM "TCGA_HG19_DATA_V0"."TCGA_HG19_DATA_V0"."RNASEQ_GENE_EXPRESSION_UNC_RSEM" e
    WHERE e."HGNC_gene_symbol" = 'TP53'
      AND e."project_short_name" = 'TCGA-BRCA'
      AND e."normalized_count" > 0
      AND e."normalized_count" IS NOT NULL
),

-- Step 2: Get TP53 mutation types for TCGA-BRCA, aggregated per case
-- If a case has multiple different mutation types, concatenate them sorted
tp53_mutation_groups AS (
    SELECT
        m."case_barcode",
        LISTAGG(DISTINCT m."Variant_Classification", ', ')
            WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY m."Variant_Classification") AS mutation_group
    FROM "TCGA_HG19_DATA_V0"."TCGA_HG19_DATA_V0"."SOMATIC_MUTATION_MC3" m
    WHERE m."Hugo_Symbol" = 'TP53'
      AND m."project_short_name" = 'TCGA-BRCA'
    GROUP BY m."case_barcode"
),

-- Step 3: Combine expression with mutation group
-- Cases without TP53 mutation get group 'WT' (wild-type)
combined AS (
    SELECT
        LOG(10, e."normalized_count") AS log_expression,
        COALESCE(mg.mutation_group, 'WT') AS mutation_group
    FROM tp53_expression e
    LEFT JOIN tp53_mutation_groups mg
        ON e."case_barcode" = mg."case_barcode"
),

-- Step 4: Grand statistics (across all samples)
grand_stats AS (
    SELECT
        COUNT(*) AS N,
        AVG(log_expression) AS grand_mean
    FROM combined
),

-- Step 5: Per-group statistics
group_stats AS (
    SELECT
        mutation_group,
        COUNT(*) AS n_j,
        AVG(log_expression) AS mean_j
    FROM combined
    GROUP BY mutation_group
),

-- Step 6: Number of groups
k_val AS (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS k FROM group_stats
),

-- Step 7: Compute SSB = SUM(n_j * (mean_j - grand_mean)^2)
ssb AS (
    SELECT SUM(g.n_j * POWER(g.mean_j - gr.grand_mean, 2)) AS SSB
    FROM group_stats g, grand_stats gr
),

-- Step 8: Compute SSW = SUM of squared deviations within each group
ssw AS (
    SELECT SUM(POWER(c.log_expression - g.mean_j, 2)) AS SSW
    FROM combined c
    JOIN group_stats g ON c.mutation_group = g.mutation_group
)

-- Step 9: Final ANOVA results
SELECT
    gr.N                                                                   AS total_samples,
    k.k                                                                    AS num_mutation_types,
    ROUND(ssb.SSB / (k.k - 1), 4)                                          AS mean_square_between,
    ROUND(ssw.SSW / (gr.N - k.k), 4)                                       AS mean_square_within,
    ROUND((ssb.SSB / (k.k - 1)) / NULLIF(ssw.SSW / (gr.N - k.k), 0), 4)    AS f_statistic
FROM grand_stats gr, k_val k, ssb, ssw;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: Filter KIRP patients with non-null clinical_stage
kirp_patients AS (
    SELECT "case_barcode", "clinical_stage"
    FROM "TCGA_HG38_DATA_V0"."TCGA_BIOCLIN_V0"."CLINICAL"
    WHERE "disease_code" = 'KIRP' 
      AND "clinical_stage" IS NOT NULL
      AND "clinical_stage" != 'None'
),

-- Step 2: Get expression data for the three genes
gene_expression AS (
    SELECT 
        e."case_barcode",
        e."gene_name",
        e."HTSeq__FPKM_UQ"
    FROM "TCGA_HG38_DATA_V0"."TCGA_HG38_DATA_V0"."RNASEQ_GENE_EXPRESSION" e
    INNER JOIN kirp_patients p ON e."case_barcode" = p."case_barcode"
    WHERE e."gene_name" IN ('MT-CO3', 'MT-CO1', 'MT-CO2')
),

-- Step 3: Pivot expression data to one row per patient
pivoted_expression AS (
    SELECT 
        "case_barcode",
        MAX(CASE WHEN "gene_name" = 'MT-CO3' THEN "HTSeq__FPKM_UQ" END) AS "mt_co3",
        MAX(CASE WHEN "gene_name" = 'MT-CO1' THEN "HTSeq__FPKM_UQ" END) AS "mt_co1",
        MAX(CASE WHEN "gene_name" = 'MT-CO2' THEN "HTSeq__FPKM_UQ" END) AS "mt_co2"
    FROM gene_expression
    GROUP BY "case_barcode"
),

-- Step 4: Assign split using HASH (Snowflake equivalent of FARM_FINGERPRINT)
patient_split AS (
    SELECT 
        p."case_barcode",
        p."clinical_stage",
        e."mt_co3",
        e."mt_co1",
        e."mt_co2",
        CASE 
            WHEN MOD(ABS(HASH(p."case_barcode")), 10) < 9 THEN 'train'
            ELSE 'test'
        END AS "split"
    FROM kirp_patients p
    INNER JOIN pivoted_expression e ON p."case_barcode" = e."case_barcode"
),

-- Step 5: Calculate stage averages in training set
stage_averages AS (
    SELECT 
        "clinical_stage",
        AVG("mt_co3") AS "avg_mt_co3",
        AVG("mt_co1") AS "avg_mt_co1",
        AVG("mt_co2") AS "avg_mt_co2"
    FROM patient_split
    WHERE "split" = 'train'
    GROUP BY "clinical_stage"
),

-- Step 6: For each test patient, compute Euclidean distance to each stage average
test_patient_distances AS (
    SELECT 
        t."case_barcode",
        s."clinical_stage",
        SQRT(
            POWER(t."mt_co3" - s."avg_mt_co3", 2) +
            POWER(t."mt_co1" - s."avg_mt_co1", 2) +
            POWER(t."mt_co2" - s."avg_mt_co2", 2)
        ) AS "distance"
    FROM patient_split t
    CROSS JOIN stage_averages s
    WHERE t."split" = 'test'
),

-- Step 7: Assign each test patient to the closest stage
ranked_predictions AS (
    SELECT 
        "case_barcode",
        "clinical_stage",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY "case_barcode" ORDER BY "distance" ASC) AS "rn"
    FROM test_patient_distances
)

-- Final output
SELECT 
    "case_barcode",
    "clinical_stage" AS "predicted_clinical_stage"
FROM ranked_predictions
WHERE "rn" = 1
ORDER BY "case_barcode";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Select eligible KIRP patients with non-null clinical stage
eligible_patients AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        c."case_barcode",
        c."case_gdc_id",
        c."clinical_stage"
    FROM "TCGA_HG38_DATA_V0"."TCGA_BIOCLIN_V0"."CLINICAL" c
    WHERE c."disease_code" = 'KIRP'
      AND c."clinical_stage" IS NOT NULL
      AND c."clinical_stage" != 'None'
),

-- Step 2: Randomly split patients using HASH (deterministic, 90% train, 10% test)
patient_split AS (
    SELECT
        "case_barcode",
        "case_gdc_id",
        "clinical_stage",
        CASE WHEN ABS(HASH("case_barcode")) % 100 < 90 THEN 'train' ELSE 'test' END AS "split"
    FROM eligible_patients
),

-- Step 3: Join with RNAseq expression data for the three target genes
patient_gene_expression AS (
    SELECT
        p."case_barcode",
        p."clinical_stage",
        p."split",
        e."gene_name",
        AVG(e."HTSeq__FPKM_UQ") AS "expr_value"
    FROM patient_split p
    JOIN "TCGA_HG38_DATA_V0"."TCGA_HG38_DATA_V0"."RNASEQ_GENE_EXPRESSION" e
        ON p."case_gdc_id" = e."case_gdc_id"
    WHERE e."gene_name" IN ('MT-CO3', 'MT-CO1', 'MT-CO2')
    GROUP BY p."case_barcode", p."clinical_stage", p."split", e."gene_name"
),

-- Step 4: Calculate average expression per gene per clinical stage in training set
training_stage_averages AS (
    SELECT
        "clinical_stage",
        "gene_name",
        AVG("expr_value") AS "avg_expr"
    FROM patient_gene_expression
    WHERE "split" = 'train'
    GROUP BY "clinical_stage", "gene_name"
),

-- Step 5: Pivot training averages to one column per gene
stage_avg_pivot AS (
    SELECT
        "clinical_stage",
        MAX(CASE WHEN "gene_name" = 'MT-CO1' THEN "avg_expr" END) AS "avg_MT_CO1",
        MAX(CASE WHEN "gene_name" = 'MT-CO2' THEN "avg_expr" END) AS "avg_MT_CO2",
        MAX(CASE WHEN "gene_name" = 'MT-CO3' THEN "avg_expr" END) AS "avg_MT_CO3"
    FROM training_stage_averages
    GROUP BY "clinical_stage"
),

-- Step 6: Pivot test patient expression to one row per patient
test_patient_pivot AS (
    SELECT
        "case_barcode",
        MAX(CASE WHEN "gene_name" = 'MT-CO1' THEN "expr_value" END) AS "expr_MT_CO1",
        MAX(CASE WHEN "gene_name" = 'MT-CO2' THEN "expr_value" END) AS "expr_MT_CO2",
        MAX(CASE WHEN "gene_name" = 'MT-CO3' THEN "expr_value" END) AS "expr_MT_CO3"
    FROM patient_gene_expression
    WHERE "split" = 'test'
    GROUP BY "case_barcode"
),

-- Step 7: Cross join test patients with all stage averages, compute Euclidean distance
patient_distances AS (
    SELECT
        tp."case_barcode",
        sa."clinical_stage",
        SQRT(
            POWER(tp."expr_MT_CO1" - sa."avg_MT_CO1", 2) +
            POWER(tp."expr_MT_CO2" - sa."avg_MT_CO2", 2) +
            POWER(tp."expr_MT_CO3" - sa."avg_MT_CO3", 2)
        ) AS "euclidean_distance"
    FROM test_patient_pivot tp
    CROSS JOIN stage_avg_pivot sa
),

-- Step 8: For each test patient, rank stages by distance and pick the closest
ranked_predictions AS (
    SELECT
        "case_barcode",
        "clinical_stage",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY "case_barcode"
            ORDER BY "euclidean_distance" ASC
        ) AS "rn"
    FROM patient_distances
)

-- Step 9: Final output
SELECT
    "case_barcode",
    "clinical_stage" AS "predicted_clinical_stage"
FROM ranked_predictions
WHERE "rn" = 1
ORDER BY "case_barcode";
```
</details>

```sql
    FROM
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
  -- Step 1: Get imaging Level2 data at HTAN WUSTL excluding unwanted components and electron microscopy
  level2 AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
      Imaging_Assay_Type,
      HTAN_Data_File_ID
    FROM `isb-cgc-bq.HTAN_versioned.imaging_level2_metadata_r5`
    WHERE
      HTAN_Center = 'HTAN WUSTL'
      AND Component IS NOT NULL
      AND Component NOT LIKE '%Auxiliary%'
      AND Component NOT LIKE '%OtherAssay%'
      AND Imaging_Assay_Type NOT LIKE '%Electron%'
  ),

  -- Step 2: Trace to higher-level data files using id_provenance_r5 (parent-child by HTAN_Data_File_ID)
  provenance_children AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
      l2.Imaging_Assay_Type,
      prov.HTAN_Data_File_ID AS child_data_file_id
    FROM level2 l2
    INNER JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.HTAN_versioned.id_provenance_r5` prov
      ON l2.HTAN_Data_File_ID = prov.HTAN_Parent_Data_File_ID
  ),

  -- Step 3: Identify which children exist in Level3 (imaging_level3_segmentation_metadata_r5)
  level3 AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT child_data_file_id
    FROM provenance_children
    WHERE child_data_file_id IN (
      SELECT HTAN_Data_File_ID
      FROM `isb-cgc-bq.HTAN_versioned.imaging_level3_segmentation_metadata_r5`
      WHERE Component IS NOT NULL
        AND Component NOT LIKE '%Auxiliary%'
        AND Component NOT LIKE '%OtherAssay%'
    )
  ),

  -- Step 4: Identify which children exist in Level4 (imaging_level4_metadata_r5)
  level4 AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT child_data_file_id
    FROM provenance_children
    WHERE child_data_file_id IN (
      SELECT HTAN_Data_File_ID
      FROM `isb-cgc-bq.HTAN_versioned.imaging_level4_metadata_r5`
      WHERE Component IS NOT NULL
        AND Component NOT LIKE '%Auxiliary%'
        AND Component NOT LIKE '%OtherAssay%'
    )
  ),

  -- Step 5: Aggregate per imaging assay type to determine presence of Level3 and Level4
  level_presence AS (
    SELECT
      pc.Imaging_Assay_Type,
      MAX(CASE WHEN l3.child_data_file_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_level3,
      MAX(CASE WHEN l4.child_data_file_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_level4
    FROM provenance_children pc
    LEFT JOIN level3 l3 ON pc.child_data_file_id = l3.child_data_file_id
    LEFT JOIN level4 l4 ON pc.child_data_file_id = l4.child_data_file_id
    GROUP BY pc.Imaging_Assay_Type
  )

-- Final output: list imaging assay types and the available levels
SELECT
  l2.Imaging_Assay_Type,
  CONCAT(
    'Level2',
    IF(lp.has_level3 = 1, ', Level3', ''),
    IF(lp.has_level4 = 1, ', Level4', '')
  ) AS available_data_levels
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT Imaging_Assay_Type FROM level2) l2
LEFT JOIN level_presence lp ON l2.Imaging_Assay_Type = lp.Imaging_Assay_Type
ORDER BY l2.Imaging_Assay_Type;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Optimized query to reduce bytes scanned by using EXISTS and early filtering
WITH wustl_level2 AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    Imaging_Assay_Type,
    HTAN_Data_File_ID
  FROM `isb-cgc-bq.HTAN_versioned.imaging_level2_metadata_r5`
  WHERE HTAN_Center = 'HTAN WUSTL'
    AND Component IS NOT NULL
    AND Component NOT LIKE '%Auxiliary%'
    AND Component NOT LIKE '%OtherAssay%'
    AND Imaging_Assay_Type IS NOT NULL
    AND LOWER(Imaging_Assay_Type) NOT LIKE '%electron%microscopy%'
    AND LOWER(Imaging_Assay_Type) NOT LIKE '%em%'
)
SELECT
  l2.Imaging_Assay_Type,
  TRUE AS Level2,
  EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM `isb-cgc-bq.HTAN_versioned.id_provenance_r5` prov
    INNER JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.HTAN_versioned.imaging_level3_segmentation_metadata_r5` l3
      ON prov.entityId = l3.entityId
    WHERE prov.HTAN_Parent_Data_File_ID = l2.HTAN_Data_File_ID
      AND l3.Component IS NOT NULL
      AND l3.Component NOT LIKE '%Auxiliary%'
      AND l3.Component NOT LIKE '%OtherAssay%'
  ) AS Level3,
  EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM `isb-cgc-bq.HTAN_versioned.id_provenance_r5` prov
    INNER JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.HTAN_versioned.imaging_level4_metadata_r5` l4
      ON prov.entityId = l4.entityId
    WHERE prov.HTAN_Parent_Data_File_ID = l2.HTAN_Data_File_ID
      AND l4.Component IS NOT NULL
      AND l4.Component NOT LIKE '%Auxiliary%'
      AND l4.Component NOT LIKE '%OtherAssay%'
  ) AS Level4
FROM wustl_level2 l2
ORDER BY Imaging_Assay_Type;
```
</details>

```sql
    AND "SEX" = 'male'
```

```sql
      AND "CLUSTERS" = '41'
      AND "DEVELOPMENT_STAGE" = '74-year-old human stage'
    GROUP BY "IVAR", "SEX"
),
pivot_avg AS (
    SELECT 
        "FEATURE_NAME",
        MAX(CASE WHEN "SEX" = 'female' THEN avg_expression END) AS female_avg,
        MAX(CASE WHEN "SEX" = 'male' THEN avg_expression END) AS male_avg
    FROM sex_avg
    GROUP BY "FEATURE_NAME"
)
SELECT 
    "FEATURE_NAME",
    ROUND(female_avg - male_avg, 4) AS diff_expression
FROM pivot_avg
WHERE female_avg IS NOT NULL AND male_avg IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY diff_expression DESC
LIMIT 20;
```
