```sql
-- Compute Pearson correlation between Mitelman DB and TCGA frequencies
-- for copy number aberrations (amplifications, gains, losses, deletions)
-- in breast cancer cases (morph=3111, topo=0401).
-- Results are returned per chromosome and aberration type,
-- only including groups with at least 5 matching cytobands.

WITH
  -- total number of distinct Mitelman cases meeting the criteria
  total_cases AS (
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(CAST(RefNo AS STRING), '_', CaseNo)) AS cnt
    FROM `mitelman-db.prod.Cytogen`
    WHERE Morph = '3111' AND Topo = '0401'
  ),

  -- get all valid investigation numbers for each case (needed to join with CytoConverted)
  mitelman_cases_inv AS (
    SELECT c.RefNo, c.CaseNo, i.InvNo
    FROM `mitelman-db.prod.Cytogen` c
    INNER JOIN `mitelman-db.prod.CytogenInv` i
      ON c.RefNo = i.RefNo AND c.CaseNo = i.CaseNo
    WHERE c.Morph = '3111' AND c.Topo = '0401'
  ),

  -- count number of distinct Mitelman cases per cytoband and aberration type
  -- using CytoConverted coordinates overlapping hg38 cytobands
  mitelman_count AS (
    SELECT
      chr.chromosome,
      chr.cytoband_name,
      CASE
        WHEN cc.Type = 'Gain' THEN 'Gain'
        WHEN cc.Type = 'Loss' THEN 'Loss'
        WHEN cc.Type = 'Amplification' THEN 'Amplification'
        WHEN cc.Type = 'Deletion' THEN 'Deletion'
        ELSE 'Unknown'
      END AS aberration_type,
      COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(CAST(cc.RefNo AS STRING), '_', cc.CaseNo)) AS case_count
    FROM `mitelman-db.prod.CytoBands_hg38` chr
    INNER JOIN `mitelman-db.prod.CytoConverted` cc
      ON cc.Chr = chr.chromosome
         AND cc.Start < chr.hg38_stop
         AND cc.End > chr.hg38_start
    INNER JOIN mitelman_cases_inv mci
      ON cc.RefNo = mci.RefNo
         AND cc.CaseNo = mci.CaseNo
         AND cc.InvNo = mci.InvNo
    WHERE cc.Type IN ('Gain', 'Loss', 'Amplification', 'Deletion')
    GROUP BY chromosome, cytoband_name, aberration_type
  ),

  -- convert counts to frequencies (percentage of total cases)
  mitelman_freq AS (
    SELECT
      chromosome,
      cytoband_name,
      aberration_type,
      SAFE_DIVIDE(case_count, (SELECT cnt FROM total_cases)) * 100 AS freq
    FROM mitelman_count
  ),

  -- Compute TCGA frequencies for BRCA samples
  tcga_total_samples AS (
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT sample_id) AS cnt
    FROM `isb-cgc.tcga_2019_02.Copy_Number_Segment`
    WHERE project_id = 'TCGA-BRCA'
  ),

  tcga_segments AS (
    SELECT
      sample_id,
      chromosome,
      start_pos AS segment_start,
      end_pos AS segment_end,
      segment_mean,
      CASE
        WHEN segment_mean > 0.8 THEN 'Amplification'
        WHEN segment_mean > 0.2 AND segment_mean <= 0.8 THEN 'Gain'
        WHEN segment_mean < -0.8 THEN 'Deletion'
        WHEN segment_mean < -0.2 AND segment_mean >= -0.8 THEN 'Loss'
        ELSE 'Normal'
      END AS aberration_type
    FROM `isb-cgc.tcga_2019_02.Copy_Number_Segment`
    WHERE project_id = 'TCGA-BRCA'
      AND segment_mean IS NOT NULL
  ),

  tcga_count AS (
    SELECT
      chr.chromosome,
      chr.cytoband_name,
      s.aberration_type,
      COUNT(DISTINCT s.sample_id) AS sample_count
    FROM `mitelman-db.prod.CytoBands_hg38` chr
    INNER JOIN tcga_segments s
      ON s.chromosome = chr.chromosome
         AND s.segment_start < chr.hg38_stop
         AND s.segment_end > chr.hg38_start
    WHERE s.aberration_type IN ('Amplification', 'Gain', 'Loss', 'Deletion')
    GROUP BY chromosome, cytoband_name, aberration_type
  ),

  tcga_freq AS (
    SELECT
      chromosome,
      cytoband_name,
      aberration_type,
      SAFE_DIVIDE(sample_count, (SELECT cnt FROM tcga_total_samples)) * 100 AS freq
    FROM tcga_count
  ),

  -- join Mitelman and TCGA frequencies on chromosome, cytoband, and aberration type
  combined AS (
    SELECT
      m.chromosome,
      m.cytoband_name,
      m.aberration_type,
      m.freq AS mitelman_freq,
      t.freq AS tcga_freq
    FROM mitelman_freq m
    INNER JOIN tcga_freq t
      ON m.chromosome = t.chromosome
         AND m.cytoband_name = t.cytoband_name
         AND m.aberration_type = t.aberration_type
  )

-- final correlation per chromosome and aberration type
SELECT
  chromosome,
  aberration_type,
  ROUND(CORR(mitelman_freq, tcga_freq), 4) AS correlation_coefficient,
  ROUND(`isb-cgc-bq.functions.corr_pvalue_current`(CORR(mitelman_freq, tcga_freq), COUNT(*)), 4) AS p_value
FROM combined
GROUP BY chromosome, aberration_type
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
ORDER BY chromosome, aberration_type;
```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Compute Pearson correlation between Mitelman and TCGA copy number aberration frequencies per chromosome.
-- Uses publicly available ISB-CGC TCGA tables.
-- Only correlations with at least 5 data points (cytobands) are returned.

WITH
-- Step 1: Identify all distinct Mitelman cases with morph=3111 and topo=0401
mitelman_cases AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT RefNo, CaseNo, InvNo
  FROM `mitelman-db.prod.Cytogen`
  WHERE Morph = '3111' AND Topo = '0401'
),

-- Total number of distinct Mitelman cases
total_mitelman_cases AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM mitelman_cases
),

-- Step 2: For each cytoband, count Mitelman cases with gain or loss overlapping that cytoband
mitelman_cytoband_freq AS (
  SELECT
    cb.chromosome,
    cb.cytoband_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(cc.RefNo, '_', cc.CaseNo, '_', cc.InvNo)) AS gain_cases,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(cc_l.RefNo, '_', cc_l.CaseNo, '_', cc_l.InvNo)) AS loss_cases
  FROM `mitelman-db.prod.CytoBands_hg38` AS cb
  LEFT JOIN `mitelman-db.prod.CytoConverted` AS cc
    ON cb.chromosome = cc.Chr
   AND cc.Start < cb.hg38_stop
   AND cc.End > cb.hg38_start
   AND cc.Type = 'Gain'
   AND CONCAT(cc.RefNo, '_', cc.CaseNo, '_', cc.InvNo) IN
       (SELECT CONCAT(RefNo, '_', CaseNo, '_', InvNo) FROM mitelman_cases)
  LEFT JOIN `mitelman-db.prod.CytoConverted` AS cc_l
    ON cb.chromosome = cc_l.Chr
   AND cc_l.Start < cb.hg38_stop
   AND cc_l.End > cb.hg38_start
   AND cc_l.Type = 'Loss'
   AND CONCAT(cc_l.RefNo, '_', cc_l.CaseNo, '_', cc_l.InvNo) IN
       (SELECT CONCAT(RefNo, '_', CaseNo, '_', InvNo) FROM mitelman_cases)
  GROUP BY cb.chromosome, cb.cytoband_name
),

-- Step 3: Compute Mitelman frequencies
mitelman_freq AS (
  SELECT
    chromosome,
    cytoband_name,
    gain_cases / (SELECT cnt FROM total_mitelman_cases) AS freq_gain_mitelman,
    loss_cases / (SELECT cnt FROM total_mitelman_cases) AS freq_loss_mitelman
  FROM mitelman_cytoband_freq
),

-- Step 4: Get TCGA BRCA copy number data using the public TCGA_v2.CopyNumber table
tcga_brca_cnv AS (
  SELECT
    SampleBarcode,
    Chromosome,
    Start_Position,
    End_Position,
    Copy_Number_Value AS Value
  FROM `isb-cgc-bq.TCGA_v2.CopyNumber`
  WHERE Study = 'BRCA'
    AND SampleType = 'Tumor'
),

-- Step 5: Get total number of BRCA tumor samples
total_tcga_samples AS (
  SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT SampleBarcode) AS cnt
  FROM tcga_brca_cnv
),

-- Step 6: Map CNV to cytobands using CytoBands_hg38
tcga_cytoband_cnv AS (
  SELECT
    cnv.SampleBarcode,
    cnv.Value,
    cb.chromosome,
    cb.cytoband_name
  FROM tcga_brca_cnv AS cnv
  INNER JOIN `mitelman-db.prod.CytoBands_hg38` AS cb
    ON cnv.Chromosome = cb.chromosome
   AND cnv.Start_Position < cb.hg38_stop
   AND cnv.End_Position > cb.hg38_start
),

-- Step 7: Compute per-cytoband TCGA frequencies for each aberration type
tcga_cytoband_freq AS (
  SELECT
    chromosome,
    cytoband_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN Value = 2 THEN SampleBarcode END) / (SELECT cnt FROM total_tcga_samples) AS freq_amp,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN Value = 1 THEN SampleBarcode END) / (SELECT cnt FROM total_tcga_samples) AS freq_gain,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN Value = -1 THEN SampleBarcode END) / (SELECT cnt FROM total_tcga_samples) AS freq_hetero_loss,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN Value = -2 THEN SampleBarcode END) / (SELECT cnt FROM total_tcga_samples) AS freq_homo_deletion
  FROM tcga_cytoband_cnv
  GROUP BY chromosome, cytoband_name
),

-- Step 8: Join Mitelman and TCGA frequencies on chromosome and cytoband
combined AS (
  SELECT
    m.chromosome,
    m.cytoband_name,
    m.freq_gain_mitelman,
    m.freq_loss_mitelman,
    t.freq_amp,
    t.freq_gain AS tcga_gain,
    t.freq_hetero_loss AS tcga_hetero_loss,
    t.freq_homo_deletion AS tcga_homo_del
  FROM mitelman_freq AS m
  INNER JOIN tcga_cytoband_freq AS t
    ON m.chromosome = t.chromosome AND m.cytoband_name = t.cytoband_name
),

-- Step 9: Compute Pearson correlation for each chromosome and aberration type
corr_amp AS (
  SELECT
    chromosome,
    'amplification' AS aberration_type,
    COUNT(*) AS n,
    CORR(freq_gain_mitelman, freq_amp) AS corr
  FROM combined
  WHERE freq_gain_mitelman IS NOT NULL AND freq_amp IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY chromosome
),
corr_gain AS (
  SELECT
    chromosome,
    'gain' AS aberration_type,
    COUNT(*) AS n,
    CORR(freq_gain_mitelman, tcga_gain) AS corr
  FROM combined
  WHERE freq_gain_mitelman IS NOT NULL AND tcga_gain IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY chromosome
),
corr_loss AS (
  SELECT
    chromosome,
    'loss' AS aberration_type,
    COUNT(*) AS n,
    CORR(freq_loss_mitelman, tcga_hetero_loss) AS corr
  FROM combined
  WHERE freq_loss_mitelman IS NOT NULL AND tcga_hetero_loss IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY chromosome
),
corr_del AS (
  SELECT
    chromosome,
    'deletion' AS aberration_type,
    COUNT(*) AS n,
    CORR(freq_loss_mitelman, tcga_homo_del) AS corr
  FROM combined
  WHERE freq_loss_mitelman IS NOT NULL AND tcga_homo_del IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY chromosome
),

-- Union all four aberration types
all_corr AS (
  SELECT * FROM corr_amp
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM corr_gain
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM corr_loss
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM corr_del
)

-- Step 10: Filter by at least 5 data points and compute p-value
SELECT
  chromosome,
  aberration_type,
  ROUND(corr, 4) AS correlation,
  ROUND(`isb-cgc-bq.functions.corr_pvalue_current`(corr, n), 6) AS p_value
FROM all_corr
WHERE n >= 5 AND corr IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY chromosome, aberration_type;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH prioritized_venue AS (
  SELECT 
    p.id,
    -- Prioritize venue: journal > proceedings > book > book series
    COALESCE(
      NULLIF(p.journal.title, 'None'),
      NULLIF(p.proceedings_title.preferred, 'None'),
      NULLIF(p.book_title.preferred, 'None'),
      NULLIF(p.book_series_title.preferred, 'None')
    ) AS venue_title,
    p.date_inserted,
    p.research_org_city_names
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.dimensions_ai_covid19.publications` p
  WHERE p.date_inserted >= TIMESTAMP('2021-01-01')
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 
      FROM UNNEST(p.research_org_city_names) AS city
      WHERE city = 'Qianjiang'
    )
)
SELECT DISTINCT venue_title
FROM prioritized_venue
WHERE venue_title IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY venue_title;
```

```sql
WITH publication_data AS (
  SELECT
    id,
    COALESCE(
      journal.title,
      proceedings_title.preferred,
      book_title.preferred,
      book_series_title.preferred
    ) AS venue_title
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.dimensions_ai_covid19.publications`
  WHERE
    date_inserted >= TIMESTAMP('2021-01-01')
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM UNNEST(research_org_city_names) AS city
      WHERE LOWER(city) = LOWER('Qianjiang')
    )
)
SELECT venue_title
FROM publication_data;
```

```sql
-- Step 1: Filter activities based on molecule properties, pChEMBL, standard value, and duplicate limits
WITH filtered_activities AS (
    SELECT 
        a.assay_id,
        a.doc_id,
        a.molregno,
        a.standard_type,
        a.standard_value,
        a.standard_relation,
        a.activity_id,
        a.pchembl_value,
        a.potential_duplicate,
        cp.heavy_atoms,
        cs.canonical_smiles
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.activities` a
    JOIN `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.compound_properties` cp 
        ON a.molregno = cp.molregno
    JOIN `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.compound_structures` cs 
        ON a.molregno = cs.molregno
    WHERE 
        -- heavy atoms between 10 and 15
        SAFE_CAST(cp.heavy_atoms AS INT64) BETWEEN 10 AND 15
        -- pChEMBL > 10 and not null
        AND a.pchembl_value IS NOT NULL 
        AND SAFE_CAST(a.pchembl_value AS FLOAT64) > 10
        -- standard_value not null
        AND a.standard_value IS NOT NULL
),

-- Step 2: Aggregate per molecule, assay, standard type
activity_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        assay_id,
        standard_type,
        molregno,
        COUNT(*) AS activity_count,
        SUM(SAFE_CAST(potential_duplicate AS INT64)) AS dup_count,
        -- Pick the activity with the highest activity_id as representative
        ARRAY_AGG(activity_id ORDER BY activity_id DESC LIMIT 1)[OFFSET(0)] AS rep_activity_id,
        ARRAY_AGG(doc_id ORDER BY activity_id DESC LIMIT 1)[OFFSET(0)] AS rep_doc_id,
        ARRAY_AGG(standard_value ORDER BY activity_id DESC LIMIT 1)[OFFSET(0)] AS rep_std_value,
        ARRAY_AGG(standard_relation ORDER BY activity_id DESC LIMIT 1)[OFFSET(0)] AS rep_std_relation,
        ARRAY_AGG(canonical_smiles ORDER BY activity_id DESC LIMIT 1)[OFFSET(0)] AS canonical_smiles,
        ANY_VALUE(heavy_atoms) AS heavy_atoms   -- same for all rows of the molecule
    FROM filtered_activities
    GROUP BY assay_id, standard_type, molregno
    HAVING 
        activity_count < 5 
        AND dup_count < 2
),

-- Step 3: Self-join to find pairs (different molecules, same assay and standard type)
pairs AS (
    SELECT 
        a.assay_id,
        a.standard_type,
        a.molregno AS molregno1,
        b.molregno AS molregno2,
        a.rep_activity_id AS act_id1,
        b.rep_activity_id AS act_id2,
        a.rep_doc_id AS doc_id1,
        b.rep_doc_id AS doc_id2,
        a.rep_std_value AS std_val1,
        b.rep_std_value AS std_val2,
        a.rep_std_relation AS std_rel1,
        b.rep_std_relation AS std_rel2,
        a.canonical_smiles AS smi1,
        b.canonical_smiles AS smi2,
        GREATEST(SAFE_CAST(a.heavy_atoms AS INT64), SAFE_CAST(b.heavy_atoms AS INT64)) AS max_heavy_atoms
    FROM activity_stats a
    JOIN activity_stats b 
        ON a.assay_id = b.assay_id 
        AND a.standard_type = b.standard_type 
        AND a.molregno < b.molregno
),

-- Step 4: Compute percent rank for all documents (needed for date calculation)
doc_rank AS (
    SELECT 
        doc_id,
        journal,
        year,
        first_page,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY journal, year 
            ORDER BY SAFE_CAST(first_page AS INT64) ASC
        ) AS rn,
        COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY journal, year) AS cnt
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.docs`
    WHERE 
        year IS NOT NULL 
        AND first_page IS NOT NULL 
        AND journal IS NOT NULL
        AND SAFE_CAST(year AS INT64) IS NOT NULL
        AND SAFE_CAST(first_page AS INT64) IS NOT NULL
),

doc_date AS (
    SELECT 
        doc_id,
        SAFE_CAST(year AS INT64) AS pub_year,
        CASE 
            WHEN cnt = 1 THEN 0.0 
            ELSE (rn - 1.0) / (cnt - 1.0) 
        END AS percent_rank
    FROM doc_rank
),

doc_final_date AS (
    SELECT 
        doc_id,
        pub_year,
        FLOOR(percent_rank * 11) + 1 AS pub_month,
        (FLOOR(percent_rank * 308) % 28) + 1 AS pub_day
    FROM doc_date
),

-- Step 5: Combine pairs with document dates and compute final outputs
pair_dates AS (
    SELECT 
        p.*,
        d1.pub_year AS pub_year1,
        d1.pub_month AS pub_month1,
        d1.pub_day AS pub_day1,
        d2.pub_year AS pub_year2,
        d2.pub_month AS pub_month2,
        d2.pub_day AS pub_day2,
        -- Highest document id among the two
        GREATEST(SAFE_CAST(p.doc_id1 AS INT64), SAFE_CAST(p.doc_id2 AS INT64)) AS highest_doc_id,
        -- Latest publication date as DATE
        GREATEST(
            DATE(d1.pub_year, d1.pub_month, d1.pub_day),
            DATE(d2.pub_year, d2.pub_month, d2.pub_day)
        ) AS latest_pub_date
    FROM pairs p
    LEFT JOIN doc_final_date d1 ON p.doc_id1 = d1.doc_id
    LEFT JOIN doc_final_date d2 ON p.doc_id2 = d2.doc_id
),

final AS (
    SELECT 
        max_heavy_atoms,
        FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', latest_pub_date) AS latest_publication_date,
        highest_doc_id,
        -- Classify change in standard values
        CASE
            WHEN SAFE_CAST(std_val1 AS FLOAT64) > SAFE_CAST(std_val2 AS FLOAT64) 
                 AND std_rel1 NOT IN ('<', '<=')
                 AND std_rel2 NOT IN ('>', '>=') 
            THEN 'decrease'
            WHEN SAFE_CAST(std_val1 AS FLOAT64) < SAFE_CAST(std_val2 AS FLOAT64) 
                 AND std_rel1 NOT IN ('>', '>=')
                 AND std_rel2 NOT IN ('<', '<=') 
            THEN 'increase'
            WHEN SAFE_CAST(std_val1 AS FLOAT64) = SAFE_CAST(std_val2 AS FLOAT64) 
                 AND std_rel1 = '=' 
                 AND std_rel2 = '=' 
            THEN 'no-change'
            ELSE 'unknown'
        END AS std_change,
        -- UUID from activity IDs
        TO_HEX(MD5(TO_JSON_STRING(STRUCT(act_id1, act_id2)))) AS uuid_activity_ids,
        -- UUID from canonical SMILES
        TO_HEX(MD5(TO_JSON_STRING(STRUCT(smi1, smi2)))) AS uuid_canonical_smiles
    FROM pair_dates
)

-- Final output
SELECT * FROM final;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Compute synthetic publication date for each document
docs_with_date AS (
  SELECT 
    doc_id,
    journal,
    year,
    first_page,
    -- Year: use publication year, default 1970 if missing
    COALESCE(SAFE_CAST(year AS INT64), 1970) AS pub_year,
    -- Percent rank within same journal and year, ordered by first page numeric value
    PERCENT_RANK() OVER (
      PARTITION BY journal, year 
      ORDER BY SAFE_CAST(first_page AS INT64)
    ) AS pct_rank
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.docs_29`
  WHERE journal IS NOT NULL AND year IS NOT NULL AND first_page IS NOT NULL
),
-- Compute month and day from percent rank, then construct date
doc_date AS (
  SELECT 
    doc_id,
    pub_year,
    -- Month: floor(pct_rank * 11) + 1, cast to INT64
    CAST(FLOOR(pct_rank * 11) + 1 AS INT64) AS pub_month,
    -- Day: (floor(pct_rank * 308) % 28) + 1, cast to INT64
    CAST(MOD(CAST(FLOOR(pct_rank * 308) AS INT64), 28) + 1 AS INT64) AS pub_day
  FROM docs_with_date
),
-- Prepare filtered activities with all required conditions
filtered_activities AS (
  SELECT 
    a.activity_id,
    a.assay_id,
    a.standard_type,
    a.molregno,
    a.doc_id,
    a.standard_value,
    a.standard_relation,
    a.pchembl_value,
    -- Heavy atoms (cast to int)
    SAFE_CAST(cp.heavy_atoms AS INT64) AS heavy_atoms,
    -- Canonical SMILES
    cs.canonical_smiles,
    -- Document date
    dd.pub_year,
    dd.pub_month,
    dd.pub_day,
    -- Synthetic date as DATE
    DATE(dd.pub_year, dd.pub_month, dd.pub_day) AS pub_date,
    -- Count activities per (molregno, assay) and duplicate count
    COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY a.molregno, a.assay_id) AS activity_count,
    COUNTIF(a.potential_duplicate = '1') OVER (PARTITION BY a.molregno, a.assay_id) AS duplicate_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.activities_29` a
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.compound_properties_29` cp
    ON a.molregno = cp.molregno
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.compound_structures_29` cs
    ON a.molregno = cs.molregno
  JOIN doc_date dd
    ON a.doc_id = dd.doc_id
  WHERE 
    -- Non-null standard value
    a.standard_value IS NOT NULL
    -- pChEMBL > 10
    AND SAFE_CAST(a.pchembl_value AS FLOAT64) > 10
    -- Heavy atoms between 10 and 15 inclusive
    AND SAFE_CAST(cp.heavy_atoms AS INT64) BETWEEN 10 AND 15
    -- Standard relation must be '=' for unambiguous comparison
    AND a.standard_relation = '='
)
-- Now find pairs of different molecules in same assay and standard type
SELECT 
  -- Maximum heavy atom count (as integer)
  GREATEST(a.heavy_atoms, b.heavy_atoms) AS max_heavy_atom_count,
  -- Latest publication date
  GREATEST(a.pub_date, b.pub_date) AS latest_publication_date,
  -- Highest document ID
  GREATEST(a.doc_id, b.doc_id) AS highest_doc_id,
  -- Classify change in standard values
  CASE
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(a.standard_value AS FLOAT64) > SAFE_CAST(b.standard_value AS FLOAT64) THEN 'decrease'
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(a.standard_value AS FLOAT64) < SAFE_CAST(b.standard_value AS FLOAT64) THEN 'increase'
    ELSE 'no-change'
  END AS change_classification,
  -- UUID generated from both activity IDs and both canonical SMILES
  TO_HEX(
    MD5(
      TO_JSON_STRING(
        STRUCT(a.activity_id AS a1, b.activity_id AS a2, a.canonical_smiles AS s1, b.canonical_smiles AS s2)
      )
    )
  ) AS pair_uuid
FROM filtered_activities a
JOIN filtered_activities b
  ON a.assay_id = b.assay_id
    AND a.standard_type = b.standard_type
    AND a.molregno < b.molregno
WHERE 
  -- Both molecules must satisfy the activity count conditions
  a.activity_count < 5
  AND b.activity_count < 5
  AND a.duplicate_count < 2
  AND b.duplicate_count < 2;
```

<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- This query retrieves 2016 committees that supported at least one candidate and
-- received individual small-dollar contributions (amount > 0 and < 200) totalling more than $0.
-- For each committee: name, number of unique candidates supported, alphabetical candidate names,
-- and total sum of small-dollar contributions.

WITH
  -- Committees that are linked to at least one candidate in 2016
  committees_with_candidates AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
      c.cmte_id,
      c.cmte_nm,
      l.cand_id
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.fec.committee_2016` c
    INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.fec.candidate_committee_2016` l
      ON c.cmte_id = l.cmte_id
      AND l.fec_election_yr = 2016
  ),

  -- Candidate names for each candidate ID
  candidate_names AS (
    SELECT cand_id, cand_name
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.fec.candidate_2016`
  ),

  -- Individual contributions to 2016 committees that are small-dollar (0 < amount < 200)
  small_dollar_contributions AS (
    SELECT
      cmte_id,
      transaction_amt
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.fec.committee_contributions_2016`
    WHERE transaction_amt > 0
      AND transaction_amt < 200
  ),

  -- Aggregate small-dollar contributions per committee
  committee_small_dollar AS (
    SELECT
      cmte_id,
      SUM(transaction_amt) AS total_small_dollar
    FROM small_dollar_contributions
    GROUP BY cmte_id
    HAVING SUM(transaction_amt) > 0
  ),

  -- Combine candidate information per committee (distinct candidates)
  committee_candidates AS (
    SELECT
      cwc.cmte_id,
      cwc.cmte_nm,
      cn.cand_name
    FROM committees_with_candidates cwc
    INNER JOIN candidate_names cn
      ON cwc.cand_id = cn.cand_id
  ),

  -- Aggregate candidate count and sorted names per committee
  committee_candidate_agg AS (
    SELECT
      cmte_id,
      cmte_nm,
      COUNT(DISTINCT cand_name) AS num_candidates,
      STRING_AGG(DISTINCT cand_name, ',' ORDER BY cand_name) AS candidate_names
    FROM committee_candidates
    GROUP BY cmte_id, cmte_nm
  )

-- Final result: committees with both candidate support and small-dollar contributions
SELECT
  cca.cmte_nm AS committee_name,
  cca.num_candidates,
  cca.candidate_names,
  csd.total_small_dollar
FROM committee_candidate_agg cca
INNER JOIN committee_small_dollar csd
  ON cca.cmte_id = csd.cmte_id
ORDER BY committee_name;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH

committees_2016 AS (

  UNION ALL

  FROM `bigquery-public-data.fec.cm88`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT cmte_id, cmte_nm 
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.fec.cm90`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT cmte_id, cmte_nm 
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.fec.cm92`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT cmte_id, cmte_nm 
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.fec.cm94`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT cmte_id, cmte_nm 
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.fec.cm96`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT cmte_id, cmte_nm 
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.fec.cm98`
),
-- Small-dollar contributions per committee from indiv16
small_dollar_by_committee AS (
  SELECT 
    cmte_id,
    SUM(transaction_amt) AS total_small_dollar
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.fec.indiv16`
  WHERE transaction_amt > 0 
    AND transaction_amt < 200
  GROUP BY cmte_id
  HAVING total_small_dollar > 0 AND total_small_dollar < 200
),
-- Committees that support at least one candidate (from pas216)
committee_candidates AS (
  SELECT 
    cmte_id,
    cand_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.fec.pas216`
  GROUP BY cmte_id, cand_id
),
-- Candidate names from candidate_2016 (using cand_name column)
candidates_2016 AS (
  SELECT cand_id, cand_name AS cand_nm
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.fec.candidate_2016`
),
-- Join to get committees with both small-dollar and candidate support
qualified_committees AS (
  SELECT 
    s.cmte_id,
    s.total_small_dollar,
    cc.cand_id,
    cn.cand_nm
  FROM small_dollar_by_committee s
  JOIN committee_candidates cc ON s.cmte_id = cc.cmte_id
  LEFT JOIN candidates_2016 cn ON cc.cand_id = cn.cand_id
),
-- Aggregate per committee
committee_aggregation AS (
  SELECT 
    cmte_id,
    COUNT(DISTINCT cand_id) AS num_candidates,
    STRING_AGG(DISTINCT IFNULL(cand_nm, cand_id), ', ' ORDER BY IFNULL(cand_nm, cand_id)) AS candidate_names,
    ANY_VALUE(total_small_dollar) AS total_small_dollar_sum
  FROM qualified_committees
  GROUP BY cmte_id
)
-- Final output
SELECT 
  cm.cmte_nm AS committee_name,
  ca.num_candidates,
  ca.candidate_names,
  ROUND(ca.total_small_dollar_sum, 4) AS total_small_dollar_contributions
FROM committee_aggregation ca
JOIN committees_2016 cm ON ca.cmte_id = cm.cmte_id
ORDER BY committee_name;
```

### 63. bq418 (DB: `targetome_reactome`)
**Question**: Determine which three lowest-level Reactome pathways (with TAS evidence) have the highest chi-squared statistics, considering only Homo sapiens targets associated with sorafenib under the conditions that the median assay value is ≤ 100 and both low and high assay values are ≤ 100 or null. For each of these three pathways, how many of these targets and non-targets lie within the pathway and outside it?

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>

<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Get sorafenib drug ID
sorafenib_drug AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT drugID
    FROM `isb-cgc-bq.targetome_versioned.drug_synonyms_v1`
    WHERE LOWER(synonym) LIKE '%sorafenib%'
),

-- Get sorafenib targets with filtered assay conditions
sorafenib_targets AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT i.targetID, i.target_uniprotID
    FROM `isb-cgc-bq.targetome_versioned.interactions_v1` i
    INNER JOIN sorafenib_drug sd ON i.drugID = sd.drugID
    INNER JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.targetome_versioned.experiments_v1` e ON i.expID = e.expID
    WHERE i.targetSpecies = 'Homo sapiens'
      AND i.target_uniprotID IS NOT NULL
      AND e.exp_assayValueMedian IS NOT NULL
      AND e.exp_assayValueMedian <= 100
      AND (e.exp_assayValueLow IS NULL OR e.exp_assayValueLow <= 100)
      AND (e.exp_assayValueHigh IS NULL OR e.exp_assayValueHigh <= 100)
),

-- Get all lowest-level Homo sapiens pathways  
lowest_human_pathways AS (
    SELECT stable_id, name
    FROM `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.pathway_v77`
    WHERE lowest_level = TRUE
      AND species = 'Homo sapiens'
),

-- Get TAS evidence physical entities in these pathways
pathway_tas_entities AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT pp.pathway_stable_id, pe.uniprot_id
    FROM `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.pe_to_pathway_v77` pp
    INNER JOIN lowest_human_pathways lhp ON pp.pathway_stable_id = lhp.stable_id
    INNER JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.physical_entity_v77` pe 
        ON pp.pe_stable_id = pe.stable_id
    WHERE pp.evidence_code = 'TAS'
      AND pe.uniprot_id IS NOT NULL
),

-- Count total sorafenib targets
target_counts AS (
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT target_uniprotID) AS total_targets
    FROM sorafenib_targets
),

-- For each pathway, calculate contingency table
pathway_contingency AS (
    SELECT 
        lhp.stable_id AS pathway_id,
        lhp.name,
        -- a: targets in pathway
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN st.target_uniprotID = pte.uniprot_id 
             THEN st.target_uniprotID END) AS targets_in_pathway,
        -- b: targets not in pathway (total targets - targets in pathway)
        (SELECT total_targets FROM target_counts) - 
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN st.target_uniprotID = pte.uniprot_id 
             THEN st.target_uniprotID END) AS targets_out_pathway,
        -- c: non-targets in pathway (total TAS entities in pathway - targets in pathway)
        COUNT(DISTINCT pte.uniprot_id) - 
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN st.target_uniprotID = pte.uniprot_id 
             THEN st.target_uniprotID END) AS non_targets_in_pathway,
        -- d: non-targets not in pathway (total human TAS entities - total TAS entities in pathway)
        (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT uniprot_id) FROM pathway_tas_entities) - 
        COUNT(DISTINCT pte.uniprot_id) AS non_targets_out_pathway
    FROM lowest_human_pathways lhp
    LEFT JOIN pathway_tas_entities pte ON lhp.stable_id = pte.pathway_stable_id
    LEFT JOIN sorafenib_targets st ON pte.uniprot_id = st.target_uniprotID
    GROUP BY lhp.stable_id, lhp.name
),

-- Calculate chi-squared statistic for each pathway
pathway_chisq AS (
    SELECT 
        name,
        targets_in_pathway,
        targets_out_pathway,
        non_targets_in_pathway,
        non_targets_out_pathway,
        ROUND(
            CASE 
                WHEN (targets_in_pathway + targets_out_pathway) > 0 
                 AND (non_targets_in_pathway + non_targets_out_pathway) > 0
                 AND (targets_in_pathway + non_targets_in_pathway) > 0
                 AND (targets_out_pathway + non_targets_out_pathway) > 0
                THEN 
                    (targets_in_pathway * non_targets_out_pathway - targets_out_pathway * non_targets_in_pathway) *
                    (targets_in_pathway * non_targets_out_pathway - targets_out_pathway * non_targets_in_pathway) /
                    ((targets_in_pathway + targets_out_pathway) * 
                     (non_targets_in_pathway + non_targets_out_pathway) *
                     (targets_in_pathway + non_targets_in_pathway) *
                     (targets_out_pathway + non_targets_out_pathway))
                ELSE 0
            END, 4
        ) AS chi_squared
    FROM pathway_contingency
)

-- Top 3 pathways by chi-squared
SELECT 
    name AS pathway_name,
    targets_in_pathway,
    targets_out_pathway,
    non_targets_in_pathway,
    non_targets_out_pathway,
    chi_squared
FROM pathway_chisq
ORDER BY chi_squared DESC
LIMIT 3;
```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
  -- All human uniprot_ids that appear in Reactome with TAS evidence
  human_uniprots AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT pe.uniprot_id
    FROM `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.pe_to_pathway_v77` ppt
    JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.physical_entity_v77` pe
      ON ppt.pe_stable_id = pe.stable_id
    JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.pathway_v77` pw
      ON ppt.pathway_stable_id = pw.stable_id
    WHERE ppt.evidence_code = 'TAS'
      AND pw.species = 'Homo sapiens'
  ),

  -- Targets: sorafenib interactions with Homo sapiens targets meeting assay conditions
  target_uniprots AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT i.target_uniprotID AS uniprot_id
    FROM `isb-cgc-bq.targetome_versioned.interactions_v1` i
    JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.targetome_versioned.experiments_v1` e
      ON i.expID = e.expID AND i.sourceID = e.sourceID
    WHERE LOWER(i.drugName) = 'sorafenib'
      AND i.targetSpecies = 'Homo sapiens'
      AND e.exp_assayValueMedian IS NOT NULL
      AND e.exp_assayValueMedian <= 100
      AND (e.exp_assayValueLow IS NULL OR e.exp_assayValueLow <= 100)
      AND (e.exp_assayValueHigh IS NULL OR e.exp_assayValueHigh <= 100)
  ),

  final_targets AS (
    SELECT uniprot_id
    FROM target_uniprots
    WHERE uniprot_id IN (SELECT uniprot_id FROM human_uniprots)
  ),

  -- Lowest-level pathways with at least one TAS association to any human protein
  candidate_pathways AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT pw.stable_id
    FROM `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.pathway_v77` pw
    WHERE pw.lowest_level = TRUE
      AND pw.species = 'Homo sapiens'
      AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.pe_to_pathway_v77` ppt
        JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.physical_entity_v77` pe
          ON ppt.pe_stable_id = pe.stable_id
        WHERE ppt.pathway_stable_id = pw.stable_id
          AND ppt.evidence_code = 'TAS'
          AND pe.uniprot_id IN (SELECT uniprot_id FROM human_uniprots)
      )
  ),

  -- Summary counts
  counts AS (
    SELECT
      (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT uniprot_id) FROM human_uniprots) AS total_human,
      (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT uniprot_id) FROM final_targets) AS n_target
  ),

  -- For each candidate pathway, compute path_count and target_in
  path_stats AS (
    SELECT
      cp.stable_id,
      COUNT(DISTINCT pe.uniprot_id) AS path_count,
      COUNT(DISTINCT ft.uniprot_id) AS target_in
    FROM candidate_pathways cp
    JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.pe_to_pathway_v77` ppt
      ON cp.stable_id = ppt.pathway_stable_id
    JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.physical_entity_v77` pe
      ON ppt.pe_stable_id = pe.stable_id
    LEFT JOIN final_targets ft
      ON pe.uniprot_id = ft.uniprot_id
    WHERE ppt.evidence_code = 'TAS'
      AND pe.uniprot_id IN (SELECT uniprot_id FROM human_uniprots)
    GROUP BY cp.stable_id
  )

-- Final selection: chi-squared, three highest, output counts
SELECT
  ps.stable_id AS pathway_stable_id,
  ps.target_in AS targets_in,
  c.n_target - ps.target_in AS targets_out,
  ps.path_count - ps.target_in AS non_targets_in,
  (c.total_human - c.n_target) - (ps.path_count - ps.target_in) AS non_targets_out
FROM path_stats ps
CROSS JOIN counts c
ORDER BY
  -- chi-squared formula (using SAFE_DIVIDE to avoid division by zero)
  SAFE_DIVIDE(
    ( (ps.target_in * ((c.total_human - c.n_target) - (ps.path_count - ps.target_in))
       - (c.n_target - ps.target_in) * (ps.path_count - ps.target_in) ) ^ 2
      * c.total_human
    ),
    (c.n_target * (c.total_human - c.n_target) * ps.path_count * (c.total_human - ps.path_count))
  ) DESC
LIMIT 3;
```
</details>

```sql
-- This query finds the top 10 countries by the latest available long-term external debt,
-- excluding entries without a specified region (i.e., region is NULL or 'None').
-- Uses the standard World Bank indicator code 'DT.DOD.DLXF.CD' for long-term external debt stocks.

WITH latest_debt AS (
  -- For each country, get the most recent year's value for long-term external debt
  SELECT
    country_code,
    value,
    year
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_debt.international_debt`
  WHERE indicator_code = 'DT.DOD.DLXF.CD'
    AND value IS NOT NULL         -- exclude missing or NaN values
  QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY country_code ORDER BY year DESC) = 1
)

SELECT
  cs.short_name AS country,
  ld.value AS total_long_term_external_debt
FROM latest_debt ld
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_debt.country_summary` cs
  ON ld.country_code = cs.country_code
WHERE
  cs.region IS NOT NULL
  AND cs.region != 'None'          -- exclude aggregates and regions without a defined region
ORDER BY ld.value DESC
LIMIT 10;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify the indicator code for "long-term external debt"
WITH debt_indicator AS (
  SELECT 
    series_code,
    indicator_name,
    short_definition
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_wdi.series_summary`
  WHERE LOWER(indicator_name) LIKE '%long-term external debt%'
     OR LOWER(short_definition) LIKE '%long-term external debt%'
),

-- Step 2: Get values for that indicator across countries and years
debt_values AS (
  SELECT 
    i.country_code,
    i.country_name,
    i.year,
    i.value
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_wdi.indicators_data` i
  INNER JOIN debt_indicator d
    ON i.indicator_code = d.series_code   -- FIXED: series_code -> indicator_code
  WHERE i.value IS NOT NULL
),

-- Step 3: Join with country_summary to get region
country_data AS (
  SELECT 
    dv.country_code,
    dv.country_name,
    dv.value,
    cs.region
  FROM debt_values dv
  LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_wdi.country_summary` cs
    ON dv.country_code = cs.country_code
)

-- Step 4: Aggregate total debt per country, exclude missing region, top 10
SELECT 
  country_code,
  country_name,
  region,
  ROUND(SUM(value), 4) AS total_long_term_external_debt
FROM country_data
WHERE region IS NOT NULL 
  AND region != ''
  AND region != 'None'
GROUP BY country_code, country_name, region
ORDER BY total_long_term_external_debt DESC
LIMIT 10;
```
</details>

**Question**: Using the bigquery-public-data.open_images dataset, can you provide a count of how many distinct image URLs are categorized as 'cat' (where the image has label '/m/01yrx' with confidence=1) and how many distinct image URLs are categorized as 'other' (meaning they have no cat label '/m/01yrx' at all)?

<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

|   cat_image_url_count |   other_image_url_count |
|----------------------:|------------------------:|
|                 40231 |             9.13804e+06 |

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify all image_ids that have the cat label '/m/01yrx' with confidence=1
WITH cat_images AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT image_id
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.open_images.labels`
    WHERE label_name = '/m/01yrx'
      AND confidence = 1
),

-- Step 2: Count distinct image URLs for cat and non-cat images
cat_count AS (
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT img.original_url) AS cat_url_count
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.open_images.images` img
    INNER JOIN cat_images ci ON img.image_id = ci.image_id
),

other_count AS (
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT img.original_url) AS other_url_count
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.open_images.images` img
    WHERE img.image_id NOT IN (SELECT image_id FROM cat_images)
)

-- Step 3: Return both counts in a single row
SELECT 
    cat_url_count AS cat_image_url_count,
    other_url_count AS other_image_url_count
FROM cat_count, other_count;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Use APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT to scan less data while still providing a close estimate
WITH cat_image_ids AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT image_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.open_images.labels`
  WHERE label_name = '/m/01yrx'
    AND confidence = 1
),
cat_total AS (
  SELECT APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT(original_url) AS cat_urls
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.open_images.images`
  WHERE image_id IN (SELECT image_id FROM cat_image_ids)
),
total_urls AS (
  SELECT APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT(original_url) AS total
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.open_images.images`
)
SELECT 'cat' AS category, cat_urls AS distinct_url_count
FROM cat_total
UNION ALL
SELECT 'other', total - cat_urls
FROM total_urls, cat_total;
```
</details>

**Question**: Among all orders that do not appear in the invoice table, for each customer category calculate the maximum lost order value, then determine which customer category’s maximum lost order value is closest to the overall average of these maximum lost order values across all categories?

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>

**OR**

|   CustomerCategoryID | CustomerCategoryName   |   MAX_LOST_ORDER_VALUE |   AVG_OF_MAXES |   DIFF_FROM_AVG |
|---------------------:|:-----------------------|-----------------------:|---------------:|----------------:|
|                    6 | Gift Store             |                   5796 |        5744.48 |           51.52 |

**OR**

|   CustomerCategoryID | CustomerCategoryName   |   max_lost_order_value |   distance_to_avg |
|---------------------:|:-----------------------|-----------------------:|------------------:|
|                    6 | Gift Store             |                   5796 |             51.52 |

<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

| CUSTOMER_CATEGORY   |
|:--------------------|
| Gift Store          |

<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

| CustomerCategoryName   |
|:-----------------------|
| Gift Store             |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: Find orders not in invoices and calculate their total value
"non_invoiced_orders" AS (
    SELECT 
        so."OrderID",
        so."CustomerID",
        SUM(sol."Quantity" * sol."UnitPrice") AS "order_value"
    FROM "WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."SALES_ORDERS" so
    INNER JOIN "WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."SALES_ORDERLINES" sol 
        ON so."OrderID" = sol."OrderID"
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 
        FROM "WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."SALES_INVOICES" si
        WHERE si."OrderID" = so."OrderID"
    )
    GROUP BY so."OrderID", so."CustomerID"
),

-- Step 2: Get max lost order value per customer category
"max_per_category" AS (
    SELECT 
        cc."CustomerCategoryID",
        cc."CustomerCategoryName",
        MAX(nio."order_value") AS "max_lost_value"
    FROM "non_invoiced_orders" nio
    INNER JOIN "WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."SALES_CUSTOMERS" c 
        ON nio."CustomerID" = c."CustomerID"
    INNER JOIN "WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."SALES_CUSTOMERCATEGORIES" cc 
        ON c."CustomerCategoryID" = cc."CustomerCategoryID"
    GROUP BY cc."CustomerCategoryID", cc."CustomerCategoryName"
),

-- Step 3: Calculate overall average of max lost values
"overall_avg" AS (
    SELECT AVG("max_lost_value") AS "avg_max_lost_value"
    FROM "max_per_category"
)

-- Step 4: Find which category's max is closest to the average
SELECT 
    mpc."CustomerCategoryName" AS "CustomerCategoryName"
FROM "max_per_category" mpc
CROSS JOIN "overall_avg" oa
ORDER BY ABS(mpc."max_lost_value" - oa."avg_max_lost_value")
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Identify orders that do NOT appear in the invoice table
lost_orders AS (
    SELECT
        so."OrderID",
        so."CustomerID"
    FROM "WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."SALES_ORDERS" so
    LEFT JOIN "WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."SALES_INVOICES" si
        ON so."OrderID" = si."OrderID"
    WHERE si."InvoiceID" IS NULL
),

-- Step 2: Calculate the total value (Quantity * UnitPrice) for each lost order
order_values AS (
    SELECT
        lo."OrderID",
        SUM(sol."Quantity" * sol."UnitPrice") AS lost_order_value
    FROM lost_orders lo
    INNER JOIN "WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."SALES_ORDERLINES" sol
        ON lo."OrderID" = sol."OrderID"
    GROUP BY lo."OrderID"
),

-- Step 3: For each customer category, calculate the maximum lost order value
category_max_values AS (
    SELECT
        cc."CustomerCategoryName",
        MAX(ov.lost_order_value) AS max_lost_value
    FROM order_values ov
    INNER JOIN lost_orders lo
        ON ov."OrderID" = lo."OrderID"
    INNER JOIN "WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."SALES_CUSTOMERS" c
        ON lo."CustomerID" = c."CustomerID"
    INNER JOIN "WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."SALES_CUSTOMERCATEGORIES" cc
        ON c."CustomerCategoryID" = cc."CustomerCategoryID"
    GROUP BY cc."CustomerCategoryName"
),

-- Step 4: Compute the overall average of these per-category maximum values
overall_avg AS (
    SELECT AVG(max_lost_value) AS avg_max_lost_value
    FROM category_max_values
)

-- Step 5: Determine which customer category's max value is closest to the overall average
SELECT
    cm."CustomerCategoryName" AS customer_category
FROM category_max_values cm
CROSS JOIN overall_avg oa
ORDER BY ROUND(ABS(cm.max_lost_value - oa.avg_max_lost_value), 4)
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

### 68. bq393 (DB: `hacker_news`)
**Question**: I want to identify users who had activity followed by inactivity. Specifically, find the user ID and their corresponding month number (counting from their first activity month) for the user with the highest month number who became inactive (no activity recorded) after their last recorded activity month. For this analysis, only consider data up until September 10, 2024, and ensure the month number represents the count of months since the user's first activity. The user should have at least one month where they were expected to be active (within their activity span) but actually had no records.

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

| USER_ID     |   MONTH_NUMBER |
|:------------|---------------:|
| gaborcselle |            216 |

**OR**

| user_id   |   month_number |
|:----------|---------------:|
| adamsmith |            216 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

| user_id     |   month_number |
|:------------|---------------:|
| gaborcselle |            215 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

N/A

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Get distinct year-month combinations for each user's activity
user_activity_months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    by AS user_id,
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM timestamp) AS activity_year,
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM timestamp) AS activity_month,
    -- Create a date representation for ordering
    DATE_TRUNC(DATE(timestamp), MONTH) AS activity_month_date
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.hacker_news.full`
  WHERE 
    by IS NOT NULL
    AND by != 'None'
    AND (deleted IS NULL OR deleted = FALSE)
    AND (dead IS NULL OR dead = FALSE)
    AND timestamp <= '2024-09-10 23:59:59+00:00'
),

-- Get each user's first and last activity month
user_activity_range AS (
  SELECT
    user_id,
    MIN(activity_month_date) AS first_activity_month,
    MAX(activity_month_date) AS last_activity_month,
    -- Calculate total months span
    DATE_DIFF(MAX(activity_month_date), MIN(activity_month_date), MONTH) AS total_months_span
  FROM user_activity_months
  GROUP BY user_id
  HAVING first_activity_month < last_activity_month  -- User must have at least 2 months of activity
),

-- Generate all expected months for each user
-- Using a numbers table approach for month generation
all_users_expected_months AS (
  SELECT
    r.user_id,
    r.first_activity_month,
    r.last_activity_month,
    -- Generate month number (1-based from first activity)
    offset + 1 AS month_number,
    DATE_ADD(r.first_activity_month, INTERVAL offset MONTH) AS expected_month
  FROM user_activity_range r
  CROSS JOIN UNNEST(GENERATE_ARRAY(0, r.total_months_span)) AS offset
),

-- Find months where user had no activity
inactive_months AS (
  SELECT
    e.user_id,
    e.month_number,
    e.expected_month
  FROM all_users_expected_months e
  LEFT JOIN user_activity_months a
    ON e.user_id = a.user_id
    AND e.expected_month = a.activity_month_date
  WHERE a.user_id IS NULL  -- No activity in this month
)

-- Get the user with the highest month number who had inactivity
SELECT
  user_id,
  MAX(month_number) AS highest_inactive_month_number
FROM inactive_months
GROUP BY user_id
ORDER BY highest_inactive_month_number DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: Get distinct user activity months up to Sep 10, 2024
user_activity_months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    `by` AS user_id,
    DATE_TRUNC(DATE(timestamp), MONTH) AS activity_month
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.hacker_news.full`
  WHERE `by` IS NOT NULL 
    AND LOWER(TRIM(`by`)) != 'none'
    AND `by` != ''
    AND timestamp <= TIMESTAMP('2024-09-10')
),

-- Step 2: Compute first, last, count of active months, and span months for each user
user_first_last AS (
  SELECT
    user_id,
    MIN(activity_month) AS first_month,
    MAX(activity_month) AS last_month,
    COUNT(DISTINCT activity_month) AS num_active_months,
    1 + DATE_DIFF(MAX(activity_month), MIN(activity_month), MONTH) AS span_months
  FROM user_activity_months
  GROUP BY user_id
),

-- Step 3: Users who became inactive after last activity
-- Exclude users whose last activity is in Sep 2024 (cutoff month, can't verify inactivity)
users_inactive_after AS (
  SELECT
    ufl.user_id,
    ufl.first_month,
    ufl.last_month,
    ufl.num_active_months,
    ufl.span_months
  FROM user_first_last ufl
  WHERE ufl.last_month < DATE_TRUNC(DATE('2024-09-10'), MONTH)
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM user_activity_months uam
      WHERE uam.user_id = ufl.user_id
        AND uam.activity_month > ufl.last_month
    )
),

-- Step 4: Users with at least one gap within their activity span
users_with_gaps AS (
  SELECT
    uia.user_id,
    uia.first_month,
    uia.last_month
  FROM users_inactive_after uia
  WHERE uia.num_active_months < uia.span_months
),

-- Step 5: Compute month number (counting from first activity month = 1)
users_final AS (
  SELECT
    uwg.user_id,
    DATE_DIFF(uwg.last_month, uwg.first_month, MONTH) + 1 AS month_number
  FROM users_with_gaps uwg
)

-- Step 6: Get the user with the highest month number
SELECT
  user_id,
  month_number
FROM users_final
ORDER BY month_number DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

```sql
-- Compute median revenue and median functional expenses per year (2012-2017)
-- using APPROX_QUANTILES for efficiency, then compute the absolute difference
-- and select the three years with the smallest difference.

WITH all_years AS (
  -- Union all main 990 tables for 2012-2017, standardizing tax_pd as string
  SELECT 
    CAST(tax_pd AS STRING) AS tax_pd_str,
    totrevenue,
    totfuncexpns
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.irs_990.irs_990_2012`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 
    CAST(tax_pd AS STRING),
    totrevenue,
    totfuncexpns
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.irs_990.irs_990_2013`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 
    CAST(tax_pd AS STRING),
    totrevenue,
    totfuncexpns
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.irs_990.irs_990_2014`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 
    CAST(tax_pd AS STRING),
    totrevenue,
    totfuncexpns
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.irs_990.irs_990_2015`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 
    CAST(tax_pd AS STRING),
    totrevenue,
    totfuncexpns
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.irs_990.irs_990_2016`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 
    CAST(tax_pd AS STRING),
    totrevenue,
    totfuncexpns
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.irs_990.irs_990_2017`
),
with_year AS (
  -- Extract the calendar year from tax_period (first 4 characters)
  -- and keep only non‑null financial values
  SELECT 
    SAFE_CAST(SUBSTR(tax_pd_str, 1, 4) AS INT64) AS year,
    totrevenue,
    totfuncexpns
  FROM all_years
  WHERE SAFE_CAST(SUBSTR(tax_pd_str, 1, 4) AS INT64) BETWEEN 2012 AND 2017
    AND totrevenue IS NOT NULL
    AND totfuncexpns IS NOT NULL
),
medians AS (
  -- Compute median revenue and median expenses per year
  SELECT 
    year,
    APPROX_QUANTILES(totrevenue, 100)[OFFSET(50)] AS median_revenue,
    APPROX_QUANTILES(totfuncexpns, 100)[OFFSET(50)] AS median_func_expenses
  FROM with_year
  GROUP BY year
)
-- Output the three years with the smallest absolute difference
SELECT 
  year,
  ABS(median_revenue - median_func_expenses) AS diff
FROM medians
ORDER BY diff ASC
LIMIT 3
```
</details>

```sql
  UNION ALL

  UNION ALL

  UNION ALL
  SELECT 2017, totrevenue, totfuncexpns
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.irs_990.irs_990_2017`
)
SELECT
  year,
  median_revenue,
  median_expenses,
  ABS(median_revenue - median_expenses) AS diff
FROM (

    APPROX_QUANTILES(totrevenue, 2)[OFFSET(1)] AS median_revenue,
    APPROX_QUANTILES(totfuncexpns, 2)[OFFSET(1)] AS median_expenses
  FROM all_data

)
ORDER BY diff ASC
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Users who had a session_start in the period
sessions AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT user_pseudo_id
    FROM `firebase-public-project.analytics_153293282.events_*`
    WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20180702' AND '20180716'
      AND event_name = 'session_start'
),

-- For those users, get the earliest quickplay event in the period (first quickplay)
first_quickplay AS (
    SELECT
        s.user_pseudo_id,
        MIN(e.event_timestamp) AS first_qp_timestamp,
        -- Get the event_name of that first quickplay event
        ARRAY_AGG(e.event_name ORDER BY e.event_timestamp LIMIT 1)[OFFSET(0)] AS quickplay_type
    FROM sessions s
    JOIN `firebase-public-project.analytics_153293282.events_*` e
        ON s.user_pseudo_id = e.user_pseudo_id
    WHERE e.event_name LIKE '%_quickplay'
      AND e._TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20180702' AND '20180716'
    GROUP BY s.user_pseudo_id
),

-- Check retention on day 14 (exactly 14 days after first quickplay)
retained AS (
    SELECT
        fq.user_pseudo_id,
        fq.quickplay_type,
        fq.first_qp_timestamp,
        -- Check if any event exists in the 24-hour window starting 14 days later
        EXISTS(
            SELECT 1
            FROM `firebase-public-project.analytics_153293282.events_*` rt
            WHERE rt.user_pseudo_id = fq.user_pseudo_id
              AND rt.event_timestamp >= fq.first_qp_timestamp + 14 * 86400 * 1000000
              AND rt.event_timestamp < fq.first_qp_timestamp + 15 * 86400 * 1000000
              -- Scan all tables up to July 30 for retention window
              AND rt._TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20180702' AND '20180730'
        ) AS retained_on_day14
    FROM first_quickplay fq
)

-- Final aggregation: retention rate per quickplay type
SELECT
    quickplay_type,
    COUNT(*) AS total_users,
    SUM(CAST(retained_on_day14 AS INT64)) AS retained_users,
    ROUND(SUM(CAST(retained_on_day14 AS INT64)) / COUNT(*), 4) AS retention_rate
FROM retained
GROUP BY quickplay_type
ORDER BY quickplay_type;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: Identify users who had a session_start between July 2-16, 2018
cohort_users AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT user_pseudo_id
  FROM `firebase-public-project.analytics_153293282.events_*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20180702' AND '20180716'
    AND event_name = 'session_start'
),

-- Step 2: Find first quickplay event for each cohort user within July 2-16, 2018
first_quickplay AS (
  SELECT 
    user_pseudo_id,
    event_name AS quickplay_type,
    event_timestamp,
    PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', event_date) AS event_date
  FROM (
    SELECT 
      e.user_pseudo_id,
      e.event_name,
      e.event_timestamp,
      e.event_date,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
        PARTITION BY e.user_pseudo_id 
        ORDER BY e.event_timestamp ASC
      ) AS rn
    FROM `firebase-public-project.analytics_153293282.events_*` e
    INNER JOIN cohort_users c ON e.user_pseudo_id = c.user_pseudo_id
    WHERE e._TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20180702' AND '20180716'
      AND e.event_name LIKE '%quickplay%'
  )
  WHERE rn = 1
    AND PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', event_date) BETWEEN '2018-07-02' AND '2018-07-16'
),

-- Step 3: Check retention at exactly 14+ days after first quickplay
user_retention AS (
  SELECT 
    f.user_pseudo_id,
    f.quickplay_type,
    MAX(CASE 
      WHEN r.event_timestamp >= f.event_timestamp + 1209600000000 THEN 1 
      ELSE 0 
    END) AS retained
  FROM first_quickplay f
  LEFT JOIN `firebase-public-project.analytics_153293282.events_*` r
    ON f.user_pseudo_id = r.user_pseudo_id
    AND r._TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20180716' AND '20180815'
  GROUP BY f.user_pseudo_id, f.quickplay_type
)

-- Step 4: Compute retention rate
SELECT 
  quickplay_type,
  COUNT(DISTINCT user_pseudo_id) AS total_users,
  SUM(retained) AS retained_users,
  ROUND(
    SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(retained), COUNT(DISTINCT user_pseudo_id)) * 100, 
    2
  ) AS retention_rate_pct
FROM user_retention
GROUP BY quickplay_type
ORDER BY quickplay_type NULLS LAST;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
    -- Aggregate payments per order
    order_payments_sum AS (
        SELECT
            "order_id",
            SUM("payment_value") AS total_payment_per_order
        FROM "order_payments"
        GROUP BY "order_id"
    ),
    -- Compute per‑customer aggregation
    customer_metrics AS (
        SELECT
            c."customer_unique_id",
            COUNT(DISTINCT o."order_id") AS number_of_orders,
            SUM(ops.total_payment_per_order) AS total_payment,
            ROUND(SUM(ops.total_payment_per_order) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT o."order_id"), 4) AS avg_payment_per_order,
            MIN(o."order_purchase_timestamp") AS first_purchase,
            MAX(o."order_purchase_timestamp") AS last_purchase
        FROM "orders" o
        INNER JOIN "order_payments_sum" ops ON o."order_id" = ops."order_id"
        INNER JOIN "customers" c ON o."customer_id" = c."customer_id"
        GROUP BY c."customer_unique_id"
    ),
    -- Compute lifespan and rank
    ranked AS (
        SELECT
            number_of_orders,
            avg_payment_per_order,
            ROUND(
                CASE
                    WHEN julianday(last_purchase) - julianday(first_purchase) < 7 THEN 1.0
                    ELSE (julianday(last_purchase) - julianday(first_purchase)) / 7.0
                END,
                4
            ) AS customer_lifespan_weeks
        FROM customer_metrics
        ORDER BY avg_payment_per_order DESC NULLS LAST
        LIMIT 3
    )
-- Final output
SELECT * FROM ranked;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Compute total payment per order for each customer
WITH order_totals AS (
    SELECT 
        o."customer_id",
        o."order_id",
        o."order_purchase_timestamp",
        SUM(p."payment_value") AS total_payment
    FROM "orders" o
    INNER JOIN "order_payments" p ON o."order_id" = p."order_id"
    GROUP BY o."customer_id", o."order_id", o."order_purchase_timestamp"
),
-- Step 2: Aggregate by customer to get order count, avg payment, and date range
customer_metrics AS (
    SELECT 
        ot."customer_id",
        COUNT(DISTINCT ot."order_id") AS num_orders,
        AVG(ot."total_payment") AS avg_payment_per_order,
        MIN(ot."order_purchase_timestamp") AS first_purchase,
        MAX(ot."order_purchase_timestamp") AS last_purchase
    FROM order_totals ot
    GROUP BY ot."customer_id"
),
-- Step 3: Calculate lifespan in weeks with floor-at-1.0 rule
customer_lifespan AS (
    SELECT 
        "customer_id",
        num_orders,
        avg_payment_per_order,
        CASE 
            WHEN (julianday("last_purchase") - julianday("first_purchase")) / 7.0 < 1.0 
            THEN 1.0
            ELSE (julianday("last_purchase") - julianday("first_purchase")) / 7.0
        END AS lifespan_weeks
    FROM customer_metrics
)
-- Step 4: Return the top 3 customers by highest avg payment per order
SELECT 
    num_orders,
    ROUND(avg_payment_per_order, 4) AS avg_payment,
    ROUND(lifespan_weeks, 4) AS lifespan_weeks
FROM customer_lifespan
ORDER BY avg_payment_per_order DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 3;
```
</details>

```sql
-- Step 1: Player base info
WITH player_info AS (
    SELECT
        "player_id",
        "player_name",
        "batting_hand",
        "bowling_skill"
    FROM "player"
),

-- Step 2: Most frequent role per player (tie resolved by role name)
role_frequency AS (
    SELECT
        "player_id",
        "role",
        COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM "player_match"
    GROUP BY "player_id", "role"
),
ranked_role AS (
    SELECT
        "player_id",
        "role" AS most_frequent_role
    FROM (
        SELECT
            "player_id",
            "role",
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
                PARTITION BY "player_id"
                ORDER BY cnt DESC, "role"
            ) AS rn
        FROM role_frequency
    ) t
    WHERE rn = 1
),

-- Step 3: Total runs scored (by striker)
total_runs AS (
    SELECT
        b."striker" AS player_id,
        SUM(s."runs_scored") AS total_runs
    FROM "ball_by_ball" b
    JOIN "batsman_scored" s
        ON b."match_id" = s."match_id"
        AND b."innings_no" = s."innings_no"
        AND b."over_id" = s."over_id"
        AND b."ball_id" = s."ball_id"
    GROUP BY b."striker"
),

-- Step 4: Total matches played
matches_played AS (
    SELECT
        "player_id",
        COUNT(DISTINCT "match_id") AS total_matches
    FROM "player_match"
    GROUP BY "player_id"
),

-- Step 5: Total dismissals (as batsman out)
dismissals AS (
    SELECT
        "player_out" AS player_id,
        COUNT(*) AS total_dismissals
    FROM "wicket_taken"
    GROUP BY "player_out"
),

-- Step 6: Per match batting aggregates (for highest score and threshold counts)
per_match_runs AS (
    SELECT
        b."striker" AS player_id,
        b."match_id",
        SUM(s."runs_scored") AS match_runs
    FROM "ball_by_ball" b
    JOIN "batsman_scored" s
        ON b."match_id" = s."match_id"
        AND b."innings_no" = s."innings_no"
        AND b."over_id" = s."over_id"
        AND b."ball_id" = s."ball_id"
    GROUP BY b."striker", b."match_id"
),
batting_stats AS (
    SELECT
        player_id,
        MAX(match_runs) AS highest_score,
        SUM(CASE WHEN match_runs >= 30 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS matches_ge30,
        SUM(CASE WHEN match_runs >= 50 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS matches_ge50,
        SUM(CASE WHEN match_runs >= 100 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS matches_ge100
    FROM per_match_runs
    GROUP BY player_id
),

-- Step 7: Balls faced (by striker)
balls_faced AS (
    SELECT
        "striker" AS player_id,
        COUNT(*) AS balls_faced
    FROM "ball_by_ball"
    GROUP BY "striker"
),

-- Step 8: Total wickets taken (as bowler)
wickets_taken AS (
    SELECT
        b."bowler" AS player_id,
        COUNT(*) AS total_wickets
    FROM "wicket_taken" w
    JOIN "ball_by_ball" b
        ON w."match_id" = b."match_id"
        AND w."innings_no" = b."innings_no"
        AND w."over_id" = b."over_id"
        AND w."ball_id" = b."ball_id"
    GROUP BY b."bowler"
),

-- Step 9: Economy rate (bowler runs conceded and balls bowled)
bowler_runs_balls AS (
    SELECT
        b."bowler" AS player_id,
        COUNT(*) AS balls_bowled,
        COALESCE(SUM(s."runs_scored"), 0) AS runs_conceded
    FROM "ball_by_ball" b
    LEFT JOIN "batsman_scored" s
        ON b."match_id" = s."match_id"
        AND b."innings_no" = s."innings_no"
        AND b."over_id" = s."over_id"
        AND b."ball_id" = s."ball_id"
    GROUP BY b."bowler"
),

-- Step 10: Per match bowling performance (wickets and runs conceded) for best performance
per_match_bowling AS (
    SELECT
        b."bowler" AS player_id,
        b."match_id",
        COUNT(w."player_out") AS wickets,
        COALESCE(SUM(s."runs_scored"), 0) AS runs_given
    FROM "ball_by_ball" b
    LEFT JOIN "wicket_taken" w
        ON b."match_id" = w."match_id"
        AND b."innings_no" = w."innings_no"
        AND b."over_id" = w."over_id"
        AND b."ball_id" = w."ball_id"
    LEFT JOIN "batsman_scored" s
        ON b."match_id" = s."match_id"
        AND b."innings_no" = s."innings_no"
        AND b."over_id" = s."over_id"
        AND b."ball_id" = s."ball_id"
    GROUP BY b."bowler", b."match_id"
),
best_bowling AS (
    SELECT
        player_id,
        CAST(wickets AS TEXT) || '-' || CAST(runs_given AS TEXT) AS best_bowling_performance
    FROM (
        SELECT
            player_id,
            wickets,
            runs_given,
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
                PARTITION BY player_id
                ORDER BY wickets DESC, runs_given ASC
            ) AS rn
        FROM per_match_bowling
    ) t
    WHERE rn = 1
)

-- Final SELECT combining all pieces
SELECT
    p."player_id",
    p."player_name",
    r."most_frequent_role",
    p."batting_hand",
    p."bowling_skill",
    COALESCE(tr."total_runs", 0) AS total_runs,
    COALESCE(mp."total_matches", 0) AS total_matches_played,
    COALESCE(d."total_dismissals", 0) AS total_dismissals,
    ROUND(
        CAST(COALESCE(tr."total_runs", 0) AS REAL) / NULLIF(d."total_dismissals", 0),
        4
    ) AS batting_average,
    COALESCE(bs."highest_score", 0) AS highest_score,
    COALESCE(bs."matches_ge30", 0) AS matches_ge30,
    COALESCE(bs."matches_ge50", 0) AS matches_ge50,
    COALESCE(bs."matches_ge100", 0) AS matches_ge100,
    COALESCE(bf."balls_faced", 0) AS total_balls_faced,
    ROUND(
        CAST(COALESCE(tr."total_runs", 0) AS REAL) / NULLIF(bf."balls_faced", 0) * 100,
        4
    ) AS strike_rate,
    COALESCE(wt."total_wickets", 0) AS total_wickets_taken,
    ROUND(
        (CAST(COALESCE(brb."runs_conceded", 0) AS REAL) / NULLIF(brb."balls_bowled", 0)) * 6,
        4
    ) AS economy_rate,
    COALESCE(bb."best_bowling_performance", '0-0') AS best_bowling_performance
FROM player_info p
LEFT JOIN ranked_role r ON p."player_id" = r."player_id"
LEFT JOIN total_runs tr ON p."player_id" = tr."player_id"
LEFT JOIN matches_played mp ON p."player_id" = mp."player_id"
LEFT JOIN dismissals d ON p."player_id" = d."player_id"
LEFT JOIN batting_stats bs ON p."player_id" = bs."player_id"
LEFT JOIN balls_faced bf ON p."player_id" = bf."player_id"
LEFT JOIN wickets_taken wt ON p."player_id" = wt."player_id"
LEFT JOIN bowler_runs_balls brb ON p."player_id" = brb."player_id"
LEFT JOIN best_bowling bb ON p."player_id" = bb."player_id"
ORDER BY p."player_id";
```
</details>

```sql
-- CTE to compute total extras per ball (since extra_runs table may have multiple rows per ball)
WITH extra_by_ball AS (
    SELECT
        match_id,
        innings_no,
        over_id,
        ball_id,
        SUM(extra_runs) AS extra_total
    FROM extra_runs
    GROUP BY match_id, innings_no, over_id, ball_id
),
-- Enrich each ball with runs scored and extras
ball_data AS (
    SELECT
        b.match_id,
        b.innings_no,
        b.over_id,
        b.ball_id,
        b.striker,
        b.non_striker,
        COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0) AS runs_scored,
        COALESCE(e.extra_total, 0) AS extra_runs
    FROM ball_by_ball b
    LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs
        ON b.match_id = bs.match_id
        AND b.innings_no = bs.innings_no
        AND b.over_id = bs.over_id
        AND b.ball_id = bs.ball_id
    LEFT JOIN extra_by_ball e
        ON b.match_id = e.match_id
        AND b.innings_no = e.innings_no
        AND b.over_id = e.over_id
        AND b.ball_id = e.ball_id
),
-- Aggregate by match and unordered player pair
partnership_agg AS (
    SELECT
        match_id,
        MIN(striker, non_striker) AS player1,   -- smaller ID
        MAX(striker, non_striker) AS player2,   -- larger ID
        SUM(runs_scored) + SUM(extra_runs) AS partnership_total,
        -- Individual runs when the player is the striker
        SUM(CASE WHEN striker < non_striker THEN runs_scored ELSE 0 END) AS individual1,
        SUM(CASE WHEN striker > non_striker THEN runs_scored ELSE 0 END) AS individual2
    FROM ball_data
    GROUP BY match_id, player1, player2
),
-- Rank partnerships per match by total runs
ranked AS (
    SELECT
        match_id,
        player1,
        player2,
        individual1,
        individual2,
        partnership_total,
        RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY match_id ORDER BY partnership_total DESC) AS rnk
    FROM partnership_agg
)
-- Final output: reorder players by individual score (desc), then by player ID (desc) in case of tie
SELECT
    match_id,
    CASE
        WHEN individual1 > individual2 THEN player1
        WHEN individual2 > individual1 THEN player2
        ELSE player2   -- if individual scores equal, higher ID becomes player1
    END AS player_id_1,
    CASE
        WHEN individual1 > individual2 THEN player2
        WHEN individual2 > individual1 THEN player1
        ELSE player1
    END AS player_id_2,
    CASE
        WHEN individual1 > individual2 THEN individual1
        WHEN individual2 > individual1 THEN individual2
        ELSE individual2   -- player1' score = individual2 (since player2 has higher ID)
    END AS individual_score_1,
    CASE
        WHEN individual1 > individual2 THEN individual2
        WHEN individual2 > individual1 THEN individual1
        ELSE individual1
    END AS individual_score_2,
    partnership_total
FROM ranked
WHERE rnk = 1
ORDER BY match_id, player_id_1; -- order for readability
```
</details>

<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH ball_data AS (
    SELECT 
        b."match_id",
        b."striker",
        b."non_striker",
        COALESCE(bs."runs_scored", 0) AS runs_scored
    FROM "ball_by_ball" b
    LEFT JOIN "batsman_scored" bs
        ON b."match_id" = bs."match_id"
        AND b."innings_no" = bs."innings_no"
        AND b."over_id" = bs."over_id"
        AND b."ball_id" = bs."ball_id"
),
individual_scores AS (
    SELECT 
        "match_id",
        "striker" AS "player_id",
        SUM("runs_scored") AS individual_score
    FROM ball_data
    GROUP BY "match_id", "striker"
),
partnerships AS (
    SELECT 
        "match_id",
        CASE WHEN "striker" < "non_striker" THEN "striker" ELSE "non_striker" END AS "player_a",
        CASE WHEN "striker" > "non_striker" THEN "striker" ELSE "non_striker" END AS "player_b",
        SUM("runs_scored") AS partnership_runs
    FROM ball_data
    GROUP BY "match_id", 
             CASE WHEN "striker" < "non_striker" THEN "striker" ELSE "non_striker" END,
             CASE WHEN "striker" > "non_striker" THEN "striker" ELSE "non_striker" END
),
ranked_partnerships AS (
    SELECT 
        p.*,
        RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p."match_id" ORDER BY p."partnership_runs" DESC) AS rnk
    FROM partnerships p
),
top_partnerships AS (
    SELECT 
        rp."match_id",
        rp."player_a",
        rp."player_b",
        rp."partnership_runs",
        COALESCE(i1."individual_score", 0) AS score_a,
        COALESCE(i2."individual_score", 0) AS score_b
    FROM ranked_partnerships rp
    LEFT JOIN individual_scores i1 
        ON rp."match_id" = i1."match_id" AND rp."player_a" = i1."player_id"
    LEFT JOIN individual_scores i2
        ON rp."match_id" = i2."match_id" AND rp."player_b" = i2."player_id"
    WHERE rp."rnk" = 1
)
SELECT 
    CASE 
        WHEN score_a > score_b THEN "player_a"
        WHEN score_b > score_a THEN "player_b"
        WHEN "player_a" > "player_b" THEN "player_a"
        ELSE "player_b"
    END AS "player1_id",
    CASE 
        WHEN score_a > score_b THEN "player_b"
        WHEN score_b > score_a THEN "player_a"
        WHEN "player_a" > "player_b" THEN "player_b"
        ELSE "player_a"
    END AS "player2_id",
    CASE 
        WHEN score_a > score_b THEN score_a
        WHEN score_b > score_a THEN score_b
        WHEN "player_a" > "player_b" THEN score_a
        ELSE score_b
    END AS "player1_score",
    CASE 
        WHEN score_a > score_b THEN score_b
        WHEN score_b > score_a THEN score_a
        WHEN "player_a" > "player_b" THEN score_b
        ELSE score_a
    END AS "player2_score",
    "partnership_runs"
FROM top_partnerships
ORDER BY "match_id";
```

```sql
WITH
    first_payment AS (
        SELECT p1.*
        FROM payment p1
        WHERE NOT EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM payment p2
            WHERE p2.customer_id = p1.customer_id
              AND (p2.payment_date < p1.payment_date OR (p2.payment_date = p1.payment_date AND p2.payment_id < p1.payment_id))
        )
    ),
    customer_first_rental AS (
        SELECT fp.customer_id, f.rating
        FROM first_payment fp
        JOIN rental r ON fp.rental_id = r.rental_id
        JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
        JOIN film f ON i.film_id = f.film_id
    ),
    customer_total_spent AS (
        SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total_spent
        FROM payment
        GROUP BY customer_id
    ),
    customer_total_rentals AS (
        SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS total_rentals
        FROM rental
        GROUP BY customer_id
    )
SELECT
    cfr.rating,
    ROUND(AVG(cts.total_spent), 4) AS avg_total_amount_spent,
    ROUND(AVG(ctr.total_rentals - 1), 4) AS avg_subsequent_rentals
FROM customer_first_rental cfr
JOIN customer_total_spent cts ON cfr.customer_id = cts.customer_id
JOIN customer_total_rentals ctr ON cfr.customer_id = ctr.customer_id
GROUP BY cfr.rating
ORDER BY cfr.rating;
```

```sql
WITH 
-- Clean salary values: remove currency symbol, commas, convert monthly to annual
cleaned_salaries AS (
    SELECT 
        "Location",
        "CompanyName",
        CASE 
            WHEN "Salary" LIKE '%/mo' THEN 
                CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE("Salary", '₹', ''), ',', ''), '/mo', '') AS REAL) * 12
            ELSE 
                CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE("Salary", '₹', ''), ',', ''), '/yr', '') AS REAL)
        END AS annual_salary
    FROM "SalaryDataset"
    WHERE "Location" IN ('Mumbai', 'Pune', 'New Delhi', 'Hyderabad')
),
-- Average salary per company per city
city_company_avg AS (
    SELECT 
        "Location",
        "CompanyName",
        ROUND(AVG("annual_salary"), 4) AS avg_salary_in_state
    FROM cleaned_salaries
    GROUP BY "Location", "CompanyName"
),
-- National average across all four cities
national_avg AS (
    SELECT ROUND(AVG("annual_salary"), 4) AS avg_salary_in_country
    FROM cleaned_salaries
),
-- Rank companies within each city by average salary descending
ranked_companies AS (
    SELECT 
        cca."Location",
        cca."CompanyName",
        cca.avg_salary_in_state,
        na.avg_salary_in_country,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY cca."Location" 
            ORDER BY cca.avg_salary_in_state DESC NULLS LAST
        ) AS rank
    FROM city_company_avg cca
    CROSS JOIN national_avg na
)
-- Final output: top 5 per location
SELECT 
    "Location",
    "CompanyName",
    avg_salary_in_state AS "Average Salary in State",
    avg_salary_in_country AS "Average Salary in Country"
FROM ranked_companies
WHERE rank <= 5
ORDER BY "Location", rank;
```
</details>

```sql
-- ============================================================
-- Step 1: Clean Salary data by removing non-numeric characters
-- and converting to annual numeric salary
-- ============================================================
WITH cleaned_salaries AS (
    SELECT
        "Location",
        "CompanyName",
        CASE
            -- If salary is monthly (contains '/mo'), multiply by 12 to annualize
            WHEN "Salary" LIKE '%/mo' THEN
                CAST(
                    REPLACE(
                        REPLACE(
                            REPLACE(
                                REPLACE("Salary", '₹', ''),
                            ',', ''),
                        '/mo', ''),
                    '/yr', '')
                AS REAL) * 12
            -- If salary is yearly ('/yr') or other, use as-is
            ELSE
                CAST(
                    REPLACE(
                        REPLACE(
                            REPLACE(
                                REPLACE("Salary", '₹', ''),
                            ',', ''),
                        '/mo', ''),
                    '/yr', '')
                AS REAL)
        END AS "AnnualSalary"
    FROM "SalaryDataset"
),

-- ============================================================
-- Step 2: Compute the overall national average salary
-- (using ALL locations, not just the 4 target cities)
-- ============================================================
national_average AS (
    SELECT
        AVG("AnnualSalary") AS "NationalAvgSalary"
    FROM "cleaned_salaries"
),

-- ============================================================
-- Step 3: Filter to only the 4 target cities
-- ============================================================
target_city_salaries AS (
    SELECT
        "Location",
        "CompanyName",
        "AnnualSalary"
    FROM "cleaned_salaries"
    WHERE "Location" IN ('Mumbai', 'Pune', 'New Delhi', 'Hyderabad')
),

-- ============================================================
-- Step 4: Calculate average salary per company per city
-- ============================================================
city_company_averages AS (
    SELECT
        "Location",
        "CompanyName",
        AVG("AnnualSalary") AS "AvgSalaryInCity"
    FROM "target_city_salaries"
    GROUP BY "Location", "CompanyName"
),

-- ============================================================
-- Step 5: Join with national average and rank companies
-- within each city by descending average salary
-- ============================================================
ranked_companies AS (
    SELECT
        c."Location",
        c."CompanyName",
        ROUND(c."AvgSalaryInCity", 4)          AS "Average Salary in State",
        ROUND(n."NationalAvgSalary", 4)        AS "Average Salary in Country",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY c."Location"
            ORDER BY c."AvgSalaryInCity" DESC  NULLS LAST
        ) AS "rank"
    FROM "city_company_averages" c
    CROSS JOIN "national_average" n
)

-- ============================================================
-- Step 6: Final output — top 5 companies per city
-- ============================================================
SELECT
    "Location",
    "CompanyName"                                AS "Company Name",
    "Average Salary in State",
    "Average Salary in Country"
FROM "ranked_companies"
WHERE "rank" <= 5
ORDER BY
    "Location",
    "rank";
```
</details>
